meta.blurb_uz: Peterburgning chekkasidagi qorong'i xonada qirq yoshli iste'fodagi amaldor o'tirib, o'zi haqida yozadi: «Men kasal odamman... Men g'arazli odamman.» Birinchi qismda u aql, ikki karra ikki — to'rt, «billur saroy» va inson erkinligi haqida achchiq, paradoksal monolog o'qiydi. Ikkinchi qismda yigirma yil oldingi voqealarni eslaydi: maktabdoshlari bilan sharmandali ziyofat va yosh Liza bilan bo'lgan, umrbod unutilmaydigan uchrashuv.
meta.why_uz: Ko'pchilik ekzistensializmning ilk asari deb biladigan, Nitsshe, Kamyu va Sartrga ta'sir qilgan qisqa, lekin portlovchi roman. «Sizif afsonasi»dan keyin uning tabiiy davomi: Kamyu tilga olgan «yer osti odami» aynan shu yerda. Konstans Garnettning klassik inglizcha tarjimasi — C1 darajasidagi o'quvchi uchun murakkab, ziddiyatli, jonli nutq va falsafiy ingliz tilini o'rganishning ajoyib maktabi.
meta.author_uz: Fyodor Mixaylovich Dostoyevskiy (1821–1881) — rus yozuvchisi. 1849-yilda inqilobiy to'garakda qatnashgani uchun o'limga hukm qilingan, qatl oldidan so'nggi lahzada afv etilib, to'rt yil Sibir katorgasiga yuborilgan. «Yer osti qaydlari» (1864) uning buyuk romanlari — «Jinoyat va jazo», «Telba», «Jinlar», «Aka-uka Karamazovlar» — uchun ostona bo'ldi.
meta.edition_uz: To'liq matn: Konstans Garnett inglizcha tarjimasi (1918; Project Gutenberg #600), o'zbekcha tarjimasi WordDrop tomonidan qo'lda qilingan. Nekrasov she'ridan olingan epigraf Juliet Soskice tarjimasida. Muqova rasmi — Vintage Classics nashri dizayni (unda Pevear–Volokhonskiy tarjimasi ko'rsatilgan, lekin bu yerdagi matn — Garnett tarjimasi; Pevear–Volokhonskiy tarjimasi mualliflik huquqi bilan himoyalangan).
meta.warn_uz: Asarda fohishalik muhiti, ayolni ataylab xo'rlash va ruhiy shafqatsizlik, zo'ravonlik, o'lim va qashshoqlikning og'ir tasvirlari bor; hikoyachining ayollar va odamlar haqidagi ko'p gaplari kinik va haqoratli. Shuningdek, XIX asr rus milliy qarashlariga xos ba'zi umumlashtirishlar uchraydi.

chapters.title: A sick and spiteful man

paras.en: The author of the diary and the diary itself are, of course, imaginary. Nevertheless it is clear that such persons as the writer of these notes not only may, but positively must, exist in our society, when we consider the circumstances in the midst of which our society is formed. I have tried to expose to the view of the public more distinctly than is commonly done, one of the characters of the recent past. He is one of the representatives of a generation still living. In this fragment, entitled "Underground," this person introduces himself and his views, and, as it were, tries to explain the causes owing to which he has made his appearance and was bound to make his appearance in our midst. In the second fragment there are added the actual notes of this person concerning certain events in his life.—Author's note.
paras.uz: Kundalik muallifi ham, kundalikning o'zi ham, albatta, to'qima. Shunga qaramay, jamiyatimiz qanday sharoitlar orasida shakllanayotganini hisobga olsak, bu qaydlar muallifi kabi odamlar jamiyatimizda nafaqat bo'lishi mumkin, balki albatta bo'lishi kerakligi aniq. Men yaqin o'tmish qahramonlaridan birini jamoatchilik nazariga odatdagidan aniqroq ko'rsatishga harakat qildim. U hali ham yashayotgan avlodning vakillaridan biri. «Yer osti» deb nomlangan bu parchada bu odam o'zini va qarashlarini tanishtiradi va go'yo oramizda paydo bo'lganining va paydo bo'lishi muqarrar bo'lganining sabablarini tushuntirishga urinadi. Ikkinchi parchaga esa bu odamning hayotidagi ba'zi voqealar haqidagi asl qaydlari qo'shilgan. — Muallif izohi.

paras.en: I am a sick man.... I am a spiteful man. I am an unattractive man. I believe my liver is diseased. However, I know nothing at all about my disease, and do not know for certain what ails me. I don't consult a doctor for it, and never have, though I have a respect for medicine and doctors. Besides, I am extremely superstitious, sufficiently so to respect medicine, anyway (I am well-educated enough not to be superstitious, but I am superstitious). No, I refuse to consult a doctor from spite. That you probably will not understand. Well, I understand it, though. Of course, I can't explain who it is precisely that I am mortifying in this case by my spite: I am perfectly well aware that I cannot "pay out" the doctors by not consulting them; I know better than anyone that by all this I am only injuring myself and no one else. But still, if I don't consult a doctor it is from spite. My liver is bad, well—let it get worse!
paras.uz: Men kasal odamman... Men g'arazli odamman. Men yoqimsiz odamman. Menimcha, jigarim kasal. Biroq men kasalligim haqida hech narsa bilmayman va menga aniq nima bo'lganini ham bilmayman. Buning uchun shifokorga bormayman va hech qachon bormaganman, garchi tibbiyotni va shifokorlarni hurmat qilsam ham. Bundan tashqari, men nihoyatda irimchiman, hech bo'lmaganda tibbiyotni hurmat qiladigan darajada (men irimchi bo'lmaslik uchun yetarlicha o'qimishliman, lekin irimchiman). Yo'q, men shifokorga g'arazdan bormayman. Buni siz, ehtimol, tushunmaysiz. Men esa tushunaman. Albatta, bu holda o'z g'arazim bilan aynan kimni xo'rlayotganimni tushuntira olmayman: shifokorlarga bormaslik bilan ulardan «o'ch ololmasligimni» juda yaxshi bilaman; bularning hammasi bilan faqat o'zimga zarar yetkazayotganimni, boshqa hech kimga emasligini hammadan yaxshiroq bilaman. Lekin baribir, agar shifokorga bormasam, bu g'arazdan. Jigarim yomonmi, mayli — battar bo'laversin!

paras.en: I have been going on like that for a long time—twenty years. Now I am forty. I used to be in the government service, but am no longer. I was a spiteful official. I was rude and took pleasure in being so. I did not take bribes, you see, so I was bound to find a recompense in that, at least. (A poor jest, but I will not scratch it out. I wrote it thinking it would sound very witty; but now that I have seen myself that I only wanted to show off in a despicable way, I will not scratch it out on purpose!)
paras.uz: Men uzoq vaqtdan beri shunday yashayapman — yigirma yildan beri. Hozir men qirq yoshdaman. Ilgari davlat xizmatida edim, endi emasman. Men g'arazli amaldor edim. Qo'pol edim va bundan zavq olardim. Axir pora olmasdim, shuning uchun hech bo'lmaganda shundan o'zimga mukofot topishim kerak edi. (Arzimas hazil, lekin uni o'chirmayman. Men uni juda o'tkir eshitiladi deb o'ylab yozgan edim; endi esa o'zim ko'rib turibmanki, faqat jirkanch tarzda maqtanmoqchi bo'lganman, shuning uchun ataylab o'chirmayman!)

paras.en: When petitioners used to come for information to the table at which I sat, I used to grind my teeth at them, and felt intense enjoyment when I succeeded in making anybody unhappy. I almost did succeed. For the most part they were all timid people—of course, they were petitioners. But of the uppish ones there was one officer in particular I could not endure. He simply would not be humble, and clanked his sword in a disgusting way. I carried on a feud with him for eighteen months over that sword. At last I got the better of him. He left off clanking it. That happened in my youth, though.
paras.uz: Arzchilar men o'tirgan stol oldiga ma'lumot olish uchun kelishganda, ularga tish g'ijirlatardim va kimnidir xafa qilishga muvaffaq bo'lganimda kuchli zavq his qilardim. Deyarli har doim muvaffaq bo'lardim. Ko'pincha ular hammasi tortinchoq odamlar edi — axir arzchilar. Lekin kekkayganlar orasida bir zobit bor ediki, unga sira chiday olmasdim. U hech qachon kamtar bo'lishni istamasdi va qilichini jirkanch tarzda shaqillatardi. O'sha qilich uchun u bilan o'n sakkiz oy adovat qildim. Oxiri uni yengdim. U shaqillatishni bas qildi. Bu, to'g'ri, yoshligimda bo'lgan.

paras.en: But do you know, gentlemen, what was the chief point about my spite? Why, the whole point, the real sting of it lay in the fact that continually, even in the moment of the acutest spleen, I was inwardly conscious with shame that I was not only not a spiteful but not even an embittered man, that I was simply scaring sparrows at random and amusing myself by it. I might foam at the mouth, but bring me a doll to play with, give me a cup of tea with sugar in it, and maybe I should be appeased. I might even be genuinely touched, though probably I should grind my teeth at myself afterwards and lie awake at night with shame for months after. That was my way.
paras.uz: Lekin bilasizmi, janoblar, mening g'arazimning asosiy nuqtasi nima edi? Gap shundaki, butun gap, uning asl nishi shunda ediki, doimo, hatto eng qattiq jahl chiqqan lahzada ham, men ichimda uyat bilan nafaqat g'arazli, balki hatto achchig'langan odam ham emasligimni, shunchaki chumchuqlarni behuda cho'chitib, bundan o'zimni ovuntirayotganimni anglardim. Og'zimdan ko'pik sachratishim mumkin edi, lekin menga o'ynash uchun qo'g'irchoq olib kelinglar, shakarli bir piyola choy beringlar — balki tinchlanib qolardim. Hatto chin dildan ta'sirlanishim ham mumkin edi, garchi keyin, ehtimol, o'zimga tish g'ijirlatib, oylab tunlari uyatdan uxlolmay yotsam ham. Mening odatim shunday edi.

paras.en: I was lying when I said just now that I was a spiteful official. I was lying from spite. I was simply amusing myself with the petitioners and with the officer, and in reality I never could become spiteful. I was conscious every moment in myself of many, very many elements absolutely opposite to that. I felt them positively swarming in me, these opposite elements. I knew that they had been swarming in me all my life and craving some outlet from me, but I would not let them, would not let them, purposely would not let them come out. They tormented me till I was ashamed: they drove me to convulsions and—sickened me, at last, how they sickened me! Now, are not you fancying, gentlemen, that I am expressing remorse for something now, that I am asking your forgiveness for something? I am sure you are fancying that ... However, I assure you I do not care if you are....
paras.uz: Hozirgina g'arazli amaldor edim deganimda yolg'on gapirdim. G'arazdan yolg'on gapirdim. Men shunchaki arzchilar va zobit bilan o'zimni ovuntirardim, aslida esa hech qachon g'arazli bo'la olmasdim. Har lahza o'zimda bunga mutlaqo qarama-qarshi bo'lgan ko'p, juda ko'p unsurlarni anglardim. Men ularning ichimda g'ujg'on o'ynayotganini his qilardim, bu qarama-qarshi unsurlarni. Ular butun umrim davomida ichimda g'ujg'on o'ynaganini va mendan qandaydir chiqish yo'li so'raganini bilardim, lekin men ularga yo'l qo'ymasdim, yo'l qo'ymasdim, ataylab tashqariga chiqishiga yo'l qo'ymasdim. Ular meni uyalguncha qiynardi: talvasaga solardi va — oxiri ko'nglimni aynitardi, qanday aynitardi! Xo'sh, janoblar, endi menga go'yo nimadandir tavba qilayotgandek, sizdan nimadir uchun kechirim so'rayotgandek tuyulmayaptimi? Ishonchim komilki, shunday tuyulyapti... Biroq sizni ishontirib aytamanki, shunday tuyulsa ham, menga baribir...

paras.en: It was not only that I could not become spiteful, I did not know how to become anything; neither spiteful nor kind, neither a rascal nor an honest man, neither a hero nor an insect. Now, I am living out my life in my corner, taunting myself with the spiteful and useless consolation that an intelligent man cannot become anything seriously, and it is only the fool who becomes anything. Yes, a man in the nineteenth century must and morally ought to be pre-eminently a characterless creature; a man of character, an active man is pre-eminently a limited creature. That is my conviction of forty years. I am forty years old now, and you know forty years is a whole lifetime; you know it is extreme old age. To live longer than forty years is bad manners, is vulgar, immoral. Who does live beyond forty? Answer that, sincerely and honestly I will tell you who do: fools and worthless fellows.
paras.uz: Gap faqat g'arazli bo'la olmaganimda emas edi, men umuman hech narsa bo'lishni bilmasdim: na g'arazli, na mehribon, na yaramas, na halol odam, na qahramon, na hasharot. Endi esa men o'z burchagimda umrimni o'tkazyapman, aqlli odam jiddiy ravishda hech narsa bo'la olmaydi, faqat ahmoqgina nimadir bo'ladi, degan g'arazli va foydasiz tasalli bilan o'zimni masxara qilib. Ha, o'n to'qqizinchi asr odami asosan xarakteri yo'q mavjudot bo'lishi kerak va axloqan majbur; xarakterli odam, faol odam esa asosan cheklangan mavjudotdir. Bu mening qirq yillik e'tiqodim. Men hozir qirq yoshdaman, qirq yil esa butun bir umr-ku; axir bu eng chuqur qarilik. Qirq yildan ortiq yashash odobsizlik, tubanlik, axloqsizlik. Qirqdan ortiq kim yashaydi? Bunga samimiy va halol javob bering. Men sizga aytaman kimlar yashaydi: ahmoqlar va yaramaslar.

paras.en: I tell all old men that to their face, all these venerable old men, all these silver-haired and reverend seniors! I tell the whole world that to its face! I have a right to say so, for I shall go on living to sixty myself. To seventy! To eighty! ... Stay, let me take breath ...
paras.uz: Buni men barcha qariyalarga yuzlariga aytaman, barcha muhtaram qariyalarga, barcha kumush sochli va muhtaram oqsoqollarga! Butun dunyoga yuziga aytaman! Buni aytishga haqqim bor, chunki o'zim oltmishgacha yashayman. Yetmishgacha! Saksongacha!.. To'xtang, nafasimni rostlay...

paras.en: You imagine no doubt, gentlemen, that I want to amuse you. You are mistaken in that, too. I am by no means such a mirthful person as you imagine, or as you may imagine; however, irritated by all this babble (and I feel that you are irritated) you think fit to ask me who I am—then my answer is, I am a collegiate assessor. I was in the service that I might have something to eat (and solely for that reason), and when last year a distant relation left me six thousand roubles in his will I immediately retired from the service and settled down in my corner. I used to live in this corner before, but now I have settled down in it. My room is a wretched, horrid one in the outskirts of the town. My servant is an old country-woman, ill-natured from stupidity, and, moreover, there is always a nasty smell about her.
paras.uz: Siz, shubhasiz, men sizni kuldirmoqchiman deb o'ylayapsiz, janoblar. Bunda ham adashyapsiz. Men siz o'ylaganingizdek yoki o'ylashingiz mumkin bo'lganidek quvnoq odam emasman; biroq, bu valdirashdan jahlingiz chiqib (jahlingiz chiqayotganini his qilib turibman), mendan kimsan, deb so'rashni lozim ko'rsangiz, — unda javobim shu: men kollejskiy asessorman. Xizmat qilganim yeyishga biror narsa bo'lsin deb edi (faqat shu sababdan), o'tgan yili esa uzoq bir qarindoshim vasiyatnomasida menga olti ming rubl qoldirgach, men darhol iste'foga chiqib, o'z burchagimga joylashdim. Ilgari ham shu burchakda yashardim, lekin endi unga butunlay o'rnashib oldim. Xonam shahar chekkasidagi ayanchli, xunuk xona. Xizmatkorim — ahmoqligidan jahldor bo'lgan qishloqlik kampir, buning ustiga undan doim yoqimsiz hid keladi.

paras.en: I am told that the Petersburg climate is bad for me, and that with my small means it is very expensive to live in Petersburg. I know all that better than all these sage and experienced counsellors and monitors.... But I am remaining in Petersburg; I am not going away from Petersburg! I am not going away because ... Ech! Why, it is absolutely no matter whether I am going away or not going away.
paras.uz: Menga Peterburg iqlimi menga zararli ekanini va kam mablag'im bilan Peterburgda yashash juda qimmatligini aytishadi. Bularning hammasini men o'sha donishmand va tajribali maslahatchilar va nasihatgo'ylardan yaxshiroq bilaman... Lekin men Peterburgda qolyapman; men Peterburgdan ketmayman! Ketmayman, chunki... Eh! Axir ketamanmi yoki ketmaymanmi — mutlaqo farqi yo'q.

paras.en: But what can a decent man speak of with most pleasure?
paras.uz: Lekin odobli odam nima haqida eng katta zavq bilan gapirishi mumkin?

paras.en: Answer: Of himself.
paras.uz: Javob: o'zi haqida.

paras.en: Well, so I will talk about myself.
paras.uz: Xo'sh, unda men ham o'zim haqimda gapiraman.

chapters.recap_uz: Muallif izohi va hikoyachining o'zini tanishtirishi: qirq yoshli iste'fodagi amaldor, kasal, g'arazli, Peterburg chekkasidagi burchagida yashaydi. U g'arazli bo'la olmaganini, umuman hech narsa — na qahramon, na hasharot bo'la olmaganini tan oladi.

chapters.title: Too much consciousness

paras.en: I want now to tell you, gentlemen, whether you care to hear it or not, why I could not even become an insect. I tell you solemnly, that I have many times tried to become an insect. But I was not equal even to that. I swear, gentlemen, that to be too conscious is an illness—a real thorough-going illness. For man's everyday needs, it would have been quite enough to have the ordinary human consciousness, that is, half or a quarter of the amount which falls to the lot of a cultivated man of our unhappy nineteenth century, especially one who has the fatal ill-luck to inhabit Petersburg, the most theoretical and intentional town on the whole terrestrial globe. (There are intentional and unintentional towns.) It would have been quite enough, for instance, to have the consciousness by which all so-called direct persons and men of action live. I bet you think I am writing all this from affectation, to be witty at the expense of men of action; and what is more, that from ill-bred affectation, I am clanking a sword like my officer. But, gentlemen, whoever can pride himself on his diseases and even swagger over them?
paras.uz: Endi men sizga, janoblar, eshitishni istaysizmi yoki yo'qmi, nega hatto hasharot ham bo'la olmaganimni aytib bermoqchiman. Sizga tantanali aytaman: men ko'p marta hasharot bo'lishga uringanman. Lekin bunga ham qurbim yetmadi. Qasamki, janoblar, haddan tashqari ongli bo'lish — kasallik, haqiqiy, to'laqonli kasallik. Insonning kundalik ehtiyojlari uchun oddiy inson ongi, ya'ni bizning baxtsiz o'n to'qqizinchi asrimizning madaniyatli odamiga, ayniqsa butun yer sharidagi eng nazariy va eng qasddan qurilgan shahar — Peterburgda yashashdek halokatli omadsizlikka uchragan odamga nasib etadigan ongning yarmi yoki choragi ham butunlay yetarli bo'lardi. (Qasddan qurilgan va qasdsiz shaharlar bo'ladi.) Masalan, barcha «to'g'ridan-to'g'ri odamlar» va «harakat odamlari» deb ataladiganlar yashaydigan ong ham butunlay yetarli bo'lardi. Garov o'ynayman, siz bularning hammasini men harakat odamlari hisobiga o'tkir gapirish uchun, o'zimni ko'rsatish uchun yozyapman deb o'ylayapsiz; buning ustiga, tarbiyasiz kibrdan zobitim kabi qilich shaqillatyapman deb o'ylayapsiz. Lekin, janoblar, kim o'z kasalliklari bilan faxrlana oladi va hatto ular bilan kerilib yura oladi?

paras.en: Though, after all, everyone does do that; people do pride themselves on their diseases, and I do, may be, more than anyone. We will not dispute it; my contention was absurd. But yet I am firmly persuaded that a great deal of consciousness, every sort of consciousness, in fact, is a disease. I stick to that. Let us leave that, too, for a minute. Tell me this: why does it happen that at the very, yes, at the very moments when I am most capable of feeling every refinement of all that is "sublime and beautiful," as they used to say at one time, it would, as though of design, happen to me not only to feel but to do such ugly things, such that ... Well, in short, actions that all, perhaps, commit; but which, as though purposely, occurred to me at the very time when I was most conscious that they ought not to be committed.
paras.uz: Darvoqe, axir hamma shunday qiladi; odamlar o'z kasalliklari bilan faxrlanishadi, men esa, ehtimol, hammadan ko'proq. Bahslashmaymiz; e'tirozim bema'ni edi. Lekin baribir qat'iy ishonamanki, ko'p ong, umuman har qanday ong — kasallik. Bunda turib olaman. Buni ham bir daqiqaga qoldiraylik. Menga ayting-chi: nega aynan, ha, aynan bir vaqtlar aytilganidek «go'zal va ulug'vor» bo'lgan hamma narsaning har bir nozikligini his qilishga eng qodir bo'lgan lahzalarimda, go'yo ataylab, menda nafaqat his qilish, balki shunday xunuk ishlar qilish ham sodir bo'lardi, shunday... Xullas, ehtimol, hamma qiladigan ishlar; lekin ular go'yo ataylab menga aynan ularni qilmaslik kerakligini eng ko'p anglagan paytimda yuz berardi.

paras.en: The more conscious I was of goodness and of all that was "sublime and beautiful," the more deeply I sank into my mire and the more ready I was to sink in it altogether. But the chief point was that all this was, as it were, not accidental in me, but as though it were bound to be so. It was as though it were my most normal condition, and not in the least disease or depravity, so that at last all desire in me to struggle against this depravity passed. It ended by my almost believing (perhaps actually believing) that this was perhaps my normal condition. But at first, in the beginning, what agonies I endured in that struggle! I did not believe it was the same with other people, and all my life I hid this fact about myself as a secret.
paras.uz: Men yaxshilikni va «go'zal va ulug'vor» bo'lgan hamma narsani qanchalik ko'p anglasam, o'z botqog'imga shunchalik chuqurroq botardim va unga butunlay cho'kishga shunchalik tayyor bo'lardim. Lekin asosiy gap shunda ediki, bularning hammasi menda go'yo tasodifiy emas, balki shunday bo'lishi shart bo'lgandek edi. Go'yo bu mening eng odatiy holatim bo'lgandek, mutlaqo kasallik yoki buzuqlik emasdek edi, shuning uchun oxiri menda bu buzuqlikka qarshi kurashish istagi butunlay yo'qoldi. Oxiri bu, ehtimol, mening odatiy holatimdir, deb deyarli ishonib qoldim (balki haqiqatan ishonib qoldim). Lekin avvaliga, boshida, bu kurashda qanday azoblar chekdim! Boshqalarda ham shunday deb ishonmasdim va butun umrim davomida o'zimdagi bu holatni sir sifatida yashirdim.

paras.en: I was ashamed (even now, perhaps, I am ashamed): I got to the point of feeling a sort of secret abnormal, despicable enjoyment in returning home to my corner on some disgusting Petersburg night, acutely conscious that that day I had committed a loathsome action again, that what was done could never be undone, and secretly, inwardly gnawing, gnawing at myself for it, tearing and consuming myself till at last the bitterness turned into a sort of shameful accursed sweetness, and at last—into positive real enjoyment! Yes, into enjoyment, into enjoyment! I insist upon that. I have spoken of this because I keep wanting to know for a fact whether other people feel such enjoyment?
paras.uz: Men uyalardim (balki hozir ham uyalaman): men qandaydir jirkanch Peterburg tunida o'z burchagimga qaytib, o'sha kuni yana qabih ish qilganimni, qilingan ishni hech qachon qaytarib bo'lmasligini o'tkir anglash va buning uchun yashirincha, ichimdan o'zimni kemirish, kemirish, o'zimni tirnab, yeb bitirish orqali, oxiri achchiqlik qandaydir uyatli, la'nati shirinlikka va nihoyat — haqiqiy, chinakam zavqqa aylanguncha, qandaydir yashirin, g'ayritabiiy, tuban zavq his qiladigan darajaga yetib kelgan edim! Ha, zavqqa, zavqqa! Bunda turib olaman. Bu haqda gapirdim, chunki boshqalar ham bunday zavqni his qiladimi, buni aniq bilishni istayman.

paras.en: I will explain; the enjoyment was just from the too intense consciousness of one's own degradation; it was from feeling oneself that one had reached the last barrier, that it was horrible, but that it could not be otherwise; that there was no escape for you; that you never could become a different man; that even if time and faith were still left you to change into something different you would most likely not wish to change; or if you did wish to, even then you would do nothing; because perhaps in reality there was nothing for you to change into.
paras.uz: Tushuntirib beraman: zavq aynan o'z xo'rligingni haddan tashqari kuchli anglashdan edi; oxirgi chegaraga yetib kelganingni, bu dahshatli ekanini, lekin boshqacha bo'lishi mumkin emasligini his qilishdan edi; sen uchun chiqish yo'li yo'qligini; hech qachon boshqa odamga aylana olmasligingni; hatto boshqa narsaga aylanish uchun vaqt va ishonch qolgan bo'lsa ham, ehtimol, o'zgarishni istamasliging; yoki istasang ham, baribir hech narsa qilmasliging; chunki, ehtimol, aslida aylanadigan narsa ham yo'qligini his qilishdan edi.

paras.en: And the worst of it was, and the root of it all, that it was all in accord with the normal fundamental laws of over-acute consciousness, and with the inertia that was the direct result of those laws, and that consequently one was not only unable to change but could do absolutely nothing. Thus it would follow, as the result of acute consciousness, that one is not to blame in being a scoundrel; as though that were any consolation to the scoundrel once he has come to realise that he actually is a scoundrel. But enough.... Ech, I have talked a lot of nonsense, but what have I explained? How is enjoyment in this to be explained? But I will explain it. I will get to the bottom of it! That is why I have taken up my pen....
paras.uz: Eng yomoni va hamma narsaning ildizi shunda ediki, bularning hammasi haddan tashqari o'tkir ongning odatiy asosiy qonunlariga va shu qonunlarning bevosita natijasi bo'lgan inertsiyaga muvofiq edi va demak, inson nafaqat o'zgara olmasdi, balki mutlaqo hech narsa qila olmasdi. Shunday qilib, o'tkir ong natijasida, yaramas bo'lganing uchun aybdor emassan degan xulosa kelib chiqardi; go'yo yaramas o'zining haqiqatan yaramas ekanini anglab yetgandan keyin bu unga qandaydir tasalli bo'ladigandek. Lekin bas... Eh, ko'p bema'ni gaplar gapirdim, lekin nimani tushuntirdim? Bundagi zavqni qanday tushuntirish mumkin? Lekin tushuntiraman. Tagiga yetaman! Qo'limga qalam olganim ham shuning uchun...

paras.en: I, for instance, have a great deal of amour propre. I am as suspicious and prone to take offence as a humpback or a dwarf. But upon my word I sometimes have had moments when if I had happened to be slapped in the face I should, perhaps, have been positively glad of it. I say, in earnest, that I should probably have been able to discover even in that a peculiar sort of enjoyment—the enjoyment, of course, of despair; but in despair there are the most intense enjoyments, especially when one is very acutely conscious of the hopelessness of one's position. And when one is slapped in the face—why then the consciousness of being rubbed into a pulp would positively overwhelm one. The worst of it is, look at it which way one will, it still turns out that I was always the most to blame in everything.
paras.uz: Men, masalan, juda izzattalabman. Men bukri yoki pakana kabi shubhali va arazchiman. Lekin rostini aytsam, ba'zan shunday lahzalarim bo'lganki, agar yuzimga tarsaki tushirishganida, ehtimol, bundan hatto xursand bo'lgan bo'lardim. Jiddiy aytyapman: ehtimol, hatto bunda ham o'ziga xos zavqni topa olgan bo'lardim — albatta, umidsizlik zavqini; lekin umidsizlikda eng kuchli zavqlar bo'ladi, ayniqsa inson o'z ahvolining umidsizligini juda o'tkir anglaganda. Yuzingga tarsaki tushirishganda esa — o'shanda ezib, xamirga aylantirilganingni anglash seni butunlay bosib ketadi. Eng yomoni, qaysi tomondan qarama, baribir men har doim hamma narsada eng aybdor bo'lib chiqardim.

paras.en: And what is most humiliating of all, to blame for no fault of my own but, so to say, through the laws of nature. In the first place, to blame because I am cleverer than any of the people surrounding me. (I have always considered myself cleverer than any of the people surrounding me, and sometimes, would you believe it, have been positively ashamed of it. At any rate, I have all my life, as it were, turned my eyes away and never could look people straight in the face.) To blame, finally, because even if I had had magnanimity, I should only have had more suffering from the sense of its uselessness. I should certainly have never been able to do anything from being magnanimous—neither to forgive, for my assailant would perhaps have slapped me from the laws of nature, and one cannot forgive the laws of nature; nor to forget, for even if it were owing to the laws of nature, it is insulting all the same.
paras.uz: Eng xo'rlovchisi esa — o'z aybim bilan emas, balki, ta'bir joiz bo'lsa, tabiat qonunlari tufayli aybdor bo'lish. Birinchidan, atrofimdagi har qanday odamdan aqlliroq bo'lganim uchun aybdor. (Men doim o'zimni atrofimdagi har qanday odamdan aqlliroq deb hisoblaganman va ba'zan, ishonasizmi, bundan hatto uyalganman. Har holda, butun umr go'yo ko'zimni olib qochganman va hech qachon odamlarning yuziga to'g'ri qaray olmaganman.) Nihoyat, agar menda olijanoblik bo'lganida ham, uning foydasizligini anglashdan faqat ko'proq azob chekkan bo'lardim, shuning uchun aybdor. Olijanoblikdan hech qachon hech narsa qila olmagan bo'lardim — na kechira olardim, chunki meni urgan odam, ehtimol, tabiat qonunlariga ko'ra urgan bo'lardi, tabiat qonunlarini esa kechirib bo'lmaydi; na unuta olardim, chunki hatto tabiat qonunlari tufayli bo'lsa ham, baribir haqoratli.

paras.en: Finally, even if I had wanted to be anything but magnanimous, had desired on the contrary to revenge myself on my assailant, I could not have revenged myself on any one for anything because I should certainly never have made up my mind to do anything, even if I had been able to. Why should I not have made up my mind? About that in particular I want to say a few words.
paras.uz: Nihoyat, agar men olijanob bo'lishni emas, aksincha, meni urgandan o'ch olishni istaganimda ham, hech kimdan hech narsa uchun o'ch ololmagan bo'lardim, chunki qila olganimda ham, hech qachon biror narsa qilishga qaror qila olmagan bo'lardim. Nega qaror qila olmagan bo'lardim? Aynan shu haqda bir necha so'z aytmoqchiman.

quiz.q: What does the narrator call 'a real thorough-going illness'?
quiz.why_uz: Haddan tashqari ongli bo'lish — haqiqiy kasallik.

quiz.q: What strange feeling does he describe?
quiz.why_uz: O'z xo'rligini anglashdan yashirin zavq.

chapters.recap_uz: Hikoyachi haddan tashqari ong — kasallik ekanini aytadi. U o'z xo'rligidan, qilgan qabih ishlaridan yashirin zavq olishini tan oladi va bu zavqni tushuntirishga urinadi.

chapters.title: The mouse and the stone wall

paras.en: With people who know how to revenge themselves and to stand up for themselves in general, how is it done? Why, when they are possessed, let us suppose, by the feeling of revenge, then for the time there is nothing else but that feeling left in their whole being. Such a gentleman simply dashes straight for his object like an infuriated bull with its horns down, and nothing but a wall will stop him. (By the way: facing the wall, such gentlemen—that is, the "direct" persons and men of action—are genuinely nonplussed. For them a wall is not an evasion, as for us people who think and consequently do nothing; it is not an excuse for turning aside, an excuse for which we are always very glad, though we scarcely believe in it ourselves, as a rule. No, they are nonplussed in all sincerity. The wall has for them something tranquillising, morally soothing, final—maybe even something mysterious ... But of the wall later.)
paras.uz: O'ch olishni va umuman o'zini himoya qilishni biladigan odamlarda bu qanday bo'ladi? Masalan, ularni, faraz qilaylik, qasos tuyg'usi chulg'ab olganda, o'sha paytda butun borlig'ida shu tuyg'udan boshqa hech narsa qolmaydi. Bunday janob shoxlarini egib olgan quturgan buqadek to'g'ri maqsadi sari otiladi va uni faqat devor to'xtata oladi. (Aytgancha: devor oldida bunday janoblar — ya'ni «to'g'ridan-to'g'ri» odamlar va harakat odamlari — chin dildan dovdirab qolishadi. Ular uchun devor — biz, fikrlaydigan va shuning uchun hech narsa qilmaydigan odamlar uchun bo'lganidek, bahona emas; u yo'ldan qaytish uchun bahona emas, biz bunday bahonadan doim juda xursand bo'lamiz, garchi odatda o'zimiz ham unga zo'rg'a ishonsak ham. Yo'q, ular chin dildan dovdirab qolishadi. Devorda ular uchun qandaydir tinchlantiruvchi, axloqan yupatuvchi, yakuniy — balki hatto qandaydir sirli narsa bor... Lekin devor haqida keyinroq.)

paras.en: Well, such a direct person I regard as the real normal man, as his tender mother nature wished to see him when she graciously brought him into being on the earth. I envy such a man till I am green in the face. He is stupid. I am not disputing that, but perhaps the normal man should be stupid, how do you know? Perhaps it is very beautiful, in fact. And I am the more persuaded of that suspicion, if one can call it so, by the fact that if you take, for instance, the antithesis of the normal man, that is, the man of acute consciousness, who has come, of course, not out of the lap of nature but out of a retort (this is almost mysticism, gentlemen, but I suspect this, too), this retort-made man is sometimes so nonplussed in the presence of his antithesis that with all his exaggerated consciousness he genuinely thinks of himself as a mouse and not a man.
paras.uz: Xo'sh, men bunday to'g'ridan-to'g'ri odamni haqiqiy normal odam deb hisoblayman, mehribon ona tabiat uni yer yuziga iltifot bilan keltirganda qanday ko'rishni istagan bo'lsa, xuddi shunday. Men bunday odamga ko'm-ko'k bo'lib ketguncha hasad qilaman. U ahmoq. Bunga e'tiroz bildirmayman, lekin, balki, normal odam ahmoq bo'lishi kerakdir, qayerdan bilasiz? Balki bu hatto juda go'zaldir. Bu, agar shunday deyish mumkin bo'lsa, gumonimga meni yana shu narsa ishontiradiki, agar, masalan, normal odamning antitezasini — ya'ni o'tkir ongli odamni olsak, u, albatta, tabiat bag'ridan emas, balki retortadan chiqqan (bu deyarli mistika, janoblar, lekin men bundan ham shubhalanaman), — bu retortada yasalgan odam o'z antitezasi oldida ba'zan shunchalik dovdirab qoladiki, butun mubolag'ali ongi bilan o'zini chin dildan odam emas, sichqon deb hisoblaydi.

paras.en: It may be an acutely conscious mouse, yet it is a mouse, while the other is a man, and therefore, et caetera, et caetera. And the worst of it is, he himself, his very own self, looks on himself as a mouse; no one asks him to do so; and that is an important point. Now let us look at this mouse in action. Let us suppose, for instance, that it feels insulted, too (and it almost always does feel insulted), and wants to revenge itself, too. There may even be a greater accumulation of spite in it than in l'homme de la nature et de la vérité. The base and nasty desire to vent that spite on its assailant rankles perhaps even more nastily in it than in l'homme de la nature et de la vérité. For through his innate stupidity the latter looks upon his revenge as justice pure and simple; while in consequence of his acute consciousness the mouse does not believe in the justice of it.
paras.uz: Bu o'tkir ongli sichqon bo'lishi mumkin, lekin baribir sichqon, ikkinchisi esa odam, demak, va hokazo, va hokazo. Eng yomoni, u o'zi, o'zining o'zi o'zini sichqon deb biladi; buni undan hech kim so'ramaydi; bu esa muhim nuqta. Endi bu sichqonni harakatda ko'raylik. Faraz qilaylik, masalan, u ham haqoratlangan (u deyarli har doim haqoratlangan bo'ladi) va u ham o'ch olmoqchi. Unda hatto l'homme de la nature et de la vérité — «tabiat va haqiqat odami»dagidan ham ko'proq g'araz to'plangan bo'lishi mumkin. G'arazini o'zini haqorat qilgan odamga to'kib solishdek tuban va jirkanch istak unda, ehtimol, l'homme de la nature et de la vérité dagidan ham jirkanchroq yonadi. Chunki u tug'ma ahmoqligi tufayli o'z qasosini oddiy va sof adolat deb biladi; sichqon esa o'tkir ongi tufayli uning adolatiga ishonmaydi.

paras.en: To come at last to the deed itself, to the very act of revenge. Apart from the one fundamental nastiness the luckless mouse succeeds in creating around it so many other nastinesses in the form of doubts and questions, adds to the one question so many unsettled questions that there inevitably works up around it a sort of fatal brew, a stinking mess, made up of its doubts, emotions, and of the contempt spat upon it by the direct men of action who stand solemnly about it as judges and arbitrators, laughing at it till their healthy sides ache. Of course the only thing left for it is to dismiss all that with a wave of its paw, and, with a smile of assumed contempt in which it does not even itself believe, creep ignominiously into its mouse-hole. There in its nasty, stinking, underground home our insulted, crushed and ridiculed mouse promptly becomes absorbed in cold, malignant and, above all, everlasting spite.
paras.uz: Nihoyat ishning o'ziga, qasos harakatining o'ziga kelaylik. Bitta asosiy jirkanchlikdan tashqari, baxtsiz sichqon o'z atrofida shubhalar va savollar shaklidagi shunchalik ko'p boshqa jirkanchliklarni yaratishga muvaffaq bo'ladi, bitta savolga shunchalik ko'p hal qilinmagan savollarni qo'shadiki, uning atrofida muqarrar ravishda qandaydir halokatli qorishma, uning shubhalari, hayajonlari va uning atrofida hakam va sudyalardek tantanavor turgan, sog'lom biqinlari og'riguncha uning ustidan kulayotgan to'g'ridan-to'g'ri harakat odamlari unga tupurgan nafratdan iborat sasib ketgan bo'tqa yig'iladi. Albatta, unga faqat bitta narsa qoladi — bularning hammasiga panjasini siltab, o'zi ham ishonmaydigan soxta nafrat tabassumi bilan sharmandalarcha o'z inchasiga sudralib kirish. U yerda, o'zining jirkanch, sasigan yer osti uyida haqoratlangan, ezilgan va masxara qilingan sichqonimiz darhol sovuq, zaharli va, eng muhimi, abadiy g'arazga botadi.

paras.en: For forty years together it will remember its injury down to the smallest, most ignominious details, and every time will add, of itself, details still more ignominious, spitefully teasing and tormenting itself with its own imagination. It will itself be ashamed of its imaginings, but yet it will recall it all, it will go over and over every detail, it will invent unheard of things against itself, pretending that those things might happen, and will forgive nothing. Maybe it will begin to revenge itself, too, but, as it were, piecemeal, in trivial ways, from behind the stove, incognito, without believing either in its own right to vengeance, or in the success of its revenge, knowing that from all its efforts at revenge it will suffer a hundred times more than he on whom it revenges itself, while he, I daresay, will not even scratch himself. On its deathbed it will recall it all over again, with interest accumulated over all the years and ...
paras.uz: Qirq yil davomida u o'z haqoratini eng mayda, eng sharmandali tafsilotlarigacha eslaydi va har safar o'zidan yanada sharmandaliroq tafsilotlar qo'shib, o'z tasavvuri bilan o'zini g'araz bilan masxara qiladi va qiynaydi. O'z xayollaridan o'zi uyaladi, lekin baribir hammasini eslaydi, har bir tafsilotni qayta-qayta ko'zdan kechiradi, o'ziga qarshi eshitilmagan narsalarni o'ylab topadi, go'yo ular sodir bo'lishi mumkindek ko'rsatadi va hech narsani kechirmaydi. Balki u o'ch ola boshlar ham, lekin go'yo bo'laklab, arzimas yo'llar bilan, pechka ortidan, inkognito, na o'z qasos olish huquqiga, na qasosining muvaffaqiyatiga ishonib, qasos olish uchun qilgan barcha urinishlaridan o'zi o'ch olayotgan odamdan yuz marta ko'proq azob chekishini bilgan holda, u esa, ehtimol, hatto qashinmaydi ham. O'lim to'shagida u yana hammasini butun yillar davomida yig'ilgan foizlari bilan eslaydi va...

paras.en: But it is just in that cold, abominable half despair, half belief, in that conscious burying oneself alive for grief in the underworld for forty years, in that acutely recognised and yet partly doubtful hopelessness of one's position, in that hell of unsatisfied desires turned inward, in that fever of oscillations, of resolutions determined for ever and repented of again a minute later—that the savour of that strange enjoyment of which I have spoken lies. It is so subtle, so difficult of analysis, that persons who are a little limited, or even simply persons of strong nerves, will not understand a single atom of it. "Possibly," you will add on your own account with a grin, "people will not understand it either who have never received a slap in the face," and in that way you will politely hint to me that I, too, perhaps, have had the experience of a slap in the face in my life, and so I speak as one who knows.
paras.uz: Lekin aynan o'sha sovuq, jirkanch yarim umidsizlik, yarim ishonchda, qayg'udan qirq yil yer ostida o'zini ongli ravishda tiriklay ko'mishda, o'z ahvolining o'tkir anglangan va shu bilan birga qisman shubhali umidsizligida, ichkariga burilgan qondirilmagan istaklar do'zaxida, abadiy qabul qilingan va bir daqiqadan keyin yana tavba qilingan qarorlar, ikkilanishlar isitmasida — men aytgan o'sha g'alati zavqning ta'mi yotadi. U shunchalik nozik, tahlil qilish shunchalik qiyinki, biroz cheklangan odamlar yoki hatto shunchaki asablari mustahkam odamlar undan bir zarrasini ham tushunmaydi. «Balki, — deb qo'shimcha qilasiz siz o'zingizdan irjayib, — yuziga hech qachon tarsaki yemaganlar ham tushunmas», va shu bilan menga xushmuomalalik bilan, ehtimol, men ham hayotimda tarsaki yeyish tajribasiga ega bo'lganman, shuning uchun biladigan odamdek gapiryapman, deb ishora qilasiz.

paras.en: I bet that you are thinking that. But set your minds at rest, gentlemen, I have not received a slap in the face, though it is absolutely a matter of indifference to me what you may think about it. Possibly, I even regret, myself, that I have given so few slaps in the face during my life. But enough ... Not another word on that subject of such extreme interest to you.
paras.uz: Garov o'ynayman, siz shunday o'ylayapsiz. Lekin xotirjam bo'ling, janoblar, men yuzimga tarsaki yemaganman, garchi bu haqda nima o'ylashingiz menga mutlaqo farqsiz bo'lsa ham. Balki men hatto hayotim davomida kam tarsaki tushirganimdan afsuslanarman ham. Lekin bas... Siz uchun nihoyatda qiziq bo'lgan bu mavzu haqida boshqa bir og'iz ham so'z yo'q.

paras.en: I will continue calmly concerning persons with strong nerves who do not understand a certain refinement of enjoyment. Though in certain circumstances these gentlemen bellow their loudest like bulls, though this, let us suppose, does them the greatest credit, yet, as I have said already, confronted with the impossible they subside at once. The impossible means the stone wall! What stone wall? Why, of course, the laws of nature, the deductions of natural science, mathematics. As soon as they prove to you, for instance, that you are descended from a monkey, then it is no use scowling, accept it for a fact. When they prove to you that in reality one drop of your own fat must be dearer to you than a hundred thousand of your fellow-creatures, and that this conclusion is the final solution of all so-called virtues and duties and all such prejudices and fancies, then you have just to accept it, there is no help for it, for twice two is a law of mathematics. Just try refuting it.
paras.uz: Zavqning ma'lum bir nozikligini tushunmaydigan asablari mustahkam odamlar haqida xotirjam davom ettiraman. Garchi bu janoblar ma'lum vaziyatlarda buqalardek bor ovozda o'kirsalar ham, garchi bu, faraz qilaylik, ularga eng katta sharaf keltirsa ham, lekin, aytganimdek, imkonsizlik oldida ular darhol so'nib qolishadi. Imkonsizlik — bu tosh devor! Qanday tosh devor? Albatta, tabiat qonunlari, tabiiy fanlar xulosalari, matematika. Ular sizga, masalan, maymundan kelib chiqqaningizni isbotlashlari bilanoq, qovoq solishning foydasi yo'q, buni fakt sifatida qabul qiling. Ular sizga aslida o'z yog'ingizning bir tomchisi yuz ming hamjinsingizdan azizroq bo'lishi kerakligini va bu xulosa barcha fazilatlar va burchlar deb ataladigan narsalar va shunga o'xshash barcha xurofot va xayollarning yakuniy yechimi ekanini isbotlashganda, uni shunchaki qabul qilishingiz kerak, iloj yo'q, chunki ikki karra ikki — matematika qonuni. Raddiya berib ko'ring-chi.

paras.en: "Upon my word, they will shout at you, it is no use protesting: it is a case of twice two makes four! Nature does not ask your permission, she has nothing to do with your wishes, and whether you like her laws or dislike them, you are bound to accept her as she is, and consequently all her conclusions. A wall, you see, is a wall ... And so on, and so on."
paras.uz: «Rostini aytganda, — deb baqirishadi sizga, — e'tiroz bildirishning foydasi yo'q: bu ikki karra ikki — to'rt degan gap! Tabiat sizdan ruxsat so'ramaydi, uning istaklaringiz bilan ishi yo'q va uning qonunlari sizga yoqadimi yoki yo'qmi, siz uni qanday bo'lsa shunday, demak, uning barcha xulosalari bilan birga qabul qilishga majbursiz. Devor, ko'rdingizmi, devor... Va hokazo, va hokazo.»

paras.en: Merciful Heavens! But what do I care for the laws of nature and arithmetic, when, for some reason I dislike those laws and the fact that twice two makes four? Of course I cannot break through the wall by battering my head against it if I really have not the strength to knock it down, but I am not going to be reconciled to it simply because it is a stone wall and I have not the strength.
paras.uz: Yo rabbiy! Lekin, agar menga qandaydir sababdan bu qonunlar va ikki karra ikki — to'rt ekani yoqmasa, tabiat va arifmetika qonunlari menga nima? Albatta, agar haqiqatan uni yiqitishga kuchim yetmasa, boshimni urib devorni teshib o'ta olmayman, lekin men u bilan faqat u tosh devor bo'lgani va menda kuch yetmagani uchun yarashib ketmayman.

paras.en: As though such a stone wall really were a consolation, and really did contain some word of conciliation, simply because it is as true as twice two makes four. Oh, absurdity of absurdities!
paras.uz: Go'yo bunday tosh devor haqiqatan ham tasalli bo'lgandek va haqiqatan ham unda qandaydir murosa so'zi bordek, faqat u ikki karra ikki — to'rt qadar haqiqat bo'lgani uchun. Oh, bema'nilarning bema'nisi!

paras.en: How much better it is to understand it all, to recognise it all, all the impossibilities and the stone wall; not to be reconciled to one of those impossibilities and stone walls if it disgusts you to be reconciled to it; by the way of the most inevitable, logical combinations to reach the most revolting conclusions on the everlasting theme, that even for the stone wall you are yourself somehow to blame, though again it is as clear as day you are not to blame in the least, and therefore grinding your teeth in silent impotence to sink into luxurious inertia, brooding on the fact that there is no one even for you to feel vindictive against, that you have not, and perhaps never will have, an object for your spite, that it is a sleight of hand, a bit of juggling, a card-sharper's trick, that it is simply a mess, no knowing what and no knowing who, but in spite of all these uncertainties and jugglings, still there is an ache in you, and the more you do not know, the worse the ache.
paras.uz: Hammasini tushunish, hammasini anglash, barcha imkonsizliklar va tosh devorni tan olish qanchalik yaxshiroq; agar bu imkonsizliklar va tosh devorlardan biri bilan yarashish sizga jirkanch bo'lsa, birortasi bilan ham yarashmaslik; eng muqarrar, mantiqiy birikmalar orqali abadiy mavzu bo'yicha eng jirkanch xulosalarga — hatto tosh devor uchun ham qandaydir tarzda o'zingiz aybdor ekansiz degan xulosaga yetish, garchi yana kunduzgidek ravshanki, siz zarracha ham aybdor emassiz, va shuning uchun jim ojizlikda tish g'ijirlatib, hashamatli inertsiyaga botish, hatto siz uchun ham o'ch oladigan hech kim yo'qligi, g'arazingiz uchun ob'ekt yo'qligi va, ehtimol, hech qachon bo'lmasligi, bu qo'l chaqqonligi, qandaydir nayrang, qimorboz hiylasi ekani, shunchaki bo'tqa ekani, nima ekani ham, kim ekani ham noma'lum, lekin bu barcha noaniqliklar va nayranglarga qaramay, ichingizda baribir og'riq borligi va qanchalik kam bilsangiz, og'riq shunchalik kuchliroq ekani haqida o'ylash.

chapters.title: Pleasure in toothache

paras.en: "Ha, ha, ha! You will be finding enjoyment in toothache next," you cry, with a laugh.
paras.uz: «Ha-ha-ha! Endi tish og'rig'idan ham zavq topasiz», — deb kulib qichqirasiz.

paras.en: "Well, even in toothache there is enjoyment," I answer. I had toothache for a whole month and I know there is. In that case, of course, people are not spiteful in silence, but moan; but they are not candid moans, they are malignant moans, and the malignancy is the whole point. The enjoyment of the sufferer finds expression in those moans; if he did not feel enjoyment in them he would not moan. It is a good example, gentlemen, and I will develop it. Those moans express in the first place all the aimlessness of your pain, which is so humiliating to your consciousness; the whole legal system of nature on which you spit disdainfully, of course, but from which you suffer all the same while she does not.
paras.uz: «Xo'sh, tish og'rig'ida ham zavq bor», — deb javob beraman. Mening bir oy tishim og'rigan va bilaman, bor. Bu holda, albatta, odamlar jim g'arazlanmaydi, ingraydi; lekin bu samimiy ingroqlar emas, g'arazli ingroqlar va butun gap ana shu g'arazda. Azob chekuvchining zavqi shu ingroqlarda ifoda topadi; agar u ulardan zavq olmaganida, ingramagan bo'lardi. Bu yaxshi misol, janoblar, va men uni rivojlantiraman. Bu ingroqlar, birinchidan, og'rig'ingizning ongingiz uchun shunchalik xo'rlovchi bo'lgan butun maqsadsizligini; siz, albatta, nafrat bilan tupuradigan, lekin baribir undan azob chekadigan, u esa azob chekmaydigan tabiatning butun qonuniy tartibini ifodalaydi.

paras.en: They express the consciousness that you have no enemy to punish, but that you have pain; the consciousness that in spite of all possible Wagenheims you are in complete slavery to your teeth; that if someone wishes it, your teeth will leave off aching, and if he does not, they will go on aching another three months; and that finally if you are still contumacious and still protest, all that is left you for your own gratification is to thrash yourself or beat your wall with your fist as hard as you can, and absolutely nothing more. Well, these mortal insults, these jeers on the part of someone unknown, end at last in an enjoyment which sometimes reaches the highest degree of voluptuousness.
paras.uz: Ular siz jazolaydigan dushman yo'qligini, lekin og'riq borligini anglashni ifodalaydi; har qanday Vagengeymlarga qaramay, siz tishlaringizning to'liq quli ekaningizni; agar kimdir istasa, tishlaringiz og'rishdan to'xtaydi, istamasa — yana uch oy og'riydi; va nihoyat, agar hali ham qaysarlik qilib, e'tiroz bildirsangiz, o'zingizni qondirish uchun faqat o'zingizni savalash yoki devorni bor kuchingiz bilan musht bilan urish qoladi va boshqa mutlaqo hech narsa qolmaydi. Xo'sh, bu o'lim darajasidagi haqoratlar, qandaydir noma'lum kimsaning bu masxaralari oxir-oqibat ba'zan shahvoniylikning eng yuqori darajasiga yetadigan zavq bilan tugaydi.

paras.en: I ask you, gentlemen, listen sometimes to the moans of an educated man of the nineteenth century suffering from toothache, on the second or third day of the attack, when he is beginning to moan, not as he moaned on the first day, that is, not simply because he has toothache, not just as any coarse peasant, but as a man affected by progress and European civilisation, a man who is "divorced from the soil and the national elements," as they express it now-a-days. His moans become nasty, disgustingly malignant, and go on for whole days and nights.
paras.uz: Sizdan iltimos qilaman, janoblar, ba'zan o'n to'qqizinchi asrning tishi og'riyotgan o'qimishli odamining ingroqlariga quloq soling, xurujning ikkinchi yoki uchinchi kunida, u birinchi kundagidek emas, ya'ni shunchaki tishi og'rigani uchun emas, har qanday qo'pol dehqon kabi emas, balki taraqqiyot va Yevropa sivilizatsiyasi ta'sir qilgan odam, hozir aytishganidek, «tuproqdan va xalqona unsurlardan uzilgan» odam kabi ingray boshlaganda. Uning ingroqlari jirkanch, ko'ngilni aynitadigan darajada g'arazli bo'lib qoladi va kechayu kunduz davom etadi.

paras.en: And of course he knows himself that he is doing himself no sort of good with his moans; he knows better than anyone that he is only lacerating and harassing himself and others for nothing; he knows that even the audience before whom he is making his efforts, and his whole family, listen to him with loathing, do not put a ha'porth of faith in him, and inwardly understand that he might moan differently, more simply, without trills and flourishes, and that he is only amusing himself like that from ill-humour, from malignancy. Well, in all these recognitions and disgraces it is that there lies a voluptuous pleasure. As though he would say: "I am worrying you, I am lacerating your hearts, I am keeping everyone in the house awake. Well, stay awake then, you, too, feel every minute that I have toothache. I am not a hero to you now, as I tried to seem before, but simply a nasty person, an impostor. Well, so be it, then!
paras.uz: Albatta, uning o'zi ingroqlari bilan o'ziga hech qanday foyda keltirmayotganini biladi; u o'zini ham, boshqalarni ham behuda tirnab, qiynayotganini hammadan yaxshiroq biladi; u hatto oldida harakat qilayotgan tomoshabinlar ham, butun oilasi ham uni jirkanib tinglashini, unga zarracha ishonmasligini va ichlarida u boshqacha, soddaroq, trellar va bezaklarsiz ingrashi mumkinligini, faqat jahldorlik va g'arazdan shunday o'zini ovuntirayotganini tushunishlarini biladi. Xo'sh, aynan shu barcha e'tiroflar va sharmandaliklarda shahvoniy rohat yotadi. Go'yo u aytayotgandek: «Men sizni bezovta qilyapman, yuraklaringizni tirnayapman, uydagi hammani uxlatmayapman. Mayli, uxlamang, siz ham har daqiqa tishim og'riyotganini his qiling. Men endi siz uchun ilgari ko'rinishga uringanimdek qahramon emasman, balki shunchaki jirkanch odam, firibgarman. Xo'sh, shunday bo'lsa bo'laversin!

paras.en: I am very glad that you see through me. It is nasty for you to hear my despicable moans: well, let it be nasty; here I will let you have a nastier flourish in a minute...." You do not understand even now, gentlemen? No, it seems our development and our consciousness must go further to understand all the intricacies of this pleasure. You laugh? Delighted. My jests, gentlemen, are of course in bad taste, jerky, involved, lacking self-confidence. But of course that is because I do not respect myself. Can a man of perception respect himself at all?
paras.uz: Meni ko'rib turganingizdan juda xursandman. Jirkanch ingroqlarimni eshitish sizga yoqimsizmi: mayli, yoqimsiz bo'laversin; mana, bir daqiqadan keyin sizga yanada jirkanchroq bezak qilaman...» Hali ham tushunmayapsizmi, janoblar? Yo'q, aftidan, bu rohatning barcha nozikliklarini tushunish uchun rivojlanishimiz va ongimiz yana ham uzoqroqqa borishi kerak. Kulyapsizmi? Juda xursandman. Mening hazillarim, janoblar, albatta, didsiz, uzuq-yuluq, chalkash, o'ziga ishonchsiz. Lekin, albatta, bu men o'zimni hurmat qilmaganim uchun. Idrokli odam umuman o'zini hurmat qila oladimi?

chapters.title: Inertia and the primary cause

paras.en: Come, can a man who attempts to find enjoyment in the very feeling of his own degradation possibly have a spark of respect for himself? I am not saying this now from any mawkish kind of remorse. And, indeed, I could never endure saying, "Forgive me, Papa, I won't do it again," not because I am incapable of saying that—on the contrary, perhaps just because I have been too capable of it, and in what a way, too. As though of design I used to get into trouble in cases when I was not to blame in any way. That was the nastiest part of it. At the same time I was genuinely touched and penitent, I used to shed tears and, of course, deceived myself, though I was not acting in the least and there was a sick feeling in my heart at the time....
paras.uz: Qani, o'z xo'rligini his qilishning o'zidan zavq topishga urinadigan odam o'zini zarracha bo'lsa ham hurmat qila oladimi? Buni hozir qandaydir ko'ngilchan pushaymonlikdan aytayotganim yo'q. Haqiqatan ham, men hech qachon «Kechiring, dadajon, boshqa qilmayman» deyishga chiday olmasdim — buni aytishga qodir bo'lmaganim uchun emas, aksincha, balki aynan bunga haddan tashqari qodir bo'lganim uchun, yana qanday qodir! Go'yo ataylab hech qanday aybim bo'lmagan hollarda balolarga yo'liqardim. Eng jirkanchi shu edi. Shu bilan birga men chin dildan ta'sirlanib, tavba qilardim, ko'z yosh to'kardim va, albatta, o'zimni aldardim, garchi zarracha ham o'ynamagan bo'lsam ham va o'sha paytda yuragimda xasta tuyg'u bo'lsa ham...

paras.en: For that one could not blame even the laws of nature, though the laws of nature have continually all my life offended me more than anything. It is loathsome to remember it all, but it was loathsome even then. Of course, a minute or so later I would realise wrathfully that it was all a lie, a revolting lie, an affected lie, that is, all this penitence, this emotion, these vows of reform. You will ask why did I worry myself with such antics: answer, because it was very dull to sit with one's hands folded, and so one began cutting capers. That is really it. Observe yourselves more carefully, gentlemen, then you will understand that it is so. I invented adventures for myself and made up a life, so as at least to live in some way.
paras.uz: Buning uchun hatto tabiat qonunlarini ham ayblab bo'lmasdi, garchi tabiat qonunlari butun umrim davomida meni hamma narsadan ko'ra ko'proq xafa qilib kelgan bo'lsa ham. Bularning hammasini eslash jirkanch, lekin o'shanda ham jirkanch edi. Albatta, bir daqiqadan keyin men g'azab bilan bularning hammasi yolg'on, jirkanch yolg'on, sun'iy yolg'on ekanini — ya'ni bu butun tavba, bu hayajon, bu tuzalish va'dalari — anglab yetardim. Nega o'zimni shunday qiliqlar bilan qiynardim, deb so'raysiz: javob — qo'l qovushtirib o'tirish juda zerikarli edi, shuning uchun odam qiliq qila boshlardi. Haqiqatan ham shunday. O'zingizni diqqatliroq kuzating, janoblar, shunda shunday ekanini tushunasiz. Men o'zimga sarguzashtlar o'ylab topardim va hech bo'lmaganda qandaydir yashash uchun hayot to'qirdim.

paras.en: How many times it has happened to me—well, for instance, to take offence simply on purpose, for nothing; and one knows oneself, of course, that one is offended at nothing; that one is putting it on, but yet one brings oneself at last to the point of being really offended. All my life I have had an impulse to play such pranks, so that in the end I could not control it in myself. Another time, twice, in fact, I tried hard to be in love. I suffered, too, gentlemen, I assure you. In the depth of my heart there was no faith in my suffering, only a faint stir of mockery, but yet I did suffer, and in the real, orthodox way; I was jealous, beside myself ... And it was all from ennui, gentlemen, all from ennui; inertia overcame me. You know the direct, legitimate fruit of consciousness is inertia, that is, conscious sitting-with-the-hands-folded. I have referred to this already.
paras.uz: Necha marta menda shunday bo'lgan — masalan, shunchaki ataylab, hech narsadan xafa bo'lish; va odam, albatta, o'zi hech narsadan xafa bo'layotganini, o'zini shunday ko'rsatayotganini biladi, lekin baribir oxiri o'zini haqiqatan ham xafa bo'lish darajasiga yetkazadi. Butun umrim davomida menda shunday qiliqlar qilishga turtki bo'lgan, oxiri uni o'zimda nazorat qila olmay qoldim. Boshqa safar, aniqrog'i ikki marta, men astoydil oshiq bo'lishga urindim. Azob ham chekdim, janoblar, sizni ishontiraman. Yuragim tubida azobimga ishonch yo'q edi, faqat zaif masxara tebranardi, lekin baribir azob chekdim, yana haqiqiy, qonuniy tarzda; rashk qildim, o'zimni yo'qotdim... Va bularning hammasi zerikishdan edi, janoblar, hammasi zerikishdan; meni inertsiya bosgan edi. Bilasiz, ongning bevosita, qonuniy mevasi — inertsiya, ya'ni ongli ravishda qo'l qovushtirib o'tirish. Bu haqda allaqachon gapirdim.

paras.en: I repeat, I repeat with emphasis: all "direct" persons and men of action are active just because they are stupid and limited. How explain that? I will tell you: in consequence of their limitation they take immediate and secondary causes for primary ones, and in that way persuade themselves more quickly and easily than other people do that they have found an infallible foundation for their activity, and their minds are at ease and you know that is the chief thing. To begin to act, you know, you must first have your mind completely at ease and no trace of doubt left in it. Why, how am I, for example, to set my mind at rest? Where are the primary causes on which I am to build? Where are my foundations? Where am I to get them from? I exercise myself in reflection, and consequently with me every primary cause at once draws after itself another still more primary, and so on to infinity.
paras.uz: Takrorlayman, urg'u bilan takrorlayman: barcha «to'g'ridan-to'g'ri» odamlar va harakat odamlari aynan ahmoq va cheklangani uchun faoldir. Buni qanday tushuntirish mumkin? Aytaman: ular cheklanganliklari tufayli yaqin va ikkinchi darajali sabablarni birlamchi sabablar deb qabul qilishadi va shu tariqa boshqa odamlarga qaraganda tezroq va osonroq faoliyatlari uchun xatosiz asos topdik deb o'zlarini ishontirishadi va ko'ngillari tinchlanadi, bilasizki, asosiysi shu. Harakatni boshlash uchun, bilasiz, avvalo ko'nglingiz butunlay tinch bo'lishi va unda shubhaning zarracha izi ham qolmasligi kerak. Xo'sh, men, masalan, ko'nglimni qanday tinchlantiraman? Men ustiga quradigan birlamchi sabablar qayerda? Mening asoslarim qayerda? Ularni qayerdan olaman? Men fikrlash bilan mashq qilaman, shuning uchun menda har bir birlamchi sabab darhol o'zidan keyin yanada birlamchiroq boshqasini ergashtiradi va shunday cheksizlikkacha.

paras.en: That is just the essence of every sort of consciousness and reflection. It must be a case of the laws of nature again. What is the result of it in the end? Why, just the same. Remember I spoke just now of vengeance. (I am sure you did not take it in.) I said that a man revenges himself because he sees justice in it. Therefore he has found a primary cause, that is, justice. And so he is at rest on all sides, and consequently he carries out his revenge calmly and successfully, being persuaded that he is doing a just and honest thing. But I see no justice in it, I find no sort of virtue in it either, and consequently if I attempt to revenge myself, it is only out of spite. Spite, of course, might overcome everything, all my doubts, and so might serve quite successfully in place of a primary cause, precisely because it is not a cause.
paras.uz: Har qanday ong va fikrlashning mohiyati aynan shu. Bu yana tabiat qonunlari bo'lsa kerak. Oxir-oqibat natijasi nima? Xuddi o'shanday. Eslang, hozirgina qasos haqida gapirdim. (Ishonchim komilki, siz buni tushunmadingiz.) Men odam o'ch oladi, chunki unda adolat ko'radi, dedim. Demak, u birlamchi sababni, ya'ni adolatni topgan. Shuning uchun u har tomondan tinch va demak, adolatli va halol ish qilayotganiga ishongan holda qasosini xotirjam va muvaffaqiyatli amalga oshiradi. Lekin men bunda adolat ko'rmayman, hech qanday fazilat ham topmayman, shuning uchun agar o'ch olishga urinsam, bu faqat g'arazdan. G'araz, albatta, hamma narsani, barcha shubhalarimni yengishi va shu tariqa birlamchi sabab o'rnida juda muvaffaqiyatli xizmat qilishi mumkin edi, aynan u sabab bo'lmagani uchun.

paras.en: But what is to be done if I have not even spite (I began with that just now, you know). In consequence again of those accursed laws of consciousness, anger in me is subject to chemical disintegration. You look into it, the object flies off into air, your reasons evaporate, the criminal is not to be found, the wrong becomes not a wrong but a phantom, something like the toothache, for which no one is to blame, and consequently there is only the same outlet left again—that is, to beat the wall as hard as you can. So you give it up with a wave of the hand because you have not found a fundamental cause. And try letting yourself be carried away by your feelings, blindly, without reflection, without a primary cause, repelling consciousness at least for a time; hate or love, if only not to sit with your hands folded. The day after tomorrow, at the latest, you will begin despising yourself for having knowingly deceived yourself.
paras.uz: Lekin agar menda hatto g'araz ham bo'lmasa (bilasiz, men hozirgina shundan boshlagan edim), nima qilish kerak? Yana o'sha la'nati ong qonunlari tufayli, mendagi jahl kimyoviy parchalanishga uchraydi. Qarasangiz, ob'ekt havoga uchib ketadi, sabablaringiz bug'lanadi, aybdor topilmaydi, haqorat haqorat emas, sharpaga, hech kim aybdor bo'lmagan tish og'rig'iga o'xshash narsaga aylanadi va demak, yana o'sha yagona chiqish yo'li qoladi — ya'ni devorni bor kuchingiz bilan urish. Shuning uchun asosiy sabab topmaganingiz uchun qo'l siltab voz kechasiz. Tuyg'ularingizga ko'r-ko'rona, fikrlamasdan, birlamchi sababsiz, hech bo'lmaganda bir muddat ongni haydab, berilib ko'ring-chi; nafratlaning yoki seving, faqat qo'l qovushtirib o'tirmaslik uchun. Ko'pi bilan indinga o'zingizni bila turib aldaganingiz uchun o'zingizdan nafratlana boshlaysiz.

paras.en: Result: a soap-bubble and inertia. Oh, gentlemen, do you know, perhaps I consider myself an intelligent man, only because all my life I have been able neither to begin nor to finish anything. Granted I am a babbler, a harmless vexatious babbler, like all of us. But what is to be done if the direct and sole vocation of every intelligent man is babble, that is, the intentional pouring of water through a sieve?
paras.uz: Natija: sovun pufagi va inertsiya. Oh, janoblar, bilasizmi, balki men o'zimni faqat butun umrim davomida hech narsani na boshlay, na tugata olganim uchun aqlli odam deb hisoblarman. Mayli, men valdiroqman, hammamiz kabi zararsiz, zerikarli valdiroqman. Lekin agar har bir aqlli odamning bevosita va yagona chaqiruvi valdirash, ya'ni ataylab elakda suv tashish bo'lsa, nima qilish kerak?

chapters.title: If only I were a sluggard

paras.en: Oh, if I had done nothing simply from laziness! Heavens, how I should have respected myself, then. I should have respected myself because I should at least have been capable of being lazy; there would at least have been one quality, as it were, positive in me, in which I could have believed myself. Question: What is he? Answer: A sluggard; how very pleasant it would have been to hear that of oneself! It would mean that I was positively defined, it would mean that there was something to say about me. "Sluggard"—why, it is a calling and vocation, it is a career. Do not jest, it is so. I should then be a member of the best club by right, and should find my occupation in continually respecting myself. I knew a gentleman who prided himself all his life on being a connoisseur of Lafitte. He considered this as his positive virtue, and never doubted himself.
paras.uz: Oh, agar men hech narsa qilmagan bo'lsam, faqat dangasalikdan qilmaganimda edi! Xudoyim, o'shanda o'zimni qanchalik hurmat qilgan bo'lardim. O'zimni hurmat qilgan bo'lardim, chunki hech bo'lmaganda dangasa bo'lishga qodir bo'lardim; menda hech bo'lmaganda bitta, go'yo ijobiy fazilat bo'lardi va men unga o'zimni ishontira olardim. Savol: u kim? Javob: yalqov; o'zing haqingda buni eshitish qanchalik yoqimli bo'lardi! Bu men aniq ta'riflangan bo'lardim degani, men haqimda aytadigan nimadir bor degani bo'lardi. «Yalqov» — axir bu chaqiriq va kasb, bu martaba. Hazillashmang, shunday. O'shanda men haqli ravishda eng yaxshi klub a'zosi bo'lardim va o'zimni doimo hurmat qilishda mashg'ulot topardim. Men butun umri davomida Lafit vinosining bilimdoni ekani bilan faxrlangan bir janobni bilardim. U buni o'zining ijobiy fazilati deb hisoblardi va hech qachon o'zidan shubhalanmasdi.

paras.en: He died, not simply with a tranquil, but with a triumphant conscience, and he was quite right, too. Then I should have chosen a career for myself, I should have been a sluggard and a glutton, not a simple one, but, for instance, one with sympathies for everything sublime and beautiful. How do you like that? I have long had visions of it. That "sublime and beautiful" weighs heavily on my mind at forty But that is at forty; then—oh, then it would have been different! I should have found for myself a form of activity in keeping with it, to be precise, drinking to the health of everything "sublime and beautiful." I should have snatched at every opportunity to drop a tear into my glass and then to drain it to all that is "sublime and beautiful." I should then have turned everything into the sublime and the beautiful; in the nastiest, unquestionable trash, I should have sought out the sublime and the beautiful.
paras.uz: U nafaqat xotirjam, balki g'olibona vijdon bilan o'ldi va mutlaqo haq edi ham. O'shanda men o'zimga martaba tanlagan bo'lardim, yalqov va ochko'z bo'lardim, oddiy emas, balki, masalan, hamma go'zal va ulug'vor narsalarga hamdard bo'lgan. Bu sizga qanday yoqadi? Men buni ancha vaqtdan beri orzu qilaman. Bu «go'zal va ulug'vor» qirq yoshimda ongimga og'ir botmoqda. Lekin bu qirq yoshda; o'shanda esa — oh, o'shanda boshqacha bo'lardi! Men o'zimga shunga mos faoliyat shaklini topgan bo'lardim, aniqrog'i, «go'zal va ulug'vor» bo'lgan hamma narsaning sog'lig'i uchun ichish. Har bir imkoniyatni tutib olib, qadahimga ko'z yoshi tomizardim, keyin uni «go'zal va ulug'vor» bo'lgan hamma narsa uchun bo'shatardim. O'shanda men hamma narsani go'zal va ulug'vorga aylantirgan bo'lardim; eng jirkanch, shubhasiz axlatda ham go'zal va ulug'vorni izlab topgan bo'lardim.

paras.en: I should have exuded tears like a wet sponge. An artist, for instance, paints a picture worthy of Gay. At once I drink to the health of the artist who painted the picture worthy of Gay, because I love all that is "sublime and beautiful." An author has written as you will: at once I drink to the health of "anyone you will" because I love all that is "sublime and beautiful."
paras.uz: Men ho'l shimgichdek ko'z yosh sizdirgan bo'lardim. Masalan, rassom Gega munosib rasm chizadi. Darhol Gega munosib rasm chizgan rassomning sog'lig'i uchun ichaman, chunki «go'zal va ulug'vor» bo'lgan hamma narsani sevaman. Muallif «xohlaganingizcha» yozdi: darhol «kim xohlasangiz»ning sog'lig'i uchun ichaman, chunki «go'zal va ulug'vor» bo'lgan hamma narsani sevaman.

paras.en: I should claim respect for doing so. I should persecute anyone who would not show me respect. I should live at ease, I should die with dignity, why, it is charming, perfectly charming! And what a good round belly I should have grown, what a treble chin I should have established, what a ruby nose I should have coloured for myself, so that everyone would have said, looking at me: "Here is an asset! Here is something real and solid!" And, say what you like, it is very agreeable to hear such remarks about oneself in this negative age.
paras.uz: Buning uchun hurmat talab qilgan bo'lardim. Menga hurmat ko'rsatmaganlarni ta'qib qilgan bo'lardim. Bemalol yashardim, qadr-qimmat bilan o'lardim, axir bu ajoyib, mutlaqo ajoyib! Qanday yaxshi yumaloq qorin o'stirgan bo'lardim, qanday uch qavat iyak qo'ygan bo'lardim, qanday yoqut burun bo'yab olgan bo'lardim, shunda menga qaragan har kim: «Mana boylik! Mana haqiqiy va mustahkam narsa!» degan bo'lardi. Nima desangiz deng, bu inkor asrida o'zing haqingda shunday gaplarni eshitish juda yoqimli.
