chapters.title: The most advantageous advantage

paras.en: But these are all golden dreams. Oh, tell me, who was it first announced, who was it first proclaimed, that man only does nasty things because he does not know his own interests; and that if he were enlightened, if his eyes were opened to his real normal interests, man would at once cease to do nasty things, would at once become good and noble because, being enlightened and understanding his real advantage, he would see his own advantage in the good and nothing else, and we all know that not one man can, consciously, act against his own interests, consequently, so to say, through necessity, he would begin doing good? Oh, the babe! Oh, the pure, innocent child! Why, in the first place, when in all these thousands of years has there been a time when man has acted only from his own interest?
paras.uz: Lekin bularning hammasi oltin orzular. Oh, ayting-chi, kim birinchi bo'lib e'lon qilgan, kim birinchi bo'lib jar solgan: odam faqat o'z manfaatlarini bilmagani uchun jirkanch ishlar qiladi; agar uni ma'rifatli qilishsa, ko'zlarini haqiqiy, normal manfaatlariga ochishsa, odam darhol jirkanch ishlar qilishdan to'xtaydi, darhol yaxshi va olijanob bo'ladi, chunki ma'rifatli bo'lib va o'zining haqiqiy foydasini tushunib, u o'z foydasini yaxshilikda ko'radi va boshqa hech narsada ko'rmaydi, biz esa hech bir odam ongli ravishda o'z manfaatlariga qarshi harakat qila olmasligini bilamiz, demak, ta'bir joiz bo'lsa, zaruriyatdan yaxshilik qila boshlaydi, deb? Oh, go'dak! Oh, pok, beg'ubor bola! Axir, birinchidan, shu ming yilliklar davomida qachon odam faqat o'z manfaatidan kelib chiqib harakat qilgan payt bo'lgan?

paras.en: What is to be done with the millions of facts that bear witness that men, consciously, that is fully understanding their real interests, have left them in the background and have rushed headlong on another path, to meet peril and danger, compelled to this course by nobody and by nothing, but, as it were, simply disliking the beaten track, and have obstinately, wilfully, struck out another difficult, absurd way, seeking it almost in the darkness. So, I suppose, this obstinacy and perversity were pleasanter to them than any advantage.... Advantage! What is advantage? And will you take it upon yourself to define with perfect accuracy in what the advantage of man consists? And what if it so happens that a man's advantage, sometimes, not only may, but even must, consist in his desiring in certain cases what is harmful to himself and not advantageous. And if so, if there can be such a case, the whole principle falls into dust. What do you think—are there such cases?
paras.uz: Odamlar ongli ravishda, ya'ni o'z haqiqiy manfaatlarini to'liq tushunib, ularni chetga surib qo'yganliklari va boshqa yo'lga, xavf va xatarga peshvoz chiqib, boshi bilan otilganliklari, bunga hech kim va hech narsa majbur qilmagan holda, balki go'yo shunchaki bosilgan yo'lni yoqtirmay, qaysarlik bilan, o'z xohishi bilan boshqa qiyin, bema'ni yo'lni deyarli zulmatda izlab ochganliklariga guvohlik beradigan millionlab faktlar bilan nima qilish kerak? Demak, bu qaysarlik va o'jarlik ular uchun har qanday foydadan yoqimliroq bo'lgan bo'lsa kerak... Foyda! Foyda nima? Insonning foydasi nimadan iboratligini mutlaq aniqlik bilan ta'riflashni zimmangizga olasizmi? Agar shunday bo'lib chiqsa-chi, insonning foydasi ba'zan ma'lum hollarda o'ziga zararli bo'lgan, foydali bo'lmagan narsani istashdan iborat bo'lishi nafaqat mumkin, balki hatto shart bo'lsa-chi? Agar shunday bo'lsa, agar shunday hol bo'lishi mumkin bo'lsa, butun tamoyil changga aylanadi. Siz nima deb o'ylaysiz — bunday hollar bormi?

paras.en: You laugh; laugh away, gentlemen, but only answer me: have man's advantages been reckoned up with perfect certainty? Are there not some which not only have not been included but cannot possibly be included under any classification? You see, you gentlemen have, to the best of my knowledge, taken your whole register of human advantages from the averages of statistical figures and politico-economical formulas. Your advantages are prosperity, wealth, freedom, peace—and so on, and so on. So that the man who should, for instance, go openly and knowingly in opposition to all that list would to your thinking, and indeed mine, too, of course, be an obscurantist or an absolute madman: would not he? But, you know, this is what is surprising: why does it so happen that all these statisticians, sages and lovers of humanity, when they reckon up human advantages invariably leave out one? They don't even take it into their reckoning in the form in which it should be taken, and the whole reckoning depends upon that.
paras.uz: Kulyapsiz; kulavering, janoblar, faqat menga javob bering: insonning foydalari mutlaq aniqlik bilan hisoblab chiqilganmi? Shunday foydalar yo'qmi-ki, ular nafaqat kiritilmagan, balki hech qanday tasnifga umuman kiritib bo'lmaydi? Ko'ryapsizmi, siz, janoblar, men bilishimcha, inson foydalarining butun ro'yxatini statistik raqamlarning o'rtachalari va siyosiy-iqtisodiy formulalardan olgansiz. Sizning foydalaringiz — farovonlik, boylik, erkinlik, tinchlik — va hokazo, va hokazo. Shunday qilib, masalan, bu ro'yxatning hammasiga ochiqdan-ochiq va bila turib qarshi boradigan odam sizning fikringizcha, haqiqatan ham meniki bo'yicha ham, albatta, obskurant yoki mutlaq telba bo'lardi: shunday emasmi? Lekin, bilasizmi, hayron qoladigan narsa shu: nega bu barcha statistiklar, donishmandlar va insoniyat do'stlari inson foydalarini hisoblaganda har doim bittasini tushirib qoldirishadi? Ular uni hatto hisobga olinishi kerak bo'lgan shaklda ham hisobga olishmaydi, holbuki butun hisob shunga bog'liq.

paras.en: It would be no greater matter, they would simply have to take it, this advantage, and add it to the list. But the trouble is, that this strange advantage does not fall under any classification and is not in place in any list. I have a friend for instance ... Ech! Gentlemen, but of course he is your friend, too; and indeed there is no one, no one to whom he is not a friend! When he prepares for any undertaking this gentleman immediately explains to you, elegantly and clearly, exactly how he must act in accordance with the laws of reason and truth.
paras.uz: Bu katta gap bo'lmasdi, ular shunchaki bu foydani olib, ro'yxatga qo'shishlari kerak bo'lardi. Lekin muammo shundaki, bu g'alati foyda hech qanday tasnifga tushmaydi va hech qanday ro'yxatda o'rni yo'q. Masalan, mening bir do'stim bor... Eh! Janoblar, axir u sizning ham do'stingiz; haqiqatan ham, u do'st bo'lmagan hech kim, hech kim yo'q! Biror ishga tayyorlanganda bu janob darhol sizga nafis va aniq qilib, aql va haqiqat qonunlariga muvofiq aynan qanday harakat qilishi kerakligini tushuntiradi.

paras.en: What is more, he will talk to you with excitement and passion of the true normal interests of man; with irony he will upbraid the short-sighted fools who do not understand their own interests, nor the true significance of virtue; and, within a quarter of an hour, without any sudden outside provocation, but simply through something inside him which is stronger than all his interests, he will go off on quite a different tack—that is, act in direct opposition to what he has just been saying about himself, in opposition to the laws of reason, in opposition to his own advantage, in fact in opposition to everything ... I warn you that my friend is a compound personality and therefore it is difficult to blame him as an individual.
paras.uz: Bundan tashqari, u sizga insonning haqiqiy normal manfaatlari haqida hayajon va ehtiros bilan gapiradi; o'z manfaatlarini ham, fazilatning haqiqiy ahamiyatini ham tushunmaydigan kalta o'ylovchi ahmoqlarni kinoya bilan koyiydi; va chorak soat o'tmay, hech qanday to'satdan tashqi turtkisiz, balki shunchaki ichidagi barcha manfaatlaridan kuchliroq nimadir tufayli butunlay boshqa yo'lga burilib ketadi — ya'ni hozirgina o'zi haqida aytganlariga, aql qonunlariga, o'z foydasiga, xullas, hamma narsaga bevosita zid harakat qiladi... Ogohlantirib qo'yay, do'stim — jamoaviy shaxs, shuning uchun uni alohida shaxs sifatida ayblash qiyin.

paras.en: The fact is, gentlemen, it seems there must really exist something that is dearer to almost every man than his greatest advantages, or (not to be illogical) there is a most advantageous advantage (the very one omitted of which we spoke just now) which is more important and more advantageous than all other advantages, for the sake of which a man if necessary is ready to act in opposition to all laws; that is, in opposition to reason, honour, peace, prosperity—in fact, in opposition to all those excellent and useful things if only he can attain that fundamental, most advantageous advantage which is dearer to him than all. "Yes, but it's advantage all the same," you will retort. But excuse me, I'll make the point clear, and it is not a case of playing upon words. What matters is, that this advantage is remarkable from the very fact that it breaks down all our classifications, and continually shatters every system constructed by lovers of mankind for the benefit of mankind.
paras.uz: Gap shundaki, janoblar, aftidan, deyarli har bir odam uchun eng katta foydalaridan ham azizroq bo'lgan nimadir haqiqatan mavjud bo'lsa kerak, yoki (mantiqsiz bo'lmaslik uchun) boshqa barcha foydalardan muhimroq va foydaliroq bo'lgan eng foydali foyda (biz hozirgina gapirgan o'sha tushirib qoldirilgani) bor, uning uchun odam kerak bo'lsa barcha qonunlarga qarshi harakat qilishga tayyor; ya'ni aqlga, sharafga, tinchlikka, farovonlikka — xullas, o'sha barcha ajoyib va foydali narsalarga qarshi, faqat o'zi uchun hammasidan azizroq bo'lgan o'sha asosiy, eng foydali foydaga erishsa bas. «Ha, lekin baribir bu foyda-ku», deb e'tiroz bildirasiz. Lekin kechirasiz, fikrimni aniqlashtiraman va bu so'z o'yini emas. Muhimi shuki, bu foyda aynan barcha tasniflarimizni buzishi va insoniyat do'stlari insoniyat manfaati uchun qurgan har qanday tizimni doimo chil-chil sindirishi bilan ajoyib.

paras.en: In fact, it upsets everything. But before I mention this advantage to you, I want to compromise myself personally, and therefore I boldly declare that all these fine systems, all these theories for explaining to mankind their real normal interests, in order that inevitably striving to pursue these interests they may at once become good and noble—are, in my opinion, so far, mere logical exercises! Yes, logical exercises. Why, to maintain this theory of the regeneration of mankind by means of the pursuit of his own advantage is to my mind almost the same thing ... As to affirm, for instance, following Buckle, that through civilisation mankind becomes softer, and consequently less bloodthirsty and less fitted for warfare. Logically it does seem to follow from his arguments. But man has such a predilection for systems and abstract deductions that he is ready to distort the truth intentionally, he is ready to deny the evidence of his senses only to justify his logic.
paras.uz: Xullas, u hamma narsani ag'dar-to'ntar qiladi. Lekin bu foydani sizga aytishdan oldin, shaxsan o'zimni obro'sizlantirmoqchiman, shuning uchun jasorat bilan e'lon qilamanki, bu barcha chiroyli tizimlar, insoniyatga uning haqiqiy normal manfaatlarini tushuntirish uchun bu barcha nazariyalar — toki u bu manfaatlarga muqarrar intilib, darhol yaxshi va olijanob bo'lsin deb — mening fikrimcha, hozircha shunchaki mantiqiy mashqlar! Ha, mantiqiy mashqlar. Axir insoniyatni o'z foydasiga intilish orqali qayta tug'ilishi haqidagi bu nazariyani himoya qilish menimcha deyarli xuddi... masalan, Boklga ergashib, sivilizatsiya tufayli inson yumshoqroq, demak, kamroq qonxo'r va urushga kamroq yaroqli bo'ladi, deb tasdiqlash bilan bir xil. Mantiqan uning dalillaridan bu kelib chiqayotganga o'xshaydi. Lekin inson tizimlar va mavhum xulosalarga shunchalik moyilki, faqat mantig'ini oqlash uchun haqiqatni ataylab buzishga, o'z sezgilarining guvohligini inkor etishga tayyor.

paras.en: I take this example because it is the most glaring instance of it. Only look about you: blood is being spilt in streams, and in the merriest way, as though it were champagne. Take the whole of the nineteenth century in which Buckle lived. Take Napoleon—the Great and also the present one. Take North America—the eternal union. Take the farce of Schleswig-Holstein.... And what is it that civilisation softens in us? The only gain of civilisation for mankind is the greater capacity for variety of sensations—and absolutely nothing more. And through the development of this many-sidedness man may come to finding enjoyment in bloodshed. In fact, this has already happened to him.
paras.uz: Men bu misolni olyapman, chunki bu eng yaqqol namuna. Atrofingizga qarang: qon daryo bo'lib oqmoqda, yana eng quvnoq tarzda, go'yo shampan vinosidek. Bokl yashagan butun o'n to'qqizinchi asrni oling. Napoleonni oling — Buyugini ham, hozirgisini ham. Shimoliy Amerikani oling — abadiy ittifoqni. Shlezvig-Golshteyn masxarabozligini oling... Sivilizatsiya bizda nimani yumshatadi? Sivilizatsiyaning insoniyatga yagona foydasi — sezgilar xilma-xilligiga ko'proq qobiliyat, boshqa mutlaqo hech narsa emas. Bu ko'p qirralilikning rivojlanishi orqali inson qon to'kishdan zavq topishgacha yetishi mumkin. Haqiqatan ham, bu u bilan allaqachon sodir bo'lgan.

paras.en: Have you noticed that it is the most civilised gentlemen who have been the subtlest slaughterers, to whom the Attilas and Stenka Razins could not hold a candle, and if they are not so conspicuous as the Attilas and Stenka Razins it is simply because they are so often met with, are so ordinary and have become so familiar to us. In any case civilisation has made mankind if not more bloodthirsty, at least more vilely, more loathsomely bloodthirsty. In old days he saw justice in bloodshed and with his conscience at peace exterminated those he thought proper. Now we do think bloodshed abominable and yet we engage in this abomination, and with more energy than ever. Which is worse? Decide that for yourselves. They say that Cleopatra (excuse an instance from Roman history) was fond of sticking gold pins into her slave-girls' breasts and derived gratification from their screams and writhings.
paras.uz: Payqadingizmi, eng nozik qassoblar aynan eng madaniyatli janoblar bo'lgan, Attilalar va Stenka Razinlar ularning oldida hech narsa emas, agar ular Attilalar va Stenka Razinlar kabi ko'zga tashlanmasa, bu shunchaki ular juda tez-tez uchrashi, juda oddiy bo'lgani va bizga juda tanish bo'lib qolgani uchun. Har holda, sivilizatsiya insoniyatni, qonxo'rroq bo'lmasa ham, hech bo'lmaganda yanada tubanroq, yanada jirkanchroq qonxo'r qildi. Qadimda u qon to'kishda adolat ko'rgan va vijdoni tinch holda o'zi lozim deb bilganlarni qirib tashlagan. Endi biz qon to'kishni jirkanch deb hisoblaymiz, shunga qaramay bu jirkanchlik bilan shug'ullanamiz, yana har qachongidan ham g'ayrat bilan. Qaysi biri yomonroq? Buni o'zingiz hal qiling. Aytishlaricha, Kleopatra (Rim tarixidan misol uchun kechirasiz) cho'ri qizlarining ko'kragiga oltin ignalar sanchishni yaxshi ko'rgan va ularning chinqiriqlari va to'lg'anishlaridan rohat olgan.

paras.en: You will say that that was in the comparatively barbarous times; that these are barbarous times too, because also, comparatively speaking, pins are stuck in even now; that though man has now learned to see more clearly than in barbarous ages, he is still far from having learnt to act as reason and science would dictate. But yet you are fully convinced that he will be sure to learn when he gets rid of certain old bad habits, and when common sense and science have completely re-educated human nature and turned it in a normal direction. You are confident that then man will cease from intentional error and will, so to say, be compelled not to want to set his will against his normal interests.
paras.uz: Siz bu nisbatan vahshiy zamonlarda bo'lgan, deysiz; hozir ham vahshiy zamonlar, chunki nisbatan aytganda, ignalar hozir ham sanchiladi; garchi inson endi vahshiy asrlardagidan aniqroq ko'rishni o'rgangan bo'lsa ham, u hali aql va ilm buyurganidek harakat qilishni o'rganishdan juda uzoq, deysiz. Shunga qaramay siz u ba'zi eski yomon odatlardan qutulganda, sog'lom aql va ilm inson tabiatini butunlay qayta tarbiyalab, uni normal yo'nalishga burganda, albatta o'rganishiga to'liq ishonasiz. Siz o'shanda inson qasddan xato qilishdan to'xtashiga va, ta'bir joiz bo'lsa, o'z irodasini normal manfaatlariga qarshi qo'yishni istamaslikka majbur bo'lishiga ishonchingiz komil.

paras.en: That is not all; then, you say, science itself will teach man (though to my mind it's a superfluous luxury) that he never has really had any caprice or will of his own, and that he himself is something of the nature of a piano-key or the stop of an organ, and that there are, besides, things called the laws of nature; so that everything he does is not done by his willing it, but is done of itself, by the laws of nature. Consequently we have only to discover these laws of nature, and man will no longer have to answer for his actions and life will become exceedingly easy for him.
paras.uz: Bu hammasi emas; o'shanda, deysiz, ilmning o'zi insonga (garchi menimcha bu ortiqcha hashamat bo'lsa ham) uning hech qachon haqiqatan o'z injiqligi yoki irodasi bo'lmaganini, uning o'zi qandaydir fortepiano klavishasi yoki organ registriga o'xshash narsa ekanini va bundan tashqari tabiat qonunlari deb ataladigan narsalar borligini o'rgatadi; shunday qilib, u qilgan hamma narsa uning istagi bilan qilinmaydi, balki o'z-o'zidan, tabiat qonunlariga ko'ra qilinadi. Demak, biz faqat bu tabiat qonunlarini kashf etishimiz kerak va inson endi o'z harakatlari uchun javob bermaydi va hayot unga nihoyatda oson bo'ladi.

paras.en: All human actions will then, of course, be tabulated according to these laws, mathematically, like tables of logarithms up to 108,000, and entered in an index; or, better still, there would be published certain edifying works of the nature of encyclopaedic lexicons, in which everything will be so clearly calculated and explained that there will be no more incidents or adventures in the world.
paras.uz: Shunda insonning barcha harakatlari, albatta, bu qonunlarga ko'ra, matematik tarzda, 108 000 gacha bo'lgan logarifm jadvallari kabi jadvalga solinadi va ko'rsatkichga kiritiladi; yoki undan ham yaxshisi, qomusiy lug'atlar tusidagi ba'zi ibratli asarlar nashr etiladi, ularda hamma narsa shunchalik aniq hisoblangan va tushuntirilgan bo'ladiki, dunyoda endi hech qanday voqea yoki sarguzasht bo'lmaydi.

paras.en: Then—this is all what you say—new economic relations will be established, all ready-made and worked out with mathematical exactitude, so that every possible question will vanish in the twinkling of an eye, simply because every possible answer to it will be provided. Then the "Palace of Crystal" will be built. Then ... In fact, those will be halcyon days. Of course there is no guaranteeing (this is my comment) that it will not be, for instance, frightfully dull then (for what will one have to do when everything will be calculated and tabulated), but on the other hand everything will be extraordinarily rational. Of course boredom may lead you to anything. It is boredom sets one sticking golden pins into people, but all that would not matter. What is bad (this is my comment again) is that I dare say people will be thankful for the gold pins then.
paras.uz: O'shanda — bularning hammasini siz aytyapsiz — yangi iqtisodiy munosabatlar o'rnatiladi, hammasi tayyor va matematik aniqlik bilan ishlab chiqilgan, shunda har qanday savol ko'z ochib-yumguncha yo'qoladi, shunchaki unga har qanday javob tayyorlab qo'yilgani uchun. O'shanda «Billur saroy» quriladi. O'shanda... Xullas, bular oltin kunlar bo'ladi. Albatta, kafolat yo'q (bu mening izohim), masalan, o'shanda dahshatli zerikarli bo'lmasligiga (chunki hamma narsa hisoblangan va jadvalga solingan bo'lsa, nima qilish kerak bo'ladi), lekin boshqa tomondan hamma narsa nihoyatda oqilona bo'ladi. Albatta, zerikish sizni har narsaga olib borishi mumkin. Odamlarga oltin ignalar sanchishga zerikish undaydi, lekin bularning hammasi muhim bo'lmasdi. Yomoni (bu yana mening izohim) shuki, menimcha, o'shanda odamlar oltin ignalar uchun minnatdor bo'lishadi.

paras.en: Man is stupid, you know, phenomenally stupid; or rather he is not at all stupid, but he is so ungrateful that you could not find another like him in all creation. I, for instance, would not be in the least surprised if all of a sudden, à propos of nothing, in the midst of general prosperity a gentleman with an ignoble, or rather with a reactionary and ironical, countenance were to arise and, putting his arms akimbo, say to us all: "I say, gentleman, hadn't we better kick over the whole show and scatter rationalism to the winds, simply to send these logarithms to the devil, and to enable us to live once more at our own sweet foolish will!" That again would not matter, but what is annoying is that he would be sure to find followers—such is the nature of man.
paras.uz: Inson ahmoq, bilasizmi, ajoyib darajada ahmoq; aniqrog'i, u umuman ahmoq emas, lekin shunchalik noshukurki, butun yaratilishda unga o'xshashini topa olmaysiz. Men, masalan, agar birdan, hech narsadan-hech narsa yo'q, umumiy farovonlik o'rtasida qandaydir tuban, aniqrog'i, reaksion va kinoyali basharali bir janob paydo bo'lib, qo'llarini beliga tirab, hammamizga: «Janoblar, nima deysiz, bu butun tomoshani tepib ag'darib, ratsionalizmni shamolga sovursak bo'lmaydimi, shunchaki bu logarifmlarni shaytonga jo'natish va yana o'zimizning shirin, ahmoqona irodamiz bilan yashash uchun!» desa, zarracha ham hayron bo'lmasdim. Bu ham muhim bo'lmasdi, lekin alamlisi shuki, u albatta izdoshlar topardi — inson tabiati shunday.

paras.en: And all that for the most foolish reason, which, one would think, was hardly worth mentioning: that is, that man everywhere and at all times, whoever he may be, has preferred to act as he chose and not in the least as his reason and advantage dictated. And one may choose what is contrary to one's own interests, and sometimes one positively ought (that is my idea). One's own free unfettered choice, one's own caprice, however wild it may be, one's own fancy worked up at times to frenzy—is that very "most advantageous advantage" which we have overlooked, which comes under no classification and against which all systems and theories are continually being shattered to atoms. And how do these wiseacres know that man wants a normal, a virtuous choice? What has made them conceive that man must want a rationally advantageous choice? What man wants is simply independent choice, whatever that independence may cost and wherever it may lead. And choice, of course, the devil only knows what choice.
paras.uz: Va bularning hammasi eng ahmoqona sabab tufayli, aytib o'tishga ham arzimaydigandek tuyuladigan sabab: ya'ni inson hamma joyda va hamma vaqt, kim bo'lmasin, aqli va foydasi buyurganidek emas, balki o'zi xohlaganidek harakat qilishni afzal ko'rgan. Inson o'z manfaatlariga zid narsani tanlashi mumkin, ba'zan esa hatto shart (bu mening g'oyam). O'zining erkin, kishanlanmagan tanlovi, o'zining injiqligi, qanchalik yovvoyi bo'lmasin, ba'zan telbalikkacha qizigan o'z xayoli — mana o'sha biz e'tibordan chetda qoldirgan «eng foydali foyda», u hech qanday tasnifga tushmaydi va unga qarshi barcha tizimlar va nazariyalar doimo chil-chil bo'ladi. Bu donishmandlar insonga normal, fazilatli tanlov kerakligini qayerdan bilishadi? Nima ularni inson albatta oqilona foydali tanlovni istashi kerak, deb o'ylashga majbur qildi? Insonga kerak bo'lgan narsa — shunchaki mustaqil tanlov, bu mustaqillik qanchaga tushmasin va qayerga olib bormasin. Tanlov esa, albatta, qanday tanlov ekanini faqat shayton biladi.

quiz.q: What is the 'most advantageous advantage' that systems leave out?
quiz.why_uz: Insonning o'z erkin, kishanlanmagan tanlovi.

quiz.q: What does the narrator say civilisation gives mankind?
o: A greater capacity for variety of sensations
quiz.why_uz: Sezgilar xilma-xilligiga ko'proq qobiliyat — boshqa hech narsa emas.

chapters.recap_uz: Hikoyachi inson faqat o'z manfaatini bilmagani uchun yomonlik qiladi, degan ma'rifatparvar nazariyaga hujum qiladi. Sivilizatsiya insonni yumshatmagan; «billur saroy» utopiyasi zerikarli bo'lardi. Insonning eng foydali foydasi — o'z erkin, mustaqil tanlovi, hatto u aqlga zid bo'lsa ham.

chapters.title: Not a piano-key

paras.en: "Ha! Ha! Ha! But you know there is no such thing as choice in reality, say what you like," you will interpose with a chuckle. "Science has succeeded in so far analysing man that we know already that choice and what is called freedom of will is nothing else than—"
paras.uz: «Ha-ha-ha! Lekin bilasizmi, nima desangiz deng, aslida tanlov degan narsa yo'q, — deb kulib gapimni bo'lasiz. — Ilm insonni shu darajada tahlil qildiki, biz tanlov va iroda erkinligi deb ataladigan narsa boshqa hech narsa emas, balki...»

paras.en: Stay, gentlemen, I meant to begin with that myself I confess, I was rather frightened. I was just going to say that the devil only knows what choice depends on, and that perhaps that was a very good thing, but I remembered the teaching of science ... And pulled myself up. And here you have begun upon it. Indeed, if there really is some day discovered a formula for all our desires and caprices—that is, an explanation of what they depend upon, by what laws they arise, how they develop, what they are aiming at in one case and in another and so on, that is a real mathematical formula—then, most likely, man will at once cease to feel desire, indeed, he will be certain to. For who would want to choose by rule? Besides, he will at once be transformed from a human being into an organ-stop or something of the sort; for what is a man without desires, without free will and without choice, if not a stop in an organ? What do you think? Let us reckon the chances—can such a thing happen or not?
paras.uz: To'xtang, janoblar, men o'zim shundan boshlamoqchi edim. Tan olaman, ancha cho'chib ketdim. Men endigina tanlov nimaga bog'liqligini faqat shayton biladi va, balki, bu juda yaxshidir, demoqchi edim, lekin ilm ta'limotini esladim... va o'zimni to'xtatdim. Mana siz esa buni boshladingiz. Haqiqatan ham, agar bir kun barcha istak va injiqliklarimizning formulasi — ya'ni ular nimaga bog'liqligi, qanday qonunlar bo'yicha paydo bo'lishi, qanday rivojlanishi, bir holda va boshqa holda nimaga intilishi va hokazolar haqidagi tushuntirish, ya'ni haqiqiy matematik formula — topilsa, unda, ehtimol, inson darhol istashdan to'xtaydi, aniqrog'i, albatta to'xtaydi. Chunki kim qoida bo'yicha tanlashni istaydi? Bundan tashqari, u darhol insondan organ registriga yoki shunga o'xshash narsaga aylanadi; chunki istaklarsiz, erkin irodasiz va tanlovsiz inson organ registridan boshqa nima? Siz nima deb o'ylaysiz? Keling, imkoniyatlarni hisoblaylik — bunday narsa sodir bo'lishi mumkinmi yoki yo'qmi?

paras.en: "H'm!" You decide. "Our choice is usually mistaken from a false view of our advantage. We sometimes choose absolute nonsense because in our foolishness we see in that nonsense the easiest means for attaining a supposed advantage. But when all that is explained and worked out on paper (which is perfectly possible, for it is contemptible and senseless to suppose that some laws of nature man will never understand), then certainly so-called desires will no longer exist. For if a desire should come into conflict with reason we shall then reason and not desire, because it will be impossible retaining our reason to be senseless in our desires, and in that way knowingly act against reason and desire to injure ourselves. And as all choice and reasoning can be really calculated—because there will some day be discovered the laws of our so-called free will—so, joking apart, there may one day be something like a table constructed of them, so that we really shall choose in accordance with it.
paras.uz: «Hm! — deb qaror qilasiz siz. — Bizning tanlovimiz odatda foydamizga noto'g'ri qarashdan adashadi. Biz ba'zan mutlaq bema'nilikni tanlaymiz, chunki ahmoqligimizda bu bema'nilikda taxmin qilingan foydaga erishishning eng oson vositasini ko'ramiz. Lekin bularning hammasi tushuntirilib, qog'ozda ishlab chiqilganda (bu mutlaqo mumkin, chunki inson tabiatning ba'zi qonunlarini hech qachon tushunmaydi deb taxmin qilish jirkanch va ma'nosiz), unda, albatta, istaklar deb ataladigan narsalar endi mavjud bo'lmaydi. Chunki agar istak aql bilan ziddiyatga kelsa, biz o'shanda istamasdan, fikr yuritamiz, chunki aqlimizni saqlagan holda istaklarimizda ma'nosiz bo'lish va shu tariqa bila turib aqlga qarshi harakat qilib, o'zimizga zarar yetkazishni istash imkonsiz bo'ladi. Barcha tanlov va mulohazani haqiqatan hisoblash mumkin bo'lgani uchun — chunki bir kun iroda erkinligi deb ataladigan narsamizning qonunlari ham topiladi — hazil-mazahni chetga qo'ysak, bir kun ulardan qandaydir jadvalga o'xshash narsa tuzilishi mumkin, shunda biz haqiqatan unga muvofiq tanlaymiz.

paras.en: If, for instance, some day they calculate and prove to me that I made a long nose at someone because I could not help making a long nose at him and that I had to do it in that particular way, what freedom is left me, especially if I am a learned man and have taken my degree somewhere? Then I should be able to calculate my whole life for thirty years beforehand. In short, if this could be arranged there would be nothing left for us to do; anyway, we should have to understand that. And, in fact, we ought unwearyingly to repeat to ourselves that at such and such a time and in such and such circumstances nature does not ask our leave; that we have got to take her as she is and not fashion her to suit our fancy, and if we really aspire to formulas and tables of rules, and well, even ...
paras.uz: Agar, masalan, bir kun ular hisoblab, menga kimgadir burun ko'rsatganimni, chunki unga burun ko'rsatmay qola olmaganimni va buni aynan shu tarzda qilishim kerak bo'lganini isbotlashsa, menga qanday erkinlik qoladi, ayniqsa agar men olim bo'lsam va qayerdadir ilmiy daraja olgan bo'lsam? O'shanda men butun hayotimni o'ttiz yil oldindan hisoblab bera olardim. Xullas, agar bunday tartib o'rnatilsa, bizga qiladigan hech narsa qolmasdi; har holda, buni tushunishimiz kerak bo'lardi. Va haqiqatan ham, biz o'zimizga charchamasdan takrorlashimiz kerakki, falon vaqtda va falon sharoitda tabiat bizdan ruxsat so'ramaydi; uni qanday bo'lsa shunday qabul qilishimiz kerak, xayolimizga moslab yasamasligimiz kerak, va agar biz haqiqatan formulalar va qoidalar jadvallariga intilsak, xo'sh, hatto...

paras.en: To the chemical retort, there's no help for it, we must accept the retort too, or else it will be accepted without our consent...."
paras.uz: kimyoviy retortaga ham, iloj yo'q, retortani ham qabul qilishimiz kerak, aks holda u bizning roziligimizsiz qabul qilinadi...»

paras.en: Yes, but here I come to a stop! Gentlemen, you must excuse me for being over-philosophical; it's the result of forty years underground! Allow me to indulge my fancy. You see, gentlemen, reason is an excellent thing, there's no disputing that, but reason is nothing but reason and satisfies only the rational side of man's nature, while will is a manifestation of the whole life, that is, of the whole human life including reason and all the impulses. And although our life, in this manifestation of it, is often worthless, yet it is life and not simply extracting square roots. Here I, for instance, quite naturally want to live, in order to satisfy all my capacities for life, and not simply my capacity for reasoning, that is, not simply one twentieth of my capacity for life. What does reason know?
paras.uz: Ha, lekin shu yerda men to'xtab qolaman! Janoblar, haddan tashqari falsafa so'qayotganim uchun meni kechiring; bu yer ostidagi qirq yilning natijasi! Xayolimga erk berishga ruxsat eting. Ko'ryapsizmi, janoblar, aql ajoyib narsa, bunga bahs yo'q, lekin aql — faqat aql va inson tabiatining faqat aqliy tomonini qondiradi, iroda esa butun hayotning, ya'ni aql va barcha turtkilarni o'z ichiga olgan butun inson hayotining namoyon bo'lishi. Garchi bu ko'rinishdagi hayotimiz ko'pincha arzimas bo'lsa ham, baribir bu hayot, shunchaki kvadrat ildiz chiqarish emas. Mana men, masalan, mutlaqo tabiiy ravishda shunchaki fikrlash qobiliyatimni emas, ya'ni shunchaki hayot qobiliyatimning yigirmadan bir qismini emas, balki barcha hayot qobiliyatlarimni qondirish uchun yashashni istayman. Aql nimani biladi?

paras.en: Reason only knows what it has succeeded in learning (some things, perhaps, it will never learn; this is a poor comfort, but why not say so frankly?) And human nature acts as a whole, with everything that is in it, consciously or unconsciously, and, even if it goes wrong, it lives. I suspect, gentlemen, that you are looking at me with compassion; you tell me again that an enlightened and developed man, such, in short, as the future man will be, cannot consciously desire anything disadvantageous to himself, that that can be proved mathematically. I thoroughly agree, it can—by mathematics. But I repeat for the hundredth time, there is one case, one only, when man may consciously, purposely, desire what is injurious to himself, what is stupid, very stupid—simply in order to have the right to desire for himself even what is very stupid and not to be bound by an obligation to desire only what is sensible.
paras.uz: Aql faqat o'rganishga ulgurgan narsasini biladi (ba'zi narsalarni, ehtimol, hech qachon o'rganmaydi; bu arzimas tasalli, lekin nega buni ochiq aytmaslik kerak?). Inson tabiati esa butunligicha, unda bor hamma narsa bilan, ongli yoki ongsiz harakat qiladi va adashsa ham, yashaydi. Shubhalanamanki, janoblar, siz menga rahm bilan qarayapsiz; menga yana ma'rifatli va rivojlangan odam, xullas, kelajak odami qanday bo'lsa, shunday odam ongli ravishda o'zi uchun foydasiz biror narsani istay olmasligini, buni matematik isbotlash mumkinligini aytyapsiz. To'liq qo'shilaman, mumkin — matematika bilan. Lekin yuzinchi marta takrorlayman, bitta hol, faqat bitta hol bor, qachonki inson ongli ravishda, ataylab o'zi uchun zararli, ahmoqona, juda ahmoqona narsani istashi mumkin — shunchaki o'zi uchun hatto juda ahmoqona narsani ham istash huquqiga ega bo'lish va faqat oqilona narsanigina istash majburiyati bilan bog'lanmaslik uchun.

paras.en: Of course, this very stupid thing, this caprice of ours, may be in reality, gentlemen, more advantageous for us than anything else on earth, especially in certain cases. And in particular it may be more advantageous than any advantage even when it does us obvious harm, and contradicts the soundest conclusions of our reason concerning our advantage—for in any circumstances it preserves for us what is most precious and most important—that is, our personality, our individuality. Some, you see, maintain that this really is the most precious thing for mankind; choice can, of course, if it chooses, be in agreement with reason; and especially if this be not abused but kept within bounds. It is profitable and sometimes even praiseworthy. But very often, and even most often, choice is utterly and stubbornly opposed to reason ... And ... And ... Do you know that that, too, is profitable, sometimes even praiseworthy? Gentlemen, let us suppose that man is not stupid.
paras.uz: Albatta, bu juda ahmoqona narsa, bu injiqligimiz aslida, janoblar, biz uchun yer yuzidagi hamma narsadan foydaliroq bo'lishi mumkin, ayniqsa ma'lum hollarda. Xususan, u bizga aniq zarar yetkazganda va aqlimizning foydamiz haqidagi eng sog'lom xulosalariga zid kelganda ham har qanday foydadan foydaliroq bo'lishi mumkin — chunki u har qanday sharoitda biz uchun eng qimmatli va eng muhim narsani — ya'ni shaxsiyatimizni, o'ziga xosligimizni saqlab qoladi. Ba'zilar, ko'ryapsizmi, bu haqiqatan ham insoniyat uchun eng qimmatli narsa deb ta'kidlashadi; tanlov, albatta, agar xohlasa, aql bilan mos kelishi mumkin; ayniqsa undan suiiste'mol qilinmasa, chegarada tutilsa. Bu foydali va ba'zan hatto maqtovga loyiq. Lekin juda tez-tez, hatto ko'pincha, tanlov aqlga butunlay va qaysarlik bilan qarshi turadi... va... va... bilasizmi, bu ham foydali, ba'zan hatto maqtovga loyiq? Janoblar, faraz qilaylik, inson ahmoq emas.

paras.en: (Indeed one cannot refuse to suppose that, if only from the one consideration, that, if man is stupid, then who is wise?) But if he is not stupid, he is monstrously ungrateful! Phenomenally ungrateful. In fact, I believe that the best definition of man is the ungrateful biped. But that is not all, that is not his worst defect; his worst defect is his perpetual moral obliquity, perpetual—from the days of the Flood to the Schleswig-Holstein period. Moral obliquity and consequently lack of good sense; for it has long been accepted that lack of good sense is due to no other cause than moral obliquity. Put it to the test and cast your eyes upon the history of mankind. What will you see? Is it a grand spectacle? Grand, if you like. Take the Colossus of Rhodes, for instance, that's worth something. With good reason
paras.uz: (Haqiqatan ham, buni faraz qilishdan bosh tortib bo'lmaydi, hech bo'lmaganda bitta mulohazadan: agar inson ahmoq bo'lsa, unda kim aqlli?) Lekin agar u ahmoq bo'lmasa, u dahshatli darajada noshukur! Ajoyib darajada noshukur. Haqiqatan ham, menimcha, insonning eng yaxshi ta'rifi — noshukur ikki oyoqli. Lekin bu hammasi emas, bu uning eng yomon nuqsoni emas; uning eng yomon nuqsoni — doimiy axloqiy egriligi, doimiy — To'fon kunlaridan Shlezvig-Golshteyn davrigacha. Axloqiy egrilik va demak, sog'lom fikrning yo'qligi; chunki sog'lom fikrning yo'qligi axloqiy egrilikdan boshqa hech qanday sababga bog'liq emasligi allaqachon qabul qilingan. Buni sinab ko'ring va ko'zingizni insoniyat tarixiga tashlang. Nimani ko'rasiz? Ulug'vor tomoshami? Xohlasangiz, ulug'vor. Masalan, Rodos Kolossini oling, bu nimagadir arziydi.

paras.en: Mr. Anaevsky testifies of it that some say that it is the work of man's hands, while others maintain that it has been created by nature herself. Is it many-coloured? May be it is many-coloured, too: if one takes the dress uniforms, military and civilian, of all peoples in all ages—that alone is worth something, and if you take the undress uniforms you will never get to the end of it; no historian would be equal to the job. Is it monotonous? May be it's monotonous too: it's fighting and fighting; they are fighting now, they fought first and they fought last—you will admit, that it is almost too monotonous. In short, one may say anything about the history of the world—anything that might enter the most disordered imagination. The only thing one can't say is that it's rational. The very word sticks in one's throat.
paras.uz: Janob Anayevskiy u haqda bejiz guvohlik bermaydi: ba'zilar uni inson qo'li ishi desa, boshqalar uni tabiatning o'zi yaratgan deb ta'kidlaydi. Rang-barangmi? Balki rang-barang ham: agar barcha davrlardagi barcha xalqlarning harbiy va fuqarolik bayram formalarini olsak — buning o'zi nimagadir arziydi, kundalik formalarni olsangiz esa, oxiriga hech qachon yetmaysiz; hech bir tarixchi bu ishning uddasidan chiqa olmasdi. Bir xilmi? Balki bir xil ham: urush va urush; hozir urushyapti, avval ham urushgan, keyin ham urushgan — tan olasiz, bu deyarli haddan tashqari bir xil. Xullas, jahon tarixi haqida hamma narsani aytish mumkin — eng tartibsiz tasavvurga kelishi mumkin bo'lgan hamma narsani. Aytib bo'lmaydigan yagona narsa — u oqilona. Bu so'zning o'zi tomoqqa tiqiladi.

paras.en: And, indeed, this is the odd thing that is continually happening: there are continually turning up in life moral and rational persons, sages and lovers of humanity who make it their object to live all their lives as morally and rationally as possible, to be, so to speak, a light to their neighbours simply in order to show them that it is possible to live morally and rationally in this world. And yet we all know that those very people sooner or later have been false to themselves, playing some queer trick, often a most unseemly one. Now I ask you: what can be expected of man since he is a being endowed with strange qualities?
paras.uz: Haqiqatan ham, doimo sodir bo'ladigan g'alati narsa shu: hayotda doimo axloqli va oqilona odamlar, donishmandlar va insoniyat do'stlari paydo bo'ladi, ular butun umri davomida iloji boricha axloqli va oqilona yashashni, ta'bir joiz bo'lsa, yaqinlariga nur bo'lishni o'z maqsadi qiladi, shunchaki ularga bu dunyoda axloqli va oqilona yashash mumkinligini ko'rsatish uchun. Shunga qaramay, hammamiz bilamizki, aynan o'sha odamlar ertami-kechmi o'zlariga xiyonat qilishgan, qandaydir g'alati qiliq, ko'pincha eng nomaqbul qiliq qilishgan. Endi sizdan so'rayman: g'alati xususiyatlarga ega mavjudot bo'lgan insondan nima kutish mumkin?

paras.en: Shower upon him every earthly blessing, drown him in a sea of happiness, so that nothing but bubbles of bliss can be seen on the surface; give him economic prosperity, such that he should have nothing else to do but sleep, eat cakes and busy himself with the continuation of his species, and even then out of sheer ingratitude, sheer spite, man would play you some nasty trick. He would even risk his cakes and would deliberately desire the most fatal rubbish, the most uneconomical absurdity, simply to introduce into all this positive good sense his fatal fantastic element. It is just his fantastic dreams, his vulgar folly that he will desire to retain, simply in order to prove to himself—as though that were so necessary—that men still are men and not the keys of a piano, which the laws of nature threaten to control so completely that soon one will be able to desire nothing but by the calendar.
paras.uz: Unga barcha yerdagi ne'matlarni yog'diring, uni baxt dengiziga g'arq qiling, shunda yuzada faqat saodat pufakchalari ko'rinsin; unga shunday iqtisodiy farovonlik beringki, uxlash, pirojniy yeyish va o'z zotini davom ettirish bilan band bo'lishdan boshqa qiladigan hech narsasi qolmasin, shunda ham inson sof noshukurlikdan, sof g'arazdan sizga qandaydir jirkanch qiliq qiladi. U hatto pirojniylarini xavf ostiga qo'yadi va ataylab eng halokatli axlatni, eng iqtisodsiz bema'nilikni istaydi, shunchaki bu butun ijobiy sog'lom fikrga o'zining halokatli, xayoliy unsurini qo'shish uchun. U aynan o'zining xayoliy orzularini, tuban ahmoqligini saqlab qolishni istaydi, shunchaki o'ziga — go'yo bu shunchalik zarur bo'lgandek — odamlar hali ham odamlar ekanini, tabiat qonunlari shunchalik to'liq boshqarish bilan tahdid qiladigan fortepiano klavishalari emasligini isbotlash uchun, chunki tez orada kalendar bo'yicha bo'lmasa hech narsani istab bo'lmay qoladi.

paras.en: And that is not all: even if man really were nothing but a piano-key, even if this were proved to him by natural science and mathematics, even then he would not become reasonable, but would purposely do something perverse out of simple ingratitude, simply to gain his point. And if he does not find means he will contrive destruction and chaos, will contrive sufferings of all sorts, only to gain his point! He will launch a curse upon the world, and as only man can curse (it is his privilege, the primary distinction between him and other animals), may be by his curse alone he will attain his object—that is, convince himself that he is a man and not a piano-key!
paras.uz: Bu hammasi emas: hatto inson haqiqatan ham fortepiano klavishasidan boshqa hech narsa bo'lmaganida, hatto bu unga tabiiy fanlar va matematika tomonidan isbotlanganda ham, u baribir aqlli bo'lmasdi, balki oddiy noshukurlikdan, shunchaki o'zinikini o'tkazish uchun ataylab qandaydir teskari ish qilardi. Agar vosita topmasa, vayronagarchilik va tartibsizlik o'ylab topadi, har xil azoblar o'ylab topadi, faqat o'zinikini o'tkazish uchun! U dunyoga la'nat yog'diradi va faqat inson la'natlay olgani uchun (bu uning imtiyozi, uni boshqa hayvonlardan ajratib turadigan asosiy farq), balki faqat la'nati bilan o'z maqsadiga erishadi — ya'ni o'zini fortepiano klavishasi emas, inson ekaniga ishontiradi!

paras.en: If you say that all this, too, can be calculated and tabulated—chaos and darkness and curses, so that the mere possibility of calculating it all beforehand would stop it all, and reason would reassert itself, then man would purposely go mad in order to be rid of reason and gain his point! I believe in it, I answer for it, for the whole work of man really seems to consist in nothing but proving to himself every minute that he is a man and not a piano-key! It may be at the cost of his skin, it may be by cannibalism! And this being so, can one help being tempted to rejoice that it has not yet come off, and that desire still depends on something we don't know?
paras.uz: Agar siz bularning hammasini ham — tartibsizlik, zulmat va la'natlarni — hisoblash va jadvalga solish mumkin, shunda hammasini oldindan hisoblash imkoniyatining o'zi hammasini to'xtatadi va aql yana o'z huquqini tiklaydi, desangiz, unda inson aqldan qutulish va o'zinikini o'tkazish uchun ataylab aqldan ozadi! Men bunga ishonaman, buning uchun javob beraman, chunki insonning butun ishi haqiqatan ham har daqiqa o'ziga fortepiano klavishasi emas, inson ekanini isbotlashdan iborat bo'lib ko'rinadi! Bu terisi evaziga bo'lishi mumkin, odamxo'rlik bilan bo'lishi mumkin! Shunday ekan, bu hali amalga oshmaganidan va istak hali biz bilmaydigan nimagadir bog'liqligidan xursand bo'lish vasvasasiga berilmaslik mumkinmi?

paras.en: You will scream at me (that is, if you condescend to do so) that no one is touching my free will, that all they are concerned with is that my will should of itself, of its own free will, coincide with my own normal interests, with the laws of nature and arithmetic.
paras.uz: Siz menga (agar bunga tushishni lozim ko'rsangiz) hech kim erkin irodamga tegmayotganini, ularning butun tashvishi faqat irodam o'z-o'zidan, o'z erkin irodasi bilan mening normal manfaatlarim, tabiat va arifmetika qonunlari bilan mos kelishi ekanini aytib baqirasiz.

paras.en: Good heavens, gentlemen, what sort of free will is left when we come to tabulation and arithmetic, when it will all be a case of twice two make four? Twice two makes four without my will. As if free will meant that!
paras.uz: Yo Xudo, janoblar, jadval va arifmetikaga kelganimizda, hammasi ikki karra ikki — to'rt bo'lib qolganda qanday erkin iroda qoladi? Ikki karra ikki mening irodamsiz ham to'rt. Go'yo erkin iroda shunday narsani anglatgandek!

gloss.ex: …have begun upon it. Indeed, if there really is some day discovered a formula for all our desires and caprices—that is, an explanation of what they depend upon,…
…e? Besides, he will at once be transformed from a human being into an organ-stop or something of the sort; for what is a man without desires, without free will…
…stupid, then who is wise?) But if he is not stupid, he is monstrously ungrateful! Phenomenally ungrateful. In fact, I believe that the best definition of man is…
And that is not all: even if man really were nothing but a piano-key, even if this were proved to him by natural science and mathematics, even then h…
…hat is most precious and most important—that is, our personality, our individuality. Some, you see, maintain that this really is the most precious thing for man…

quiz.q: What would man become if all his desires were calculated?
quiz.why_uz: Istaklar formulasi topilsa, inson organ registriga aylanadi.

quiz.q: What is the best definition of man, according to the narrator?
quiz.why_uz: «Insonning eng yaxshi ta'rifi — noshukur ikki oyoqli».

chapters.recap_uz: Agar barcha istaklar formulaga solinsa, inson organ registriga aylanadi. Aql — hayotning faqat yigirmadan bir qismi; iroda butun hayotni ifodalaydi. Inson noshukur ikki oyoqli mavjudot: hatto baxt dengiziga g'arq qilinsa ham, u fortepiano klavishasi emas, odam ekanini isbotlash uchun bema'nilik qiladi.

chapters.title: Twice two makes five

paras.en: Gentlemen, I am joking, and I know myself that my jokes are not brilliant, but you know one can take everything as a joke. I am, perhaps, jesting against the grain. Gentlemen, I am tormented by questions; answer them for me. You, for instance, want to cure men of their old habits and reform their will in accordance with science and good sense. But how do you know, not only that it is possible, but also that it is desirable to reform man in that way? And what leads you to the conclusion that man's inclinations need reforming? In short, how do you know that such a reformation will be a benefit to man? And to go to the root of the matter, why are you so positively convinced that not to act against his real normal interests guaranteed by the conclusions of reason and arithmetic is certainly always advantageous for man and must always be a law for mankind? So far, you know, this is only your supposition.
paras.uz: Janoblar, men hazillashyapman va hazillarim zo'r emasligini o'zim bilaman, lekin bilasiz, hamma narsani hazilga olish mumkin. Men, ehtimol, ko'nglimga qarshi hazillashyapman. Janoblar, meni savollar qiynayapti; ularga men uchun javob bering. Siz, masalan, odamlarni eski odatlaridan davolab, irodasini ilm va sog'lom fikrga muvofiq isloh qilmoqchisiz. Lekin insonni shu tarzda isloh qilish nafaqat mumkin, balki istalgan ekanini qayerdan bilasiz? Va inson moyilliklari isloh qilinishi kerak degan xulosaga sizni nima olib keldi? Xullas, bunday isloh insonga foyda keltirishini qayerdan bilasiz? Va masalaning ildiziga borsak, aql va arifmetika xulosalari kafolatlagan haqiqiy normal manfaatlariga qarshi harakat qilmaslik inson uchun albatta har doim foydali va har doim insoniyat uchun qonun bo'lishi kerakligiga nega bunchalik qat'iy ishonasiz? Bilasizmi, hozircha bu faqat sizning farazingiz.

paras.en: It may be the law of logic, but not the law of humanity. You think, gentlemen, perhaps that I am mad? Allow me to defend myself. I agree that man is pre-eminently a creative animal, predestined to strive consciously for an object and to engage in engineering—that is, incessantly and eternally to make new roads, wherever they may lead. But the reason why he wants sometimes to go off at a tangent may just be that he is predestined to make the road, and perhaps, too, that however stupid the "direct" practical man may be, the thought sometimes will occur to him that the road almost always does lead somewhere, and that the destination it leads to is less important than the process of making it, and that the chief thing is to save the well-conducted child from despising engineering, and so giving way to the fatal idleness, which, as we all know, is the mother of all the vices.
paras.uz: Bu mantiq qonuni bo'lishi mumkin, lekin insoniyat qonuni emas. Siz, janoblar, balki meni telba deb o'ylayotgandirsiz? O'zimni himoya qilishga ruxsat bering. Men inson eng avvalo ijodkor hayvon, ongli ravishda maqsadga intilishga va muhandislik bilan shug'ullanishga — ya'ni tinimsiz va abadiy yangi yo'llar ochishga, ular qayerga olib bormasin — mahkum ekaniga qo'shilaman. Lekin u nega ba'zan yo'ldan chetga burilib ketishni istashining sababi, balki aynan u yo'l ochishga mahkumligidadir, balki shuningdek, «to'g'ridan-to'g'ri» amaliy odam qanchalik ahmoq bo'lmasin, ba'zan unga yo'l deyarli har doim qayergadir olib borishi, u olib boradigan manzil uni ochish jarayonidan kamroq muhim ekanligi va asosiysi — tarbiyali bolani muhandislikdan nafratlanishdan va shu tariqa hammamiz biladigan barcha illatlarning onasi bo'lgan halokatli bekorchilikka berilishdan saqlab qolish ekani haqidagi fikr kelishidadir.

paras.en: Man likes to make roads and to create, that is a fact beyond dispute. But why has he such a passionate love for destruction and chaos also? Tell me that! But on that point I want to say a couple of words myself. May it not be that he loves chaos and destruction (there can be no disputing that he does sometimes love it) because he is instinctively afraid of attaining his object and completing the edifice he is constructing? Who knows, perhaps he only loves that edifice from a distance, and is by no means in love with it at close quarters; perhaps he only loves building it and does not want to live in it, but will leave it, when completed, for the use of les animaux domestiques—such as the ants, the sheep, and so on. Now the ants have quite a different taste. They have a marvellous edifice of that pattern which endures for ever—the ant-heap.
paras.uz: Inson yo'l qurishni va yaratishni yaxshi ko'radi, bu bahssiz fakt. Lekin nega u vayronagarchilik va tartibsizlikni ham ehtiros bilan sevadi? Buni menga ayting! Lekin bu masalada o'zim bir-ikki so'z aytmoqchiman. Balki u tartibsizlik va vayronagarchilikni sevar (uning ba'zan buni sevishiga bahs yo'q), chunki instinktiv ravishda maqsadiga erishishdan va qurayotgan binosini tugatishdan qo'rqar? Kim biladi, balki u bu binoni faqat uzoqdan sevar, yaqindan esa umuman oshiq emasdir; balki u uni faqat qurishni sevar, unda yashashni istamas, balki tugagach, uni les animaux domestiques — uy hayvonlari, masalan, chumolilar, qo'ylar va hokazolar foydalanishi uchun qoldirar. Chumolilarning esa didi butunlay boshqacha. Ularda abadiy turadigan o'sha andozadagi ajoyib bino bor — chumoli uyasi.

paras.en: With the ant-heap the respectable race of ants began and with the ant-heap they will probably end, which does the greatest credit to their perseverance and good sense. But man is a frivolous and incongruous creature, and perhaps, like a chess player, loves the process of the game, not the end of it. And who knows (there is no saying with certainty), perhaps the only goal on earth to which mankind is striving lies in this incessant process of attaining, in other words, in life itself, and not in the thing to be attained, which must always be expressed as a formula, as positive as twice two makes four, and such positiveness is not life, gentlemen, but is the beginning of death. Anyway, man has always been afraid of this mathematical certainty, and I am afraid of it now. Granted that man does nothing but seek that mathematical certainty, he traverses oceans, sacrifices his life in the quest, but to succeed, really to find it, dreads, I assure you.
paras.uz: Muhtaram chumolilar zoti chumoli uyasi bilan boshlangan va, ehtimol, chumoli uyasi bilan tugaydi, bu ularning sabr-toqati va sog'lom fikriga eng katta sharaf keltiradi. Lekin inson yengiltak va nomuvofiq mavjudot va, balki, shaxmatchi kabi o'yinning oxirini emas, jarayonini sevar. Kim biladi (aniq aytib bo'lmaydi), balki insoniyat yer yuzida intilayotgan yagona maqsad erishishning shu tinimsiz jarayonida, boshqacha aytganda, hayotning o'zida yotar, erishiladigan narsada emas, u esa doimo formula sifatida, ikki karra ikki — to'rt kabi aniq ifodalanishi kerak, bunday aniqlik esa, janoblar, hayot emas, balki o'limning boshlanishi. Har holda, inson doimo bu matematik aniqlikdan qo'rqqan, men esa hozir undan qo'rqaman. Mayli, inson shu matematik aniqlikni izlashdan boshqa hech narsa qilmaydi, uni izlab okeanlarni kezib chiqadi, hayotini qurbon qiladi, lekin muvaffaqiyat qozonishdan, uni haqiqatan topishdan — sizni ishontiraman — qo'rqadi.

paras.en: He feels that when he has found it there will be nothing for him to look for. When workmen have finished their work they do at least receive their pay, they go to the tavern, then they are taken to the police-station—and there is occupation for a week. But where can man go? Anyway, one can observe a certain awkwardness about him when he has attained such objects. He loves the process of attaining, but does not quite like to have attained, and that, of course, is very absurd. In fact, man is a comical creature; there seems to be a kind of jest in it all. But yet mathematical certainty is after all, something insufferable. Twice two makes four seems to me simply a piece of insolence. Twice two makes four is a pert coxcomb who stands with arms akimbo barring your path and spitting.
paras.uz: U uni topganda izlaydigan hech narsa qolmasligini his qiladi. Ishchilar ishini tugatganda, hech bo'lmaganda haqini olishadi, maykhonaga borishadi, keyin ularni politsiya mahkamasiga olib ketishadi — va bir haftalik mashg'ulot bor. Lekin inson qayerga borsin? Har holda, u bunday maqsadlarga erishganda unda qandaydir noqulaylikni kuzatish mumkin. U erishish jarayonini sevadi, lekin erishib bo'lishni unchalik yoqtirmaydi va bu, albatta, juda kulgili. Xullas, inson kulgili mavjudot; bularning hammasida qandaydir hazil borga o'xshaydi. Lekin baribir matematik aniqlik — oxir-oqibat chidab bo'lmas narsa. Ikki karra ikki — to'rt menga shunchaki surbetlik bo'lib tuyuladi. Ikki karra ikki — to'rt — qo'llarini beliga tirab, yo'lingizni to'sib, tupurib turgan beadab olifta.

paras.en: I admit that twice two makes four is an excellent thing, but if we are to give everything its due, twice two makes five is sometimes a very charming thing too.
paras.uz: Tan olaman, ikki karra ikki — to'rt ajoyib narsa, lekin agar hamma narsaga haqqini beradigan bo'lsak, ikki karra ikki — besh ham ba'zan juda yoqimli narsa.

paras.en: And why are you so firmly, so triumphantly, convinced that only the normal and the positive—in other words, only what is conducive to welfare—is for the advantage of man? Is not reason in error as regards advantage? Does not man, perhaps, love something besides well-being? Perhaps he is just as fond of suffering? Perhaps suffering is just as great a benefit to him as well-being? Man is sometimes extraordinarily, passionately, in love with suffering, and that is a fact. There is no need to appeal to universal history to prove that; only ask yourself, if you are a man and have lived at all. As far as my personal opinion is concerned, to care only for well-being seems to me positively ill-bred. Whether it's good or bad, it is sometimes very pleasant, too, to smash things. I hold no brief for suffering nor for well-being either. I am standing for ... My caprice, and for its being guaranteed to me when necessary.
paras.uz: Nega siz faqat normal va ijobiy narsa — boshqacha aytganda, faqat farovonlikka xizmat qiladigan narsa — inson foydasiga ekaniga bunchalik qat'iy, bunchalik g'olibona ishonasiz? Aql foyda masalasida adashmayaptimi? Balki inson farovonlikdan tashqari yana nimanidir sevar? Balki u azobni ham xuddi shunchalik yaxshi ko'rar? Balki azob ham unga farovonlik kabi katta ne'matdir? Inson ba'zan azobni g'ayrioddiy, ehtirosli tarzda sevadi va bu fakt. Buni isbotlash uchun jahon tarixiga murojaat qilish shart emas; agar siz inson bo'lsangiz va umuman yashagan bo'lsangiz, o'zingizdan so'rang. Shaxsiy fikrimga kelsak, faqat farovonlik haqida qayg'urish menga hatto tarbiyasizlik bo'lib tuyuladi. Yaxshimi yoki yomonmi, ba'zan narsalarni sindirish ham juda yoqimli. Men na azobni, na farovonlikni himoya qilaman. Men... o'z injiqligim uchun va kerak bo'lganda u menga kafolatlanishi uchun turibman.

paras.en: Suffering would be out of place in vaudevilles, for instance; I know that. In the "Palace of Crystal" it is unthinkable; suffering means doubt, negation, and what would be the good of a "palace of crystal" if there could be any doubt about it? And yet I think man will never renounce real suffering, that is, destruction and chaos. Why, suffering is the sole origin of consciousness. Though I did lay it down at the beginning that consciousness is the greatest misfortune for man, yet I know man prizes it and would not give it up for any satisfaction. Consciousness, for instance, is infinitely superior to twice two makes four. Once you have mathematical certainty there is nothing left to do or to understand. There will be nothing left but to bottle up your five senses and plunge into contemplation. While if you stick to consciousness, even though the same result is attained, you can at least flog yourself at times, and that will, at any rate, liven you up.
paras.uz: Azob, masalan, vodevillarda o'rinsiz bo'lardi; buni bilaman. «Billur saroy»da u aqlga sig'maydi; azob — bu shubha, inkor, agar «billur saroy» haqida qandaydir shubha bo'lishi mumkin bo'lsa, undan nima foyda? Shunga qaramay, menimcha, inson hech qachon haqiqiy azobdan, ya'ni vayronagarchilik va tartibsizlikdan voz kechmaydi. Axir azob — ongning yagona manbai. Garchi boshida ong — inson uchun eng katta baxtsizlik deb qo'ygan bo'lsam ham, bilamanki, inson uni qadrlaydi va hech qanday qoniqish uchun undan voz kechmaydi. Ong, masalan, ikki karra ikki — to'rtdan cheksiz yuqori turadi. Matematik aniqlikka ega bo'lganingizdan keyin qiladigan yoki tushunadigan hech narsa qolmaydi. Besh sezgingizni shishaga solib, mushohadaga sho'ng'ishdan boshqa hech narsa qolmaydi. Ongga yopishib olsangiz esa, garchi natija bir xil bo'lsa ham, hech bo'lmaganda ba'zan o'zingizni savalay olasiz va bu, har holda, sizni jonlantiradi.

paras.en: Reactionary as it is, corporal punishment is better than nothing.
paras.uz: Reaksion bo'lsa ham, tan jazosi hech narsadan yaxshiroq.

o: He is afraid of finishing the building he constructs
quiz.why_uz: U maqsadga yetish va binoni tugatishdan instinktiv qo'rqadi.

quiz.q: What is 'the sole origin of consciousness'?
quiz.why_uz: «Azob — ongning yagona manbai».

chapters.recap_uz: Inson yo'l qurishni, maqsadga intilishni yaxshi ko'radi, lekin maqsadga yetishdan qo'rqadi; chumoli uyasiga o'xshagan tayyor binoda yashashni istamaydi. Matematik aniqlik — o'limning boshlanishi. Inson azobni ham sevadi, chunki azob — ongning yagona manbai.

chapters.title: A palace or a hen-house

paras.en: You believe in a palace of crystal that can never be destroyed—a palace at which one will not be able to put out one's tongue or make a long nose on the sly. And perhaps that is just why I am afraid of this edifice, that it is of crystal and can never be destroyed and that one cannot put one's tongue out at it even on the sly.
paras.uz: Siz hech qachon vayron qilib bo'lmaydigan billur saroyga ishonasiz — unga yashirincha til chiqarib ham, burun ko'rsatib ham bo'lmaydigan saroyga. Balki men bu binodan aynan shuning uchun qo'rqarman — u billurdan va hech qachon vayron qilib bo'lmaydi va unga hatto yashirincha ham til chiqarib bo'lmaydi.

paras.en: You see, if it were not a palace, but a hen-house, I might creep into it to avoid getting wet, and yet I would not call the hen-house a palace out of gratitude to it for keeping me dry. You laugh and say that in such circumstances a hen-house is as good as a mansion. Yes, I answer, if one had to live simply to keep out of the rain.
paras.uz: Ko'ryapsizmi, agar bu saroy emas, tovuqxona bo'lganida, ho'l bo'lmaslik uchun unga kirib olishim mumkin edi, lekin baribir meni quruq saqlagani uchun minnatdorchilikdan tovuqxonani saroy deb atamas edim. Siz kulib, bunday sharoitda tovuqxona ham qasr qadar yaxshi deysiz. Ha, deb javob beraman, agar odam faqat yomg'irdan panoh topish uchun yashashi kerak bo'lsa.

paras.en: But what is to be done if I have taken it into my head that that is not the only object in life, and that if one must live one had better live in a mansion? That is my choice, my desire. You will only eradicate it when you have changed my preference. Well, do change it, allure me with something else, give me another ideal. But meanwhile I will not take a hen-house for a mansion. The palace of crystal may be an idle dream, it may be that it is inconsistent with the laws of nature and that I have invented it only through my own stupidity, through the old-fashioned irrational habits of my generation. But what does it matter to me that it is inconsistent? That makes no difference since it exists in my desires, or rather exists as long as my desires exist. Perhaps you are laughing again?
paras.uz: Lekin agar men hayotda faqat shu maqsad emas, agar yashash kerak bo'lsa, qasrda yashagan ma'qul, degan fikrni boshimga olgan bo'lsam, nima qilish kerak? Bu mening tanlovim, mening istagim. Uni faqat mening afzalligimni o'zgartirganingizda yo'q qila olasiz. Xo'sh, o'zgartiring, meni boshqa narsa bilan o'ziga torting, menga boshqa ideal bering. Lekin hozircha men tovuqxonani qasr deb qabul qilmayman. Billur saroy behuda orzu bo'lishi mumkin, u tabiat qonunlariga mos kelmasligi va men uni faqat o'z ahmoqligim, avlodimning eskicha aqlsiz odatlari tufayli o'ylab topgan bo'lishim mumkin. Lekin uning mos kelmasligi menga nima? Hech qanday farqi yo'q, chunki u mening istaklarimda mavjud, aniqrog'i, istaklarim mavjud ekan, u ham mavjud. Balki yana kulyapsiz?

paras.en: Laugh away; I will put up with any mockery rather than pretend that I am satisfied when I am hungry. I know, anyway, that I will not be put off with a compromise, with a recurring zero, simply because it is consistent with the laws of nature and actually exists. I will not accept as the crown of my desires a block of buildings with tenements for the poor on a lease of a thousand years, and perhaps with a sign-board of a dentist hanging out. Destroy my desires, eradicate my ideals, show me something better, and I will follow you. You will say, perhaps, that it is not worth your trouble; but in that case I can give you the same answer. We are discussing things seriously; but if you won't deign to give me your attention, I will drop your acquaintance. I can retreat into my underground hole.
paras.uz: Kulavering; och bo'lganimda to'q ekanimni ko'rsatgandan ko'ra har qanday masxaraga chidayman. Har holda, bilamanki, meni murosa bilan, takrorlanuvchi nol bilan, faqat u tabiat qonunlariga mos kelgani va haqiqatan mavjud bo'lgani uchun aldab bo'lmaydi. Men istaklarimning toji sifatida kambag'allar uchun ming yillik ijaraga beriladigan kvartiralari bor, balki osilib turgan tish shifokori lavhasi bilan bino blokini qabul qilmayman. Istaklarimni yo'q qiling, ideallarimni yo'q qiling, menga yaxshiroq narsani ko'rsating, men sizga ergashaman. Siz, balki, bu sizning mehnatingizga arzimaydi deysiz; lekin unda men ham sizga xuddi shunday javob bera olaman. Biz jiddiy narsalarni muhokama qilyapmiz; lekin agar menga e'tibor berishni lozim ko'rmasangiz, tanishligimizni uzaman. Men yer ostidagi inimga chekina olaman.

paras.en: But while I am alive and have desires I would rather my hand were withered off than bring one brick to such a building! Don't remind me that I have just rejected the palace of crystal for the sole reason that one cannot put out one's tongue at it. I did not say because I am so fond of putting my tongue out. Perhaps the thing I resented was, that of all your edifices there has not been one at which one could not put out one's tongue. On the contrary, I would let my tongue be cut off out of gratitude if things could be so arranged that I should lose all desire to put it out. It is not my fault that things cannot be so arranged, and that one must be satisfied with model flats. Then why am I made with such desires? Can I have been constructed simply in order to come to the conclusion that all my construction is a cheat? Can this be my whole purpose? I do not believe it.
paras.uz: Lekin tirik ekanman va istaklarim bor ekan, bunday binoga bitta g'isht olib borgandan ko'ra qo'lim qurib qolsin! Menga billur saroyni faqat unga til chiqarib bo'lmagani uchun rad etganimni eslatmang. Men til chiqarishni juda yaxshi ko'rganim uchun demadim. Balki meni ranjitgan narsa — sizning barcha binolaringiz ichida til chiqarib bo'lmaydiganini bitta ham bo'lmagani edi. Aksincha, agar narsalarni shunday tartibga solish mumkin bo'lsa-ki, til chiqarish istagimni butunlay yo'qotsam, minnatdorchilikdan tilimni kestirgan bo'lardim. Narsalarni shunday tartibga solib bo'lmasligi va namunaviy kvartiralar bilan qanoatlanish kerakligi mening aybim emas. Unda nega men bunday istaklar bilan yaratilganman? Nahotki men faqat butun tuzilishim aldov degan xulosaga kelish uchun yaratilgan bo'lsam? Nahotki butun maqsadim shu bo'lsa? Ishonmayman.

paras.en: But do you know what: I am convinced that we underground folk ought to be kept on a curb. Though we may sit forty years underground without speaking, when we do come out into the light of day and break out we talk and talk and talk....
paras.uz: Lekin bilasizmi nima: men biz, yer osti odamlarini jilovda tutish kerak, deb ishonaman. Garchi biz yer ostida qirq yil gapirmasdan o'tira olsak ham, kunduzi yorug'iga chiqib, otilib chiqqanimizda, gapiramiz, gapiramiz va gapiramiz...

quiz.q: Why is the narrator afraid of the crystal palace?
o: It can never be destroyed and one cannot put one's tongue out at it
quiz.why_uz: Billurdan, vayron qilib bo'lmaydi va unga til chiqarib bo'lmaydi.

quiz.q: Will he take a hen-house for a mansion?
