chapters.recap_uz: Hikoyachi abadiy, vayron qilib bo'lmaydigan billur saroyga qarshi chiqadi: unga til chiqarib bo'lmaydi. U tovuqxonani saroy deb qabul qilmaydi va istaklari yo'q qilinmaguncha bunday binoga bir g'isht ham qo'ymaydi.

chapters.title: Why write at all?

paras.en: The long and the short of it is, gentlemen, that it is better to do nothing! Better conscious inertia! And so hurrah for underground! Though I have said that I envy the normal man to the last drop of my bile, yet I should not care to be in his place such as he is now (though I shall not cease envying him). No, no; anyway the underground life is more advantageous. There, at any rate, one can ... Oh, but even now I am lying! I am lying because I know myself that it is not underground that is better, but something different, quite different, for which I am thirsting, but which I cannot find! Damn underground!
paras.uz: Qisqasi, janoblar, hech narsa qilmagan yaxshiroq! Ongli inertsiya yaxshiroq! Demak, yashasin yer osti! Garchi normal odamga o'tim oxirgi tomchisigacha hasad qilaman desam ham, uning hozirgi holatidagi o'rnida bo'lishni istamasdim (garchi unga hasad qilishdan to'xtamasam ham). Yo'q, yo'q; har holda yer osti hayoti foydaliroq. U yerda, hech bo'lmaganda, odam... Oh, lekin hozir ham yolg'on gapiryapman! Yolg'on gapiryapman, chunki o'zim bilamanki, yaxshirog'i yer osti emas, balki boshqa narsa, butunlay boshqa narsa, men unga tashnaman, lekin topa olmayman! Jahannamga yer osti!

paras.en: I will tell you another thing that would be better, and that is, if I myself believed in anything of what I have just written. I swear to you, gentlemen, there is not one thing, not one word of what I have written that I really believe. That is, I believe it, perhaps, but at the same time I feel and suspect that I am lying like a cobbler.
paras.uz: Sizga yana bir narsani aytay, yaxshirog'i shu bo'lardi: agar men o'zim hozirgina yozganlarimdan biror narsaga ishonganimda edi. Sizga qasam ichaman, janoblar, men yozganlarimdan birorta narsaga, birorta so'zga haqiqatan ishonmayman. Ya'ni ishonaman, balki, lekin ayni paytda etikdo'zdek yolg'on gapirayotganimni his qilaman va shubhalanaman.

paras.en: "Then why have you written all this?" You will say to me. "I ought to put you underground for forty years without anything to do and then come to you in your cellar, to find out what stage you have reached! How can a man be left with nothing to do for forty years?"
paras.uz: «Unda nega bularning hammasini yozdingiz? — deysiz menga. — Sizni qirq yil hech qanday ishsiz yer ostiga qo'yish, keyin yerto'langizga kelib, qanday holatga yetganingizni bilish kerak edi! Qanday qilib odamni qirq yil ishsiz qoldirish mumkin?»

paras.en: "Isn't that shameful, isn't that humiliating?" You will say, perhaps, wagging your heads contemptuously. "You thirst for life and try to settle the problems of life by a logical tangle. And how persistent, how insolent are your sallies, and at the same time what a scare you are in! You talk nonsense and are pleased with it; you say impudent things and are in continual alarm and apologising for them. You declare that you are afraid of nothing and at the same time try to ingratiate yourself in our good opinion. You declare that you are gnashing your teeth and at the same time you try to be witty so as to amuse us. You know that your witticisms are not witty, but you are evidently well satisfied with their literary value. You may, perhaps, have really suffered, but you have no respect for your own suffering. You may have sincerity, but you have no modesty; out of the pettiest vanity you expose your sincerity to publicity and ignominy.
paras.uz: «Bu uyat emasmi, bu xo'rlik emasmi? — deysiz, ehtimol, nafrat bilan bosh chayqab. — Siz hayotga tashnasiz va hayot muammolarini mantiqiy chigallik bilan hal qilmoqchisiz. Hujumlaringiz qanchalik qaysar, qanchalik surbet, ayni paytda qanchalik qo'rqasiz! Bema'ni gaplarni gapirasiz va bundan mamnunsiz; surbet gaplar aytasiz va doimo xavotirda bo'lib, ular uchun uzr so'raysiz. Hech narsadan qo'rqmayman deb e'lon qilasiz va ayni paytda bizning yaxshi fikrimizni qozonishga harakat qilasiz. Tish g'ijirlatayotganingizni e'lon qilasiz va ayni paytda bizni kuldirish uchun o'tkir gapirishga urinasiz. O'tkir so'zlaringiz o'tkir emasligini bilasiz, lekin aftidan ularning adabiy qimmatidan juda mamnunsiz. Balki siz haqiqatan azob chekkandirsiz, lekin o'z azobingizni hurmat qilmaysiz. Balki sizda samimiylik bordir, lekin kamtarlik yo'q; eng mayda shuhratparastlikdan samimiyligingizni ommaga va sharmandalikka ko'rsatasiz.

paras.en: You doubtlessly mean to say something, but hide your last word through fear, because you have not the resolution to utter it, and only have a cowardly impudence. You boast of consciousness, but you are not sure of your ground, for though your mind works, yet your heart is darkened and corrupt, and you cannot have a full, genuine consciousness without a pure heart. And how intrusive you are, how you insist and grimace! Lies, lies, lies!"
paras.uz: Siz, shubhasiz, nimadir aytmoqchisiz, lekin so'nggi so'zingizni qo'rquvdan yashirasiz, chunki uni aytishga qat'iyatingiz yo'q, faqat qo'rqoqona surbetligingiz bor. Ong bilan maqtanasiz, lekin zamiringizga ishonchingiz yo'q, chunki aqlingiz ishlasa ham, yuragingiz qorong'ilashgan va buzilgan, pok yuraksiz esa to'liq, haqiqiy ongga ega bo'lib bo'lmaydi. Qanchalik suqilib kirasiz, qanchalik turib olasiz va basharangizni burishtirasiz! Yolg'on, yolg'on, yolg'on!»

paras.en: Of course I have myself made up all the things you say. That, too, is from underground. I have been for forty years listening to you through a crack under the floor. I have invented them myself, there was nothing else I could invent. It is no wonder that I have learned it by heart and it has taken a literary form....
paras.uz: Albatta, siz aytayotgan bu gaplarning hammasini o'zim to'qidim. Bu ham yer ostidan. Men qirq yil davomida sizni pol ostidagi yoriqdan tinglab keldim. Ularni o'zim o'ylab topdim, boshqa o'ylab topadigan narsam yo'q edi. Ularni yod bilib olganim va ular adabiy shakl olganiga ajablanmasa ham bo'ladi...

paras.en: But can you really be so credulous as to think that I will print all this and give it to you to read too? And another problem: why do I call you "gentlemen," why do I address you as though you really were my readers? Such confessions as I intend to make are never printed nor given to other people to read. Anyway, I am not strong-minded enough for that, and I don't see why I should be. But you see a fancy has occurred to me and I want to realise it at all costs. Let me explain.
paras.uz: Lekin nahotki siz haqiqatan men bularning hammasini chop etib, sizga o'qish uchun beraman deb o'ylaydigan darajada ishonuvchan bo'lsangiz? Yana bir muammo: nega men sizni «janoblar» deb atayman, nega sizga go'yo haqiqatan o'quvchilarim bo'lgandek murojaat qilaman? Men qilmoqchi bo'lgan bunday e'tiroflar hech qachon chop etilmaydi va boshqalarga o'qish uchun berilmaydi. Har holda, menda bunga yetarli irodam yo'q va nega bo'lishi kerakligini ham ko'rmayman. Lekin ko'ryapsizmi, xayolimga bir fikr keldi va men uni har qanday holatda amalga oshirmoqchiman. Tushuntirib beray.

paras.en: Every man has reminiscences which he would not tell to everyone, but only to his friends. He has other matters in his mind which he would not reveal even to his friends, but only to himself, and that in secret. But there are other things which a man is afraid to tell even to himself, and every decent man has a number of such things stored away in his mind. The more decent he is, the greater the number of such things in his mind. Anyway, I have only lately determined to remember some of my early adventures. Till now I have always avoided them, even with a certain uneasiness. Now, when I am not only recalling them, but have actually decided to write an account of them, I want to try the experiment whether one can, even with oneself, be perfectly open and not take fright at the whole truth.
paras.uz: Har bir odamning hammaga emas, faqat do'stlariga aytadigan xotiralari bor. Uning ongida do'stlariga ham oshkor qilmaydigan, faqat o'ziga, u ham yashirincha aytadigan boshqa narsalar bor. Lekin shunday narsalar ham borki, odam ularni hatto o'ziga aytishdan ham qo'rqadi va har bir odobli odamning ongida bunday narsalardan bir talayi saqlanadi. U qanchalik odobli bo'lsa, ongida bunday narsalar shunchalik ko'p bo'ladi. Har holda, men yaqindagina ilk sarguzashtlarimdan ba'zilarini eslashga qaror qildim. Shu paytgacha men ulardan doim, hatto qandaydir bezovtalik bilan qochib kelganman. Endi esa, ularni nafaqat eslayotganimda, balki haqiqatan ular haqida yozishga qaror qilganimda, odam hatto o'zi bilan ham mutlaqo ochiq bo'lib, butun haqiqatdan qo'rqmasligi mumkinmi, shuni sinab ko'rmoqchiman.

paras.en: I will observe, in parenthesis, that Heine says that a true autobiography is almost an impossibility, and that man is bound to lie about himself. He considers that Rousseau certainly told lies about himself in his confessions, and even intentionally lied, out of vanity. I am convinced that Heine is right; I quite understand how sometimes one may, out of sheer vanity, attribute regular crimes to oneself, and indeed I can very well conceive that kind of vanity. But Heine judged of people who made their confessions to the public. I write only for myself, and I wish to declare once and for all that if I write as though I were addressing readers, that is simply because it is easier for me to write in that form. It is a form, an empty form—I shall never have readers. I have made this plain already ...
paras.uz: Qavs ichida qayd etamanki, Geyne haqiqiy avtobiografiya deyarli imkonsiz va inson o'zi haqida albatta yolg'on gapiradi, deydi. Uning fikricha, Russo o'z «E'tiroflar»ida o'zi haqida albatta yolg'on gapirgan va hatto shuhratparastlikdan ataylab yolg'on gapirgan. Ishonchim komilki, Geyne haq; ba'zan odam sof shuhratparastlikdan o'ziga haqiqiy jinoyatlarni nisbat berishi mumkinligini juda yaxshi tushunaman, haqiqatan ham shunday shuhratparastlikni juda yaxshi tasavvur qila olaman. Lekin Geyne o'z e'tiroflarini ommaga qilgan odamlar haqida hukm chiqargan. Men faqat o'zim uchun yozaman va bir marta va abadiy e'lon qilmoqchimanki, agar men go'yo o'quvchilarga murojaat qilayotgandek yozsam, bu shunchaki menga shu shaklda yozish osonroq bo'lgani uchun. Bu shakl, bo'sh shakl — mening hech qachon o'quvchilarim bo'lmaydi. Buni allaqachon aniq aytdim...

paras.en: I don't wish to be hampered by any restrictions in the compilation of my notes. I shall not attempt any system or method. I will jot things down as I remember them.
paras.uz: Qaydlarimni tuzishda hech qanday cheklovlar bilan bog'lanishni istamayman. Hech qanday tizim yoki usulga urinmayman. Narsalarni eslaganimdek yozib qo'yaman.

paras.en: But here, perhaps, someone will catch at the word and ask me: if you really don't reckon on readers, why do you make such compacts with yourself—and on paper too—that is, that you won't attempt any system or method, that you jot things down as you remember them, and so on, and so on? Why are you explaining? Why do you apologise?
paras.uz: Lekin shu yerda, balki, kimdir so'zimdan ushlab, mendan so'rar: agar siz haqiqatan o'quvchilarga umid qilmasangiz, nega o'zingiz bilan — yana qog'ozda — shunday shartnomalar tuzasiz, ya'ni hech qanday tizim yoki usulga urinmaysiz, narsalarni eslaganingizdek yozib qo'yasiz va hokazo, va hokazo? Nega tushuntiryapsiz? Nega uzr so'rayapsiz?

paras.en: Well, there it is, I answer.
paras.uz: Xo'sh, gap shunda, deb javob beraman.

paras.en: There is a whole psychology in all this, though. Perhaps it is simply that I am a coward. And perhaps that I purposely imagine an audience before me in order that I may be more dignified while I write. There are perhaps thousands of reasons. Again, what is my object precisely in writing? If it is not for the benefit of the public why should I not simply recall these incidents in my own mind without putting them on paper?
paras.uz: Darvoqe, bularning hammasida butun bir psixologiya bor. Balki men shunchaki qo'rqoqdirman. Balki yozayotganimda salobatliroq bo'lish uchun oldimda ataylab tomoshabinlarni tasavvur qilarman. Balki minglab sabablar bordir. Yana, yozishdan aynan maqsadim nima? Agar bu jamoatchilik foydasi uchun bo'lmasa, nega bu voqealarni qog'ozga tushirmasdan shunchaki xayolimda eslamasligim kerak?

paras.en: Quite so; but yet it is more imposing on paper. There is something more impressive in it; I shall be better able to criticise myself and improve my style. Besides, I shall perhaps obtain actual relief from writing. Today, for instance, I am particularly oppressed by one memory of a distant past. It came back vividly to my mind a few days ago, and has remained haunting me like an annoying tune that one cannot get rid of. And yet I must get rid of it somehow. I have hundreds of such reminiscences; but at times some one stands out from the hundred and oppresses me. For some reason I believe that if I write it down I should get rid of it. Why not try?
paras.uz: To'g'ri; lekin baribir qog'ozda salobatliroq. Unda qandaydir ta'sirliroq narsa bor; o'zimni tanqid qilish va uslubimni yaxshilash imkoniyatim ko'proq bo'ladi. Bundan tashqari, balki yozishdan haqiqatan yengillik topaman. Bugun, masalan, meni uzoq o'tmishdagi bir xotira ayniqsa ezmoqda. U bir necha kun oldin xayolimga yorqin qaytdi va qutulib bo'lmaydigan zerikarli kuy kabi meni ta'qib qilib kelmoqda. Shunga qaramay, undan qandaydir qutulishim kerak. Menda bunday xotiralardan yuzlab bor; lekin ba'zan yuztadan bittasi ajralib chiqib, meni ezadi. Negadir, agar uni yozib qo'ysam, undan qutulaman, deb ishonaman. Nega sinab ko'rmaslik kerak?

paras.en: Besides, I am bored, and I never have anything to do. Writing will be a sort of work. They say work makes man kind-hearted and honest. Well, here is a chance for me, anyway.
paras.uz: Bundan tashqari, men zerikkanman va hech qachon qiladigan ishim bo'lmaydi. Yozish o'ziga xos ish bo'ladi. Aytishlaricha, mehnat insonni mehribon va halol qiladi. Xo'sh, har holda, menga imkoniyat.

paras.en: Snow is falling today, yellow and dingy. It fell yesterday, too, and a few days ago. I fancy it is the wet snow that has reminded me of that incident which I cannot shake off now. And so let it be a story à propos of the falling snow.
paras.uz: Bugun qor yog'yapti, sariq va xira. Kecha ham, bir necha kun oldin ham yog'gan edi. Menimcha, hozir qutula olmayotgan o'sha voqeani menga aynan ho'l qor eslatdi. Shunday ekan, bu yog'ayotgan qor munosabati bilan hikoya bo'lsin.

chapters.recap_uz: Birinchi qism yakuni: «yashasin yer osti» — lekin bu ham yolg'on. Hikoyachi xayoliy o'quvchilarning ta'nalarini o'zi yozadi, Geyne va Russoni eslaydi va faqat o'zi uchun, butun haqiqatdan qo'rqmasdan yozishga qaror qiladi. Ho'l qor unga bir voqeani eslatadi.

chapters.title: The officer on the Nevsky

paras.en: When from dark error's subjugation / My words of passionate exhortation / Had wrenched thy fainting spirit free; / And writhing prone in thine affliction / Thou didst recall with malediction / The vice that had encompassed thee: / And when thy slumbering conscience, fretting / By recollection's torturing flame, / Thou didst reveal the hideous setting / Of thy life's current ere I came: / When suddenly I saw thee sicken, / And weeping, hide thine anguished face, / Revolted, maddened, horror-stricken, / At memories of foul disgrace. — Nekrassov (translated by Juliet Soskice)
paras.uz: Zulmatli adashuv asoratidan / Mening otashin nasihatim / Behol ruhingni xalos etganda; / Iztirobda yerga yiqilib, to'lg'anib, / Seni o'rab olgan illatni / La'nat bilan yodga olganingda; / Mudragan vijdoning esa / Xotiraning qiynovchi alangasida tolganida, / Men kelguncha hayoting oqimining / Xunuk manzarasini oshkor etganingda; / Birdan xastalanganingni ko'rganimda, / Yig'lab, iztirobli yuzingni yashirganingda, / Jirkanib, telbalanib, dahshatga tushib / Iflos sharmandalik xotiralaridan... — Nekrasov (Juliet Soskice inglizcha tarjimasi)

paras.en: At that time I was only twenty-four. My life was even then gloomy, ill-regulated, and as solitary as that of a savage. I made friends with no one and positively avoided talking, and buried myself more and more in my hole. At work in the office I never looked at anyone, and was perfectly well aware that my companions looked upon me, not only as a queer fellow, but even looked upon me—I always fancied this—with a sort of loathing. I sometimes wondered why it was that nobody except me fancied that he was looked upon with aversion? One of the clerks had a most repulsive, pock-marked face, which looked positively villainous. I believe I should not have dared to look at anyone with such an unsightly countenance. Another had such a very dirty old uniform that there was an unpleasant odour in his proximity. Yet not one of these gentlemen showed the slightest self-consciousness—either about their clothes or their countenance or their character in any way.
paras.uz: O'shanda men bor-yo'g'i yigirma to'rt yoshda edim. Hayotim o'shandayoq g'amgin, tartibsiz va yovvoyinikidek yolg'iz edi. Hech kim bilan do'stlashmasdim, gaplashishdan hatto qochardim va inimga tobora chuqurroq kirib borardim. Idoradagi ishda men hech kimga qaramasdim va hamkasblarim menga nafaqat g'alati odam sifatida qarashini, balki — menga doim shunday tuyulardi — qandaydir jirkanish bilan qarashini juda yaxshi bilardim. Ba'zan hayron bo'lardim: nega mendan boshqa hech kim o'ziga jirkanish bilan qarashayotgandek o'ylamaydi? Kotiblardan birining yuzi nihoyatda jirkanch, cho'tir edi, u hatto yovuz ko'rinardi. Menimcha, men shunday xunuk basharam bilan hech kimga qarashga jur'at etmagan bo'lardim. Boshqasining formasi shunchalik eski va iflos ediki, uning yonida yoqimsiz hid kelardi. Shunga qaramay, bu janoblarning birortasi ham zarracha xijolat ko'rsatmasdi — na kiyimi, na basharasi, na xarakteri haqida.

paras.en: Neither of them ever imagined that they were looked at with repulsion; if they had imagined it they would not have minded—so long as their superiors did not look at them in that way. It is clear to me now that, owing to my unbounded vanity and to the high standard I set for myself, I often looked at myself with furious discontent, which verged on loathing, and so I inwardly attributed the same feeling to everyone. I hated my face, for instance: I thought it disgusting, and even suspected that there was something base in my expression, and so every day when I turned up at the office I tried to behave as independently as possible, and to assume a lofty expression, so that I might not be suspected of being abject. "My face may be ugly," I thought, "but let it be lofty, expressive, and, above all, extremely intelligent." But I was positively and painfully certain that it was impossible for my countenance ever to express those qualities.
paras.uz: Ularning hech biri o'ziga jirkanish bilan qarashlarini xayoliga ham keltirmasdi; agar xayoliga keltirganida ham, parvo qilmagan bo'lardi — faqat boshliqlari ularga shunday qaramasa bas. Endi menga aniqki, cheksiz shuhratparastligim va o'zimga qo'ygan yuksak mezonim tufayli men ko'pincha o'zimga jirkanishga yaqin bo'lgan g'azabli norozilik bilan qarardim, shuning uchun ichimda bu tuyg'uni hammaga nisbat berardim. Men, masalan, yuzimdan nafratlanardim: uni jirkanch deb o'ylardim va hatto ifodamda qandaydir tuban narsa bor deb shubhalanardim, shuning uchun har kuni idoraga kelganimda iloji boricha mustaqil o'zimni tutishga va meni tubanlikda gumon qilishmasligi uchun yuksak ifoda qilishga urinardim. «Yuzim xunuk bo'lishi mumkin, — deb o'ylardim, — lekin u yuksak, ifodali va, eng muhimi, nihoyatda aqlli bo'lsin.» Lekin yuzim hech qachon bu fazilatlarni ifodalay olmasligiga qat'iy va og'riqli ishonardim.

paras.en: And what was worst of all, I thought it actually stupid looking, and I would have been quite satisfied if I could have looked intelligent. In fact, I would even have put up with looking base if, at the same time, my face could have been thought strikingly intelligent.
paras.uz: Eng yomoni esa — men uni hatto ahmoqona ko'rinadi deb o'ylardim va agar aqlli ko'rina olganimda, butunlay qanoatlangan bo'lardim. Haqiqatan ham, agar ayni paytda yuzim hayratlanarli darajada aqlli deb hisoblanganida, hatto tuban ko'rinishga ham chidagan bo'lardim.

paras.en: Of course, I hated my fellow clerks one and all, and I despised them all, yet at the same time I was, as it were, afraid of them. In fact, it happened at times that I thought more highly of them than of myself. It somehow happened quite suddenly that I alternated between despising them and thinking them superior to myself. A cultivated and decent man cannot be vain without setting a fearfully high standard for himself, and without despising and almost hating himself at certain moments. But whether I despised them or thought them superior I dropped my eyes almost every time I met anyone. I even made experiments whether I could face so and so's looking at me, and I was always the first to drop my eyes. This worried me to distraction. I had a sickly dread, too, of being ridiculous, and so had a slavish passion for the conventional in everything external.
paras.uz: Albatta, men barcha hamkasblarimdan birma-bir nafratlanardim va hammasini mensimasdim, lekin ayni paytda go'yo ulardan qo'rqardim. Haqiqatan ham, ba'zan ularni o'zimdan ko'ra yuqoriroq deb o'ylardim. Qandaydir tarzda men birdan ularni mensimaslik va ularni o'zimdan ustun deb o'ylash orasida tebranib turardim. Madaniyatli va odobli odam o'ziga dahshatli yuksak mezon qo'ymasdan va ma'lum lahzalarda o'zini mensimasdan va deyarli nafratlanmasdan shuhratparast bo'la olmaydi. Lekin ularni mensimasam ham, ustun deb bilsam ham, deyarli har safar biror kishini uchratganimda ko'zimni yerga tushirardim. Hatto falonchining menga qarashiga bardosh bera olamanmi, deb tajribalar ham qilardim va har doim birinchi bo'lib ko'zimni olib qochardim. Bu meni aqldan ozdirguday qiynardi. Kulgili bo'lishdan ham xasta qo'rqardim, shuning uchun tashqi ko'rinishdagi hamma narsada odatiy narsaga qullarcha ehtiros bor edi.

paras.en: I loved to fall into the common rut, and had a whole-hearted terror of any kind of eccentricity in myself. But how could I live up to it? I was morbidly sensitive as a man of our age should be. They were all stupid, and as like one another as so many sheep. Perhaps I was the only one in the office who fancied that I was a coward and a slave, and I fancied it just because I was more highly developed. But it was not only that I fancied it, it really was so. I was a coward and a slave. I say this without the slightest embarrassment. Every decent man of our age must be a coward and a slave. That is his normal condition. Of that I am firmly persuaded. He is made and constructed to that very end.
paras.uz: Men umumiy izga tushishni yaxshi ko'rardim va o'zimdagi har qanday g'ayrioddiylikdan chin dildan dahshatga tushardim. Lekin bunga qanday rioya qila olardim? Men zamonamiz odami bo'lishi kerakdek kasallik darajasida sezgir edim. Ularning hammasi ahmoq va qo'ylardek bir-biriga o'xshardi. Balki idorada o'zini qo'rqoq va qul deb hisoblagan yagona odam men edim va men shunday deb hisoblardim, chunki men yuqoriroq rivojlangan edim. Lekin gap faqat shunday deb hisoblashimda emas edi, haqiqatan shunday edi. Men qo'rqoq va qul edim. Buni zarracha xijolat tortmasdan aytaman. Zamonamizning har bir odobli odami qo'rqoq va qul bo'lishi kerak. Bu uning normal holati. Bunga qat'iy ishonaman. U aynan shu maqsadda yaratilgan va qurilgan.

paras.en: And not only at the present time owing to some casual circumstances, but always, at all times, a decent man is bound to be a coward and a slave. It is the law of nature for all decent people all over the earth. If anyone of them happens to be valiant about something, he need not be comforted nor carried away by that; he would show the white feather just the same before something else. That is how it invariably and inevitably ends. Only donkeys and mules are valiant, and they only till they are pushed up to the wall. It is not worth while to pay attention to them for they really are of no consequence.
paras.uz: Va nafaqat hozirgi vaqtda qandaydir tasodifiy sharoitlar tufayli, balki doimo, har qanday zamonda odobli odam qo'rqoq va qul bo'lishga mahkum. Bu butun yer yuzidagi barcha odobli odamlar uchun tabiat qonuni. Agar ulardan biri qaysidir narsada jasur bo'lib qolsa, bundan na tasalli topishi, na berilib ketishi kerak; u baribir boshqa narsa oldida dumini qisadi. Bu har doim va muqarrar ravishda shunday tugaydi. Faqat eshaklar va xachirlar jasur, ular ham faqat devorga tiralguncha. Ularga e'tibor berishga arzimaydi, chunki ular haqiqatan ham ahamiyatsiz.

paras.en: Another circumstance, too, worried me in those days: that there was no one like me and I was unlike anyone else. "I am alone and they are everyone," I thought—and pondered.
paras.uz: O'sha kunlarda meni yana bir holat qiynardi: menga o'xshagan hech kim yo'q edi va men hech kimga o'xshamasdim. «Men yolg'izman, ular esa — hamma», — deb o'ylardim va mulohaza qilardim.

paras.en: From that it is evident that I was still a youngster.
paras.uz: Bundan ko'rinib turibdiki, men hali yosh bola edim.

paras.en: The very opposite sometimes happened. It was loathsome sometimes to go to the office; things reached such a point that I often came home ill. But all at once, à propos of nothing, there would come a phase of scepticism and indifference (everything happened in phases to me), and I would laugh myself at my intolerance and fastidiousness, I would reproach myself with being romantic. At one time I was unwilling to speak to anyone, while at other times I would not only talk, but go to the length of contemplating making friends with them. All my fastidiousness would suddenly, for no rhyme or reason, vanish. Who knows, perhaps I never had really had it, and it had simply been affected, and got out of books. I have not decided that question even now. Once I quite made friends with them, visited their homes, played preference, drank vodka, talked of promotions.... But here let me make a digression.
paras.uz: Ba'zan buning aksi ham bo'lardi. Ba'zan idoraga borish jirkanch edi; ish shu darajaga yetdiki, ko'pincha uyga kasal bo'lib qaytardim. Lekin birdan, hech narsadan-hech narsa yo'q, skeptitsizm va befarqlik davri kelardi (menda hamma narsa davrlar bilan kechardi) va men o'zim toqatsizligim va injiqligim ustidan kulardim, o'zimni romantiklikda ayblardim. Bir paytlar men hech kim bilan gaplashishni istamasdim, boshqa paytlarda esa nafaqat gaplashardim, balki ular bilan do'stlashishni o'ylashgacha borardim. Butun injiqligim birdan, hech qanday sababsiz yo'qolardi. Kim biladi, balki menda u hech qachon haqiqatan bo'lmagandir, shunchaki sun'iy, kitoblardan olingandir. Bu savolni hozir ham hal qilmaganman. Bir marta men ular bilan butunlay do'stlashib oldim, uylariga bordim, preferans o'ynadim, aroq ichdim, lavozim ko'tarilishi haqida gaplashdim... Lekin shu yerda bir chekinish qilay.

paras.en: We Russians, speaking generally, have never had those foolish transcendental "romantics"—German, and still more French—on whom nothing produces any effect; if there were an earthquake, if all France perished at the barricades, they would still be the same, they would not even have the decency to affect a change, but would still go on singing their transcendental songs to the hour of their death, because they are fools. We, in Russia, have no fools; that is well known. That is what distinguishes us from foreign lands. Consequently these transcendental natures are not found amongst us in their pure form. The idea that they are is due to our "realistic" journalists and critics of that day, always on the look out for Kostanzhoglos and Uncle Pyotr Ivanitchs and foolishly accepting them as our ideal; they have slandered our romantics, taking them for the same transcendental sort as in Germany or France.
paras.uz: Biz, ruslarda, umuman olganda, hech qachon o'sha ahmoq transsendental «romantiklar» — nemis, undan ham ko'proq fransuz romantiklari bo'lmagan, ularga hech narsa ta'sir qilmaydi; zilzila bo'lsa ham, butun Fransiya barrikadalarda halok bo'lsa ham, ular o'shandayligicha qolishadi, hatto o'zgarishni ko'rsatishga odob ham qilishmaydi, balki o'lim soatigacha transsendental qo'shiqlarini kuylashda davom etishadi, chunki ular ahmoq. Bizda, Rossiyada, ahmoqlar yo'q; bu hammaga ma'lum. Bizni chet ellardan ajratib turadigan narsa shu. Demak, bunday transsendental tabiatlar bizda sof holda uchramaydi. Ular bor degan fikr o'sha davrdagi «realist» jurnalistlarimiz va tanqidchilarimizdan kelib chiqqan, ular doimo Kostanjoglolar va Pyotr Ivanovich amakilarni izlab yurishgan va ahmoqona ularni idealimiz deb qabul qilishgan; ular romantiklarimizga tuhmat qilib, ularni Germaniya yoki Fransiyadagidek transsendental tur deb qabul qilishgan.

paras.en: On the contrary, the characteristics of our "romantics" are absolutely and directly opposed to the transcendental European type, and no European standard can be applied to them.
paras.uz: Aksincha, bizning «romantiklarimiz» xususiyatlari transsendental Yevropa turiga mutlaqo va bevosita zid va ularga hech qanday Yevropa mezonini qo'llab bo'lmaydi.

paras.en: (Allow me to make use of this word "romantic"—an old-fashioned and much respected word which has done good service and is familiar to all.) The characteristics of our romantic are to understand everything, to see everything and to see it often incomparably more clearly than our most realistic minds see it; to refuse to accept anyone or anything, but at the same time not to despise anything; to give way, to yield, from policy; never to lose sight of a useful practical object (such as rent-free quarters at the government expense, pensions, decorations), to keep their eye on that object through all the enthusiasms and volumes of lyrical poems, and at the same time to preserve "the sublime and the beautiful" inviolate within them to the hour of their death, and to preserve themselves also, incidentally, like some precious jewel wrapped in cotton wool if only for the benefit of "the sublime and the beautiful." Our "romantic" is a man of great breadth and the greatest rogue of all our rogues, I assure you....
paras.uz: (Menga «romantik» so'zidan foydalanishga ruxsat bering — yaxshi xizmat qilgan va hammaga tanish bo'lgan eskicha va juda hurmatli so'z.) Bizning romantikimizning xususiyatlari — hamma narsani tushunish, hamma narsani ko'rish va ko'pincha eng realist aqllarimizdan beqiyos aniqroq ko'rish; hech kimni va hech narsani qabul qilmaslik, lekin ayni paytda hech narsani mensimaslik; siyosatdan yon berish, chekinish; hech qachon foydali amaliy maqsadni (masalan, davlat hisobidan bepul kvartira, pensiyalar, nishonlar) ko'zdan qochirmaslik, barcha ishtiyoqlar va lirik she'rlar jildlari orasidan ham shu maqsadni kuzatib turish va ayni paytda «go'zal va ulug'vor»ni o'lim soatigacha ichida daxlsiz saqlash va yo'l-yo'lakay o'zini ham, hech bo'lmaganda «go'zal va ulug'vor» manfaati uchun, paxtaga o'ralgan qimmatbaho javohir kabi saqlash. Bizning «romantikimiz» — keng odam va barcha firibgarlarimizning eng kattasi, sizni ishontiraman...

paras.en: I can assure you from experience, indeed. Of course, that is, if he is intelligent. But what am I saying! The romantic is always intelligent, and I only meant to observe that although we have had foolish romantics they don't count, and they were only so because in the flower of their youth they degenerated into Germans, and to preserve their precious jewel more comfortably, settled somewhere out there—by preference in Weimar or the Black Forest.
paras.uz: Sizni tajribamdan ishontira olaman. Albatta, agar u aqlli bo'lsa. Lekin men nima deyapman! Romantik doimo aqlli, men faqat garchi bizda ahmoq romantiklar bo'lgan bo'lsa ham, ular hisobga kirmaydi, ular faqat yoshligining gullagan chog'ida nemislarga aylanib ketgani va qimmatbaho javohirini qulayroq saqlash uchun u yoqlarda — afzalroq Veymar yoki Shvarsvaldda — joylashib olgani uchun shunday bo'lgan, demoqchi edim.

paras.en: I, for instance, genuinely despised my official work and did not openly abuse it simply because I was in it myself and got a salary for it. Anyway, take note, I did not openly abuse it. Our romantic would rather go out of his mind—a thing, however, which very rarely happens—than take to open abuse, unless he had some other career in view; and he is never kicked out. At most, they would take him to the lunatic asylum as "the King of Spain" if he should go very mad. But it is only the thin, fair people who go out of their minds in Russia. Innumerable "romantics" attain later in life to considerable rank in the service. Their many-sidedness is remarkable! And what a faculty they have for the most contradictory sensations! I was comforted by this thought even in those days, and I am of the same opinion now.
paras.uz: Men, masalan, rasmiy ishimni chin dildan mensimasdim va uni ochiqdan-ochiq so'kmasdim, shunchaki o'zim unda ishlaganim va buning uchun maosh olganim uchun. Har holda, e'tibor bering, ochiqdan-ochiq so'kmasdim. Bizning romantikimiz, agar ko'z oldida boshqa martaba bo'lmasa, ochiq so'kishga o'tgandan ko'ra aqldan ozishni afzal ko'radi — garchi bu juda kamdan-kam bo'lsa ham; uni hech qachon tepib haydashmaydi. Ko'pi bilan, agar juda aqldan ozsa, uni «Ispaniya qiroli» sifatida jinnixonaga olib ketishadi. Lekin Rossiyada faqat oriq, malla odamlar aqldan ozadi. Son-sanoqsiz «romantiklar» keyinroq xizmatda ancha yuqori martabalarga erishadi. Ularning ko'p qirraliligi ajoyib! Va eng qarama-qarshi tuyg'ularga qanday qobiliyatlari bor! Men o'sha kunlarda ham bu fikrdan tasalli topardim va hozir ham xuddi shu fikrdaman.

paras.en: That is why there are so many "broad natures" among us who never lose their ideal even in the depths of degradation; and though they never stir a finger for their ideal, though they are arrant thieves and knaves, yet they tearfully cherish their first ideal and are extraordinarily honest at heart. Yes, it is only among us that the most incorrigible rogue can be absolutely and loftily honest at heart without in the least ceasing to be a rogue. I repeat, our romantics, frequently, become such accomplished rascals (I use the term "rascals" affectionately), suddenly display such a sense of reality and practical knowledge that their bewildered superiors and the public generally can only ejaculate in amazement.
paras.uz: Shuning uchun bizda xo'rlikning eng tubida ham idealini yo'qotmaydigan «keng tabiatlar» shunchalik ko'p; garchi ular ideali uchun bir barmoqlarini ham qimirlatmasalar ham, garchi ular ashaddiy o'g'ri va firibgar bo'lsalar ham, baribir birinchi idealini ko'z yoshi bilan ardoqlashadi va yuraklarida g'ayrioddiy darajada halol. Ha, faqat bizdagina eng tuzatib bo'lmas firibgar firibgar bo'lishdan zarracha to'xtamasdan, yuragida mutlaqo va yuksak darajada halol bo'lishi mumkin. Takrorlayman, bizning romantiklarimiz ko'pincha shunday mohir yaramaslarga aylanadi («yaramas» so'zini mehr bilan ishlataman), birdan shunday haqiqat hissi va amaliy bilim ko'rsatadilarki, dovdirab qolgan boshliqlari va umuman jamoatchilik faqat hayratdan og'iz ochib qoladi.

paras.en: Their many-sidedness is really amazing, and goodness knows what it may develop into later on, and what the future has in store for us. It is not a poor material! I do not say this from any foolish or boastful patriotism. But I feel sure that you are again imagining that I am joking. Or perhaps it's just the contrary and you are convinced that I really think so. Anyway, gentlemen, I shall welcome both views as an honour and a special favour. And do forgive my digression.
paras.uz: Ularning ko'p qirraliligi haqiqatan hayratlanarli va keyinchalik nimaga aylanishi va kelajak bizga nima tayyorlab qo'yganini Xudo biladi. Bu yomon material emas! Buni qandaydir ahmoqona yoki maqtanchoq vatanparvarlikdan aytayotganim yo'q. Lekin ishonchim komilki, siz yana meni hazillashyapti deb o'ylayapsiz. Yoki, balki, aksincha, men haqiqatan shunday o'ylayman deb ishonchingiz komildir. Har holda, janoblar, ikkala qarashni ham sharaf va alohida iltifot sifatida qabul qilaman. Chekinishim uchun meni kechiring.

paras.en: I did not, of course, maintain friendly relations with my comrades and soon was at loggerheads with them, and in my youth and inexperience I even gave up bowing to them, as though I had cut off all relations. That, however, only happened to me once. As a rule, I was always alone.
paras.uz: Albatta, men o'rtoqlarim bilan do'stona munosabatni saqlab qolmadim va tez orada ular bilan urishib qoldim, yoshligim va tajribasizligimda hatto ular bilan salomlashishni ham to'xtatdim, go'yo barcha aloqalarni uzgandek. Bu, biroq, menda faqat bir marta bo'lgan. Odatda men doim yolg'iz edim.

paras.en: In the first place I spent most of my time at home, reading. I tried to stifle all that was continually seething within me by means of external impressions. And the only external means I had was reading. Reading, of course, was a great help—exciting me, giving me pleasure and pain. But at times it bored me fearfully. One longed for movement in spite of everything, and I plunged all at once into dark, underground, loathsome vice of the pettiest kind. My wretched passions were acute, smarting, from my continual, sickly irritability I had hysterical impulses, with tears and convulsions. I had no resource except reading, that is, there was nothing in my surroundings which I could respect and which attracted me. I was overwhelmed with depression, too; I had an hysterical craving for incongruity and for contrast, and so I took to vice. I have not said all this to justify myself.... But, no! I am lying. I did want to justify myself. I make that little observation for my own benefit, gentlemen. I don't want to lie. I vowed to myself I would not.
paras.uz: Birinchidan, men vaqtimning ko'p qismini uyda, kitob o'qib o'tkazardim. Ichimda doimo qaynab turgan hamma narsani tashqi taassurotlar yordamida bo'g'ishga urinardim. Mendagi yagona tashqi vosita esa o'qish edi. O'qish, albatta, katta yordam edi — meni hayajonga solar, zavq ham, og'riq ham berardi. Lekin ba'zan meni dahshatli zeriktirardi. Hamma narsaga qaramay harakatga tashna bo'lardi odam va men birdan eng mayda turdagi qorong'i, yer osti, jirkanch buzuqlikka sho'ng'irdim. Ayanchli ehtiroslarim o'tkir, achishtiruvchi edi, doimiy, xasta jahldorligimdan menda ko'z yoshlari va talvasalar bilan isterik turtkilar bo'lardi. Menda o'qishdan boshqa hech qanday vosita yo'q edi, ya'ni atrofimda men hurmat qila oladigan va meni o'ziga tortadigan hech narsa yo'q edi. Meni tushkunlik ham bosgan edi; menda nomuvofiqlik va qarama-qarshilikka isterik tashnalik bor edi, shuning uchun buzuqlikka berildim. Bularning hammasini o'zimni oqlash uchun aytmadim... Lekin, yo'q! Yolg'on gapiryapman. O'zimni oqlamoqchi edim. Bu kichik izohni o'zim uchun qilyapman, janoblar. Yolg'on gapirishni istamayman. O'zimga yolg'on gapirmaslikka va'da bergan edim.

paras.en: And so, furtively, timidly, in solitude, at night, I indulged in filthy vice, with a feeling of shame which never deserted me, even at the most loathsome moments, and which at such moments nearly made me curse. Already even then I had my underground world in my soul. I was fearfully afraid of being seen, of being met, of being recognised. I visited various obscure haunts.
paras.uz: Shunday qilib, yashirincha, tortinib, yolg'izlikda, tunda men iflos buzuqlikka berilardim, hatto eng jirkanch lahzalarda ham meni hech qachon tark etmagan va bunday lahzalarda meni la'natlashga deyarli majbur qiladigan uyat tuyg'usi bilan. O'shandayoq qalbimda o'zimning yer osti dunyom bor edi. Meni ko'rib qolishlaridan, uchratib qolishlaridan, tanib qolishlaridan dahshatli qo'rqardim. Turli xil qorong'i joylarga borardim.

paras.en: One night as I was passing a tavern I saw through a lighted window some gentlemen fighting with billiard cues, and saw one of them thrown out of the window. At other times I should have felt very much disgusted, but I was in such a mood at the time, that I actually envied the gentleman thrown out of the window—and I envied him so much that I even went into the tavern and into the billiard-room. "Perhaps," I thought, "I'll have a fight, too, and they'll throw me out of the window."
paras.uz: Bir kecha bir maykhona yonidan o'tayotib, yoritilgan deraza orqali ba'zi janoblar bilyard kiylari bilan urishayotganini ko'rdim va ulardan birini derazadan uloqtirib yuborishganini ko'rdim. Boshqa paytda men juda jirkangan bo'lardim, lekin o'sha paytda shunday kayfiyatda edimki, derazadan uloqtirilgan janobga haqiqatan hasad qildim — shunchalik hasad qildimki, hatto maykhonaga, bilyard xonasiga kirdim. «Balki, — deb o'yladim, — men ham urishaman va meni ham derazadan uloqtirib yuborishadi.»

paras.en: I was not drunk—but what is one to do—depression will drive a man to such a pitch of hysteria? But nothing happened. It seemed that I was not even equal to being thrown out of the window and I went away without having my fight.
paras.uz: Men mast emas edim — lekin nima qilish kerak, tushkunlik odamni shunday isteriya darajasiga olib boradi-da? Lekin hech narsa bo'lmadi. Ma'lum bo'ldiki, men hatto derazadan uloqtirilishga ham qodir emasman va urishmasdan ketdim.

paras.en: An officer put me in my place from the first moment.
paras.uz: Bir zobit birinchi lahzadanoq meni o'z joyimga qo'ydi.

paras.en: I was standing by the billiard-table and in my ignorance blocking up the way, and he wanted to pass; he took me by the shoulders and without a word—without a warning or explanation—moved me from where I was standing to another spot and passed by as though he had not noticed me. I could have forgiven blows, but I could not forgive his having moved me without noticing me.
paras.uz: Men bilyard stoli yonida turib, bilmaganimdan yo'lni to'sib qo'ygan edim, u esa o'tmoqchi edi; u meni yelkalarimdan ushlab, indamasdan — hech qanday ogohlantirish yoki tushuntirishsiz — turgan joyimdan boshqa joyga surib qo'ydi va go'yo meni payqamagandek o'tib ketdi. Men urishlarni kechira olardim, lekin u meni payqamasdan surib qo'yganini kechira olmasdim.

paras.en: Devil knows what I would have given for a real regular quarrel—a more decent, a more literary one, so to speak. I had been treated like a fly. This officer was over six foot, while I was a spindly little fellow. But the quarrel was in my hands. I had only to protest and I certainly would have been thrown out of the window. But I changed my mind and preferred to beat a resentful retreat.
paras.uz: Haqiqiy, to'g'ri janjal uchun — ta'bir joiz bo'lsa, odobliroq, adabiyroq janjal uchun nimalarni bermagan bo'lardim, shayton biladi. Menga pashshadek munosabatda bo'lishgan edi. Bu zobitning bo'yi ikki metrcha edi, men esa ozg'in, kichkina odam edim. Lekin janjal mening qo'limda edi. Faqat e'tiroz bildirishim kerak edi va meni albatta derazadan uloqtirib yuborishardi. Lekin fikrimni o'zgartirdim va g'azab bilan chekinishni afzal ko'rdim.

paras.en: I went out of the tavern straight home, confused and troubled, and the next night I went out again with the same lewd intentions, still more furtively, abjectly and miserably than before, as it were, with tears in my eyes—but still I did go out again. Don't imagine, though, it was cowardice made me slink away from the officer; I never have been a coward at heart, though I have always been a coward in action. Don't be in a hurry to laugh—I assure you I can explain it all.
paras.uz: Maykhonadan chiqib, sarosimada va bezovta holda to'g'ri uyga bordim, ertasi kechasi esa yana o'sha buzuq niyatlar bilan, avvalgidan ham yashirinroq, tubanroq va ayanchliroq, go'yo ko'zlarimda yosh bilan — lekin baribir yana chiqdim. Lekin meni zobitdan qochishga qo'rqoqlik majbur qildi deb o'ylamang; men yuragimda hech qachon qo'rqoq bo'lmaganman, garchi harakatda doim qo'rqoq bo'lsam ham. Kulishga shoshilmang — sizni ishontiraman, hammasini tushuntirib bera olaman.

paras.en: Oh, if only that officer had been one of the sort who would consent to fight a duel! But no, he was one of those gentlemen (alas, long extinct!) Who preferred fighting with cues or, like Gogol's Lieutenant Pirogov, appealing to the police. They did not fight duels and would have thought a duel with a civilian like me an utterly unseemly procedure in any case—and they looked upon the duel altogether as something impossible, something free-thinking and French. But they were quite ready to bully, especially when they were over six foot.
paras.uz: Oh, agar o'sha zobit duelga rozi bo'ladiganlar toifasidan bo'lganida edi! Lekin yo'q, u kiylar bilan urishishni yoki Gogolning leytenant Pirogovi kabi politsiyaga murojaat qilishni afzal ko'radigan janoblardan (afsus, allaqachon yo'q bo'lib ketgan!) edi. Ular duel qilishmasdi va men kabi fuqaro bilan duelni har qanday holatda mutlaqo nomaqbul ish deb hisoblashgan bo'lardi — ular duelga umuman imkonsiz, qandaydir erkin fikrlovchi va fransuzcha narsa sifatida qarashardi. Lekin ular, ayniqsa bo'yi ikki metr bo'lganda, zo'ravonlik qilishga butunlay tayyor edi.

paras.en: I did not slink away through cowardice, but through an unbounded vanity. I was afraid not of his six foot, not of getting a sound thrashing and being thrown out of the window; I should have had physical courage enough, I assure you; but I had not the moral courage. What I was afraid of was that everyone present, from the insolent marker down to the lowest little stinking, pimply clerk in a greasy collar, would jeer at me and fail to understand when I began to protest and to address them in literary language. For of the point of honour—not of honour, but of the point of honour (point d'honneur)—one cannot speak among us except in literary language. You can't allude to the "point of honour" in ordinary language. I was fully convinced (the sense of reality, in spite of all my romanticism!) That they would all simply split their sides with laughter, and that the officer would not simply beat me, that is, without insulting me, but would certainly prod me in the back with his knee, kick me round the billiard-table, and only then perhaps have pity and drop me out of the window.
paras.uz: Men qo'rqoqlikdan emas, cheksiz shuhratparastlikdan qochdim. Men uning ikki metrlik bo'yidan, yaxshilab kaltaklanib, derazadan uloqtirilishdan qo'rqmadim; sizni ishontiraman, jismoniy jasoratim yetarli bo'lardi; lekin ma'naviy jasoratim yo'q edi. Men qo'rqqan narsa — men e'tiroz bildirib, ularga adabiy tilda murojaat qila boshlaganimda, hozir bo'lganlarning hammasi, surbet markyordan tortib yog'li yoqali eng past, sasigan, husnbuzarli kotibgacha, ustimdan kulishi va tushunmasligi edi. Chunki sharaf nuqtasi haqida — sharaf haqida emas, sharaf nuqtasi (point d'honneur) haqida — bizda adabiy tildan boshqa tilda gapirib bo'lmaydi. Oddiy tilda «sharaf nuqtasi»ga ishora qilib bo'lmaydi. Men to'liq ishonardim (romantizmimga qaramay, haqiqat hissi!), ular hammasi shunchaki kulgidan yorilib ketishadi, zobit esa meni shunchaki, ya'ni haqoratsiz urmaydi, balki albatta tizzasi bilan orqamga turtadi, bilyard stoli atrofida tepib aylantiradi va shundan keyingina, balki, rahmi kelib, meni derazadan tashlab yuboradi.

paras.en: Of course, this trivial incident could not with me end in that. I often met that officer afterwards in the street and noticed him very carefully. I am not quite sure whether he recognised me, I imagine not; I judge from certain signs. But I—I stared at him with spite and hatred and so it went on ... For several years! My resentment grew even deeper with years. At first I began making stealthy inquiries about this officer. It was difficult for me to do so, for I knew no one. But one day I heard someone shout his surname in the street as I was following him at a distance, as though I were tied to him—and so I learnt his surname. Another time I followed him to his flat, and for ten kopecks learned from the porter where he lived, on which storey, whether he lived alone or with others, and so on—in fact, everything one could learn from a porter.
paras.uz: Albatta, bu arzimas voqea men bilan shu bilan tugay olmasdi. Keyinchalik men o'sha zobitni ko'chada tez-tez uchratib, uni juda diqqat bilan kuzatardim. U meni tanidimi, aniq bilmayman, menimcha, yo'q; buni ba'zi belgilarga qarab aytaman. Lekin men — men unga g'araz va nafrat bilan tikilardim va bu shunday davom etdi... bir necha yil! Yillar o'tib g'azabim yanada chuqurlashdi. Avvaliga men bu zobit haqida yashirincha surishtira boshladim. Bu men uchun qiyin edi, chunki hech kimni tanimasdim. Lekin bir kuni uni uzoqdan, go'yo unga bog'langandek ergashib borayotganimda, ko'chada kimdir uning familiyasini baqirganini eshitdim — shunday qilib familiyasini bilib oldim. Boshqa safar uni kvartirasigacha kuzatib bordim va o'n tiyinga qorovuldan qayerda yashashini, qaysi qavatda, yolg'izmi yoki boshqalar bilanmi va hokazo — xullas, qorovuldan bilish mumkin bo'lgan hamma narsani bilib oldim.

paras.en: One morning, though I had never tried my hand with the pen, it suddenly occurred to me to write a satire on this officer in the form of a novel which would unmask his villainy. I wrote the novel with relish. I did unmask his villainy, I even exaggerated it; at first I so altered his surname that it could easily be recognised, but on second thoughts I changed it, and sent the story to the Otetchestvenniya Zapiski. But at that time such attacks were not the fashion and my story was not printed. That was a great vexation to me.
paras.uz: Bir kuni ertalab, garchi hech qachon qalam ushlab ko'rmagan bo'lsam ham, birdan xayolimga bu zobit haqida uning yovuzligini fosh qiladigan qissa shaklida hajviya yozish fikri keldi. Qissani zavq bilan yozdim. Uning yovuzligini fosh qildim, hatto bo'rttirib yubordim; avvaliga familiyasini osongina tanib olinadigan qilib o'zgartirdim, lekin o'ylab ko'rib uni o'zgartirdim va hikoyani «Otechestvenniye zapiski» jurnaliga yubordim. Lekin o'sha paytda bunday hujumlar urf emas edi va hikoyam chop etilmadi. Bu men uchun katta alam bo'ldi.

paras.en: Sometimes I was positively choked with resentment. At last I determined to challenge my enemy to a duel. I composed a splendid, charming letter to him, imploring him to apologise to me, and hinting rather plainly at a duel in case of refusal. The letter was so composed that if the officer had had the least understanding of the sublime and the beautiful he would certainly have flung himself on my neck and have offered me his friendship. And how fine that would have been! How we should have got on together! "He could have shielded me with his higher rank, while I could have improved his mind with my culture, and, well ... My ideas, and all sorts of things might have happened." Only fancy, this was two years after his insult to me, and my challenge would have been a ridiculous anachronism, in spite of all the ingenuity of my letter in disguising and explaining away the anachronism.
paras.uz: Ba'zan men g'azabdan rosa bo'g'ilardim. Nihoyat dushmanimni duelga chaqirishga qaror qildim. Men unga ajoyib, maftunkor maktub tuzdim, undan kechirim so'rashini yolvorib iltimos qildim va rad etgan taqdirda duelga ancha aniq ishora qildim. Maktub shunday tuzilgan ediki, agar zobitda go'zal va ulug'vorni zarracha tushunish bo'lganida, u albatta bo'ynimga tashlanib, menga do'stligini taklif qilgan bo'lardi. Bu qanchalik ajoyib bo'lardi! Qanday yaxshi til topishgan bo'lardik! «U meni yuqoriroq martabasi bilan himoya qila olardi, men esa uning aqlini madaniyatim bilan yuksaltira olardim, xo'sh... g'oyalarim bilan va har xil narsalar sodir bo'lishi mumkin edi.» Tasavvur qiling, bu uning haqoratidan ikki yil keyin edi va maktubimning anaxronizmni yashirish va tushuntirishdagi butun zukkoligiga qaramay, chaqirig'im kulgili anaxronizm bo'lgan bo'lardi.

paras.en: But, thank God (to this day I thank the Almighty with tears in my eyes) I did not send the letter to him. Cold shivers run down my back when I think of what might have happened if I had sent it.
paras.uz: Lekin, Xudoga shukur (shu kungacha ko'zlarimda yosh bilan Qodir Tangriga shukrona aytaman), men maktubni unga yubormadim. Agar yuborganimda nima bo'lishi mumkinligini o'ylaganimda orqamdan sovuq ter oqadi.

paras.en: And all at once I revenged myself in the simplest way, by a stroke of genius! A brilliant thought suddenly dawned upon me. Sometimes on holidays I used to stroll along the sunny side of the Nevsky about four o'clock in the afternoon. Though it was hardly a stroll so much as a series of innumerable miseries, humiliations and resentments; but no doubt that was just what I wanted. I used to wriggle along in a most unseemly fashion, like an eel, continually moving aside to make way for generals, for officers of the guards and the hussars, or for ladies. At such minutes there used to be a convulsive twinge at my heart, and I used to feel hot all down my back at the mere thought of the wretchedness of my attire, of the wretchedness and abjectness of my little scurrying figure.
paras.uz: Va birdan men eng oddiy yo'l bilan, dahoyona zarba bilan o'ch oldim! Birdan xayolimga yorqin fikr keldi. Ba'zan bayram kunlari men soat to'rtlarda Nevskiyning quyoshli tomonida sayr qilardim. Garchi bu sayrdan ko'ra son-sanoqsiz azoblar, xo'rliklar va g'azablar silsilasi bo'lsa ham; lekin, shubhasiz, menga aynan shu kerak edi. Men generallar, gvardiya va gusar zobitlari yoki xonimlarga yo'l berish uchun doimo chetga surilib, ilonbaliqdek eng nomaqbul tarzda burilib-buralib yurardim. Bunday daqiqalarda yuragim talvasali sanchilar va kiyimimning ayanchliligi, yugurib-yelib yurgan kichik qiyofamning ayanchliligi va tubanligi haqidagi fikrning o'zidan butun orqam qizib ketardi.

paras.en: This was a regular martyrdom, a continual, intolerable humiliation at the thought, which passed into an incessant and direct sensation, that I was a mere fly in the eyes of all this world, a nasty, disgusting fly—more intelligent, more highly developed, more refined in feeling than any of them, of course—but a fly that was continually making way for everyone, insulted and injured by everyone. Why I inflicted this torture upon myself, why I went to the Nevsky, I don't know. I felt simply drawn there at every possible opportunity.
paras.uz: Bu haqiqiy azob, bu butun dunyo nazarida men shunchaki pashsha, jirkanch, ko'ngilni aynitadigan pashsha — albatta, ularning har biridan aqlliroq, yuqoriroq rivojlangan, tuyg'uda noziroq — lekin doimo hammaga yo'l beradigan, hamma tomonidan haqoratlangan va xo'rlangan pashsha ekanim haqidagi, tinimsiz va bevosita sezgiga aylangan fikrdan doimiy, chidab bo'lmas xo'rlik edi. Nega o'zimni bu qiynoqqa solardim, nega Nevskiyga borardim — bilmayman. Shunchaki har imkoniyatda meni u yerga tortardi.

paras.en: Already then I began to experience a rush of the enjoyment of which I spoke in the first chapter. After my affair with the officer I felt even more drawn there than before: it was on the Nevsky that I met him most frequently, there I could admire him. He, too, went there chiefly on holidays, He, too, turned out of his path for generals and persons of high rank, and he too, wriggled between them like an eel; but people, like me, or even better dressed than me, he simply walked over; he made straight for them as though there was nothing but empty space before him, and never, under any circumstances, turned aside. I gloated over my resentment watching him and ... Always resentfully made way for him. It exasperated me that even in the street I could not be on an even footing with him.
paras.uz: O'shandayoq men birinchi bobda gapirgan zavqning to'lqinini his qila boshladim. Zobit bilan bo'lgan voqeadan keyin meni u yerga avvalgidan ham ko'proq torta boshladi: uni eng ko'p Nevskiyda uchratardim, u yerda unga mahliyo bo'la olardim. U ham u yerga asosan bayram kunlari borardi, u ham generallar va yuqori martabali kishilarga yo'l berib burilardi va u ham ular orasida ilonbaliqdek burilib-buralib yurardi; lekin men kabi yoki hatto mendan yaxshiroq kiyingan odamlarni u shunchaki bosib o'tardi; ularga to'g'ri borardi, go'yo oldida bo'sh joydan boshqa hech narsa yo'qdek, va hech qachon, hech qanday holatda chetga burilmasdi. Men uni kuzatib g'azabimdan huzur qilardim va... doimo g'azab bilan unga yo'l berardim. Hatto ko'chada ham u bilan teng tura olmasligim meni jahldor qilardi.

paras.en: "Why must you invariably be the first to move aside?" I kept asking myself in hysterical rage, waking up sometimes at three o'clock in the morning. "Why is it you and not he? There's no regulation about it; there's no written law. Let the making way be equal as it usually is when refined people meet; he moves half-way and you move half-way; you pass with mutual respect."
paras.uz: «Nega har doim aynan sen birinchi bo'lib chetga surilishing kerak? — deb o'zimdan isterik g'azab bilan so'rardim, ba'zan tungi soat uchda uyg'onib. — Nega sen, nega u emas? Bu haqda hech qanday nizom yo'q; hech qanday yozma qonun yo'q. Yo'l berish teng bo'lsin, odatda nozik odamlar uchrashganda bo'lganidek; u yarim yo'l chetga suriladi, sen yarim yo'l; o'zaro hurmat bilan o'tasizlar.»

paras.en: But that never happened, and I always moved aside, while he did not even notice my making way for him. And lo and behold a bright idea dawned upon me! "What," I thought, "if I meet him and don't move on one side? What if I don't move aside on purpose, even if I knock up against him? How would that be?" This audacious idea took such a hold on me that it gave me no peace. I was dreaming of it continually, horribly, and I purposely went more frequently to the Nevsky in order to picture more vividly how I should do it when I did do it. I was delighted. This intention seemed to me more and more practical and possible.
paras.uz: Lekin bu hech qachon bo'lmasdi va men doim chetga surilardim, u esa hatto unga yo'l berayotganimni payqamasdi ham. Va mana, xayolimga yorqin fikr keldi! «Agar, — deb o'yladim, — uni uchratib, chetga surilmasam-chi? Agar unga urilib ketsam ham, ataylab chetga surilmasam-chi? Bu qanday bo'lardi?» Bu jasur fikr meni shunchalik chulg'ab oldiki, menga tinchlik bermadi. Men u haqda doimo, dahshatli tarzda orzu qilardim va buni qilganimda qanday qilishimni yorqinroq tasavvur qilish uchun ataylab Nevskiyga tez-tez borardim. Men xursand edim. Bu niyat menga tobora amaliyroq va mumkinroq tuyulardi.

paras.en: "Of course I shall not really push him," I thought, already more good-natured in my joy. "I will simply not turn aside, will run up against him, not very violently, but just shouldering each other—just as much as decency permits. I will push against him just as much as he pushes against me." At last I made up my mind completely. But my preparations took a great deal of time. To begin with, when I carried out my plan I should need to be looking rather more decent, and so I had to think of my get-up. "In case of emergency, if, for instance, there were any sort of public scandal (and the public there is of the most recherché: the Countess walks there; Prince D. Walks there; all the literary world is there), I must be well dressed; that inspires respect and of itself puts us on an equal footing in the eyes of the society."
paras.uz: «Albatta, uni haqiqatan itarmayman, — deb o'yladim, quvonchimdan allaqachon xushfe'lroq bo'lib. — Shunchaki chetga burilmayman, unga urilaman, unchalik qattiq emas, shunchaki yelkama-yelka — odob ruxsat bergan darajada. U meni qanchalik itarsa, men ham uni shunchalik itaraman.» Nihoyat men butunlay qaror qildim. Lekin tayyorgarligim ko'p vaqt oldi. Avvalo, rejamni amalga oshirganimda ancha odobliroq ko'rinishim kerak edi, shuning uchun kiyimim haqida o'ylashim kerak edi. «Har ehtimolga qarshi, agar, masalan, qandaydir ommaviy janjal bo'lsa (u yerdagi omma esa eng tanlangan: grafinya u yerda sayr qiladi; knyaz D. u yerda sayr qiladi; butun adabiy dunyo u yerda), men yaxshi kiyingan bo'lishim kerak; bu hurmat uyg'otadi va o'z-o'zidan jamiyat nazarida bizni teng qilib qo'yadi.»

paras.en: With this object I asked for some of my salary in advance, and bought at Tchurkin's a pair of black gloves and a decent hat. Black gloves seemed to me both more dignified and bon ton than the lemon-coloured ones which I had contemplated at first. "The colour is too gaudy, it looks as though one were trying to be conspicuous," and I did not take the lemon-coloured ones. I had got ready long beforehand a good shirt, with white bone studs; my overcoat was the only thing that held me back. The coat in itself was a very good one, it kept me warm; but it was wadded and it had a raccoon collar which was the height of vulgarity. I had to change the collar at any sacrifice, and to have a beaver one like an officer's. For this purpose I began visiting the Gostiny Dvor and after several attempts I pitched upon a piece of cheap German beaver.
paras.uz: Shu maqsadda men maoshimning bir qismini oldindan so'radim va Churkinning do'konidan bir juft qora qo'lqop va odobli shlyapa sotib oldim. Qora qo'lqoplar menga avvaliga ko'zlagan limon rangli qo'lqoplardan ko'ra salobatliroq va bon ton — odobga mosroq tuyuldi. «Rangi haddan tashqari yorqin, go'yo odam ko'zga tashlanishga urinayotgandek ko'rinadi», — deb limon ranglilarini olmadim. Men ancha oldin oq suyak tugmali yaxshi ko'ylak tayyorlab qo'ygan edim; meni faqat paltom ushlab turardi. Paltoning o'zi juda yaxshi edi, meni issiq tutardi; lekin u paxtali edi va yenot mo'ynali yoqasi bor edi, bu tubanlikning cho'qqisi edi. Har qanday qurbonlik evaziga yoqani o'zgartirib, zobitlarnikidek qunduz yoqa qo'yishim kerak edi. Shu maqsadda Gostiniy Dvorga borib tura boshladim va bir necha urinishdan keyin arzon nemis qunduzining bir bo'lagini tanladim.

paras.en: Though these German beavers soon grow shabby and look wretched, yet at first they look exceedingly well, and I only needed it for the occasion. I asked the price; even so, it was too expensive. After thinking it over thoroughly I decided to sell my raccoon collar. The rest of the money—a considerable sum for me, I decided to borrow from Anton Antonitch Syetotchkin, my immediate superior, an unassuming person, though grave and judicious. He never lent money to anyone, but I had, on entering the service, been specially recommended to him by an important personage who had got me my berth. I was horribly worried. To borrow from Anton Antonitch seemed to me monstrous and shameful. I did not sleep for two or three nights. Indeed, I did not sleep well at that time, I was in a fever; I had a vague sinking at my heart or else a sudden throbbing, throbbing, throbbing!
paras.uz: Garchi bu nemis qunduzlari tez eskirib, ayanchli ko'rinsa ham, avvaliga ular nihoyatda yaxshi ko'rinadi, menga esa u faqat shu voqea uchun kerak edi. Narxini so'radim; shunda ham juda qimmat edi. Yaxshilab o'ylab ko'rib, yenot yoqamni sotishga qaror qildim. Qolgan pulni — men uchun ancha katta summani — bevosita boshlig'im, kamtar, lekin jiddiy va mulohazali odam Anton Antonovich Setochkindan qarz olishga qaror qildim. U hech qachon hech kimga qarz bermasdi, lekin men xizmatga kirganimda menga lavozim olib bergan muhim shaxs meni unga alohida tavsiya qilgan edi. Men dahshatli xavotirda edim. Anton Antonovichdan qarz olish menga dahshatli va sharmandali tuyulardi. Ikki-uch kecha uxlamadim. Haqiqatan ham, o'sha paytda yaxshi uxlamasdim, isitmalardim; yuragim noaniq so'nardi yoki birdan urardi, urardi, urardi!

paras.en: Anton Antonitch was surprised at first, then he frowned, then he reflected, and did after all lend me the money, receiving from me a written authorisation to take from my salary a fortnight later the sum that he had lent me.
paras.uz: Anton Antonovich avvaliga hayron bo'ldi, keyin qovog'ini soldi, keyin o'ylab qoldi va baribir menga pulni qarz berdi, mendan ikki haftadan keyin maoshimdan qarz bergan summani olishga yozma ruxsat oldi.

paras.en: In this way everything was at last ready. The handsome beaver replaced the mean-looking raccoon, and I began by degrees to get to work. It would never have done to act offhand, at random; the plan had to be carried out skilfully, by degrees. But I must confess that after many efforts I began to despair: we simply could not run into each other. I made every preparation, I was quite determined—it seemed as though we should run into one another directly—and before I knew what I was doing I had stepped aside for him again and he had passed without noticing me. I even prayed as I approached him that God would grant me determination. One time I had made up my mind thoroughly, but it ended in my stumbling and falling at his feet because at the very last instant when I was six inches from him my courage failed me. He very calmly stepped over me, while I flew on one side like a ball. That night I was ill again, feverish and delirious.
paras.uz: Shu tariqa nihoyat hammasi tayyor bo'ldi. Chiroyli qunduz xunuk ko'rinishli yenot o'rnini egalladi va men asta-sekin ishga kirishdim. Darhol, tavakkal harakat qilish yaramasdi; rejani mohirona, bosqichma-bosqich amalga oshirish kerak edi. Lekin tan olishim kerakki, ko'p urinishlardan keyin umidsizlikka tusha boshladim: biz shunchaki bir-birimizga urila olmasdik. Men hamma tayyorgarlikni ko'rardim, butunlay qat'iy edim — go'yo hozir bir-birimizga urilib ketadigandek tuyulardi — va nima qilayotganimni anglamasimdan, yana unga yo'l berib chetga chiqqan bo'lardim, u esa meni payqamasdan o'tib ketardi. Hatto unga yaqinlashganimda Xudodan menga qat'iyat berishini so'rab duo qilardim. Bir safar men butunlay qaror qilgan edim, lekin bu mening qoqilib, uning oyog'i ostiga yiqilishim bilan tugadi, chunki undan o'n besh santimetr qolganda, eng so'nggi lahzada jasoratim meni tark etdi. U juda xotirjamlik bilan mening ustimdan hatlab o'tdi, men esa to'pdek bir chetga uchib ketdim. O'sha kechasi yana kasal bo'ldim, isitmaladim va alahsiradim.

paras.en: And suddenly it ended most happily. The night before I had made up my mind not to carry out my fatal plan and to abandon it all, and with that object I went to the Nevsky for the last time, just to see how I would abandon it all. Suddenly, three paces from my enemy, I unexpectedly made up my mind—I closed my eyes, and we ran full tilt, shoulder to shoulder, against one another! I did not budge an inch and passed him on a perfectly equal footing! He did not even look round and pretended not to notice it; but he was only pretending, I am convinced of that. I am convinced of that to this day! Of course, I got the worst of it—he was stronger, but that was not the point. The point was that I had attained my object, I had kept up my dignity, I had not yielded a step, and had put myself publicly on an equal social footing with him.
paras.uz: Va birdan bu eng baxtli tarzda tugadi. Oldingi kechasi men halokatli rejamni amalga oshirmaslikka va hammasidan voz kechishga qaror qilgan edim va shu maqsadda Nevskiyga oxirgi marta, shunchaki hammasidan qanday voz kechishimni ko'rish uchun bordim. Birdan, dushmanimdan uch qadam narida kutilmaganda qaror qildim — ko'zlarimni yumdim va biz yelkama-yelka, bor tezlik bilan bir-birimizga urildik! Men bir qarich ham surilmadim va undan mutlaqo teng holda o'tdim! U hatto orqasiga qaramadi va buni payqamagandek ko'rsatdi; lekin u faqat o'zini shunday ko'rsatdi, bunga ishonchim komil. Shu kungacha bunga ishonchim komil! Albatta, ko'proq men zarar ko'rdim — u kuchliroq edi, lekin gap bunda emas edi. Gap shunda ediki, men maqsadimga erishdim, qadr-qimmatimni saqladim, bir qadam ham yon bermadim va o'zimni omma oldida u bilan teng ijtimoiy darajaga qo'ydim.

paras.en: I returned home feeling that I was fully avenged for everything. I was delighted. I was triumphant and sang Italian arias. Of course, I will not describe to you what happened to me three days later; if you have read my first chapter you can guess for yourself. The officer was afterwards transferred; I have not seen him now for fourteen years. What is the dear fellow doing now? Whom is he walking over?
paras.uz: Uyga hamma narsa uchun to'liq o'ch olganimni his qilib qaytdim. Men xursand edim. Men g'olib edim va italyan ariyalarini kuyladim. Albatta, uch kundan keyin menga nima bo'lganini sizga tasvirlab bermayman; agar birinchi bobimni o'qigan bo'lsangiz, o'zingiz taxmin qila olasiz. Keyinroq zobitni boshqa joyga o'tkazishdi; men uni o'n to'rt yildan beri ko'rmayman. Aziz odam hozir nima qilyapti ekan? Kimni bosib o'tyapti ekan?
