chapters.recap_uz: Ikkinchi qism, yigirma yil oldin: yigirma to'rt yoshli hikoyachi idorada yolg'iz, hamkasblaridan nafratlanadi va qo'rqadi. «Romantiklar» haqida chekinish. Bilyardxonada bir zobit uni pashshadek surib qo'yadi; yillar davomida u qasos rejalaydi va nihoyat Nevskiyda zobit bilan yelkama-yelka urilib, «g'alaba» qozonadi.

chapters.title: Dreams of the sublime

paras.en: But the period of my dissipation would end and I always felt very sick afterwards. It was followed by remorse—I tried to drive it away; I felt too sick. By degrees, however, I grew used to that too. I grew used to everything, or rather I voluntarily resigned myself to enduring it. But I had a means of escape that reconciled everything—that was to find refuge in "the sublime and the beautiful," in dreams, of course. I was a terrible dreamer, I would dream for three months on end, tucked away in my corner, and you may believe me that at those moments I had no resemblance to the gentleman who, in the perturbation of his chicken heart, put a collar of German beaver on his great-coat. I suddenly became a hero. I would not have admitted my six-foot lieutenant even if he had called on me. I could not even picture him before me then.
paras.uz: Lekin buzuqlik davrim tugardi va keyin doimo ko'nglim juda aynirdi. Undan keyin pushaymonlik kelardi — men uni haydashga urinardim; ko'nglim haddan tashqari aynirdi. Biroq asta-sekin men bunga ham ko'nikdim. Men hamma narsaga ko'nikdim, aniqrog'i, ixtiyoriy ravishda unga chidashga rozi bo'ldim. Lekin menda hamma narsani yarashtiruvchi qochish vositasi bor edi — bu «go'zal va ulug'vor»da, albatta, orzularda panoh topish edi. Men dahshatli xayolparast edim, burchagimga biqinib, uch oylab ketma-ket orzu qilardim va ishonaverishingiz mumkinki, o'sha lahzalarda men tovuq yuragining sarosimasida paltosiga nemis qunduzi yoqasini qo'ygan janobga hech o'xshamasdim. Men birdan qahramonga aylanardim. O'shanda ikki metrlik leytenantim meni ziyorat qilganida ham uni qabul qilmagan bo'lardim. O'shanda uni hatto ko'z oldimga ham keltira olmasdim.

paras.en: What were my dreams and how I could satisfy myself with them—it is hard to say now, but at the time I was satisfied with them. Though, indeed, even now, I am to some extent satisfied with them. Dreams were particularly sweet and vivid after a spell of dissipation; they came with remorse and with tears, with curses and transports. There were moments of such positive intoxication, of such happiness, that there was not the faintest trace of irony within me, on my honour. I had faith, hope, love. I believed blindly at such times that by some miracle, by some external circumstance, all this would suddenly open out, expand; that suddenly a vista of suitable activity—beneficent, good, and, above all, ready made (what sort of activity I had no idea, but the great thing was that it should be all ready for me)—would rise up before me—and I should come out into the light of day, almost riding a white horse and crowned with laurel.
paras.uz: Orzularim nima edi va ular bilan qanday qanoatlanardim — hozir aytish qiyin, lekin o'shanda ular bilan qanoatlanardim. Darvoqe, hatto hozir ham ma'lum darajada ular bilan qanoatlanaman. Orzular ayniqsa buzuqlik davridan keyin shirin va yorqin bo'lardi; ular pushaymonlik va ko'z yoshlari bilan, la'natlar va vajdlar bilan kelardi. Shunday haqiqiy mastlik, shunday baxt lahzalari bo'lardiki, ichimda kinoyaning zarracha izi ham qolmasdi, sharafim haqqi. Menda iymon, umid, muhabbat bor edi. Bunday paytlarda ko'r-ko'rona ishonardimki, qandaydir mo''jiza bilan, qandaydir tashqi holat tufayli bularning hammasi birdan ochilib, kengayib ketadi; birdan oldimda munosib faoliyat — xayrli, yaxshi va, eng muhimi, tayyor faoliyat (qanday faoliyat ekanini bilmasdim, lekin muhimi u men uchun butunlay tayyor bo'lishi edi) manzarasi paydo bo'ladi — va men deyarli oq otga minib, dafna gulchambari kiyib kunduz yorug'iga chiqaman.

paras.en: Anything but the foremost place I could not conceive for myself, and for that very reason I quite contentedly occupied the lowest in reality. Either to be a hero or to grovel in the mud—there was nothing between. That was my ruin, for when I was in the mud I comforted myself with the thought that at other times I was a hero, and the hero was a cloak for the mud: for an ordinary man it was shameful to defile himself, but a hero was too lofty to be utterly defiled, and so he might defile himself. It is worth noting that these attacks of the "sublime and the beautiful" visited me even during the period of dissipation and just at the times when I was touching the bottom. They came in separate spurts, as though reminding me of themselves, but did not banish the dissipation by their appearance.
paras.uz: Men o'zim uchun birinchi o'rindan boshqa hech narsani tasavvur qila olmasdim va aynan shuning uchun haqiqatda eng pastki o'rinni butunlay mamnunlik bilan egallardim. Yo qahramon bo'lish, yo loyda emaklash — o'rtasida hech narsa yo'q edi. Bu meni halok qildi, chunki loyda bo'lganimda boshqa paytlarda qahramon ekanim haqidagi fikr bilan o'zimni yupatardim, qahramon esa loy uchun yopinchiq edi: oddiy odam uchun o'zini bulg'ash uyat edi, lekin qahramon butunlay bulg'anish uchun haddan tashqari yuksak edi, shuning uchun u o'zini bulg'ashi mumkin edi. Shuni qayd etish arziydiki, «go'zal va ulug'vor» xurujlari menga hatto buzuqlik davrida ham, aynan tubga tegib turgan paytlarimda ham tashrif buyurardi. Ular alohida otilishlar bilan, go'yo o'zlarini eslatgandek kelardi, lekin paydo bo'lishi bilan buzuqlikni haydab yubormasdi.

paras.en: On the contrary, they seemed to add a zest to it by contrast, and were only sufficiently present to serve as an appetising sauce. That sauce was made up of contradictions and sufferings, of agonising inward analysis, and all these pangs and pin-pricks gave a certain piquancy, even a significance to my dissipation—in fact, completely answered the purpose of an appetising sauce. There was a certain depth of meaning in it. And I could hardly have resigned myself to the simple, vulgar, direct debauchery of a clerk and have endured all the filthiness of it. What could have allured me about it then and have drawn me at night into the street? No, I had a lofty way of getting out of it all.
paras.uz: Aksincha, ular qarama-qarshilik orqali unga ta'm qo'shayotgandek tuyulardi va faqat ishtahani ochuvchi sous bo'lib xizmat qilish uchun yetarli darajada hozir edi. Bu sous ziddiyatlar va azoblardan, qiynovchi ichki tahlildan tarkib topgan edi va bu barcha og'riqlar va igna sanchishlar buzuqligimga qandaydir o'tkirlik, hatto ma'no berardi — xullas, ishtahani ochuvchi sous vazifasini to'liq bajarardi. Unda qandaydir chuqur ma'no bor edi. Men kotibning oddiy, tuban, to'g'ridan-to'g'ri buzuqligiga va uning butun iflosligiga chidashga zo'rg'a rozi bo'lardim. O'shanda unda meni nima o'ziga tortib, tunda ko'chaga olib chiqishi mumkin edi? Yo'q, mening bularning hammasidan chiqishning yuksak yo'lim bor edi.

paras.en: And what loving-kindness, oh Lord, what loving-kindness I felt at times in those dreams of mine! In those "flights into the sublime and the beautiful"; though it was fantastic love, though it was never applied to anything human in reality, yet there was so much of this love that one did not feel afterwards even the impulse to apply it in reality; that would have been superfluous. Everything, however, passed satisfactorily by a lazy and fascinating transition into the sphere of art, that is, into the beautiful forms of life, lying ready, largely stolen from the poets and novelists and adapted to all sorts of needs and uses. I, for instance, was triumphant over everyone; everyone, of course, was in dust and ashes, and was forced spontaneously to recognise my superiority, and I forgave them all.
paras.uz: Va qanday mehr-shafqat, ey Rabbim, qanday mehr-shafqat his qilardim ba'zan o'sha orzularimda! O'sha «go'zal va ulug'vorga parvozlar»da; garchi bu xayoliy muhabbat bo'lsa ham, garchi u hech qachon haqiqatda insoniy narsaga qo'llanilmagan bo'lsa ham, bu muhabbat shunchalik ko'p ediki, keyin uni haqiqatda qo'llashga hatto turtki ham his qilmasdi odam; bu ortiqcha bo'lardi. Biroq hamma narsa san'at sohasiga, ya'ni tayyor yotgan, asosan shoirlar va romanchilardan o'g'irlangan va har xil ehtiyoj va maqsadlarga moslashtirilgan hayotning go'zal shakllariga dangasa va maftunkor o'tish bilan qoniqarli o'tardi. Men, masalan, hammadan ustun kelardim; hamma, albatta, chang va kulda bo'lardi va o'z-o'zidan mening ustunligimni tan olishga majbur bo'lardi, men esa hammasini kechirardim.

paras.en: I was a poet and a grand gentleman, I fell in love; I came in for countless millions and immediately devoted them to humanity, and at the same time I confessed before all the people my shameful deeds, which, of course, were not merely shameful, but had in them much that was "sublime and beautiful" something in the Manfred style. Everyone would kiss me and weep (what idiots they would be if they did not), while I should go barefoot and hungry preaching new ideas and fighting a victorious Austerlitz against the obscurantists. Then the band would play a march, an amnesty would be declared, the Pope would agree to retire from Rome to Brazil; then there would be a ball for the whole of Italy at the Villa Borghese on the shores of Lake Como, Lake Como being for that purpose transferred to the neighbourhood of Rome; then would come a scene in the bushes, and so on, and so on—as though you did not know all about it?
paras.uz: Men shoir va ulug' janob edim, oshiq bo'lardim; menga son-sanoqsiz millionlar meros qolardi va men ularni darhol insoniyatga bag'ishlardim, ayni paytda butun xalq oldida sharmandali qilmishlarimni tan olardim, ular, albatta, shunchaki sharmandali emas, balki ularda ko'p «go'zal va ulug'vor» narsa, qandaydir Manfred uslubidagi narsa bor edi. Hamma meni o'pib yig'lardi (agar yig'lamasalar, qanday ahmoq bo'lishardi), men esa yalangoyoq va och holda yangi g'oyalarni targ'ib qilib, obskurantlarga qarshi g'olibona Austerlits jangini olib borardim. Keyin orkestr marsh chalardi, amnistiya e'lon qilinardi, Papa Rimdan Braziliyaga ketishga rozi bo'lardi; keyin Komo ko'li bo'yidagi Borgeze villasida butun Italiya uchun bal bo'lardi, Komo ko'li shu maqsadda Rim yaqiniga ko'chirilardi; keyin butalar orasida sahna bo'lardi va hokazo, va hokazo — go'yo siz bularning hammasini bilmagandek?

paras.en: You will say that it is vulgar and contemptible to drag all this into public after all the tears and transports which I have myself confessed. But why is it contemptible? Can you imagine that I am ashamed of it all, and that it was stupider than anything in your life, gentlemen? And I can assure you that some of these fancies were by no means badly composed.... It did not all happen on the shores of Lake Como. And yet you are right—it really is vulgar and contemptible. And most contemptible of all it is that now I am attempting to justify myself to you. And even more contemptible than that is my making this remark now. But that's enough, or there will be no end to it; each step will be more contemptible than the last....
paras.uz: Siz men o'zim tan olgan barcha ko'z yoshlari va vajdlardan keyin bularning hammasini ommaga sudrab chiqish tubanlik va jirkanchlik deysiz. Lekin nega jirkanch? Nahotki men bularning hammasidan uyalaman va bu sizning hayotingizdagi har qanday narsadan ahmoqonaroq edi deb tasavvur qila olsangiz, janoblar? Sizni ishontiraman, bu xayollarning ba'zilari umuman yomon tuzilmagan edi... Hammasi Komo ko'li bo'yida sodir bo'lmagan. Shunga qaramay siz haqsiz — bu haqiqatan tuban va jirkanch. Eng jirkanchi esa — hozir sizning oldingizda o'zimni oqlashga urinayotganim. Bundan ham jirkanchrog'i — hozir shu izohni qilayotganim. Lekin bas, aks holda oxiri bo'lmaydi; har bir qadam oldingisidan jirkanchroq bo'ladi...

paras.en: I could never stand more than three months of dreaming at a time without feeling an irresistible desire to plunge into society. To plunge into society meant to visit my superior at the office, Anton Antonitch Syetotchkin. He was the only permanent acquaintance I have had in my life, and I wonder at the fact myself now. But I only went to see him when that phase came over me, and when my dreams had reached such a point of bliss that it became essential at once to embrace my fellows and all mankind; and for that purpose I needed, at least, one human being, actually existing. I had to call on Anton Antonitch, however, on Tuesday—his at-home day; so I had always to time my passionate desire to embrace humanity so that it might fall on a Tuesday.
paras.uz: Men hech qachon jamiyatga sho'ng'ish uchun chidab bo'lmas istak his qilmasdan uch oydan ortiq orzu qila olmasdim. Jamiyatga sho'ng'ish idoradagi boshlig'im Anton Antonovich Setochkinni ziyorat qilish degani edi. U hayotimdagi yagona doimiy tanishim edi va hozir bunga o'zim hayron qolaman. Lekin men uni faqat o'sha davr kelganda va orzularim shunday saodat darajasiga yetganda ziyorat qilardim-ki, darhol hamjinslarimni va butun insoniyatni quchoqlash zarur bo'lib qolardi; buning uchun esa menga hech bo'lmaganda bitta, haqiqatan mavjud inson kerak edi. Biroq Anton Antonovichning oldiga seshanba kuni — uning mehmon qabul qiladigan kuni borishim kerak edi; shuning uchun insoniyatni quchoqlashga bo'lgan ehtirosli istagimni doimo seshanbaga to'g'ri keladigan qilib moslashtirishim kerak edi.

paras.en: This Anton Antonitch lived on the fourth storey in a house in Five Corners, in four low-pitched rooms, one smaller than the other, of a particularly frugal and sallow appearance. He had two daughters and their aunt, who used to pour out the tea. Of the daughters one was thirteen and another fourteen, they both had snub noses, and I was awfully shy of them because they were always whispering and giggling together. The master of the house usually sat in his study on a leather couch in front of the table with some grey-headed gentleman, usually a colleague from our office or some other department. I never saw more than two or three visitors there, always the same. They talked about the excise duty; about business in the senate, about salaries, about promotions, about His Excellency, and the best means of pleasing him, and so on.
paras.uz: Bu Anton Antonovich Besh Burchakdagi bir uyning to'rtinchi qavatida, birin-ketin kichrayib boradigan, ayniqsa tejamkor va sarg'ish ko'rinishli to'rtta past shiftli xonada yashardi. Uning ikki qizi va choy quyib beradigan xolasi bor edi. Qizlarning biri o'n uch, ikkinchisi o'n to'rt yoshda edi, ikkalasining ham burni puchuq edi va men ulardan juda tortinardim, chunki ular doim bir-biri bilan shivirlashib, xixillab kulishardi. Uy egasi odatda o'z kabinetida stol oldidagi charm divanda qandaydir oq sochli janob, odatda bizning idoradan yoki boshqa bo'limdan hamkasbi bilan o'tirardi. U yerda men hech qachon ikki-uchtadan ortiq mehmon ko'rmaganman, doim o'shalar. Ular aksiz solig'i haqida; senatdagi ishlar haqida, maoshlar haqida, lavozim ko'tarilishi haqida, Janobi Oliylari va uni xursand qilishning eng yaxshi vositalari haqida va hokazo gaplashishardi.

paras.en: I had the patience to sit like a fool beside these people for four hours at a stretch, listening to them without knowing what to say to them or venturing to say a word. I became stupefied, several times I felt myself perspiring, I was overcome by a sort of paralysis; but this was pleasant and good for me. On returning home I deferred for a time my desire to embrace all mankind.
paras.uz: Men bu odamlar yonida to'rt soat davomida ahmoqdek o'tirib, ularga nima deyishni bilmasdan va bir og'iz so'z aytishga jur'at etmasdan tinglashga sabr qilardim. Esim ketib qolardi, bir necha marta terlaganimni his qilardim, meni qandaydir falaj bosardi; lekin bu yoqimli va men uchun foydali edi. Uyga qaytgach, butun insoniyatni quchoqlash istagimni bir muddatga kechiktirardim.

paras.en: I had however one other acquaintance of a sort, Simonov, who was an old schoolfellow. I had a number of schoolfellows, indeed, in Petersburg, but I did not associate with them and had even given up nodding to them in the street. I believe I had transferred into the department I was in simply to avoid their company and to cut off all connection with my hateful childhood. Curses on that school and all those terrible years of penal servitude! In short, I parted from my schoolfellows as soon as I got out into the world. There were two or three left to whom I nodded in the street. One of them was Simonov, who had in no way been distinguished at school, was of a quiet and equable disposition; but I discovered in him a certain independence of character and even honesty I don't even suppose that he was particularly stupid.
paras.uz: Biroq menda yana bir o'ziga xos tanish bor edi — eski maktabdoshim Simonov. Peterburgda maktabdoshlarim, haqiqatan ham, ko'p edi, lekin men ular bilan munosabatda bo'lmasdim va hatto ko'chada ularga bosh irg'ashni ham to'xtatgan edim. Menimcha, men ishlayotgan bo'limga shunchaki ularning davrasidan qochish va nafratli bolaligim bilan barcha aloqani uzish uchun o'tgan edim. La'nat o'sha maktabga va o'sha dahshatli katorga yillariga! Xullas, men dunyoga chiqishim bilanoq maktabdoshlarim bilan ajrashdim. Ko'chada bosh irg'aydigan ikki-uch kishi qoldi. Ulardan biri maktabda hech narsa bilan ajralib turmagan, sokin va bir maromdagi xarakterli Simonov edi; lekin men unda xarakterning qandaydir mustaqilligini va hatto halolligini topdim. Uni unchalik ahmoq deb ham o'ylamayman.

paras.en: I had at one time spent some rather soulful moments with him, but these had not lasted long and had somehow been suddenly clouded over. He was evidently uncomfortable at these reminiscences, and was, I fancy, always afraid that I might take up the same tone again. I suspected that he had an aversion for me, but still I went on going to see him, not being quite certain of it.
paras.uz: Bir vaqtlar u bilan ancha samimiy lahzalarni o'tkazgan edim, lekin ular uzoq davom etmagan va qandaydir birdan bulut bosgan edi. Aftidan, u bu xotiralardan noqulay his qilardi va, menimcha, men yana o'sha ohangni boshlab yuborishimdan doim qo'rqardi. Men undan unga nisbatan jirkanishi bor deb shubhalanardim, lekin bunga to'liq ishonchim bo'lmagani uchun uni ziyorat qilishda davom etardim.

paras.en: And so on one occasion, unable to endure my solitude and knowing that as it was Thursday Anton Antonitch's door would be closed, I thought of Simonov. Climbing up to his fourth storey I was thinking that the man disliked me and that it was a mistake to go and see him. But as it always happened that such reflections impelled me, as though purposely, to put myself into a false position, I went in. It was almost a year since I had last seen Simonov.
paras.uz: Shunday qilib, bir safar yolg'izligimga chiday olmay va payshanba bo'lgani uchun Anton Antonovichning eshigi yopiq bo'lishini bilib, Simonovni esladim. Uning to'rtinchi qavatiga ko'tarilayotib, bu odam meni yoqtirmasligini va uni ziyorat qilish xato ekanini o'ylardim. Lekin har doim shunday bo'lardiki, bunday mulohazalar meni go'yo ataylab o'zimni noqulay ahvolga solishga undardi, shuning uchun kirdim. Simonovni oxirgi marta ko'rganimga deyarli bir yil bo'lgan edi.

gloss.ex: But the period of my dissipation would end and I always felt very sick afterwards. It was followed by remorse—I…
…he sublime and the beautiful," in dreams, of course. I was a terrible dreamer, I would dream for three months on end, tucked away in my corner, and you may beli…
…t into the light of day, almost riding a white horse and crowned with laurel.
…go barefoot and hungry preaching new ideas and fighting a victorious Austerlitz against the obscurantists. Then the band would play a march, an amnesty would b…
…ce of a sort, Simonov, who was an old schoolfellow. I had a number of schoolfellows, indeed, in Petersburg, but I did not associate with them and had even given…

quiz.q: What was the narrator's means of escape after dissipation?
o: Dreams of 'the sublime and the beautiful'
quiz.why_uz: U «go'zal va ulug'vor»da, orzularda panoh topardi.

quiz.q: Why did he visit Anton Antonitch?
o: To satisfy his need to embrace humanity
quiz.why_uz: Orzulari cho'qqisida unga hech bo'lmaganda bitta tirik odam kerak edi.

chapters.recap_uz: Buzuqlik davrlaridan keyin hikoyachi oylab orzularga — «go'zal va ulug'vor»ga — sho'ng'iydi: u qahramon, shoir, insoniyat xaloskori bo'ladi. Uch oydan keyin esa odamlarni quchoqlash istagi bilan boshlig'i Anton Antonovichnikiga boradi. Bir kuni yolg'izlikka chiday olmay, maktabdoshi Simonovnikiga yo'l oladi.

chapters.title: Inviting himself

paras.en: I found two of my old schoolfellows with him. They seemed to be discussing an important matter. All of them took scarcely any notice of my entrance, which was strange, for I had not met them for years. Evidently they looked upon me as something on the level of a common fly. I had not been treated like that even at school, though they all hated me. I knew, of course, that they must despise me now for my lack of success in the service, and for my having let myself sink so low, going about badly dressed and so on—which seemed to them a sign of my incapacity and insignificance. But I had not expected such contempt. Simonov was positively surprised at my turning up. Even in old days he had always seemed surprised at my coming. All this disconcerted me: I sat down, feeling rather miserable, and began listening to what they were saying.
paras.uz: Uning oldida ikkita eski maktabdoshimni topdim. Ular qandaydir muhim masalani muhokama qilayotganga o'xshardi. Ularning hech biri mening kirib kelishimga deyarli e'tibor bermadi, bu g'alati edi, chunki men ularni yillardan beri ko'rmagan edim. Aftidan, ular menga oddiy pashsha darajasidagi narsadek qarashardi. Maktabda ham menga bunday munosabatda bo'lishmagan edi, garchi ularning hammasi mendan nafratlanganlar bo'lsa ham. Albatta, men ular endi xizmatdagi muvaffaqiyatsizligim, o'zimni shunchalik pastga tushirib qo'yganim, yomon kiyinib yurganim va hokazolar uchun meni mensimasligi kerakligini bilardim — bu ularga qobiliyatsizligim va arzimasligimning belgisi bo'lib tuyulardi. Lekin men bunday nafratni kutmagan edim. Simonov mening kelganimdan rosa hayron bo'ldi. Hatto eski kunlarda ham u kelganimdan doim hayron bo'lgandek ko'rinardi. Bularning hammasi meni sarosimaga soldi: men ancha ayanchli his qilib o'tirdim va ular nima haqida gaplashayotganini tinglay boshladim.

paras.en: They were engaged in warm and earnest conversation about a farewell dinner which they wanted to arrange for the next day to a comrade of theirs called Zverkov, an officer in the army, who was going away to a distant province. This Zverkov had been all the time at school with me too. I had begun to hate him particularly in the upper forms. In the lower forms he had simply been a pretty, playful boy whom everybody liked. I had hated him, however, even in the lower forms, just because he was a pretty and playful boy. He was always bad at his lessons and got worse and worse as he went on; however, he left with a good certificate, as he had powerful interests. During his last year at school he came in for an estate of two hundred serfs, and as almost all of us were poor he took up a swaggering tone among us.
paras.uz: Ular ertasi kuni uzoq viloyatga ketayotgan o'rtoqlari, armiya zobiti Zverkov uchun uyushtirmoqchi bo'lgan xayrlashuv ziyofati haqida qizg'in va jiddiy suhbat qurishardi. Bu Zverkov ham butun vaqt men bilan birga maktabda o'qigan edi. Men undan ayniqsa yuqori sinflarda nafratlana boshlagan edim. Quyi sinflarda u shunchaki hamma yaxshi ko'radigan chiroyli, o'ynoqi bola edi. Biroq men undan hatto quyi sinflarda ham, aynan u chiroyli va o'ynoqi bola bo'lgani uchun nafratlanardim. U darslarda doim yomon edi va borgan sari yomonlashib bordi; biroq u kuchli homiylari bo'lgani uchun yaxshi attestat bilan bitirdi. Maktabdagi so'nggi yilida unga ikki yuz krepostnoyli mulk meros qoldi va biz deyarli hammamiz kambag'al bo'lganimiz uchun u oramizda kekkaygan ohangni qo'lladi.

paras.en: He was vulgar in the extreme, but at the same time he was a good-natured fellow, even in his swaggering. In spite of superficial, fantastic and sham notions of honour and dignity, all but very few of us positively grovelled before Zverkov, and the more so the more he swaggered. And it was not from any interested motive that they grovelled, but simply because he had been favoured by the gifts of nature. Moreover, it was, as it were, an accepted idea among us that Zverkov was a specialist in regard to tact and the social graces. This last fact particularly infuriated me.
paras.uz: U haddan tashqari tuban edi, lekin ayni paytda hatto kekkayishida ham xushfe'l yigit edi. Sharaf va qadr-qimmat haqidagi yuzaki, xayoliy va soxta tushunchalarga qaramay, juda kam sonlilarimizdan boshqa hammamiz Zverkov oldida rosa emaklardik va u qanchalik ko'p kekkaygan bo'lsa, shunchalik ko'proq. Ular qandaydir g'arazli maqsad bilan emaklashmasdi, shunchaki uni tabiat ne'matlari bilan siylagani uchun. Bundan tashqari, oramizda Zverkov xushmuomalalik va jamiyatda o'zini tutish bo'yicha mutaxassis degan fikr go'yo qabul qilingan edi. Bu oxirgi narsa meni ayniqsa g'azablantirardi.

paras.en: I hated the abrupt self-confident tone of his voice, his admiration of his own witticisms, which were often frightfully stupid, though he was bold in his language; I hated his handsome, but stupid face (for which I would, however, have gladly exchanged my intelligent one), and the free-and-easy military manners in fashion in the "'forties." I hated the way in which he used to talk of his future conquests of women (he did not venture to begin his attack upon women until he had the epaulettes of an officer, and was looking forward to them with impatience), and boasted of the duels he would constantly be fighting.
paras.uz: Men uning ovozining keskin, o'ziga ishongan ohangidan, ko'pincha dahshatli ahmoqona bo'lsa ham o'z o'tkir so'zlariga mahliyo bo'lishidan nafratlanardim, garchi u tilida jasur bo'lsa ham; uning chiroyli, lekin ahmoq yuzidan (biroq men o'zimning aqlli yuzimni unga bajonidil almashtirgan bo'lardim) va «qirqinchi yillar»da urf bo'lgan erkin, bemalol harbiy odatlaridan nafratlanardim. Uning ayollar ustidan kelajakdagi g'alabalari haqida gapirishidan nafratlanardim (u zobit pogonlarini olmaguncha ayollarga hujum boshlashga jur'at etmasdi va ularni sabrsizlik bilan kutardi) va doimo o'tkazadigan duellari bilan maqtanishidan nafratlanardim.

paras.en: I remember how I, invariably so taciturn, suddenly fastened upon Zverkov, when one day talking at a leisure moment with his schoolfellows of his future relations with the fair sex, and growing as sportive as a puppy in the sun, he all at once declared that he would not leave a single village girl on his estate unnoticed, that that was his droit de seigneur, and that if the peasants dared to protest he would have them all flogged and double the tax on them, the bearded rascals. Our servile rabble applauded, but I attacked him, not from compassion for the girls and their fathers, but simply because they were applauding such an insect. I got the better of him on that occasion, but though Zverkov was stupid he was lively and impudent, and so laughed it off, and in such a way that my victory was not really complete; the laugh was on his side.
paras.uz: Esimda, doim sukutga cho'mgan men bir kuni birdan Zverkovga yopishib oldim: u bo'sh bir paytda maktabdoshlari bilan go'zal jins bilan kelajakdagi munosabatlari haqida gaplashib, quyoshdagi kuchukchadek o'ynoqi bo'lib, birdan o'z mulkidagi birorta ham qishloq qizini e'tiborsiz qoldirmasligini, bu uning droit de seigneur — xo'jayinlik huquqi ekanini va agar dehqonlar e'tiroz bildirishga jur'at etsa, ularning hammasini savalatib, soqolli yaramaslarning soliqini ikki baravar oshirishini e'lon qildi. Bizning qul olomonimiz qarsak chaldi, lekin men unga hujum qildim — qizlar va ularning otalariga rahm qilganimdan emas, shunchaki ular bunday hasharotga qarsak chalayotgani uchun. O'sha safar men undan ustun keldim, lekin Zverkov ahmoq bo'lsa ham, jonli va surbet edi, shuning uchun buni kulgiga aylantirib yubordi, shunday tarzdaki, g'alabam haqiqatan to'liq bo'lmadi; kulgi uning tomonida qoldi.

paras.en: He got the better of me on several occasions afterwards, but without malice, jestingly, casually. I remained angrily and contemptuously silent and would not answer him. When we left school he made advances to me; I did not rebuff them, for I was flattered, but we soon parted and quite naturally. Afterwards I heard of his barrack-room success as a lieutenant, and of the fast life he was leading. Then there came other rumours—of his successes in the service. By then he had taken to cutting me in the street, and I suspected that he was afraid of compromising himself by greeting a personage as insignificant as me. I saw him once in the theatre, in the third tier of boxes. By then he was wearing shoulder-straps. He was twisting and twirling about, ingratiating himself with the daughters of an ancient General. In three years he had gone off considerably, though he was still rather handsome and adroit.
paras.uz: Keyinchalik u bir necha marta mendan ustun keldi, lekin g'arazsiz, hazil bilan, yo'l-yo'lakay. Men g'azab va nafrat bilan jim turardim va unga javob bermasdim. Maktabni bitirganimizda u menga yaqinlashishga urindi; men uni rad etmadim, chunki bu meni xushnud qildi, lekin tez orada va mutlaqo tabiiy ravishda ajralishdik. Keyinroq men uning leytenant sifatidagi kazarmadagi muvaffaqiyati va olib borayotgan shov-shuvli hayoti haqida eshitdim. Keyin boshqa mish-mishlar keldi — uning xizmatdagi muvaffaqiyatlari haqida. O'shanda u ko'chada men bilan salomlashmay qo'ygan edi va men u men kabi arzimas shaxs bilan salomlashib, o'zini obro'sizlantirishdan qo'rqadi deb shubhalanardim. Men uni bir marta teatrda, lojalarning uchinchi qatorida ko'rdim. O'shanda u pogon taqib olgan edi. U qandaydir qari generalning qizlariga yaltoqlanib, burilib-buralib turardi. Uch yil ichida u ancha o'zgarib qolgan edi, garchi hali ham ancha chiroyli va epchil bo'lsa ham.

paras.en: One could see that by the time he was thirty he would be corpulent. So it was to this Zverkov that my schoolfellows were going to give a dinner on his departure. They had kept up with him for those three years, though privately they did not consider themselves on an equal footing with him, I am convinced of that.
paras.uz: O'ttiz yoshga kirganda u semirib ketishi ko'rinib turardi. Shunday qilib, maktabdoshlarim aynan shu Zverkovga ketishi munosabati bilan ziyofat bermoqchi edi. Ular o'sha uch yil davomida u bilan aloqani saqlab kelishgan, garchi ichlarida o'zlarini u bilan teng deb hisoblashmasa ham, bunga ishonchim komil.

paras.en: Of Simonov's two visitors, one was Ferfitchkin, a Russianised German—a little fellow with the face of a monkey, a blockhead who was always deriding everyone, a very bitter enemy of mine from our days in the lower forms—a vulgar, impudent, swaggering fellow, who affected a most sensitive feeling of personal honour, though, of course, he was a wretched little coward at heart. He was one of those worshippers of Zverkov who made up to the latter from interested motives, and often borrowed money from him. Simonov's other visitor, Trudolyubov, was a person in no way remarkable—a tall young fellow, in the army, with a cold face, fairly honest, though he worshipped success of every sort, and was only capable of thinking of promotion. He was some sort of distant relation of Zverkov's, and this, foolish as it seems, gave him a certain importance among us. He always thought me of no consequence whatever; his behaviour to me, though not quite courteous, was tolerable.
paras.uz: Simonovning ikki mehmonidan biri Ferfichkin edi — ruslashgan nemis, maymun yuzli kichkina odam, hammani doim masxara qiladigan kalla, quyi sinflardagi kunlarimizdan beri mening juda ashaddiy dushmanim — tuban, surbet, kekkaygan yigit, u shaxsiy sharafga eng nozik munosabatni o'zini ko'rsatardi, garchi, albatta, yuragida ayanchli kichkina qo'rqoq bo'lsa ham. U g'arazli maqsadlar bilan Zverkovga yaqinlashadigan va undan tez-tez qarz oladigan o'sha muxlislaridan biri edi. Simonovning boshqa mehmoni Trudolyubov hech qanday ajoyib bo'lmagan shaxs edi — armiyada xizmat qiladigan, sovuq yuzli, baland bo'yli yigit, ancha halol, garchi har qanday muvaffaqiyatga sig'insa ham va faqat lavozim ko'tarilishi haqida o'ylashga qodir bo'lsa ham. U Zverkovning qandaydir uzoq qarindoshi edi va bu, qanchalik ahmoqona ko'rinmasin, unga oramizda qandaydir ahamiyat berardi. U meni doim mutlaqo ahamiyatsiz deb hisoblardi; uning menga munosabati, unchalik xushmuomala bo'lmasa ham, chidasa bo'ladigan edi.

paras.en: "Well, with seven roubles each," said Trudolyubov, "twenty-one roubles between the three of us, we ought to be able to get a good dinner. Zverkov, of course, won't pay."
paras.uz: «Xo'sh, har biridan yetti rubldan, — dedi Trudolyubov, — uchalamizga yigirma bir rubl, yaxshi ziyofat qila olishimiz kerak. Zverkov, albatta, to'lamaydi.»

paras.en: "Of course not, since we are inviting him," Simonov decided.
paras.uz: «Albatta yo'q, uni biz taklif qilyapmiz-ku», — deb qaror qildi Simonov.

paras.en: "Can you imagine," Ferfitchkin interrupted hotly and conceitedly, like some insolent flunkey boasting of his master the General's decorations, "can you imagine that Zverkov will let us pay alone? He will accept from delicacy, but he will order half a dozen bottles of champagne."
paras.uz: «Nahotki tasavvur qilsangiz, — deb qizg'in va manmanlik bilan gapni bo'ldi Ferfichkin, xo'jayini generalning nishonlari bilan maqtanayotgan qandaydir surbet xizmatkor kabi, — nahotki Zverkov bizga yolg'iz to'lashga yo'l qo'yadi deb tasavvur qilsangiz? U nazokatdan qabul qiladi, lekin yarim dyujina shampan buyuradi.»

paras.en: "Do we want half a dozen for the four of us?" Observed Trudolyubov, taking notice only of the half dozen.
paras.uz: «To'rtalamizga yarim dyujina kerakmi?» — dedi Trudolyubov, faqat yarim dyujinaga e'tibor berib.

paras.en: "So the three of us, with Zverkov for the fourth, twenty-one roubles, at the Hotel de Paris at five o'clock tomorrow," Simonov, who had been asked to make the arrangements, concluded finally.
paras.uz: «Demak, uchalamiz, to'rtinchisi Zverkov, yigirma bir rubl, ertaga soat beshda «Parij» mehmonxonasida», — deb yakuniy xulosa qildi tashkil qilish topshirilgan Simonov.

paras.en: "How twenty-one roubles?" I asked in some agitation, with a show of being offended; "if you count me it will not be twenty-one, but twenty-eight roubles."
paras.uz: «Qanday qilib yigirma bir rubl? — deb so'radim men biroz hayajon bilan, xafa bo'lgandek ko'rinib. — Agar meni ham hisoblasangiz, yigirma bir emas, yigirma sakkiz rubl bo'ladi.»

paras.en: It seemed to me that to invite myself so suddenly and unexpectedly would be positively graceful, and that they would all be conquered at once and would look at me with respect.
paras.uz: Menga shunday birdan va kutilmaganda o'zimni taklif qilish rosa nafis bo'ladigandek va ularning hammasi darhol mag'lub bo'lib, menga hurmat bilan qarashadigandek tuyuldi.

paras.en: "Do you want to join, too?" Simonov observed, with no appearance of pleasure, seeming to avoid looking at me. He knew me through and through.
paras.uz: «Siz ham qo'shilmoqchimisiz?» — dedi Simonov hech qanday xursandchilik ko'rsatmasdan, menga qarashdan qochayotgandek. U meni ichimdan-tashimdan bilardi.

paras.en: It infuriated me that he knew me so thoroughly.
paras.uz: Meni shunchalik yaxshi bilishi g'azablantirdi.

paras.en: "Why not? I am an old schoolfellow of his, too, I believe, and I must own I feel hurt that you have left me out," I said, boiling over again.
paras.uz: «Nega bo'lmasin? Menimcha, men ham uning eski maktabdoshiman va tan olishim kerakki, meni chetda qoldirganingizdan xafa bo'ldim», — dedim men yana qaynab.

paras.en: "And where were we to find you?" Ferfitchkin put in roughly.
paras.uz: «Sizni qayerdan topardik?» — deb qo'pollik bilan gapga aralashdi Ferfichkin.

paras.en: "You never were on good terms with Zverkov," Trudolyubov added, frowning.
paras.uz: «Siz hech qachon Zverkov bilan yaxshi munosabatda bo'lmagansiz», — deb qo'shimcha qildi Trudolyubov qovog'ini solib.

paras.en: But I had already clutched at the idea and would not give it up.
paras.uz: Lekin men bu fikrga allaqachon yopishib olgan edim va undan voz kechmasdim.

paras.en: "It seems to me that no one has a right to form an opinion upon that," I retorted in a shaking voice, as though something tremendous had happened. "Perhaps that is just my reason for wishing it now, that I have not always been on good terms with him."
paras.uz: «Menimcha, bu haqda hech kimning fikr bildirishga haqqi yo'q, — deb e'tiroz bildirdim titroq ovozda, go'yo qandaydir dahshatli narsa yuz bergandek. — Balki hozir buni istashimning sababi aynan men u bilan doim yaxshi munosabatda bo'lmaganimdir.»

paras.en: "Oh, there's no making you out ... With these refinements," Trudolyubov jeered.
paras.uz: «Oh, sizni tushunib bo'lmaydi... bu nozikliklar bilan», — deb masxara qildi Trudolyubov.

paras.en: "We'll put your name down," Simonov decided, addressing me. "Tomorrow at five-o'clock at the Hotel de Paris."
paras.uz: «Sizni yozib qo'yamiz, — deb qaror qildi Simonov menga murojaat qilib. — Ertaga soat beshda «Parij» mehmonxonasida.»

paras.en: "What about the money?" Ferfitchkin began in an undertone, indicating me to Simonov, but he broke off, for even Simonov was embarrassed.
paras.uz: «Pul-chi?» — deb past ovozda boshladi Ferfichkin, Simonovga menga ishora qilib, lekin to'xtab qoldi, chunki hatto Simonov ham xijolat bo'ldi.

paras.en: "That will do," said Trudolyubov, getting up. "If he wants to come so much, let him."
paras.uz: «Bas, — dedi Trudolyubov o'rnidan turib. — Agar u shunchalik kelmoqchi bo'lsa, kelaversin.»

paras.en: "But it's a private thing, between us friends," Ferfitchkin said crossly, as he, too, picked up his hat. "It's not an official gathering."
paras.uz: «Lekin bu shaxsiy narsa, biz do'stlar o'rtasida, — dedi Ferfichkin jahl bilan, u ham shlyapasini olarkan. — Bu rasmiy yig'ilish emas.»

paras.en: "We do not want at all, perhaps ..."
paras.uz: «Balki biz umuman istamasmiz ham...»

paras.en: They went away. Ferfitchkin did not greet me in any way as he went out, Trudolyubov barely nodded. Simonov, with whom I was left tête-à-tête, was in a state of vexation and perplexity, and looked at me queerly. He did not sit down and did not ask me to.
paras.uz: Ular ketishdi. Ferfichkin chiqib ketayotib men bilan hech qanday tarzda xayrlashmadi, Trudolyubov zo'rg'a bosh irg'adi. Men bilan yuzma-yuz qolgan Simonov jahl va sarosimada edi va menga g'alati qarardi. U o'tirmadi va meni ham o'tirishga taklif qilmadi.

paras.en: "H'm ... Yes ... Tomorrow, then. Will you pay your subscription now? I just ask so as to know," he muttered in embarrassment.
paras.uz: «Hm... Ha... Demak, ertaga. Ulushingizni hozir to'laysizmi? Shunchaki bilish uchun so'rayapman», — deb xijolat bilan g'o'ldiradi u.

paras.en: I flushed crimson, as I did so I remembered that I had owed Simonov fifteen roubles for ages—which I had, indeed, never forgotten, though I had not paid it.
paras.uz: Men qip-qizarib ketdim, shu bilan birga Simonovdan anchadan beri o'n besh rubl qarzdor ekanimni esladim — buni, haqiqatan, hech qachon unutmagan edim, garchi to'lamagan bo'lsam ham.

paras.en: "You will understand, Simonov, that I could have no idea when I came here.... I am very much vexed that I have forgotten...."
paras.uz: «Tushunasiz, Simonov, men bu yerga kelganimda bilishim mumkin emas edi... Unutganimdan juda afsusdaman...»

paras.en: "All right, all right, that doesn't matter. You can pay tomorrow after the dinner. I simply wanted to know.... Please don't..."
paras.uz: «Mayli, mayli, bu muhim emas. Ertaga ziyofatdan keyin to'lashingiz mumkin. Men shunchaki bilmoqchi edim... Iltimos, siz...»

paras.en: He broke off and began pacing the room still more vexed. As he walked he began to stamp with his heels.
paras.uz: U gapini uzib, yanada jahldor bo'lib xonada u yoqdan-bu yoqqa yura boshladi. Yurarkan, tovonlari bilan do'pillata boshladi.

paras.en: "Am I keeping you?" I asked, after two minutes of silence.
paras.uz: «Sizni ushlab turmayapmanmi?» — deb so'radim ikki daqiqalik sukutdan keyin.

paras.en: "Oh!" He said, starting, "that is—to be truthful—yes. I have to go and see someone ... Not far from here," he added in an apologetic voice, somewhat abashed.
paras.uz: «Oh! — dedi u cho'chib. — Ya'ni — rostini aytsam — ha. Bir kishini ko'rgani borishim kerak... Bu yerdan uzoq emas», — deb qo'shimcha qildi u uzr so'ragandek ovozda, biroz xijolat bo'lib.

paras.en: "My goodness, why didn't you say so?" I cried, seizing my cap, with an astonishingly free-and-easy air, which was the last thing I should have expected of myself.
paras.uz: «Voy Xudoyim, nega aytmadingiz?» — deb qichqirdim men furajkamni olib, o'zimdan eng kam kutgan hayratlanarli darajada bemalol ko'rinish bilan.

paras.en: "It's close by ... Not two paces away," Simonov repeated, accompanying me to the front door with a fussy air which did not suit him at all. "So five o'clock, punctually, tomorrow," he called down the stairs after me. He was very glad to get rid of me. I was in a fury.
paras.uz: «Bu yaqin... ikki qadam ham emas», — deb takrorladi Simonov, meni old eshikkacha kuzatib, unga mutlaqo yarashmaydigan sarosimali ko'rinish bilan. «Demak, ertaga soat beshda, aniq», — deb zinapoyadan ortimdan qichqirdi u. U mendan qutulganidan juda xursand edi. Men g'azabda edim.

paras.en: "What possessed me, what possessed me to force myself upon them?" I wondered, grinding my teeth as I strode along the street, "for a scoundrel, a pig like that Zverkov! Of course I had better not go; of course, I must just snap my fingers at them. I am not bound in any way. I'll send Simonov a note by tomorrow's post...."
paras.uz: «Menga nima bo'ldi, menga nima bo'ldiki, ularga o'zimni tiqishtirdim? — deb o'yladim tishlarimni g'ijirlatib ko'chada odimlarkanman. — O'sha Zverkovdek yaramas, cho'chqa uchun! Albatta, bormaganim yaxshi; albatta, ularga shunchaki barmog'imni shiqillatishim kerak. Men hech qanday bog'liq emasman. Ertangi pochta bilan Simonovga xat yuboraman...»

paras.en: But what made me furious was that I knew for certain that I should go, that I should make a point of going; and the more tactless, the more unseemly my going would be, the more certainly I would go.
paras.uz: Lekin meni g'azablantirgan narsa shu ediki, men borishimni aniq bilardim, albatta borishimni; va borishim qanchalik nozikliksiz, qanchalik nomaqbul bo'lsa, shunchalik aniq borardim.

paras.en: And there was a positive obstacle to my going: I had no money. All I had was nine roubles, I had to give seven of that to my servant, Apollon, for his monthly wages. That was all I paid him—he had to keep himself.
paras.uz: Borishimga esa aniq to'siq bor edi: pulim yo'q edi. Bor-yo'g'im to'qqiz rubl edi, shundan yettisini xizmatkorim Apollonga oylik maoshi uchun berishim kerak edi. Unga to'laydiganim shu edi — u o'zini o'zi boqishi kerak edi.

paras.en: Not to pay him was impossible, considering his character. But I will talk about that fellow, about that plague of mine, another time.
paras.uz: Uning xarakterini hisobga olsak, unga to'lamaslik imkonsiz edi. Lekin u yigit haqida, o'sha balom haqida boshqa safar gapiraman.

paras.en: However, I knew I should go and should not pay him his wages.
paras.uz: Biroq men borishimni va unga maoshini to'lamasligimni bilardim.

paras.en: That night I had the most hideous dreams. No wonder; all the evening I had been oppressed by memories of my miserable days at school, and I could not shake them off. I was sent to the school by distant relations, upon whom I was dependent and of whom I have heard nothing since—they sent me there a forlorn, silent boy, already crushed by their reproaches, already troubled by doubt, and looking with savage distrust at everyone. My schoolfellows met me with spiteful and merciless jibes because I was not like any of them. But I could not endure their taunts; I could not give in to them with the ignoble readiness with which they gave in to one another. I hated them from the first, and shut myself away from everyone in timid, wounded and disproportionate pride. Their coarseness revolted me. They laughed cynically at my face, at my clumsy figure; and yet what stupid faces they had themselves.
paras.uz: O'sha kechasi men eng xunuk tushlar ko'rdim. Ajablanarli emas; butun oqshom meni maktabdagi ayanchli kunlarim xotiralari ezgan edi va ulardan qutula olmasdim. Meni maktabga men qaram bo'lgan va o'shandan beri hech narsa eshitmagan uzoq qarindoshlarim yuborgan edi — ular meni u yerga yolg'iz, jimgina bola holida, allaqachon ularning ta'nalaridan ezilgan, allaqachon shubhalardan bezovta bo'lgan va hammaga yovvoyi ishonchsizlik bilan qaraydigan holda yuborishgan edi. Maktabdoshlarim meni g'arazli va shafqatsiz masxaralar bilan kutib olishdi, chunki men ularning hech biriga o'xshamasdim. Lekin men ularning tahqirlariga chiday olmasdim; ular bir-biriga yon bergan tuban tayyorlik bilan ularga yon bera olmasdim. Men ulardan boshidanoq nafratlandim va tortinchoq, yaralangan va me'yorsiz g'urur bilan hammadan o'zimni berkitdim. Ularning qo'polligi meni jirkantirardi. Ular yuzim, beso'naqay qaddi-qomatim ustidan kinik kulishardi; holbuki ularning o'z yuzlari qanchalik ahmoqona edi!

paras.en: In our school the boys' faces seemed in a special way to degenerate and grow stupider. How many fine-looking boys came to us! In a few years they became repulsive. Even at sixteen I wondered at them morosely; even then I was struck by the pettiness of their thoughts, the stupidity of their pursuits, their games, their conversations. They had no understanding of such essential things, they took no interest in such striking, impressive subjects, that I could not help considering them inferior to myself. It was not wounded vanity that drove me to it, and for God's sake do not thrust upon me your hackneyed remarks, repeated to nausea, that "I was only a dreamer," while they even then had an understanding of life. They understood nothing, they had no idea of real life, and I swear that that was what made me most indignant with them.
paras.uz: Bizning maktabda bolalarning yuzlari qandaydir alohida tarzda buzilib, ahmoqlashib borardi. Bizga qanchadan-qancha chiroyli bolalar kelgan edi! Bir necha yil ichida ular jirkanch bo'lib qolishardi. Hatto o'n olti yoshimda ham men ularga g'amgin hayron qolardim; o'shandayoq ularning fikrlarining maydaligi, mashg'ulotlari, o'yinlari, suhbatlarining ahmoqligi meni hayratga solardi. Ular shunday muhim narsalarni tushunmasdi, shunday hayratlanarli, ta'sirli mavzular bilan qiziqmasdi-ki, men ularni o'zimdan past deb hisoblamay qola olmasdim. Meni bunga yaralangan shuhratparastlik undamagan edi va Xudo haqqi, menga ko'ngilni aynitguncha takrorlangan «men faqat xayolparast edim», ular esa o'shandayoq hayotni tushunardi, degan siyqasi chiqqan izohlaringizni tiqishtirmang. Ular hech narsani tushunmasdi, haqiqiy hayot haqida hech qanday tasavvurga ega emas edi va qasam ichamanki, meni ularga eng ko'p g'azablantirgan narsa shu edi.

paras.en: On the contrary, the most obvious, striking reality they accepted with fantastic stupidity and even at that time were accustomed to respect success. Everything that was just, but oppressed and looked down upon, they laughed at heartlessly and shamefully. They took rank for intelligence; even at sixteen they were already talking about a snug berth. Of course, a great deal of it was due to their stupidity, to the bad examples with which they had always been surrounded in their childhood and boyhood. They were monstrously depraved. Of course a great deal of that, too, was superficial and an assumption of cynicism; of course there were glimpses of youth and freshness even in their depravity; but even that freshness was not attractive, and showed itself in a certain rakishness. I hated them horribly, though perhaps I was worse than any of them. They repaid me in the same way, and did not conceal their aversion for me.
paras.uz: Aksincha, eng aniq, hayratlanarli haqiqatni ular xayoliy ahmoqlik bilan qabul qilishardi va o'shandayoq muvaffaqiyatni hurmat qilishga odatlangan edi. Adolatli, lekin ezilgan va kamsitilgan hamma narsa ustidan ular shafqatsiz va sharmandalarcha kulishardi. Ular martabani aql deb qabul qilishardi; hatto o'n olti yoshida ular allaqachon issiq joy haqida gaplashardi. Albatta, buning ko'p qismi ularning ahmoqligi, bolalik va o'smirlikda doimo qurshab olgan yomon namunalar tufayli edi. Ular dahshatli darajada buzilgan edi. Albatta, buning ham ko'p qismi yuzaki va kinizmni o'zini ko'rsatish edi; albatta, hatto ularning buzuqligida ham yoshlik va yangilik uchqunlari bor edi; lekin hatto bu yangilik ham jozibali emas edi va qandaydir shallaqilikda namoyon bo'lardi. Men ulardan dahshatli nafratlanardim, garchi, balki, ularning har biridan yomonroq bo'lsam ham. Ular menga xuddi shunday javob qaytarishardi va mendan jirkanishlarini yashirishmasdi.

paras.en: But by then I did not desire their affection: on the contrary, I continually longed for their humiliation. To escape from their derision I purposely began to make all the progress I could with my studies and forced my way to the very top. This impressed them. Moreover, they all began by degrees to grasp that I had already read books none of them could read, and understood things (not forming part of our school curriculum) of which they had not even heard. They took a savage and sarcastic view of it, but were morally impressed, especially as the teachers began to notice me on those grounds. The mockery ceased, but the hostility remained, and cold and strained relations became permanent between us. In the end I could not put up with it: with years a craving for society, for friends, developed in me.
paras.uz: Lekin o'shanda men ularning mehrini istamasdim: aksincha, doimo ularning xo'rlanishini orzu qilardim. Ularning masxarasidan qutulish uchun ataylab o'qishda iloji boricha ko'p muvaffaqiyatga erisha boshladim va eng yuqoriga yorib chiqdim. Bu ularga ta'sir qildi. Bundan tashqari, ularning hammasi asta-sekin men ularning hech biri o'qiy olmaydigan kitoblarni allaqachon o'qiganimni va ular hatto eshitmagan narsalarni (maktab dasturimizga kirmaydigan) tushunishimni anglay boshladi. Ular bunga yovvoyi va kinoyali qarashdi, lekin ma'naviy ta'sirlandilar, ayniqsa o'qituvchilar shu sababli menga e'tibor bera boshlaganidan keyin. Masxara to'xtadi, lekin dushmanlik qoldi va oramizda sovuq va tarang munosabatlar doimiy bo'lib qoldi. Oxiri men bunga chiday olmadim: yillar o'tib menda jamiyatga, do'stlarga tashnalik paydo bo'ldi.

paras.en: I attempted to get on friendly terms with some of my schoolfellows; but somehow or other my intimacy with them was always strained and soon ended of itself. Once, indeed, I did have a friend. But I was already a tyrant at heart; I wanted to exercise unbounded sway over him; I tried to instil into him a contempt for his surroundings; I required of him a disdainful and complete break with those surroundings. I frightened him with my passionate affection; I reduced him to tears, to hysterics. He was a simple and devoted soul; but when he devoted himself to me entirely I began to hate him immediately and repulsed him—as though all I needed him for was to win a victory over him, to subjugate him and nothing else. But I could not subjugate all of them; my friend was not at all like them either, he was, in fact, a rare exception.
paras.uz: Men ba'zi maktabdoshlarim bilan do'stona munosabat o'rnatishga urindim; lekin qandaydir tarzda ular bilan yaqinligim doim tarang edi va tez orada o'z-o'zidan tugardi. Bir marta, haqiqatan, mening do'stim bo'lgan. Lekin men allaqachon yuragimda zolim edim; men u ustidan cheksiz hukmronlik qilmoqchi edim; unga atrofiga nafrat singdirishga urindim; undan bu atrof bilan nafrat bilan butunlay aloqani uzishni talab qildim. Men uni ehtirosli mehrim bilan qo'rqitdim; uni ko'z yoshiga, isteriyaga yetkazdim. U sodda va sadoqatli qalb edi; lekin u o'zini menga butunlay bag'ishlaganda, men darhol undan nafratlana boshladim va uni itarib yubordim — go'yo u menga faqat ustidan g'alaba qozonish, uni bo'ysundirish uchun kerak bo'lgandek, boshqa hech narsa uchun emas. Lekin men ularning hammasini bo'ysundira olmasdim; do'stim ham ularga umuman o'xshamasdi, u, haqiqatan, kamdan-kam istisno edi.

paras.en: The first thing I did on leaving school was to give up the special job for which I had been destined so as to break all ties, to curse my past and shake the dust from off my feet.... And goodness knows why, after all that, I should go trudging off to Simonov's!
paras.uz: Maktabni tugatgach birinchi qilgan ishim — barcha aloqalarni uzish, o'tmishimni la'natlash va oyoqlarimdagi changni qoqish uchun meni tayyorlashgan maxsus ishdan voz kechish bo'ldi... Va Xudo biladi, bularning hammasidan keyin nega Simonovnikiga sudralib borishim kerak edi!

paras.en: Early next morning I roused myself and jumped out of bed with excitement, as though it were all about to happen at once. But I believed that some radical change in my life was coming, and would inevitably come that day. Owing to its rarity, perhaps, any external event, however trivial, always made me feel as though some radical change in my life were at hand. I went to the office, however, as usual, but sneaked away home two hours earlier to get ready. The great thing, I thought, is not to be the first to arrive, or they will think I am overjoyed at coming. But there were thousands of such great points to consider, and they all agitated and overwhelmed me. I polished my boots a second time with my own hands; nothing in the world would have induced Apollon to clean them twice a day, as he considered that it was more than his duties required of him.
paras.uz: Ertasi kuni erta tongda men hayajon bilan o'zimni uyg'otib, go'yo hammasi hozir sodir bo'ladigandek karavotdan sakrab turdim. Lekin men hayotimda qandaydir tub o'zgarish kelayotganiga va o'sha kuni muqarrar ravishda kelishiga ishonardim. Kamdan-kamligi tufayli, balki, har qanday tashqi voqea, qanchalik arzimas bo'lmasin, menga doim hayotimda qandaydir tub o'zgarish yaqin kelgandek his qildirardi. Biroq men odatdagidek idoraga bordim, lekin tayyorlanish uchun ikki soat oldin uyga sirg'alib ketdim. Asosiysi, deb o'yladim, birinchi bo'lib kelmaslik, aks holda ular kelganimdan haddan tashqari xursandman deb o'ylashadi. Lekin bunday asosiy jihatlardan minglab bor edi va ularning hammasi meni hayajonga solib, bosib ketardi. Men etiklarimni o'z qo'lim bilan ikkinchi marta tozaladim; dunyodagi hech narsa Apollonni ularni kuniga ikki marta tozalashga majbur qila olmasdi, chunki u buni vazifasidan ortiq deb hisoblardi.

paras.en: I stole the brushes to clean them from the passage, being careful he should not detect it, for fear of his contempt. Then I minutely examined my clothes and thought that everything looked old, worn and threadbare. I had let myself get too slovenly. My uniform, perhaps, was tidy, but I could not go out to dinner in my uniform. The worst of it was that on the knee of my trousers was a big yellow stain. I had a foreboding that that stain would deprive me of nine-tenths of my personal dignity. I knew, too, that it was very poor to think so. "But this is no time for thinking: now I am in for the real thing," I thought, and my heart sank. I knew, too, perfectly well even then, that I was monstrously exaggerating the facts. But how could I help it? I could not control myself and was already shaking with fever.
paras.uz: Ularni tozalash uchun cho'tkalarni yo'lakdan, u payqab qolmasligi uchun ehtiyot bo'lib o'g'irladim, uning nafratidan qo'rqib. Keyin kiyimlarimni sinchiklab ko'zdan kechirdim va hamma narsa eski, titilgan va yupqalashgan ko'rinyapti deb o'yladim. O'zimni haddan tashqari qarovsiz qilib qo'ygan edim. Formam, balki, ozoda edi, lekin forma bilan ziyofatga borolmasdim. Eng yomoni, shimimning tizzasida katta sariq dog' bor edi. Men bu dog' shaxsiy qadr-qimmatimning o'ndan to'qqiz qismidan mahrum qilishini oldindan sezardim. Shuningdek, bunday o'ylash juda arzimas ekanini ham bilardim. «Lekin hozir o'ylash vaqti emas: endi haqiqiy narsaga duch kelyapman», — deb o'yladim va yuragim so'nib ketdi. Men o'shandayoq faktlarni dahshatli darajada bo'rttirayotganimni mutlaqo yaxshi bilardim. Lekin nima qila olardim? O'zimni boshqara olmasdim va allaqachon isitmadan titrardim.

paras.en: With despair I pictured to myself how coldly and disdainfully that "scoundrel" Zverkov would meet me; with what dull-witted, invincible contempt the blockhead Trudolyubov would look at me; with what impudent rudeness the insect Ferfitchkin would snigger at me in order to curry favour with Zverkov; how completely Simonov would take it all in, and how he would despise me for the abjectness of my vanity and lack of spirit—and, worst of all, how paltry, unliterary, commonplace it would all be. Of course, the best thing would be not to go at all. But that was most impossible of all: if I feel impelled to do anything, I seem to be pitchforked into it. I should have jeered at myself ever afterwards: "So you funked it, you funked it, you funked the real thing!" On the contrary, I passionately longed to show all that "rabble" that I was by no means such a spiritless creature as I seemed to myself.
paras.uz: Umidsizlik bilan o'sha «yaramas» Zverkov meni qanchalik sovuq va mensimay kutib olishini; kalla Trudolyubov menga qanday o'tmas, yengilmas nafrat bilan qarashini; hasharot Ferfichkin Zverkovga yaltoqlanish uchun menga qanday surbet qo'pollik bilan pixillab kulishini; Simonov hammasini qanchalik to'liq tushunib olishini va shuhratparastligimning tubanligi va ruhsizligim uchun meni qanchalik mensimasligini — va eng yomoni, bularning hammasi qanchalik arzimas, adabiyotsiz, oddiy bo'lishini tasavvur qildim. Albatta, eng yaxshisi umuman bormaslik bo'lardi. Lekin bu hammasidan imkonsizroq edi: agar biror narsa qilishga turtki his qilsam, go'yo meni unga panshaxa bilan uloqtirishadi. Keyin butun umr o'zimni masxara qilgan bo'lardim: «Qo'rqding-ku, qo'rqding, haqiqiy narsadan qo'rqding!» Aksincha, men o'sha butun «olomon»ga o'zimga ko'ringanimdek ruhsiz mavjudot emasligimni ko'rsatishni ehtiros bilan orzu qilardim.

paras.en: What is more, even in the acutest paroxysm of this cowardly fever, I dreamed of getting the upper hand, of dominating them, carrying them away, making them like me—if only for my "elevation of thought and unmistakable wit." They would abandon Zverkov, he would sit on one side, silent and ashamed, while I should crush him. Then, perhaps, we would be reconciled and drink to our everlasting friendship; but what was most bitter and humiliating for me was that I knew even then, knew fully and for certain, that I needed nothing of all this really, that I did not really want to crush, to subdue, to attract them, and that I did not care a straw really for the result, even if I did achieve it. Oh, how I prayed for the day to pass quickly! In unutterable anguish I went to the window, opened the movable pane and looked out into the troubled darkness of the thickly falling wet snow.
paras.uz: Bundan ham ortig'i, hatto bu qo'rqoq isitmaning eng o'tkir xurujida ham men ustun kelishni, ularga hukmronlik qilishni, ularni o'zimga jalb qilishni, meni yoqtirishga majbur qilishni — hech bo'lmaganda «fikrimning yuksakligi va shubhasiz o'tkirligim» uchun — orzu qilardim. Ular Zverkovni tashlab ketishardi, u bir chetda jim va uyalib o'tirardi, men esa uni ezardim. Keyin, balki, yarashib, abadiy do'stligimiz uchun ichardik; lekin men uchun eng achchiq va xo'rlovchisi shu ediki, men o'shandayoq bilardim, to'liq va aniq bilardimki, menga bularning hech biri haqiqatan kerak emas edi, men ularni haqiqatan ezishni, bo'ysundirishni, o'zimga jalb qilishni istamasdim va erishsam ham, natija menga haqiqatan bir pul edi. Oh, kun tezroq o'tishi uchun qanday duo qilardim! Ta'riflab bo'lmas iztirob ichida derazaga bordim, fortochkani ochib, quyuq yog'ayotgan ho'l qorning bezovta zulmatiga qaradim.

paras.en: At last my wretched little clock hissed out five. I seized my hat and, trying not to look at Apollon, who had been all day expecting his month's wages, but in his foolishness was unwilling to be the first to speak about it, I slipped between him and the door and, jumping into a high-class sledge, on which I spent my last half rouble, I drove up in grand style to the Hotel de Paris.
paras.uz: Nihoyat ayanchli kichkina soatim vishillab beshni urdi. Shlyapamni olib, butun kun oylik maoshini kutgan, lekin ahmoqligidan bu haqda birinchi bo'lib gapirishni istamagan Apollonga qaramaslikka urinib, u bilan eshik orasidan sirg'alib chiqdim va oxirgi yarim rublimni sarflagan yuqori toifali chanaga sakrab minib, «Parij» mehmonxonasiga hashamat bilan yetib bordim.

"H'm ... Yes ... Tomorrow, then. Will you pay your subscription now? I just ask so as to know," he muttered in embarrassment.
