quiz.why_uz: Uzoq viloyatga ketayotgan zobit Zverkov uchun.

quiz.q: What worried him most about his clothes?
o: A big yellow stain on the knee of his trousers
quiz.why_uz: Shim tizzasidagi katta sariq dog'.

chapters.recap_uz: Simonovnikida maktabdoshlar Zverkov uchun xayrlashuv ziyofati rejalashtirishyapti. Hikoyachi Zverkovdan nafratlansa ham, o'zini ziyofatga tiqishtiradi. Kechasi og'ir maktab yillarini, yagona do'stiga ham zulm qilganini eslaydi va ertasi kuni isitmali hayajon bilan tayyorlanadi.

chapters.title: The dinner at the Hotel de Paris

paras.en: I had been certain the day before that I should be the first to arrive. But it was not a question of being the first to arrive. Not only were they not there, but I had difficulty in finding our room. The table was not laid even. What did it mean? After a good many questions I elicited from the waiters that the dinner had been ordered not for five, but for six o'clock. This was confirmed at the buffet too. I felt really ashamed to go on questioning them. It was only twenty-five minutes past five. If they changed the dinner hour they ought at least to have let me know—that is what the post is for, and not to have put me in an absurd position in my own eyes and ... And even before the waiters. I sat down; the servant began laying the table; I felt even more humiliated when he was present.
paras.uz: Kecha men birinchi bo'lib kelishimga ishonchim komil edi. Lekin gap birinchi bo'lib kelishda emas edi. Ular nafaqat u yerda yo'q edi, balki men xonamizni ham zo'rg'a topdim. Stol hatto bezatilmagan ham edi. Bu nimani anglatardi? Ko'p savollardan keyin ofitsiantlardan ziyofat soat beshga emas, oltiga buyurilganini bilib oldim. Bufetda ham buni tasdiqlashdi. Ularni so'roq qilishda davom etishdan rosa uyaldim. Soat endigina beshdan yigirma besh daqiqa o'tgan edi. Agar ziyofat vaqtini o'zgartirishgan bo'lsa, hech bo'lmaganda menga xabar berishlari kerak edi — pochta shuning uchun bor, meni o'z ko'zimda va... hatto ofitsiantlar oldida ham bema'ni ahvolga solmasliklari kerak edi. Men o'tirdim; xizmatkor stolni bezata boshladi; u yonimda bo'lganida o'zimni yanada xo'rlangan his qildim.

paras.en: Towards six o'clock they brought in candles, though there were lamps burning in the room. It had not occurred to the waiter, however, to bring them in at once when I arrived. In the next room two gloomy, angry-looking persons were eating their dinners in silence at two different tables. There was a great deal of noise, even shouting, in a room further away; one could hear the laughter of a crowd of people, and nasty little shrieks in French: there were ladies at the dinner. It was sickening, in fact. I rarely passed more unpleasant moments, so much so that when they did arrive all together punctually at six I was overjoyed to see them, as though they were my deliverers, and even forgot that it was incumbent upon me to show resentment.
paras.uz: Soat oltiga yaqin xonada lampalar yonib turgan bo'lsa ham, shamlar olib kelishdi. Biroq men kelganimda ofitsiantning xayoliga ularni darhol olib kelish kelmagan edi. Qo'shni xonada ikkita g'amgin, jahldor ko'rinishli odam ikki xil stolda jimgina ovqatlanishardi. Uzoqroqdagi xonada juda shovqin, hatto qichqiriq bor edi; olomonning kulgisi va fransuzcha jirkanch kichik chinqiriqlar eshitilardi: ziyofatda xonimlar bor edi. Xullas, ko'ngilni aynitardi. Men kamdan-kam bunday yoqimsiz daqiqalarni o'tkazganman, shu darajadaki, ular soat oltida aniq hammasi birga kelganida, go'yo ular mening xaloskorlarim bo'lgandek, ularni ko'rib nihoyatda xursand bo'ldim va hatto g'azab ko'rsatishim kerakligini ham unutdim.

paras.en: Zverkov walked in at the head of them; evidently he was the leading spirit. He and all of them were laughing; but, seeing me, Zverkov drew himself up a little, walked up to me deliberately with a slight, rather jaunty bend from the waist. He shook hands with me in a friendly, but not over-friendly, fashion, with a sort of circumspect courtesy like that of a General, as though in giving me his hand he were warding off something. I had imagined, on the contrary, that on coming in he would at once break into his habitual thin, shrill laugh and fall to making his insipid jokes and witticisms. I had been preparing for them ever since the previous day, but I had not expected such condescension, such high-official courtesy. So, then, he felt himself ineffably superior to me in every respect! If he only meant to insult me by that high-official tone, it would not matter, I thought—I could pay him back for it one way or another.
paras.uz: Ularning boshida Zverkov kirdi; aftidan u asosiy shaxs edi. U ham, hammasi ham kulishardi; lekin meni ko'rib, Zverkov biroz qaddini rostladi, belidan biroz, ancha o'ynoqi egilib, menga qasddan yaqinlashdi. U men bilan do'stona, lekin haddan tashqari do'stona emas, qandaydir general kabi ehtiyotkor xushmuomalalik bilan qo'l berib ko'rishdi, go'yo menga qo'l berib, nimanidir o'zidan qaytarayotgandek. Men, aksincha, u kirishi bilanoq odatdagi ingichka, chinqiroq kulgisiga tushib, bemaza hazillari va o'tkir so'zlarini boshlaydi deb tasavvur qilgan edim. Men kechadan beri ularga tayyorlanib kelgan edim, lekin bunday kamtarona iltifotni, bunday yuqori amaldorona xushmuomalalikni kutmagan edim. Demak, u o'zini har jihatdan mendan ta'riflab bo'lmas darajada ustun his qilardi! Agar u bu yuqori amaldorona ohang bilan meni faqat haqorat qilmoqchi bo'lsa, muhim emas, deb o'yladim — men unga bir yo'l bilan qaytara olardim.

paras.en: But what if, in reality, without the least desire to be offensive, that sheepshead had a notion in earnest that he was superior to me and could only look at me in a patronising way? The very supposition made me gasp.
paras.uz: Lekin agar, aslida, haqorat qilishni zarracha istamasdan, o'sha qo'y kalla chindan ham o'zini mendan ustun deb o'ylasa va menga faqat homiylik qilgandek qaray olsa-chi? Bu farazning o'zi nafasimni bo'g'di.

paras.en: "I was surprised to hear of your desire to join us," he began, lisping and drawling, which was something new. "You and I seem to have seen nothing of one another. You fight shy of us. You shouldn't. We are not such terrible people as you think. Well, anyway, I am glad to renew our acquaintance."
paras.uz: «Bizga qo'shilish istagingizni eshitib hayron qoldim, — deb boshladi u, shivillab va cho'zib gapirib, bu yangilik edi. — Siz bilan bir-birimizni deyarli ko'rmaganga o'xshaymiz. Siz bizdan qochasiz. Bunday qilmasligingiz kerak. Biz siz o'ylaganchalik dahshatli odamlar emasmiz. Xo'sh, har holda, tanishligimizni yangilaganimdan xursandman.»

paras.en: And he turned carelessly to put down his hat on the window.
paras.uz: Va u shlyapasini derazaga qo'yish uchun beparvo o'girildi.

paras.en: "Have you been waiting long?" Trudolyubov inquired.
paras.uz: «Uzoq kutdingizmi?» — deb so'radi Trudolyubov.

paras.en: "I arrived at five o'clock as you told me yesterday," I answered aloud, with an irritability that threatened an explosion.
paras.uz: «Kecha aytganingizdek soat beshda keldim», — deb baland ovozda, portlash bilan tahdid qiluvchi jahldorlik bilan javob berdim.

paras.en: "Didn't you let him know that we had changed the hour?" Said Trudolyubov to Simonov.
paras.uz: «Vaqtni o'zgartirganimizni unga xabar qilmadingmi?» — dedi Trudolyubov Simonovga.

paras.en: "No, I didn't. I forgot," the latter replied, with no sign of regret, and without even apologising to me he went off to order the hors d'oeuvre.
paras.uz: «Yo'q, qilmadim. Unutibman», — deb javob berdi u hech qanday afsus belgisisiz va hatto mendan uzr so'ramasdan zakuskalar buyurish uchun chiqib ketdi.

paras.en: "So you've been here a whole hour? Oh, poor fellow!" Zverkov cried ironically, for to his notions this was bound to be extremely funny. That rascal Ferfitchkin followed with his nasty little snigger like a puppy yapping. My position struck him, too, as exquisitely ludicrous and embarrassing.
paras.uz: «Demak, bu yerda butun bir soat o'tirdingizmi? Oh, bechora!» — deb kinoya bilan qichqirdi Zverkov, chunki uning tushunchasiga ko'ra bu albatta nihoyatda kulgili bo'lishi kerak edi. O'sha yaramas Ferfichkin vovullayotgan kuchukchadek jirkanch kichik pixillashi bilan unga ergashdi. Mening ahvolim unga ham nihoyatda kulgili va noqulay tuyuldi.

paras.en: "It isn't funny at all!" I cried to Ferfitchkin, more and more irritated. "It wasn't my fault, but other people's. They neglected to let me know. It was ... It was ... It was simply absurd."
paras.uz: «Bu umuman kulgili emas! — deb qichqirdim Ferfichkinga, tobora jahlim chiqib. — Bu mening aybim emas, boshqalarniki. Menga xabar berishga e'tibor qilishmadi. Bu... bu... bu shunchaki bema'nilik edi.»

paras.en: "It's not only absurd, but something else as well," muttered Trudolyubov, naively taking my part. "You are not hard enough upon it. It was simply rudeness—unintentional, of course. And how could Simonov ... H'm!"
paras.uz: «Bu nafaqat bema'nilik, balki yana boshqa narsa ham, — deb g'o'ldiradi Trudolyubov, sodda tarzda mening tomonimni olib. — Siz unga haddan tashqari yumshoq qarayapsiz. Bu shunchaki qo'pollik edi — albatta, beixtiyor. Simonov qanday qilib... Hm!»

paras.en: "If a trick like that had been played on me," observed Ferfitchkin, "I should ..."
paras.uz: «Agar menga shunday hiyla qilishganida, — dedi Ferfichkin, — men...»

paras.en: "But you should have ordered something for yourself," Zverkov interrupted, "or simply asked for dinner without waiting for us."
paras.uz: «Lekin siz o'zingizga biror narsa buyurishingiz kerak edi, — deb gapni bo'ldi Zverkov, — yoki bizni kutmasdan shunchaki ovqat so'rashingiz kerak edi.»

paras.en: "You will allow that I might have done that without your permission," I rapped out. "If I waited, it was ..."
paras.uz: «Buni sizning ruxsatingizsiz ham qila olishimni tan olasiz, — deb keskin aytdim. — Agar kutgan bo'lsam, bu...»

paras.en: "Let us sit down, gentlemen," cried Simonov, coming in. "Everything is ready; I can answer for the champagne; it is capitally frozen.... You see, I did not know your address, where was I to look for you?" He suddenly turned to me, but again he seemed to avoid looking at me. Evidently he had something against me. It must have been what happened yesterday.
paras.uz: «O'tiraylik, janoblar, — deb qichqirdi Simonov kirib. — Hammasi tayyor; shampan uchun kafolat beraman; a'lo darajada muzlatilgan... Ko'ryapsizmi, men sizning manzilingizni bilmasdim, sizni qayerdan izlardim?» — U birdan menga o'girildi, lekin yana menga qarashdan qochayotganga o'xshardi. Aftidan, menga qarshi nimadir bor edi. Bu kecha bo'lgan voqea bo'lsa kerak.

paras.en: All sat down; I did the same. It was a round table. Trudolyubov was on my left, Simonov on my right, Zverkov was sitting opposite, Ferfitchkin next to him, between him and Trudolyubov.
paras.uz: Hamma o'tirdi; men ham o'tirdim. Stol dumaloq edi. Trudolyubov chap tomonimda, Simonov o'ng tomonimda, Zverkov ro'parada, Ferfichkin uning yonida, u bilan Trudolyubov o'rtasida o'tirardi.

paras.en: "Tell me, are you ... In a government office?" Zverkov went on attending to me. Seeing that I was embarrassed he seriously thought that he ought to be friendly to me, and, so to speak, cheer me up.
paras.uz: «Ayting-chi, siz... davlat idorasidamisiz?» — deb Zverkov menga e'tibor berishda davom etdi. Mening xijolat bo'lganimni ko'rib, u jiddiy ravishda menga do'stona munosabatda bo'lishi va, ta'bir joiz bo'lsa, ko'nglimni ko'tarishi kerak deb o'ylardi.

paras.en: "Does he want me to throw a bottle at his head?" I thought, in a fury. In my novel surroundings I was unnaturally ready to be irritated.
paras.uz: «Nahotki u boshiga shisha otishimni istasa?» — deb g'azab bilan o'yladim. Yangi muhitimda men g'ayritabiiy darajada jahl chiqarishga tayyor edim.

paras.en: "In the N—— office," I answered jerkily, with my eyes on my plate.
paras.uz: «N—— idorasida», — deb uzuq-yuluq javob berdim, ko'zlarim likopchamda.

paras.en: "And ha-ave you a go-od berth? I say, what ma-a-de you leave your original job?"
paras.uz: «Va sizda ya-a-xshi joy bormi? Aytgancha, avvalgi ishingizni tashlashga nima ma-a-jbur qildi?»

paras.en: "What ma-a-de me was that I wanted to leave my original job," I drawled more than he, hardly able to control myself. Ferfitchkin went off into a guffaw. Simonov looked at me ironically. Trudolyubov left off eating and began looking at me with curiosity.
paras.uz: «Avvalgi ishimni tashlashni istaganim ma-a-jbur qildi», — deb men undan ham ko'proq cho'zib gapirdim, o'zimni zo'rg'a tutib. Ferfichkin xaxolab kulib yubordi. Simonov menga kinoya bilan qaradi. Trudolyubov ovqatlanishni to'xtatib, menga qiziqish bilan qaray boshladi.

paras.en: Zverkov winced, but he tried not to notice it.
paras.uz: Zverkov burishdi, lekin buni payqamaslikka harakat qildi.

paras.en: "And the remuneration?"
paras.uz: «Mukofot-chi?»

paras.en: "What remuneration?"
paras.uz: «Qanday mukofot?»

paras.en: "I mean, your sa-a-lary?"
paras.uz: «Ya'ni, ma-a-oshingiz?»

paras.en: "Why are you cross-examining me?" However, I told him at once what my salary was. I turned horribly red.
paras.uz: «Nega meni so'roq qilyapsiz?» Biroq men unga darhol maoshim qancha ekanini aytdim. Dahshatli qizarib ketdim.

paras.en: "It is not very handsome," Zverkov observed majestically.
paras.uz: «Unchalik ko'p emas», — dedi Zverkov salobat bilan.

paras.en: "Yes, you can't afford to dine at cafes on that," Ferfitchkin added insolently.
paras.uz: «Ha, bunga kafelarda ovqatlana olmaysiz», — deb surbetlarcha qo'shimcha qildi Ferfichkin.

paras.en: "To my thinking it's very poor," Trudolyubov observed gravely.
paras.uz: «Menimcha, bu juda kam», — dedi Trudolyubov jiddiy.

paras.en: "And how thin you have grown! How you have changed!" Added Zverkov, with a shade of venom in his voice, scanning me and my attire with a sort of insolent compassion.
paras.uz: «Qanchalik ozib ketibsiz! Qanchalik o'zgaribsiz!» — deb qo'shimcha qildi Zverkov ovozida zahar soyasi bilan, meni va kiyimimni qandaydir surbet achinish bilan ko'zdan kechirib.

paras.en: "Oh, spare his blushes," cried Ferfitchkin, sniggering.
paras.uz: «Oh, uni uyaltirmang», — deb pixillab qichqirdi Ferfichkin.

paras.en: "My dear sir, allow me to tell you I am not blushing," I broke out at last; "do you hear? I am dining here, at this cafe, at my own expense, not at other people's—note that, Mr. Ferfitchkin."
paras.uz: «Aziz janobim, sizga aytishga ruxsat eting, men qizarmayapman, — deb nihoyat portladim. — Eshityapsizmi? Men bu yerda, bu kafeda o'z hisobimdan ovqatlanyapman, boshqalarning hisobidan emas — buni qayd eting, janob Ferfichkin.»

paras.en: "Wha-at? Isn't every one here dining at his own expense? You would seem to be ..." Ferfitchkin flew out at me, turning as red as a lobster, and looking me in the face with fury.
paras.uz: «Nima-a? Bu yerda har kim o'z hisobidan ovqatlanmayaptimi? Siz go'yo...» — deb Ferfichkin menga tashlandi, qisqichbaqadek qizarib, menga g'azab bilan yuzimga qarab.

paras.en: "Tha-at," I answered, feeling I had gone too far, "and I imagine it would be better to talk of something more intelligent."
paras.uz: «Shu-u, — deb javob berdim, haddan oshib ketganimni his qilib, — va menimcha, aqlliroq narsa haqida gaplashgan yaxshiroq bo'lardi.»

paras.en: "You intend to show off your intelligence, I suppose?"
paras.uz: «Aqlingizni ko'rsatmoqchisiz, shekilli?»

paras.en: "Don't disturb yourself, that would be quite out of place here."
paras.uz: «Tashvishlanmang, bu bu yerda mutlaqo o'rinsiz bo'lardi.»

paras.en: "Why are you clacking away like that, my good sir, eh? Have you gone out of your wits in your office?"
paras.uz: «Nega bunday shaqillayapsiz, aziz janobim, a? Idorangizda aqldan ozdingizmi?»

paras.en: "Enough, gentlemen, enough!" Zverkov cried, authoritatively.
paras.uz: «Bas, janoblar, bas!» — deb buyruq ohangida qichqirdi Zverkov.

paras.en: "How stupid it is!" Muttered Simonov.
paras.uz: «Qanday ahmoqona!» — deb g'o'ldiradi Simonov.

paras.en: "It really is stupid. We have met here, a company of friends, for a farewell dinner to a comrade and you carry on an altercation," said Trudolyubov, rudely addressing himself to me alone. "You invited yourself to join us, so don't disturb the general harmony."
paras.uz: «Haqiqatan ahmoqona. Biz bu yerda do'stlar davrasi bo'lib, o'rtog'imiz bilan xayrlashuv ziyofatiga yig'ildik, siz esa janjal ko'taryapsiz, — dedi Trudolyubov, qo'pollik bilan faqat menga murojaat qilib. — Siz o'zingizni bizga qo'shilishga taklif qildingiz, shuning uchun umumiy ahillikni buzmang.»

paras.en: "Enough, enough!" Cried Zverkov. "Give over, gentlemen, it's out of place. Better let me tell you how I nearly got married the day before yesterday...."
paras.uz: «Bas, bas! — deb qichqirdi Zverkov. — To'xtating, janoblar, bu o'rinsiz. Yaxshisi, sizga o'tgan kuni qanday qilib deyarli uylanib qolganimni aytib beray...»

paras.en: And then followed a burlesque narrative of how this gentleman had almost been married two days before. There was not a word about the marriage, however, but the story was adorned with generals, colonels and kammer-junkers, while Zverkov almost took the lead among them. It was greeted with approving laughter; Ferfitchkin positively squealed.
paras.uz: Keyin bu janob ikki kun oldin qanday qilib deyarli uylanib qolgani haqida burlesk hikoya boshlandi. Biroq nikoh haqida birorta so'z yo'q edi, lekin hikoya generallar, polkovniklar va kamer-yunkerlar bilan bezatilgan edi, Zverkov esa ular orasida deyarli yetakchi edi. U ma'qullovchi kulgi bilan kutib olindi; Ferfichkin rosa chiyilladi.

paras.en: No one paid any attention to me, and I sat crushed and humiliated.
paras.uz: Hech kim menga e'tibor bermadi va men ezilgan va xo'rlangan holda o'tirardim.

paras.en: "Good Heavens, these are not the people for me!" I thought. "And what a fool I have made of myself before them! I let Ferfitchkin go too far, though. The brutes imagine they are doing me an honour in letting me sit down with them. They don't understand that it's an honour to them and not to me! I've grown thinner! My clothes! Oh, damn my trousers! Zverkov noticed the yellow stain on the knee as soon as he came in.... But what's the use! I must get up at once, this very minute, take my hat and simply go without a word ... With contempt! And tomorrow I can send a challenge. The scoundrels! As though I cared about the seven roubles. They may think.... Damn it! I don't care about the seven roubles. I'll go this minute!"
paras.uz: «Xudoyim, bular men uchun odamlar emas! — deb o'yladim. — Ularning oldida o'zimni qanday ahmoq qildim! Biroq Ferfichkinga haddan oshishga yo'l qo'ydim. Hayvonlar meni ular bilan o'tirishga qo'yib, menga sharaf ko'rsatyapmiz deb o'ylashadi. Ular bu menga emas, ularga sharaf ekanini tushunishmaydi! Ozib ketibman! Kiyimlarim! Oh, jahannamga shimim! Zverkov kirishi bilanoq tizzadagi sariq dog'ni payqadi... Lekin bundan nima foyda! Darhol, shu daqiqada turib, shlyapamni olib, indamasdan shunchaki ketishim kerak... Nafrat bilan! Ertaga esa duelga chaqiruv yuborishim mumkin. Yaramaslar! Go'yo menga yetti rubl muhimdek. Ular o'ylashlari mumkin... Jin ursin! Menga yetti rubl muhim emas. Shu daqiqada ketaman!»

paras.en: Of course I remained. I drank sherry and Lafitte by the glassful in my discomfiture. Being unaccustomed to it, I was quickly affected. My annoyance increased as the wine went to my head. I longed all at once to insult them all in a most flagrant manner and then go away. To seize the moment and show what I could do, so that they would say, "He's clever, though he is absurd," and ... And ... In fact, damn them all!
paras.uz: Albatta, men qoldim. Sarosimamda qadah-qadah sheri va Lafit ichdim. Odatlanmaganim uchun tez ta'sir qildi. Vino boshimga urgan sari g'ashligim oshib bordi. Birdan hammasini eng ochiq tarzda haqorat qilib, keyin ketishni xohladim. Lahzani tutib, nimaga qodir ekanimni ko'rsatishni, toki ular «U bema'ni bo'lsa ham, aqlli» deyishsin va... va... Xullas, jahannamga hammasi!

paras.en: I scanned them all insolently with my drowsy eyes. But they seemed to have forgotten me altogether. They were noisy, vociferous, cheerful. Zverkov was talking all the time. I began listening. Zverkov was talking of some exuberant lady whom he had at last led on to declaring her love (of course, he was lying like a horse), and how he had been helped in this affair by an intimate friend of his, a Prince Kolya, an officer in the hussars, who had three thousand serfs.
paras.uz: Men ularning hammasini uyquli ko'zlarim bilan surbetlarcha ko'zdan kechirdim. Lekin ular meni butunlay unutganga o'xshardi. Ular shovqinli, baland ovozli, quvnoq edi. Zverkov butun vaqt gapirardi. Men tinglay boshladim. Zverkov nihoyat sevgisini izhor qilishga undagan qandaydir hovliqma xonim haqida gapirardi (albatta, u otdek yolg'on gapirardi) va bu ishda unga uch ming krepostnoyi bor gusar zobiti, yaqin do'sti knyaz Kolya qanday yordam bergani haqida.

paras.en: "And yet this Kolya, who has three thousand serfs, has not put in an appearance here tonight to see you off," I cut in suddenly.
paras.uz: «Shunga qaramay, uch ming krepostnoyi bor bu Kolya bugun kechqurun sizni kuzatish uchun bu yerga kelmadi», — deb birdan gapni kesdim.

paras.en: For one minute every one was silent. "You are drunk already." Trudolyubov deigned to notice me at last, glancing contemptuously in my direction. Zverkov, without a word, examined me as though I were an insect. I dropped my eyes. Simonov made haste to fill up the glasses with champagne.
paras.uz: Bir daqiqa hamma jim qoldi. «Siz allaqachon mastsiz.» Trudolyubov nihoyat menga e'tibor berishni lozim ko'rdi, men tomonga nafrat bilan qarab. Zverkov indamasdan meni go'yo hasharotdek ko'zdan kechirdi. Men ko'zlarimni yerga tushirdim. Simonov shoshilib qadahlarni shampan bilan to'ldirdi.

paras.en: Trudolyubov raised his glass, as did everyone else but me.
paras.uz: Trudolyubov qadahini ko'tardi, mendan boshqa hamma ham.

paras.en: "Your health and good luck on the journey!" He cried to Zverkov. "To old times, to our future, hurrah!"
paras.uz: «Salomatligingiz va safarda omad uchun! — deb qichqirdi u Zverkovga. — Eski zamonlar uchun, kelajagimiz uchun, ura!»

paras.en: They all tossed off their glasses, and crowded round Zverkov to kiss him. I did not move; my full glass stood untouched before me.
paras.uz: Ularning hammasi qadahlarini bir ko'tarishda ichib, Zverkovni o'pish uchun uning atrofiga yopirilishdi. Men qimirlamadim; to'la qadahim oldimda tegilmagan holda turardi.

paras.en: "Why, aren't you going to drink it?" Roared Trudolyubov, losing patience and turning menacingly to me.
paras.uz: «Nega, ichmaysizmi?» — deb o'kirdi Trudolyubov sabri tugab, menga tahdidli o'girilib.

paras.en: "I want to make a speech separately, on my own account ... And then I'll drink it, Mr. Trudolyubov."
paras.uz: «Men alohida, o'z nomimdan nutq so'zlamoqchiman... keyin ichaman, janob Trudolyubov.»

paras.en: "Spiteful brute!" Muttered Simonov. I drew myself up in my chair and feverishly seized my glass, prepared for something extraordinary, though I did not know myself precisely what I was going to say.
paras.uz: «G'arazli hayvon!» — deb g'o'ldiradi Simonov. Men kursimda qaddimni rostladim va isitmali qadahimni ushladim, qandaydir g'ayrioddiy narsaga tayyorlanib, garchi o'zim ham aniq nima demoqchi ekanimni bilmasam ham.

paras.en: "Silence!" Cried Ferfitchkin. "Now for a display of wit!"
paras.uz: «Jim! — deb qichqirdi Ferfichkin. — Endi o'tkirlik namoyishi!»

paras.en: Zverkov waited very gravely, knowing what was coming.
paras.uz: Zverkov nima bo'lishini bilib, juda jiddiy kutib turdi.

paras.en: "Mr. Lieutenant Zverkov," I began, "let me tell you that I hate phrases, phrasemongers and men in corsets ... That's the first point, and there is a second one to follow it."
paras.uz: «Janob leytenant Zverkov, — deb boshladim, — sizga aytib qo'yay, men balandparvoz iboralardan, ibora to'quvchilardan va korset kiygan erkaklardan nafratlanaman... Bu birinchi nuqta, undan keyin ikkinchisi keladi.»

paras.en: There was a general stir.
paras.uz: Umumiy g'ala-g'ovur bo'ldi.

paras.en: "The second point is: I hate ribaldry and ribald talkers. Especially ribald talkers! The third point: I love justice, truth and honesty." I went on almost mechanically, for I was beginning to shiver with horror myself and had no idea how I came to be talking like this. "I love thought, Monsieur Zverkov; I love true comradeship, on an equal footing and not ... H'm ... I love ... But, however, why not? I will drink your health, too, Mr. Zverkov. Seduce the Circassian girls, shoot the enemies of the fatherland and ... And ... To your health, Monsieur Zverkov!"
paras.uz: «Ikkinchi nuqta: men behayolikdan va behayo gapiruvchilardan nafratlanaman. Ayniqsa behayo gapiruvchilardan! Uchinchi nuqta: men adolatni, haqiqatni va halollikni sevaman.» Men deyarli mexanik davom etardim, chunki o'zim dahshatdan titray boshlagan edim va qanday qilib bunday gapira boshlaganimni bilmasdim. «Men fikrni sevaman, musyo Zverkov; men haqiqiy o'rtoqlikni, teng asosda, emas... hm... men sevaman... Lekin, biroq, nega bo'lmasin? Men sizning sog'lig'ingiz uchun ham ichaman, janob Zverkov. Cherkes qizlarini yo'ldan uring, vatan dushmanlarini oting va... va... Sog'lig'ingiz uchun, musyo Zverkov!»

paras.en: Zverkov got up from his seat, bowed to me and said:
paras.uz: Zverkov o'rnidan turdi, menga ta'zim qildi va dedi:

paras.en: "I am very much obliged to you." He was frightfully offended and turned pale.
paras.uz: «Sizdan juda minnatdorman.» U dahshatli xafa bo'ldi va rangi oqardi.

paras.en: "Damn the fellow!" Roared Trudolyubov, bringing his fist down on the table.
paras.uz: «Jin ursin bu yigitni!» — deb o'kirdi Trudolyubov, mushtini stolga urib.

paras.en: "Well, he wants a punch in the face for that," squealed Ferfitchkin.
paras.uz: «Xo'sh, buning uchun unga yuziga musht kerak», — deb chiyilladi Ferfichkin.

paras.en: "We ought to turn him out," muttered Simonov.
paras.uz: «Uni haydab chiqarishimiz kerak», — deb g'o'ldiradi Simonov.

paras.en: "Not a word, gentlemen, not a movement!" Cried Zverkov solemnly, checking the general indignation. "I thank you all, but I can show him for myself how much value I attach to his words."
paras.uz: «Bir og'iz so'z ham, bir harakat ham, janoblar! — deb tantanali qichqirdi Zverkov, umumiy g'azabni to'xtatib. — Barchangizga rahmat, lekin men unga uning so'zlariga qanchalik qiymat berishimni o'zim ko'rsata olaman.»

paras.en: "Mr. Ferfitchkin, you will give me satisfaction tomorrow for your words just now!" I said aloud, turning with dignity to Ferfitchkin.
paras.uz: «Janob Ferfichkin, ertaga hozirgina aytgan so'zlaringiz uchun menga javob berasiz!» — dedim baland ovozda, Ferfichkinga qadr-qimmat bilan o'girilib.

paras.en: "A duel, you mean? Certainly," he answered. But probably I was so ridiculous as I challenged him and it was so out of keeping with my appearance that everyone including Ferfitchkin was prostrate with laughter.
paras.uz: «Duel demoqchimisiz? Albatta», — deb javob berdi u. Lekin, ehtimol, men uni chaqirganimda shunchalik kulgili edim va bu tashqi ko'rinishimga shunchalik mos kelmasdiki, hamma, Ferfichkin ham, kulgidan yiqilib qoldi.

paras.en: "Yes, let him alone, of course! He is quite drunk," Trudolyubov said with disgust.
paras.uz: «Ha, albatta, uni tinch qo'ying! U butunlay mast», — dedi Trudolyubov jirkanib.

paras.en: "I shall never forgive myself for letting him join us," Simonov muttered again.
paras.uz: «Uning bizga qo'shilishiga yo'l qo'yganim uchun o'zimni hech qachon kechirmayman», — deb yana g'o'ldiradi Simonov.

paras.en: "Now is the time to throw a bottle at their heads," I thought to myself. I picked up the bottle ... And filled my glass.... "No, I'd better sit on to the end," I went on thinking; "you would be pleased, my friends, if I went away. Nothing will induce me to go. I'll go on sitting here and drinking to the end, on purpose, as a sign that I don't think you of the slightest consequence. I will go on sitting and drinking, because this is a public-house and I paid my entrance money. I'll sit here and drink, for I look upon you as so many pawns, as inanimate pawns. I'll sit here and drink ... And sing if I want to, yes, sing, for I have the right to ... To sing ... H'm!"
paras.uz: «Endi ularning boshiga shisha otish vaqti», — deb o'yladim ichimda. Shishani oldim... va qadahimni to'ldirdim... «Yo'q, oxirigacha o'tirganim yaxshi, — deb o'ylashda davom etdim, — agar ketsam, do'stlarim, siz xursand bo'lardingiz. Hech narsa meni ketishga majbur qila olmaydi. Men bu yerda o'tirib, oxirigacha ichishda davom etaman, ataylab, sizni zarracha ham ahamiyatli deb hisoblamasligimning belgisi sifatida. O'tirib ichishda davom etaman, chunki bu maykhona va men kirish pulimni to'laganman. Men bu yerda o'tirib ichaman, chunki sizga shunchaki piyodalar, jonsiz piyodalar sifatida qarayman. Men bu yerda o'tirib ichaman... va xohlasam kuylayman, ha, kuylayman, chunki kuylashga... haqqim bor... hm!»

paras.en: But I did not sing. I simply tried not to look at any of them. I assumed most unconcerned attitudes and waited with impatience for them to speak first. But alas, they did not address me! And oh, how I wished, how I wished at that moment to be reconciled to them! It struck eight, at last nine. They moved from the table to the sofa. Zverkov stretched himself on a lounge and put one foot on a round table. Wine was brought there. He did, as a fact, order three bottles on his own account. I, of course, was not invited to join them. They all sat round him on the sofa. They listened to him, almost with reverence. It was evident that they were fond of him. "What for? What for?" I wondered. From time to time they were moved to drunken enthusiasm and kissed each other.
paras.uz: Lekin men kuylamadim. Shunchaki ularning hech biriga qaramaslikka harakat qildim. Eng befarq holatlarni oldim va ular birinchi bo'lib gapirishini sabrsizlik bilan kutdim. Lekin afsus, ular menga murojaat qilishmadi! Va oh, o'sha lahzada ular bilan yarashishni qanchalik, qanchalik istardim! Soat sakkizni, nihoyat to'qqizni urdi. Ular stoldan divanga o'tishdi. Zverkov kushetkaga cho'zildi va bir oyog'ini dumaloq stolga qo'ydi. U yerga vino olib kelishdi. U, haqiqatan, o'z hisobidan uch shisha buyurdi. Meni, albatta, ularga qo'shilishga taklif qilishmadi. Ularning hammasi divanda uning atrofida o'tirishdi. Ular uni deyarli ehtirom bilan tinglashardi. Ular uni yaxshi ko'rishlari ko'rinib turardi. «Nima uchun? Nima uchun?» — deb hayron bo'lardim. Vaqti-vaqti bilan ular mast hayajonga tushib, bir-birlarini o'pishardi.

paras.en: They talked of the Caucasus, of the nature of true passion, of snug berths in the service, of the income of an hussar called Podharzhevsky, whom none of them knew personally, and rejoiced in the largeness of it, of the extraordinary grace and beauty of a Princess D., whom none of them had ever seen; then it came to Shakespeare's being immortal.
paras.uz: Ular Kavkaz haqida, haqiqiy ehtirosning tabiati haqida, xizmatdagi issiq joylar haqida, hech biri shaxsan tanimaydigan Podxarjevskiy degan gusarning daromadi haqida gaplashib, uning kattaligidan quvonishardi, hech biri hech qachon ko'rmagan knyaginya D.ning g'ayrioddiy nafosati va go'zalligi haqida; keyin gap Shekspirning o'lmasligiga keldi.

paras.en: I smiled contemptuously and walked up and down the other side of the room, opposite the sofa, from the table to the stove and back again. I tried my very utmost to show them that I could do without them, and yet I purposely made a noise with my boots, thumping with my heels. But it was all in vain. They paid no attention. I had the patience to walk up and down in front of them from eight o'clock till eleven, in the same place, from the table to the stove and back again. "I walk up and down to please myself and no one can prevent me." The waiter who came into the room stopped, from time to time, to look at me. I was somewhat giddy from turning round so often; at moments it seemed to me that I was in delirium. During those three hours I was three times soaked with sweat and dry again.
paras.uz: Men nafrat bilan jilmayib, xonaning narigi tomonida, divanning ro'parasida, stoldan pechkagacha va orqaga u yoqdan-bu yoqqa yurdim. Men ularga ularsiz ham yashay olishimni ko'rsatish uchun bor kuchim bilan harakat qildim, shunga qaramay ataylab etiklarim bilan shovqin qilib, tovonlarim bilan do'pillatardim. Lekin hammasi behuda edi. Ular e'tibor bermadi. Men soat sakkizdan o'n birgacha ularning oldida, bir joyda, stoldan pechkagacha va orqaga yurishga sabr qildim. «Men o'zimga yoqqani uchun u yoqdan-bu yoqqa yuraman va hech kim menga to'sqinlik qila olmaydi.» Xonaga kirgan ofitsiant vaqti-vaqti bilan to'xtab, menga qarardi. Shunchalik ko'p aylanganimdan boshim biroz aylanardi; ba'zan menga alahsirayotgandek tuyulardi. O'sha uch soat ichida men uch marta terga botib, yana qurib qoldim.

paras.en: At times, with an intense, acute pang I was stabbed to the heart by the thought that ten years, twenty years, forty years would pass, and that even in forty years I would remember with loathing and humiliation those filthiest, most ludicrous, and most awful moments of my life. No one could have gone out of his way to degrade himself more shamelessly, and I fully realised it, fully, and yet I went on pacing up and down from the table to the stove. "Oh, if you only knew what thoughts and feelings I am capable of, how cultured I am!" I thought at moments, mentally addressing the sofa on which my enemies were sitting. But my enemies behaved as though I were not in the room. Once—only once—they turned towards me, just when Zverkov was talking about Shakespeare, and I suddenly gave a contemptuous laugh.
paras.uz: Ba'zan kuchli, o'tkir og'riq bilan yuragimga o'n yil, yigirma yil, qirq yil o'tishi va hatto qirq yildan keyin ham hayotimning o'sha eng iflos, eng kulgili va eng dahshatli lahzalarini jirkanish va xo'rlik bilan eslashim haqidagi fikr sanchilardi. Hech kim o'zini bundan ham uyatsizroq xo'rlash uchun ataylab harakat qila olmasdi va men buni to'liq, to'liq anglardim, shunga qaramay stoldan pechkagacha u yoqdan-bu yoqqa yurishda davom etardim. «Oh, agar men qanday fikr va tuyg'ularga qodir ekanimni, qanchalik madaniyatli ekanimni bilganingizda edi!» — deb o'ylardim ba'zan, xayolan dushmanlarim o'tirgan divanga murojaat qilib. Lekin dushmanlarim go'yo men xonada yo'qdek o'zlarini tutishardi. Bir marta — faqat bir marta — ular menga o'girilishdi, aynan Zverkov Shekspir haqida gapirayotganda men birdan nafrat bilan kulib yubordim.

paras.en: I laughed in such an affected and disgusting way that they all at once broke off their conversation, and silently and gravely for two minutes watched me walking up and down from the table to the stove, taking no notice of them. But nothing came of it: they said nothing, and two minutes later they ceased to notice me again. It struck eleven.
paras.uz: Men shunchalik sun'iy va jirkanch kuldimki, ularning hammasi birdan suhbatni to'xtatib, ikki daqiqa jim va jiddiy ravishda ularga e'tibor bermasdan stoldan pechkagacha u yoqdan-bu yoqqa yurayotganimni kuzatishdi. Lekin hech narsa chiqmadi: ular hech narsa demadi va ikki daqiqadan keyin yana meni payqamay qo'yishdi. Soat o'n birni urdi.

paras.en: "Friends," cried Zverkov getting up from the sofa, "let us all be off now, there!"
paras.uz: «Do'stlar, — deb qichqirdi Zverkov divandan turib, — endi hammamiz ketaylik, u yerga!»

paras.en: "Of course, of course," the others assented. I turned sharply to Zverkov. I was so harassed, so exhausted, that I would have cut my throat to put an end to it. I was in a fever; my hair, soaked with perspiration, stuck to my forehead and temples.
paras.uz: «Albatta, albatta», — deb rozi bo'lishdi boshqalar. Men keskin Zverkovga o'girildim. Shunchalik qiynalgan, shunchalik holdan toygan edimki, bunga chek qo'yish uchun tomog'imni kesgan bo'lardim. Men isitmalardim; terga botgan sochlarim peshonam va chakkalarimga yopishib qolgan edi.

paras.en: "Zverkov, I beg your pardon," I said abruptly and resolutely. "Ferfitchkin, yours too, and everyone's, everyone's: I have insulted you all!"
paras.uz: «Zverkov, sizdan kechirim so'rayman, — dedim keskin va qat'iy. — Ferfichkin, sizdan ham, va hammadan, hammadan: men hammangizni haqorat qildim!»

paras.en: "Aha! A duel is not in your line, old man," Ferfitchkin hissed venomously.
paras.uz: «Aha! Duel sening ishing emas, og'ayni», — deb zaharli vishilladi Ferfichkin.

paras.en: It sent a sharp pang to my heart.
paras.uz: Bu yuragimga o'tkir sanchiq bo'lib tegdi.

paras.en: "No, it's not the duel I am afraid of, Ferfitchkin! I am ready to fight you tomorrow, after we are reconciled. I insist upon it, in fact, and you cannot refuse. I want to show you that I am not afraid of a duel. You shall fire first and I shall fire into the air."
paras.uz: «Yo'q, men dueldan qo'rqmayman, Ferfichkin! Yarashganimizdan keyin ertaga siz bilan otishishga tayyorman. Haqiqatan, men bunda turib olaman va siz rad eta olmaysiz. Men sizga dueldan qo'rqmasligimni ko'rsatmoqchiman. Siz birinchi otasiz, men esa havoga otaman.»

paras.en: "He is comforting himself," said Simonov.
paras.uz: «U o'zini yupatyapti», — dedi Simonov.

paras.en: "He's simply raving," said Trudolyubov.
paras.uz: «U shunchaki alahsirayapti», — dedi Trudolyubov.

paras.en: "But let us pass. Why are you barring our way? What do you want?" Zverkov answered disdainfully.
paras.uz: «Lekin o'tishimizga yo'l bering. Nega yo'limizni to'syapsiz? Nima istaysiz?» — deb mensimay javob berdi Zverkov.

paras.en: They were all flushed, their eyes were bright: they had been drinking heavily.
paras.uz: Ularning hammasi qizarib ketgan, ko'zlari yaltirardi: ular ko'p ichgan edi.

paras.en: "I ask for your friendship, Zverkov; I insulted you, but ..."
paras.uz: «Men sizdan do'stligingizni so'rayman, Zverkov; men sizni haqorat qildim, lekin...»

paras.en: "Insulted? You insulted me? Understand, sir, that you never, under any circumstances, could possibly insult me."
paras.uz: «Haqorat qildingizmi? Siz meni haqorat qildingizmi? Tushuning, janob, siz hech qachon, hech qanday holatda meni haqorat qila olmaysiz.»

paras.en: "And that's enough for you. Out of the way!" Concluded Trudolyubov.
paras.uz: «Va sizga shu yetadi. Yo'ldan qoching!» — deb xulosa qildi Trudolyubov.

paras.en: "Olympia is mine, friends, that's agreed!" Cried Zverkov.
paras.uz: «Olimpiya meniki, do'stlar, kelishdik!» — deb qichqirdi Zverkov.

paras.en: "We won't dispute your right, we won't dispute your right," the others answered, laughing.
paras.uz: «Huquqingizga e'tiroz bildirmaymiz, huquqingizga e'tiroz bildirmaymiz», — deb kulib javob berishdi boshqalar.

paras.en: I stood as though spat upon. The party went noisily out of the room. Trudolyubov struck up some stupid song. Simonov remained behind for a moment to tip the waiters. I suddenly went up to him.
paras.uz: Men go'yo yuzimga tupurilgandek turib qoldim. Davra shovqin bilan xonadan chiqdi. Trudolyubov qandaydir ahmoqona qo'shiqni boshladi. Simonov ofitsiantlarga choychaqa berish uchun bir lahza orqada qoldi. Men birdan uning oldiga bordim.

paras.en: "Simonov! Give me six roubles!" I said, with desperate resolution.
paras.uz: «Simonov! Menga olti rubl bering!» — dedim umidsiz qat'iyat bilan.

paras.en: He looked at me in extreme amazement, with vacant eyes. He, too, was drunk.
paras.uz: U menga nihoyatda hayrat bilan, bo'sh ko'zlar bilan qaradi. U ham mast edi.

paras.en: "You don't mean you are coming with us?"
paras.uz: «Nahotki siz biz bilan bormoqchisiz?»

paras.en: "Yes."
paras.uz: «Ha.»

paras.en: "I've no money," he snapped out, and with a scornful laugh he went out of the room.
paras.uz: «Pulim yo'q», — deb keskin aytdi u va nafratli kulgi bilan xonadan chiqib ketdi.

paras.en: I clutched at his overcoat. It was a nightmare.
paras.uz: Men uning paltosiga yopishib oldim. Bu qorabosti edi.

paras.en: "Simonov, I saw you had money. Why do you refuse me? Am I a scoundrel? Beware of refusing me: if you knew, if you knew why I am asking! My whole future, my whole plans depend upon it!"
paras.uz: «Simonov, men sizda pul borligini ko'rdim. Nega menga rad etyapsiz? Men yaramasmanmi? Menga rad etishdan ehtiyot bo'ling: agar bilganingizda, nega so'rayotganimni bilganingizda edi! Butun kelajagim, butun rejalarim shunga bog'liq!»

paras.en: Simonov pulled out the money and almost flung it at me.
paras.uz: Simonov pulni chiqarib, menga deyarli otib yubordi.

paras.en: "Take it, if you have no sense of shame!" He pronounced pitilessly, and ran to overtake them.
paras.uz: «Oling, agar uyat hissingiz bo'lmasa!» — deb shafqatsizlarcha aytdi u va ularga yetib olish uchun yugurdi.

paras.en: I was left for a moment alone. Disorder, the remains of dinner, a broken wine-glass on the floor, spilt wine, cigarette ends, fumes of drink and delirium in my brain, an agonising misery in my heart and finally the waiter, who had seen and heard all and was looking inquisitively into my face.
paras.uz: Men bir lahza yolg'iz qoldim. Tartibsizlik, ziyofat qoldiqlari, poldagi singan qadah, to'kilgan vino, papiros qoldiqlari, miyamda ichkilik bug'lari va alahsirash, yuragimda qiynovchi iztirob va nihoyat hammasini ko'rgan va eshitgan va yuzimga qiziqish bilan qarayotgan ofitsiant.

paras.en: "I am going there!" I cried. "Either they shall all go down on their knees to beg for my friendship, or I will give Zverkov a slap in the face!"
paras.uz: «Men u yerga boraman! — deb qichqirdim. — Yo ularning hammasi tiz cho'kib mendan do'stligimni so'raydi, yoki men Zverkovning yuziga tarsaki tushiraman!»

quiz.q: Why did the narrator arrive an hour early?
o: They changed the time and didn't tell him
quiz.why_uz: Ziyofat oltiga ko'chirilgan, unga xabar berishmagan.

quiz.q: What does he do for three hours?
o: Walks up and down from the table to the stove
quiz.why_uz: U soat sakkizdan o'n birgacha stoldan pechkagacha yuradi.

chapters.recap_uz: Hikoyachi bir soat oldin keladi — vaqtni o'zgartirishgan. Zverkov uni homiylik ohangida kutib oladi, u esa qo'pol javoblar beradi, mast bo'ladi, g'alati nutq so'zlaydi, Ferfichkinni duelga chaqiradi va uch soat davomida stoldan pechkagacha yuradi. Oxirida kechirim so'raydi, rad etiladi va Simonovdan olti rubl olib, ularning ortidan yuguradi.

chapters.title: Racing through the snow

paras.en: "So this is it, this is it at last—contact with real life," I muttered as I ran headlong downstairs. "This is very different from the Pope's leaving Rome and going to Brazil, very different from the ball on Lake Como!"
paras.uz: «Demak, mana shu, nihoyat mana shu — haqiqiy hayot bilan to'qnashuv, — deb g'o'ldiradim zinapoyadan boshim bilan yugurib tusharkanman. — Bu Papaning Rimni tashlab, Braziliyaga ketishidan juda farq qiladi, Komo ko'lidagi baldan juda farq qiladi!»

paras.en: "You are a scoundrel," a thought flashed through my mind, "if you laugh at this now."
paras.uz: «Sen yaramassan, — degan fikr xayolimdan chaqmoqdek o'tdi, — agar hozir bunga kulsang.»

paras.en: "No matter!" I cried, answering myself. "Now everything is lost!"
paras.uz: «Farqi yo'q! — deb qichqirdim o'zimga javob berib. — Endi hammasi yo'qoldi!»

paras.en: There was no trace to be seen of them, but that made no difference—I knew where they had gone.
paras.uz: Ulardan iz ham ko'rinmasdi, lekin bu farq qilmasdi — ular qayerga ketganini bilardim.

paras.en: At the steps was standing a solitary night sledge-driver in a rough peasant coat, powdered over with the still falling, wet, and as it were warm, snow. It was hot and steamy. The little shaggy piebald horse was also covered with snow and coughing, I remember that very well. I made a rush for the roughly made sledge; but as soon as I raised my foot to get into it, the recollection of how Simonov had just given me six roubles seemed to double me up and I tumbled into the sledge like a sack.
paras.uz: Zinapoya yonida hali ham yog'ayotgan ho'l va go'yo iliq qorga belangan dag'al dehqon chakmonidagi yolg'iz tungi izvoshchi turardi. Issiq va bug'li edi. Kichkina hurpaygan ola ot ham qorga burkangan va yo'talardi, buni juda yaxshi eslayman. Men dag'al yasalgan chanaga otildim; lekin unga chiqish uchun oyog'imni ko'tarishim bilanoq Simonov menga hozirgina olti rubl bergani xotirasi go'yo meni ikki bukib yubordi va men chanaga qopdek ag'darildim.

paras.en: "No, I must do a great deal to make up for all that," I cried. "But I will make up for it or perish on the spot this very night. Start!"
paras.uz: «Yo'q, bularning hammasini qoplash uchun ko'p ish qilishim kerak, — deb qichqirdim. — Lekin qoplayman yoki shu kechasi shu joyda halok bo'laman. Haydang!»

paras.en: We set off. There was a perfect whirl in my head.
paras.uz: Biz yo'lga tushdik. Boshimda haqiqiy girdob aylanardi.

paras.en: "They won't go down on their knees to beg for my friendship. That is a mirage, cheap mirage, revolting, romantic and fantastical—that's another ball on Lake Como. And so I am bound to slap Zverkov's face! It is my duty to. And so it is settled; I am flying to give him a slap in the face. Hurry up!"
paras.uz: «Ular mendan do'stligimni so'rab tiz cho'kishmaydi. Bu sarob, arzon sarob, jirkanch, romantik va xayoliy — bu Komo ko'lidagi yana bir bal. Demak, men Zverkovning yuziga tarsaki tushirishim shart! Bu mening burchim. Demak, hal bo'ldi; men unga tarsaki tushirish uchun uchyapman. Tezroq!»

paras.en: The driver tugged at the reins.
paras.uz: Izvoshchi jilovni tortdi.

paras.en: "As soon as I go in I'll give it him. Ought I before giving him the slap to say a few words by way of preface? No. I'll simply go in and give it him. They will all be sitting in the drawing-room, and he with Olympia on the sofa. That damned Olympia! She laughed at my looks on one occasion and refused me. I'll pull Olympia's hair, pull Zverkov's ears! No, better one ear, and pull him by it round the room. Maybe they will all begin beating me and will kick me out. That's most likely, indeed. No matter! Anyway, I shall first slap him; the initiative will be mine; and by the laws of honour that is everything: he will be branded and cannot wipe off the slap by any blows, by nothing but a duel. He will be forced to fight. And let them beat me now. Let them, the ungrateful wretches!
paras.uz: «Kirishim bilanoq unga tushiraman. Tarsaki tushirishdan oldin muqaddima sifatida bir necha so'z aytishim kerakmi? Yo'q. Shunchaki kirib, tushiraman. Ularning hammasi mehmonxonada o'tirgan bo'ladi, u esa Olimpiya bilan divanda. O'sha la'nati Olimpiya! U bir marta tashqi ko'rinishim ustidan kulib, meni rad etgan. Olimpiyaning sochidan tortaman, Zverkovning qulog'idan tortaman! Yo'q, yaxshisi bitta qulog'idan, va uni shu bilan xona bo'ylab aylantiraman. Balki ularning hammasi meni ura boshlab, tepib haydab chiqarishar. Bu, haqiqatan, eng ehtimoli. Farqi yo'q! Har holda, avval men unga tarsaki tushiraman; tashabbus meniki bo'ladi; sharaf qonunlariga ko'ra esa bu hamma narsa: unga tamg'a bosiladi va tarsakini hech qanday urishlar bilan, dueldan boshqa hech narsa bilan yuva olmaydi. U otishishga majbur bo'ladi. Endi meni urishsa urishaversin. Urishaversin, noshukur bechoralar!

paras.en: Trudolyubov will beat me hardest, he is so strong; Ferfitchkin will be sure to catch hold sideways and tug at my hair. But no matter, no matter! That's what I am going for. The blockheads will be forced at last to see the tragedy of it all! When they drag me to the door I shall call out to them that in reality they are not worth my little finger. Get on, driver, get on!" I cried to the driver. He started and flicked his whip, I shouted so savagely.
paras.uz: Trudolyubov eng qattiq uradi, u shunchalik kuchli; Ferfichkin albatta yon tomondan ushlab, sochimdan tortadi. Lekin farqi yo'q, farqi yo'q! Men aynan shuning uchun boryapman. Kallalar nihoyat bularning hammasining fojiasini ko'rishga majbur bo'ladi! Meni eshikka sudrab borishganda, ularga aslida ular jimjilog'imga ham arzimasligini qichqiraman. Hayda, izvoshchi, hayda!» — deb qichqirdim izvoshchiga. Men shunchalik vahshiyona qichqirdimki, u cho'chib, qamchisini siltadi.

paras.en: "We shall fight at daybreak, that's a settled thing. I've done with the office. Ferfitchkin made a joke about it just now. But where can I get pistols? Nonsense! I'll get my salary in advance and buy them. And powder, and bullets? That's the second's business. And how can it all be done by daybreak? And where am I to get a second? I have no friends. Nonsense!" I cried, lashing myself up more and more. "It's of no consequence! The first person I meet in the street is bound to be my second, just as he would be bound to pull a drowning man out of water. The most eccentric things may happen. Even if I were to ask the director himself to be my second tomorrow, he would be bound to consent, if only from a feeling of chivalry, and to keep the secret! Anton Antonitch...."
paras.uz: «Tong otishi bilan otishamiz, bu hal bo'lgan narsa. Idora bilan ishim tugadi. Ferfichkin hozirgina bu haqda hazil qildi. Lekin to'pponchalarni qayerdan olaman? Bema'nilik! Maoshimni oldindan olib, sotib olaman. Porox va o'qlar-chi? Bu sekundantning ishi. Bularning hammasini tong otguncha qanday qilish mumkin? Sekundantni qayerdan olaman? Do'stlarim yo'q. Bema'nilik! — deb qichqirdim o'zimni tobora qizdirib. — Bu ahamiyatsiz! Ko'chada uchragan birinchi odam sekundantim bo'lishga majbur, xuddi cho'kayotgan odamni suvdan tortib olishga majbur bo'lgani kabi. Eng g'alati narsalar sodir bo'lishi mumkin. Hatto ertaga direktorning o'zidan sekundantim bo'lishni so'rasam ham, u hech bo'lmaganda ritsarlik tuyg'usidan rozi bo'lishga va sirni saqlashga majbur! Anton Antonovich...»

paras.en: The fact is, that at that very minute the disgusting absurdity of my plan and the other side of the question was clearer and more vivid to my imagination than it could be to anyone on earth. But ....
paras.uz: Gap shundaki, aynan o'sha daqiqada rejamning jirkanch bema'niligi va masalaning boshqa tomoni tasavvurimga yer yuzidagi har qanday odamnikidan aniqroq va yorqinroq ko'rinardi. Lekin...

paras.en: "Get on, driver, get on, you rascal, get on!"
paras.uz: «Hayda, izvoshchi, hayda, yaramas, hayda!»

paras.en: "Ugh, sir!" Said the son of toil.
paras.uz: «E-eh, janob!» — dedi mehnat farzandi.

paras.en: Cold shivers suddenly ran down me. Wouldn't it be better ... To go straight home? My God, my God! Why did I invite myself to this dinner yesterday? But no, it's impossible. And my walking up and down for three hours from the table to the stove? No, they, they and no one else must pay for my walking up and down! They must wipe out this dishonour! Drive on!
paras.uz: Birdan butun badanimdan sovuq ter oqdi. Yaxshisi... to'g'ri uyga ketsammikan? Xudoyim, Xudoyim! Nega kecha o'zimni bu ziyofatga taklif qildim? Lekin yo'q, bu imkonsiz. Uch soat stoldan pechkagacha yurganim-chi? Yo'q, ular, ular va boshqa hech kim emas, yurganim uchun to'lashi kerak! Ular bu sharmandalikni yuvishi kerak! Hayda!

paras.en: And what if they give me into custody? They won't dare! They'll be afraid of the scandal. And what if Zverkov is so contemptuous that he refuses to fight a duel? He is sure to; but in that case I'll show them ... I will turn up at the posting station when he's setting off tomorrow, I'll catch him by the leg, I'll pull off his coat when he gets into the carriage. I'll get my teeth into his hand, I'll bite him. "See what lengths you can drive a desperate man to!" He may hit me on the head and they may belabour me from behind. I will shout to the assembled multitude: "Look at this young puppy who is driving off to captivate the Circassian girls after letting me spit in his face!"
paras.uz: Agar meni hibsga berishsa-chi? Jur'at etishmaydi! Ular janjaldan qo'rqishadi. Agar Zverkov shunchalik mensimasa-ki, duel qilishdan bosh tortsa-chi? U albatta bosh tortadi; lekin u holda men ularga ko'rsataman... Ertaga u jo'nayotganda pochta stansiyasiga boraman, uni oyog'idan ushlayman, aravaga chiqayotganda paltosini yechib olaman. Tishlarimni qo'liga botiraman, uni tishlayman. «Umidsiz odamni qanday darajaga yetkazish mumkinligini ko'ring!» U boshimga urishi mumkin, ular esa orqamdan savalashi mumkin. Men to'plangan olomonga qichqiraman: «Yuzimga tupurishimga yo'l qo'yib, cherkes qizlarini maftun qilgani ketayotgan bu yosh kuchukni qarang!»

paras.en: Of course, after that everything will be over! The office will have vanished off the face of the earth. I shall be arrested, I shall be tried, I shall be dismissed from the service, thrown in prison, sent to Siberia. Never mind! In fifteen years when they let me out of prison I will trudge off to him, a beggar, in rags. I shall find him in some provincial town. He will be married and happy. He will have a grown-up daughter.... I shall say to him: "Look, monster, at my hollow cheeks and my rags! I've lost everything—my career, my happiness, art, science, the woman I loved, and all through you. Here are pistols. I have come to discharge my pistol and ... And I ... Forgive you. Then I shall fire into the air and he will hear nothing more of me...."
paras.uz: Albatta, shundan keyin hammasi tugaydi! Idora yer yuzidan yo'qolgan bo'ladi. Meni hibsga olishadi, sud qilishadi, xizmatdan haydashadi, qamoqqa tashlashadi, Sibirga jo'natishadi. Mayli! O'n besh yildan keyin meni qamoqdan chiqarishganda, tilanchi holida, juldur kiyimda uning oldiga sudralib boraman. Uni qandaydir viloyat shahrida topaman. U uylangan va baxtli bo'ladi. Uning voyaga yetgan qizi bo'ladi... Men unga aytaman: «Qara, yirtqich, cho'kkan yonoqlarim va juldurlarimga! Men hamma narsani yo'qotdim — martabamni, baxtimni, san'atni, ilmni, sevgan ayolimni, va hammasi sen tufayli. Mana to'pponchalar. Men to'pponchamni otish uchun keldim va... va men... seni kechiraman.» Keyin havoga otaman va u men haqimda boshqa hech narsa eshitmaydi...»

paras.en: I was actually on the point of tears, though I knew perfectly well at that moment that all this was out of Pushkin's Silvio and Lermontov's Masquerade. And all at once I felt horribly ashamed, so ashamed that I stopped the horse, got out of the sledge, and stood still in the snow in the middle of the street. The driver gazed at me, sighing and astonished.
paras.uz: Men hatto yig'lab yuborish arafasida edim, garchi o'sha lahzada bularning hammasi Pushkinning «Silvio»si va Lermontovning «Maskarad»idan olinganini mutlaqo yaxshi bilsam ham. Va birdan dahshatli uyaldim, shunchalik uyaldimki, otni to'xtatib, chanadan tushib, ko'cha o'rtasida qorda qotib turib qoldim. Izvoshchi menga xo'rsinib va hayron bo'lib qaradi.

paras.en: What was I to do? I could not go on there—it was evidently stupid, and I could not leave things as they were, because that would seem as though ... Heavens, how could I leave things! And after such insults! "No!" I cried, throwing myself into the sledge again. "It is ordained! It is fate! Drive on, drive on!"
paras.uz: Nima qilishim kerak edi? U yerga borishda davom eta olmasdim — bu aniq ahmoqona edi, narsalarni o'z holicha qoldira ham olmasdim, chunki bu go'yo... Xudoyim, qanday qilib narsalarni qoldira olardim! Shunday haqoratlardan keyin! «Yo'q! — deb qichqirdim yana chanaga tashlanib. — Bu taqdir! Bu peshonaga yozilgan! Hayda, hayda!»

paras.en: And in my impatience I punched the sledge-driver on the back of the neck.
paras.uz: Va sabrsizligimda izvoshchining gardaniga musht tushirdim.

paras.en: "What are you up to? What are you hitting me for?" The peasant shouted, but he whipped up his nag so that it began kicking.
paras.uz: «Nima qilyapsiz? Nega meni uryapsiz?» — deb qichqirdi dehqon, lekin otini shunday qamchiladiki, u tepina boshladi.

paras.en: The wet snow was falling in big flakes; I unbuttoned myself, regardless of it. I forgot everything else, for I had finally decided on the slap, and felt with horror that it was going to happen now, at once, and that no force could stop it. The deserted street lamps gleamed sullenly in the snowy darkness like torches at a funeral. The snow drifted under my great-coat, under my coat, under my cravat, and melted there. I did not wrap myself up—all was lost, anyway.
paras.uz: Ho'l qor katta parchalar bo'lib yog'ardi; men unga e'tibor bermasdan tugmalarimni yechdim. Qolgan hamma narsani unutdim, chunki tarsakiga nihoyat qaror qilgan edim va bu hozir, darhol sodir bo'lishini va hech qanday kuch uni to'xtata olmasligini dahshat bilan his qildim. Kimsasiz ko'cha fonarlari qorli zulmatda dafn marosimidagi mash'allardek ma'yus yaltirardi. Qor paltoim ostiga, kamzulim ostiga, galstugim ostiga kirib, u yerda erirdi. Men o'ranmadim — baribir hammasi yo'qolgan edi.

paras.en: At last we arrived. I jumped out, almost unconscious, ran up the steps and began knocking and kicking at the door. I felt fearfully weak, particularly in my legs and knees. The door was opened quickly as though they knew I was coming. As a fact, Simonov had warned them that perhaps another gentleman would arrive, and this was a place in which one had to give notice and to observe certain precautions. It was one of those "millinery establishments" which were abolished by the police a good time ago. By day it really was a shop; but at night, if one had an introduction, one might visit it for other purposes.
paras.uz: Nihoyat yetib keldik. Men deyarli hushsiz holda sakrab tushdim, zinapoyadan yugurib chiqdim va eshikni taqillatib, tepa boshladim. O'zimni dahshatli zaif his qildim, ayniqsa oyoqlarim va tizzalarimda. Eshik go'yo kelishimni bilgandek tez ochildi. Haqiqatan, Simonov ularni balki yana bir janob kelishi mumkinligi haqida ogohlantirgan edi, bu esa oldindan xabar berish va ma'lum ehtiyot choralariga rioya qilish kerak bo'lgan joy edi. Bu politsiya ancha oldin yopib qo'ygan o'sha «modalar do'konlari»dan biri edi. Kunduzi u haqiqatan do'kon edi; lekin tunda, agar tavsiyang bo'lsa, unga boshqa maqsadlarda kirish mumkin edi.

paras.en: I walked rapidly through the dark shop into the familiar drawing-room, where there was only one candle burning, and stood still in amazement: there was no one there. "Where are they?" I asked somebody. But by now, of course, they had separated. Before me was standing a person with a stupid smile, the "madam" herself, who had seen me before. A minute later a door opened and another person came in.
paras.uz: Men qorong'i do'kon orqali tez yurib, faqat bitta sham yonib turgan tanish mehmonxonaga kirdim va hayratda to'xtab qoldim: u yerda hech kim yo'q edi. «Ular qani?» — deb kimdandir so'radim. Lekin hozirga kelib, albatta, ular tarqalib ketgan edi. Oldimda ahmoqona tabassumli bir shaxs — meni ilgari ko'rgan «madam»ning o'zi turardi. Bir daqiqadan keyin eshik ochilib, yana bir shaxs kirdi.

paras.en: Taking no notice of anything I strode about the room, and, I believe, I talked to myself. I felt as though I had been saved from death and was conscious of this, joyfully, all over: I should have given that slap, I should certainly, certainly have given it! But now they were not here and ... Everything had vanished and changed! I looked round. I could not realise my condition yet. I looked mechanically at the girl who had come in: and had a glimpse of a fresh, young, rather pale face, with straight, dark eyebrows, and with grave, as it were wondering, eyes that attracted me at once; I should have hated her if she had been smiling. I began looking at her more intently and, as it were, with effort. I had not fully collected my thoughts. There was something simple and good-natured in her face, but something strangely grave.
paras.uz: Hech narsaga e'tibor bermasdan xona bo'ylab odimladim va, menimcha, o'zim bilan gaplashdim. Go'yo o'limdan qutulgandek his qildim va buni butun vujudim bilan quvonch bilan anglardim: men o'sha tarsakini tushirgan bo'lardim, albatta, albatta tushirgan bo'lardim! Lekin endi ular bu yerda yo'q edi va... hamma narsa yo'qolgan va o'zgargan edi! Atrofga qaradim. Hali ahvolimni anglay olmasdim. Kirib kelgan qizga mexanik qaradim: va yangi, yosh, ancha oqargan, to'g'ri qora qoshli va meni darhol o'ziga tortgan jiddiy, go'yo hayratlangan ko'zli yuzni ko'rib qoldim; agar u jilmayib turganida, undan nafratlangan bo'lardim. Men unga diqqatliroq va go'yo zo'r berib qaray boshladim. Fikrlarimni hali to'liq yig'ib olmagan edim. Uning yuzida qandaydir sodda va xushfe'l narsa bor edi, lekin g'alati darajada jiddiy narsa ham.

paras.en: I am sure that this stood in her way here, and no one of those fools had noticed her. She could not, however, have been called a beauty, though she was tall, strong-looking, and well built. She was very simply dressed. Something loathsome stirred within me. I went straight up to her.
paras.uz: Ishonchim komilki, bu uning bu yerda yo'lini to'sardi va o'sha ahmoqlarning hech biri uni payqamagan edi. Biroq uni go'zal deb atab bo'lmasdi, garchi u baland bo'yli, kuchli ko'rinishli va qaddi-qomati kelishgan bo'lsa ham. U juda oddiy kiyingan edi. Ichimda nimadir jirkanch narsa qo'zg'aldi. Men to'g'ri uning oldiga bordim.

paras.en: I chanced to look into the glass. My harassed face struck me as revolting in the extreme, pale, angry, abject, with dishevelled hair. "No matter, I am glad of it," I thought; "I am glad that I shall seem repulsive to her; I like that."
paras.uz: Tasodifan ko'zguga qaradim. Qiynalgan yuzim menga haddan tashqari jirkanch ko'rindi: rangpar, g'azabli, tuban, sochlari to'zg'igan. «Farqi yo'q, bundan xursandman, — deb o'yladim, — unga jirkanch ko'rinishimdan xursandman; bu menga yoqadi.»

quiz.q: What does the narrator plan to do to Zverkov?
quiz.why_uz: U Zverkovning yuziga tarsaki tushirishga qaror qiladi.

quiz.q: Whose works does his fantasy come from?
quiz.why_uz: «Bularning hammasi Pushkinning Silviosi va Lermontovning Maskaradidan».

chapters.recap_uz: Hikoyachi izvoshchida ularning ortidan uchadi, Zverkovga tarsaki tushirish, duel, Sibir va o'n besh yildan keyingi uchrashuvni tasavvur qiladi — keyin bularning hammasi Pushkin va Lermontovdan olinganini anglab, uyaladi. Uyga yetganda ular yo'q; u u yerda yosh, jiddiy ko'zli qiz — Lizani ko'radi.

chapters.title: Liza

paras.en: ... Somewhere behind a screen a clock began wheezing, as though oppressed by something, as though someone were strangling it. After an unnaturally prolonged wheezing there followed a shrill, nasty, and as it were unexpectedly rapid, chime—as though someone were suddenly jumping forward. It struck two. I woke up, though I had indeed not been asleep but lying half-conscious.
paras.uz: ...Qayerdadir parda ortida soat go'yo nimadandir ezilgandek, go'yo kimdir uni bo'g'ayotgandek xirillay boshladi. G'ayritabiiy cho'zilgan xirillashdan keyin chinqiroq, jirkanch va go'yo kutilmaganda tez zang chalindi — go'yo kimdir birdan oldinga sakragandek. Soat ikkini urdi. Men uyg'ondim, garchi haqiqatan uxlamagan, balki yarim hushsiz yotgan bo'lsam ham.

paras.en: It was almost completely dark in the narrow, cramped, low-pitched room, cumbered up with an enormous wardrobe and piles of cardboard boxes and all sorts of frippery and litter. The candle end that had been burning on the table was going out and gave a faint flicker from time to time. In a few minutes there would be complete darkness.
paras.uz: Ulkan javon, karton qutilar uyumlari va har xil latta-putta va axlat bilan to'lgan tor, siqiq, past shiftli xonada deyarli butunlay qorong'i edi. Stolda yonib turgan sham qoldig'i o'chib borar va vaqti-vaqti bilan zaif miltillardi. Bir necha daqiqadan keyin butunlay qorong'i bo'lardi.

paras.en: I was not long in coming to myself; everything came back to my mind at once, without an effort, as though it had been in ambush to pounce upon me again. And, indeed, even while I was unconscious a point seemed continually to remain in my memory unforgotten, and round it my dreams moved drearily. But strange to say, everything that had happened to me in that day seemed to me now, on waking, to be in the far, far away past, as though I had long, long ago lived all that down.
paras.uz: Men o'zimga kelishimga ko'p vaqt ketmadi; hamma narsa birdaniga, hech qanday zo'riqishsiz, go'yo menga yana tashlanish uchun pistirmada turgandek xayolimga qaytdi. Haqiqatan ham, hatto hushsiz bo'lganimda ham xotiramda doimo unutilmagan qandaydir nuqta qolgandek tuyulardi va uning atrofida tushlarim zerikarli aylanardi. Lekin g'alati, o'sha kuni men bilan sodir bo'lgan hamma narsa endi, uyg'onganimda, menga uzoq, uzoq o'tmishda bo'lgandek tuyulardi, go'yo men bularning hammasini allaqachon, uzoq vaqt oldin boshdan kechirib bo'lgandek.

paras.en: My head was full of fumes. Something seemed to be hovering over me, rousing me, exciting me, and making me restless. Misery and spite seemed surging up in me again and seeking an outlet. Suddenly I saw beside me two wide open eyes scrutinising me curiously and persistently. The look in those eyes was coldly detached, sullen, as it were utterly remote; it weighed upon me.
paras.uz: Boshim bug'larga to'la edi. Nimadir ustimda aylanib, meni uyg'otib, hayajonga solib, bezovta qilayotgandek edi. Iztirob va g'araz yana ichimda qaynab, chiqish yo'li izlayotgandek edi. Birdan yonimda meni qiziqish va qat'iyat bilan ko'zdan kechirayotgan ikkita katta ochiq ko'zni ko'rdim. Bu ko'zlardagi nigoh sovuq, befarq, qovog'i soliq, go'yo mutlaqo uzoq edi; u meni ezardi.

paras.en: A grim idea came into my brain and passed all over my body, as a horrible sensation, such as one feels when one goes into a damp and mouldy cellar. There was something unnatural in those two eyes, beginning to look at me only now. I recalled, too, that during those two hours I had not said a single word to this creature, and had, in fact, considered it utterly superfluous; in fact, the silence had for some reason gratified me. Now I suddenly realised vividly the hideous idea—revolting as a spider—of vice, which, without love, grossly and shamelessly begins with that in which true love finds its consummation. For a long time we gazed at each other like that, but she did not drop her eyes before mine and her expression did not change, so that at last I felt uncomfortable.
paras.uz: Miyamga dahshatli fikr keldi va butun badanimdan zax va mog'or bosgan yerto'laga kirganda his qilinadigan dahshatli sezgi kabi o'tdi. Faqat hozirgina menga qaray boshlagan bu ikki ko'zda qandaydir g'ayritabiiy narsa bor edi. Shuningdek, o'sha ikki soat davomida bu mavjudotga bir og'iz ham so'z aytmaganimni va haqiqatan buni mutlaqo ortiqcha deb hisoblaganimni esladim; haqiqatan, sukunat negadir menga yoqqan edi. Endi men birdan muhabbatsiz, qo'pol va uyatsiz ravishda haqiqiy muhabbat o'z cho'qqisini topadigan narsadan boshlanadigan buzuqlikning o'rgimchakdek jirkanch xunuk g'oyasini yorqin angladim. Biz uzoq vaqt bir-birimizga shunday tikilib turdik, lekin u ko'zlarimning oldida ko'zlarini yerga tushirmadi va ifodasi o'zgarmadi, shuning uchun oxiri o'zimni noqulay his qildim.

paras.en: "What is your name?" I asked abruptly, to put an end to it.
paras.uz: «Isming nima?» — deb keskin so'radim, bunga chek qo'yish uchun.

paras.en: "Liza," she answered almost in a whisper, but somehow far from graciously, and she turned her eyes away.
paras.uz: «Liza», — deb javob berdi u deyarli shivirlab, lekin qandaydir mutlaqo iltifotsiz, va ko'zlarini olib qochdi.

paras.en: I was silent.
paras.uz: Men jim qoldim.

paras.en: "What weather! The snow ... It's disgusting!" I said, almost to myself, putting my arm under my head despondently, and gazing at the ceiling.
paras.uz: «Qanday ob-havo! Qor... Jirkanch!» — dedim deyarli o'zimga, qo'limni tushkun holda boshim ostiga qo'yib, shiftga tikilib.

paras.en: She made no answer. This was horrible.
paras.uz: U javob bermadi. Bu dahshatli edi.

paras.en: "Have you always lived in Petersburg?" I asked a minute later, almost angrily, turning my head slightly towards her.
paras.uz: «Doim Peterburgda yashaganmisan?» — deb bir daqiqadan keyin deyarli jahl bilan so'radim, boshimni biroz unga burib.

paras.en: "No."
paras.uz: «Yo'q.»

paras.en: "Where do you come from?"
paras.uz: «Qayerdan kelgansan?»

paras.en: "From Riga," she answered reluctantly.
paras.uz: «Rigadan», — deb istamaygina javob berdi u.

paras.en: "Are you a German?"
paras.uz: «Nemismisan?»

paras.en: "No, Russian."
paras.uz: «Yo'q, rus.»

paras.en: "Have you been here long?"
paras.uz: «Bu yerda ko'pdan berimisan?»

paras.en: "Where?"
paras.uz: «Qayerda?»

paras.en: "In this house?"
paras.uz: «Bu uyda?»

paras.en: "A fortnight."
paras.uz: «Ikki hafta.»

paras.en: She spoke more and more jerkily. The candle went out; I could no longer distinguish her face.
paras.uz: U tobora uzuq-yuluq gapirardi. Sham o'chdi; men endi uning yuzini ajrata olmasdim.

paras.en: "Have you a father and mother?"
paras.uz: «Otang va onang bormi?»

paras.en: "Yes ... No ... I have."
paras.uz: «Ha... yo'q... bor.»

paras.en: "Where are they?"
paras.uz: «Ular qayerda?»

paras.en: "There ... In Riga."
paras.uz: «U yerda... Rigada.»

paras.en: "What are they?"
paras.uz: «Ular kim?»

paras.en: "Oh, nothing."
paras.uz: «Oh, hech kim.»

paras.en: "Nothing? Why, what class are they?"
paras.uz: «Hech kim? Axir qaysi tabaqadan?»

paras.en: "Tradespeople."
paras.uz: «Hunarmandlar.»

paras.en: "Have you always lived with them?"
paras.uz: «Doim ular bilan yashaganmisan?»

paras.en: "Yes."
paras.uz: «Ha.»

paras.en: "How old are you?"
paras.uz: «Necha yoshdasan?»

paras.en: "Twenty."
paras.uz: «Yigirma.»

paras.en: "Why did you leave them?"
paras.uz: «Nega ularni tashlab ketding?»

paras.en: "Oh, for no reason."
paras.uz: «Oh, shunchaki.»

paras.en: That answer meant "Let me alone; I feel sick, sad."
paras.uz: Bu javob «Meni tinch qo'y; ko'nglim aynayapti, g'amginman» degani edi.

paras.en: We were silent.
paras.uz: Biz jim qoldik.

paras.en: God knows why I did not go away. I felt myself more and more sick and dreary. The images of the previous day began of themselves, apart from my will, flitting through my memory in confusion. I suddenly recalled something I had seen that morning when, full of anxious thoughts, I was hurrying to the office.
paras.uz: Nega ketmaganimni Xudo biladi. O'zimni tobora ko'ngli aynigan va zerikkan his qilardim. Oldingi kunning tasvirlari o'z-o'zidan, irodamdan tashqari, xotiramda chalkash miltillay boshladi. Birdan o'sha kuni ertalab, xavotirli fikrlarga to'la holda idoraga shoshilayotganimda ko'rgan bir narsani esladim.

paras.en: "I saw them carrying a coffin out yesterday and they nearly dropped it," I suddenly said aloud, not that I desired to open the conversation, but as it were by accident.
paras.uz: «Kecha tobut olib chiqishayotganini ko'rdim, ular uni deyarli tushirib yuborishdi», — dedim birdan baland ovozda, suhbatni boshlashni istaganimdan emas, balki go'yo tasodifan.

paras.en: "A coffin?"
paras.uz: «Tobut?»

paras.en: "Yes, in the Haymarket; they were bringing it up out of a cellar."
paras.uz: «Ha, Pichanbozorda; uni yerto'ladan olib chiqishayotgan edi.»

paras.en: "From a cellar?"
paras.uz: «Yerto'ladan?»

paras.en: "Not from a cellar, but a basement. Oh, you know ... Down below ... From a house of ill-fame. It was filthy all round ... Egg-shells, litter ... A stench. It was loathsome."
paras.uz: «Yerto'ladan emas, podvaldan. Oh, bilasan-ku... pastdan... fohishaxonadan. Atrofda iflos edi... tuxum po'choqlari, axlat... sasigan hid. Jirkanch edi.»

paras.en: Silence.
paras.uz: Sukunat.

paras.en: "A nasty day to be buried," I began, simply to avoid being silent.
paras.uz: «Dafn qilish uchun yomon kun», — deb boshladim, shunchaki jim qolmaslik uchun.

paras.en: "Nasty, in what way?"
paras.uz: «Nimasi yomon?»

paras.en: "The snow, the wet." (I yawned.)
paras.uz: «Qor, namlik.» (Men esnadim.)

paras.en: "It makes no difference," she said suddenly, after a brief silence.
paras.uz: «Farqi yo'q», — dedi u birdan, qisqa sukutdan keyin.

paras.en: "No, it's horrid." (I yawned again). "The gravediggers must have sworn at getting drenched by the snow. And there must have been water in the grave."
paras.uz: «Yo'q, jirkanch.» (Men yana esnadim.) «Go'rkovlar qorda ho'l bo'lganidan so'kingan bo'lsa kerak. Qabrda suv ham bo'lgan bo'lsa kerak.»

paras.en: "Why water in the grave?" She asked, with a sort of curiosity, but speaking even more harshly and abruptly than before.
paras.uz: «Nega qabrda suv?» — deb so'radi u qandaydir qiziqish bilan, lekin avvalgidan ham qo'polroq va keskinroq gapirib.

paras.en: I suddenly began to feel provoked.
paras.uz: Birdan menda qandaydir jahl qo'zg'aldi.

paras.en: "Why, there must have been water at the bottom a foot deep. You can't dig a dry grave in Volkovo Cemetery."
paras.uz: «Axir tubida bir qarich suv bo'lgan bo'lsa kerak. Volkovo qabristonida quruq qabr qazib bo'lmaydi.»

paras.en: "Why?"
paras.uz: «Nega?»

paras.en: "Why? Why, the place is waterlogged. It's a regular marsh. So they bury them in water. I've seen it myself ... Many times."
paras.uz: «Nega? Axir u joy botqoq. Haqiqiy botqoq. Shuning uchun ularni suvga ko'mishadi. O'zim ko'rganman... ko'p marta.»

paras.en: (I had never seen it once, indeed I had never been in Volkovo, and had only heard stories of it.)
paras.uz: (Men buni bir marta ham ko'rmaganman, haqiqatan Volkovoda hech qachon bo'lmaganman va faqat u haqda hikoyalar eshitganman.)

paras.en: "Do you mean to say, you don't mind how you die?"
paras.uz: «Nahotki qanday o'lishing senga farqi yo'q?»

paras.en: "But why should I die?" She answered, as though defending herself.
paras.uz: «Lekin nega men o'lishim kerak?» — deb javob berdi u, go'yo o'zini himoya qilgandek.

paras.en: "Why, some day you will die, and you will die just the same as that dead woman. She was ... A girl like you. She died of consumption."
paras.uz: «Axir bir kun sen o'lasan va xuddi o'sha marhuma kabi o'lasan. U... senga o'xshagan qiz edi. U sildan o'ldi.»

paras.en: "A wench would have died in hospital ..." (She knows all about it already: she said "wench," not "girl.")
paras.uz: «Bunday qiz kasalxonada o'lgan bo'lardi...» (U allaqachon hammasini biladi: u «qiz» demadi, «bunday» dedi.)

paras.en: "She was in debt to her madam," I retorted, more and more provoked by the discussion; "and went on earning money for her up to the end, though she was in consumption. Some sledge-drivers standing by were talking about her to some soldiers and telling them so. No doubt they knew her. They were laughing. They were going to meet in a pot-house to drink to her memory."
paras.uz: «U madamiga qarzdor edi, — deb e'tiroz bildirdim, bahsdan tobora qizib, — va sil bo'lsa ham, oxirigacha unga pul topishda davom etgan. Yonida turgan ba'zi izvoshchilar askarlarga u haqda gapirib, shuni aytishayotgan edi. Ular uni tanishgan bo'lsa kerak. Ular kulishardi. Ular uning xotirasiga ichish uchun maykhonada uchrashmoqchi edi.»

paras.en: A great deal of this was my invention. Silence followed, profound silence. She did not stir.
paras.uz: Buning ko'p qismini men o'ylab topdim. Sukunat cho'kdi, chuqur sukunat. U qimirlamadi.

paras.en: "And is it better to die in a hospital?"
paras.uz: «Kasalxonada o'lish yaxshiroqmi?»

paras.en: "Isn't it just the same? Besides, why should I die?" She added irritably.
paras.uz: «Baribir emasmi? Bundan tashqari, nega men o'lishim kerak?» — deb jahl bilan qo'shimcha qildi u.

paras.en: "If not now, a little later."
paras.uz: «Hozir bo'lmasa, biroz keyinroq.»

paras.en: "Why a little later?"
paras.uz: «Nega biroz keyinroq?»

paras.en: "Why, indeed? Now you are young, pretty, fresh, you fetch a high price. But after another year of this life you will be very different—you will go off."
paras.uz: «Nega deysanmi? Hozir sen yoshsan, chiroylisan, yangi gulsan, qimmatga baholanasan. Lekin bu hayotning yana bir yilidan keyin sen butunlay boshqacha bo'lasan — so'lib qolasan.»

paras.en: "In a year?"
paras.uz: «Bir yilda?»

paras.en: "Anyway, in a year you will be worth less," I continued malignantly. "You will go from here to something lower, another house; a year later—to a third, lower and lower, and in seven years you will come to a basement in the Haymarket. That will be if you were lucky. But it would be much worse if you got some disease, consumption, say ... And caught a chill, or something or other. It's not easy to get over an illness in your way of life. If you catch anything you may not get rid of it. And so you would die."
paras.uz: «Har holda, bir yildan keyin arzonroq bo'lasan, — deb g'arazli davom etdim. — Bu yerdan pastroq joyga, boshqa uyga o'tasan; bir yildan keyin — uchinchisiga, tobora pastroq, yetti yildan keyin esa Pichanbozordagi podvalga yetib kelasan. Bu omading kelsa. Lekin biror kasallik, masalan, sil yuqtirsang... va shamollasang yoki boshqa biror narsa bo'lsa, ancha yomonroq bo'ladi. Sening hayot tarzingda kasallikdan qutulish oson emas. Biror narsa yuqtirsang, undan qutulmasliging mumkin. Shunday qilib o'lasan.»

paras.en: "Oh, well, then I shall die," she answered, quite vindictively, and she made a quick movement.
paras.uz: «Xo'sh, unda o'laman», — deb javob berdi u ancha qasoskorona va tez qimirlab qo'ydi.

paras.en: "But one is sorry."
paras.uz: «Lekin achinasan-ku.»

paras.en: "Sorry for whom?"
paras.uz: «Kimga achinaman?»

paras.en: "Sorry for life." Silence.
paras.uz: «Hayotga achinasan.» Sukunat.

paras.en: "Have you been engaged to be married? Eh?"
paras.uz: «Unashtirilganmisan? A?»

paras.en: "What's that to you?"
paras.uz: «Sizga nima?»

paras.en: "Oh, I am not cross-examining you. It's nothing to me. Why are you so cross? Of course you may have had your own troubles. What is it to me? It's simply that I felt sorry."
paras.uz: «Oh, men seni so'roq qilayotganim yo'q. Menga baribir. Nega bunchalik jahldorsan? Albatta, sening o'z tashvishlaring bo'lgan bo'lishi mumkin. Menga nima? Shunchaki achinib ketdim.»

paras.en: "Sorry for whom?"
paras.uz: «Kimga achindingiz?»

paras.en: "Sorry for you."
paras.uz: «Senga achindim.»

paras.en: "No need," she whispered hardly audibly, and again made a faint movement.
paras.uz: «Kerak emas», — deb zo'rg'a eshitiladigan qilib shivirladi u va yana zaif qimirladi.

paras.en: That incensed me at once. What! I was so gentle with her, and she....
paras.uz: Bu meni darhol g'azablantirdi. Qanday! Men unga shunchalik muloyim edim, u esa...

paras.en: "Why, do you think that you are on the right path?"
paras.uz: «Nima, sen to'g'ri yo'ldaman deb o'ylaysanmi?»

paras.en: "I don't think anything."
paras.uz: «Men hech narsa o'ylamayman.»

paras.en: "That's what's wrong, that you don't think. Realise it while there is still time. There still is time. You are still young, good-looking; you might love, be married, be happy...."
paras.uz: «Yomoni shu, o'ylamasliging. Hali vaqt borida angla. Hali vaqt bor. Sen hali yoshsan, ko'rkamsan; sevishing, turmushga chiqishing, baxtli bo'lishing mumkin...»

paras.en: "Not all married women are happy," she snapped out in the rude abrupt tone she had used at first.
paras.uz: «Hamma turmushga chiqqan ayollar ham baxtli emas», — deb u boshidagi qo'pol, keskin ohangda gapni kesdi.

paras.en: "Not all, of course, but anyway it is much better than the life here. Infinitely better. Besides, with love one can live even without happiness. Even in sorrow life is sweet; life is sweet, however one lives. But here what is there but ... Foulness? Phew!"
paras.uz: «Albatta, hammasi emas, lekin har holda bu yerdagi hayotdan ancha yaxshi. Cheksiz yaxshi. Bundan tashqari, muhabbat bilan baxtsiz ham yashash mumkin. Hatto qayg'uda ham hayot shirin; qanday yashamasin, hayot shirin. Bu yerda esa... iflosligdan boshqa nima bor? Tfu!»
