paras.en: I turned away with disgust; I was no longer reasoning coldly. I began to feel myself what I was saying and warmed to the subject. I was already longing to expound the cherished ideas I had brooded over in my corner. Something suddenly flared up in me. An object had appeared before me.
paras.uz: Men jirkanib yuz o'girdim; endi sovuqqonlik bilan mulohaza qilmayotgan edim. Aytayotganlarimni o'zim his qila boshladim va mavzuga qizishib ketdim. Men allaqachon burchagimda o'ylab yurgan ardoqli g'oyalarimni bayon qilishga tashna edim. Ichimda birdan nimadir alangalandi. Oldimda maqsad paydo bo'lgan edi.

paras.en: "Never mind my being here, I am not an example for you. I am, perhaps, worse than you are. I was drunk when I came here, though," I hastened, however, to say in self-defence. "Besides, a man is no example for a woman. It's a different thing. I may degrade and defile myself, but I am not anyone's slave. I come and go, and that's an end of it. I shake it off, and I am a different man. But you are a slave from the start. Yes, a slave! You give up everything, your whole freedom. If you want to break your chains afterwards, you won't be able to; you will be more and more fast in the snares. It is an accursed bondage. I know it. I won't speak of anything else, maybe you won't understand, but tell me: no doubt you are in debt to your madam?
paras.uz: «Mening bu yerda ekanimga qarama, men senga namuna emasman. Men, balki, sendan ham yomonroqman. Biroq bu yerga kelganimda mast edim», — deb shoshilib o'zimni himoya qildim. — Bundan tashqari, erkak ayolga namuna emas. Bu boshqa narsa. Men o'zimni xo'rlashim va bulg'ashim mumkin, lekin men hech kimning quli emasman. Kelaman, ketaman, vassalom. Silkitib tashlayman va boshqa odamman. Sen esa boshidan qulsan. Ha, qul! Sen hamma narsangni, butun erkinligingni berasan. Keyin zanjirlaringni uzmoqchi bo'lsang, uza olmaysan; tuzoqqa tobora mahkamroq ilinasan. Bu la'nati qullik. Bilaman. Boshqa narsa haqida gapirmayman, balki tushunmassan, lekin ayt-chi: shubhasiz, sen madamingga qarzdorsan?

paras.en: There, you see," I added, though she made no answer, but only listened in silence, entirely absorbed, "that's a bondage for you! You will never buy your freedom. They will see to that. It's like selling your soul to the devil.... And besides ... Perhaps, I too, am just as unlucky—how do you know—and wallow in the mud on purpose, out of misery? You know, men take to drink from grief; well, maybe I am here from grief. Come, tell me, what is there good here? Here you and I ... Came together ... Just now and did not say one word to one another all the time, and it was only afterwards you began staring at me like a wild creature, and I at you. Is that loving? Is that how one human being should meet another? It's hideous, that's what it is!"
paras.uz: Mana, ko'rdingmi, — deb qo'shimcha qildim, garchi u javob bermasa ham, faqat butunlay berilib, jim tinglasa ham, — mana senga qullik! Sen hech qachon erkinligingni sotib ololmaysan. Ular buni ta'minlashadi. Bu ruhingni shaytonga sotish kabi... Bundan tashqari... balki men ham xuddi shunday omadsizman — sen qayerdan bilasan — va baxtsizlikdan ataylab loyda ag'anayotgandirman? Bilasan-ku, erkaklar qayg'udan ichkilikka beriladi; xo'sh, balki men bu yerda qayg'udandirman. Qani, ayt-chi, bu yerda nima yaxshi narsa bor? Mana sen va men... hozirgina... birga bo'ldik va butun vaqt bir-birimizga bir og'iz ham so'z aytmadik, faqat keyingina sen menga yovvoyi mavjudotdek tikila boshlading, men esa senga. Bu sevishmi? Bir inson boshqasini shunday uchratishi kerakmi? Bu xunuk, mana nima!»

paras.en: "Yes!" She assented sharply and hurriedly.
paras.uz: «Ha!» — deb keskin va shoshilib rozi bo'ldi u.

paras.en: I was positively astounded by the promptitude of this "Yes." So the same thought may have been straying through her mind when she was staring at me just before. So she, too, was capable of certain thoughts? "Damn it all, this was interesting, this was a point of likeness!" I thought, almost rubbing my hands. And indeed it's easy to turn a young soul like that!
paras.uz: Men bu «ha»ning tezligidan rosa hayratga tushdim. Demak, u hozirgina menga tikilib turganida ham xayolida xuddi shu fikr kezgan bo'lsa kerak. Demak, u ham ma'lum fikrlarga qodir ekan? «Jin ursin, bu qiziq, bu o'xshashlik nuqtasi!» — deb o'yladim, deyarli qo'llarimni ishqalab. Haqiqatan ham bunday yosh qalbni burish oson!

paras.en: It was the exercise of my power that attracted me most.
paras.uz: Meni eng ko'p o'ziga tortgan narsa kuchimni ishga solish edi.

paras.en: She turned her head nearer to me, and it seemed to me in the darkness that she propped herself on her arm. Perhaps she was scrutinising me. How I regretted that I could not see her eyes. I heard her deep breathing.
paras.uz: U boshini menga yaqinroq burdi va qorong'ilikda menga u tirsagiga tayangandek tuyuldi. Balki u meni ko'zdan kechirayotgandir. Uning ko'zlarini ko'ra olmaganimdan qanchalik afsuslandim. Uning chuqur nafas olishini eshitdim.

paras.en: "Why have you come here?" I asked her, with a note of authority already in my voice.
paras.uz: «Nega bu yerga kelding?» — deb so'radim undan, ovozimda allaqachon hokimiyat ohangi bilan.

paras.en: "Oh, I don't know."
paras.uz: «Oh, bilmayman.»

paras.en: "But how nice it would be to be living in your father's house! It's warm and free; you have a home of your own."
paras.uz: «Lekin otangning uyida yashash qanchalik yaxshi bo'lardi! U yerda issiq va erkin; o'z uying bor.»

paras.en: "But what if it's worse than this?"
paras.uz: «Agar u bu yerdan yomonroq bo'lsa-chi?»

paras.en: "I must take the right tone," flashed through my mind. "I may not get far with sentimentality." But it was only a momentary thought. I swear she really did interest me. Besides, I was exhausted and moody. And cunning so easily goes hand-in-hand with feeling.
paras.uz: «To'g'ri ohangni topishim kerak, — degan fikr xayolimdan o'tdi. — Hissiyotchanlik bilan uzoqqa bormasligim mumkin.» Lekin bu bir lahzalik fikr edi. Qasamki, u meni haqiqatan qiziqtirardi. Bundan tashqari, men holdan toygan va kayfiyatsiz edim. Ayyorlik esa tuyg'u bilan juda oson yonma-yon yuradi.

paras.en: "Who denies it!" I hastened to answer. "Anything may happen. I am convinced that someone has wronged you, and that you are more sinned against than sinning. Of course, I know nothing of your story, but it's not likely a girl like you has come here of her own inclination...."
paras.uz: «Kim inkor etadi! — deb shoshilib javob berdim. — Hamma narsa bo'lishi mumkin. Ishonchim komilki, kimdir senga yomonlik qilgan va sen gunoh qilganingdan ko'ra ko'proq senga qarshi gunoh qilingan. Albatta, men sening tarixingdan hech narsa bilmayman, lekin sendek qiz bu yerga o'z xohishi bilan kelgan bo'lishi ehtimoldan uzoq...»

paras.en: "A girl like me?" She whispered, hardly audibly; but I heard it.
paras.uz: «Mendek qiz?» — deb u zo'rg'a eshitiladigan qilib shivirladi; lekin men eshitdim.

paras.en: Damn it all, I was flattering her. That was horrid. But perhaps it was a good thing.... She was silent.
paras.uz: Jin ursin, men unga xushomad qilayotgan edim. Bu jirkanch edi. Lekin balki bu yaxshi narsadir... U jim edi.

paras.en: "See, Liza, I will tell you about myself. If I had had a home from childhood, I shouldn't be what I am now. I often think that. However bad it may be at home, anyway they are your father and mother, and not enemies, strangers. Once a year at least, they'll show their love of you. Anyway, you know you are at home. I grew up without a home; and perhaps that's why I've turned so ... Unfeeling."
paras.uz: «Qara, Liza, senga o'zim haqimda aytib beraman. Agar bolaligimdan uyim bo'lganida, hozirgidek bo'lmasdim. Men buni tez-tez o'ylayman. Uyda qanchalik yomon bo'lmasin, har holda ular sening otang va onang, dushmanlar, begonalar emas. Hech bo'lmaganda yilda bir marta ular senga mehrini ko'rsatadi. Har holda, uyda ekaningni bilasan. Men uysiz o'sdim; balki shuning uchun shunchalik... hissiz bo'lib qolganman.»

paras.en: I waited again. "Perhaps she doesn't understand," I thought, "and, indeed, it is absurd—it's moralising."
paras.uz: Men yana kutdim. «Balki u tushunmas, — deb o'yladim, — haqiqatan ham bu bema'ni — bu nasihatbozlik.»

paras.en: "If I were a father and had a daughter, I believe I should love my daughter more than my sons, really," I began indirectly, as though talking of something else, to distract her attention. I must confess I blushed.
paras.uz: «Agar men ota bo'lib, qizim bo'lganida, menimcha, qizimni o'g'illarimdan ko'proq sevgan bo'lardim, rostdan», — deb men go'yo boshqa narsa haqida gapirayotgandek, uning e'tiborini chalg'itish uchun bilvosita boshladim. Tan olishim kerak, qizarib ketdim.

paras.en: "Why so?" She asked.
paras.uz: «Nega bunday?» — deb so'radi u.

paras.en: Ah! So she was listening!
paras.uz: Ah! Demak, u tinglayotgan ekan!

paras.en: "I don't know, Liza. I knew a father who was a stern, austere man, but used to go down on his knees to his daughter, used to kiss her hands, her feet, he couldn't make enough of her, really. When she danced at parties he used to stand for five hours at a stretch, gazing at her. He was mad over her: I understand that! She would fall asleep tired at night, and he would wake to kiss her in her sleep and make the sign of the cross over her. He would go about in a dirty old coat, he was stingy to everyone else, but would spend his last penny for her, giving her expensive presents, and it was his greatest delight when she was pleased with what he gave her. Fathers always love their daughters more than the mothers do. Some girls live happily at home! And I believe I should never let my daughters marry."
paras.uz: «Bilmayman, Liza. Men bir otani bilardim, u qattiqqo'l, jiddiy odam edi, lekin qizining oldida tiz cho'kardi, uning qo'llarini, oyoqlarini o'pardi, unga to'ymasdi, rostdan. Qizi ziyofatlarda raqsga tushganda, u besh soat ketma-ket unga tikilib turardi. U uning uchun aqldan ozgan edi: men buni tushunaman! Qizi tunda charchab uxlab qolardi, u esa uyquda uni o'pish va ustiga cho'qinish uchun uyg'onardi. U iflos eski paltoda yurardi, boshqa hammaga xasis edi, lekin uning uchun oxirgi tiyinini sarflab, qimmatbaho sovg'alar berardi va qizi bergan sovg'asidan xursand bo'lganda bu uning eng katta quvonchi edi. Otalar qizlarini onalardan ko'ra doimo ko'proq sevadi. Ba'zi qizlar uyda baxtli yashaydi! Menimcha, men qizlarimni hech qachon turmushga bermagan bo'lardim.»

paras.en: "What next?" She said, with a faint smile.
paras.uz: «Yana nima?» — dedi u zaif jilmayib.

paras.en: "I should be jealous, I really should. To think that she should kiss anyone else! That she should love a stranger more than her father! It's painful to imagine it. Of course, that's all nonsense, of course every father would be reasonable at last. But I believe before I should let her marry, I should worry myself to death; I should find fault with all her suitors. But I should end by letting her marry whom she herself loved. The one whom the daughter loves always seems the worst to the father, you know. That is always so. So many family troubles come from that."
paras.uz: «Rashk qilgan bo'lardim, rostdan rashk qilardim. U boshqa birovni o'pishini o'ylasang! Begonani otasidan ko'proq sevishini! Buni tasavvur qilish og'riqli. Albatta, bularning hammasi bema'nilik, albatta har qanday ota oxiri oqil bo'ladi. Lekin menimcha, uni turmushga berishdan oldin o'zimni o'lgunimcha qiynagan bo'lardim; barcha sovchilaridan ayb topgan bo'lardim. Lekin oxiri uni o'zi sevgan odamga berish bilan tugatgan bo'lardim. Bilasan, qiz sevgan odam otaga doim eng yomoni bo'lib ko'rinadi. Bu doim shunday. Shundan qanchadan-qancha oilaviy kulfatlar chiqadi.»

paras.en: "Some are glad to sell their daughters, rather than marrying them honourably."
paras.uz: «Ba'zilar qizlarini halol turmushga berishdan ko'ra sotishdan xursand.»

paras.en: Ah, so that was it!
paras.uz: Ah, gap shunda ekan!

paras.en: "Such a thing, Liza, happens in those accursed families in which there is neither love nor God," I retorted warmly, "and where there is no love, there is no sense either. There are such families, it's true, but I am not speaking of them. You must have seen wickedness in your own family, if you talk like that. Truly, you must have been unlucky. H'm! ... That sort of thing mostly comes about through poverty."
paras.uz: «Bunday narsa, Liza, na muhabbat, na Xudo bo'lmagan o'sha la'nati oilalarda bo'ladi, — deb qizg'in e'tiroz bildirdim, — muhabbat yo'q joyda esa aql ham yo'q. Bunday oilalar bor, to'g'ri, lekin men ular haqida gapirmayapman. Agar shunday gapirayotgan bo'lsang, o'z oilangda yovuzlikni ko'rgan bo'lsang kerak. Haqiqatan, sen omadsiz bo'lgan bo'lsang kerak. Hm!.. Bunday narsa asosan qashshoqlikdan kelib chiqadi.»

paras.en: "And is it any better with the gentry? Even among the poor, honest people who live happily?"
paras.uz: «Janoblarda yaxshiroqmi? Hatto kambag'allar orasida ham baxtli yashaydigan halol odamlar bor-ku?»

paras.en: "H'm ... Yes. Perhaps. Another thing, Liza, man is fond of reckoning up his troubles, but does not count his joys. If he counted them up as he ought, he would see that every lot has enough happiness provided for it. And what if all goes well with the family, if the blessing of God is upon it, if the husband is a good one, loves you, cherishes you, never leaves you! There is happiness in such a family! Even sometimes there is happiness in the midst of sorrow; and indeed sorrow is everywhere. If you marry you will find out for yourself. But think of the first years of married life with one you love: what happiness, what happiness there sometimes is in it! And indeed it's the ordinary thing. In those early days even quarrels with one's husband end happily. Some women get up quarrels with their husbands just because they love them.
paras.uz: «Hm... Ha. Balki. Yana bir narsa, Liza, inson o'z kulfatlarini sanashni yaxshi ko'radi, lekin quvonchlarini sanamaydi. Agar ularni kerakli tarzda sanasa, har bir qismatga yetarli baxt ajratilganini ko'rardi. Agar oilada hammasi yaxshi bo'lsa, unda Xudoning barakasi bo'lsa, eri yaxshi bo'lsa, seni sevsa, ardoqlasa, hech qachon tashlab ketmasa-chi! Bunday oilada baxt bor! Ba'zan hatto qayg'u o'rtasida ham baxt bo'ladi; qayg'u esa hamma joyda bor. Turmushga chiqsang, o'zing bilib olasan. Lekin sevgan odaming bilan turmushning birinchi yillarini o'yla: unda ba'zan qanday baxt, qanday baxt bo'ladi! Va bu haqiqatan oddiy narsa. O'sha dastlabki kunlarda hatto er bilan janjallar ham baxtli tugaydi. Ba'zi ayollar erlarini sevganlari uchungina ular bilan janjal ko'tarishadi.

paras.en: Indeed, I knew a woman like that: she seemed to say that because she loved him, she would torment him and make him feel it. You know that you may torment a man on purpose through love. Women are particularly given to that, thinking to themselves 'I will love him so, I will make so much of him afterwards, that it's no sin to torment him a little now.' And all in the house rejoice in the sight of you, and you are happy and gay and peaceful and honourable.... Then there are some women who are jealous. If he went off anywhere—I knew one such woman, she couldn't restrain herself, but would jump up at night and run off on the sly to find out where he was, whether he was with some other woman. That's a pity. And the woman knows herself it's wrong, and her heart fails her and she suffers, but she loves—it's all through love.
paras.uz: Haqiqatan, men shunday ayolni bilardim: u go'yo uni sevgani uchun uni qiynayman va buni his qildiraman, demoqchi edi. Bilasanmi, erkakni muhabbat tufayli ataylab qiynash mumkin. Ayollar ayniqsa bunga moyil, o'zlariga: «Men uni shunchalik sevaman, keyin uni shunchalik ardoqlayman-ki, hozir uni biroz qiynash gunoh emas», deb o'ylashadi. Uydagilarning hammasi seni ko'rib quvonadi, sen esa baxtli, quvnoq, osuda va sharaflisan... Keyin rashkchi ayollar ham bor. Agar u biror joyga ketsa — men shunday bir ayolni bilardim, u o'zini tutolmasdi, tunda sakrab turib, uning qayerdaligini, boshqa ayol bilan emasligini bilish uchun yashirincha yugurib ketardi. Bu achinarli. Ayolning o'zi ham bu noto'g'ri ekanini biladi, yuragi so'nadi, azob chekadi, lekin sevadi — hammasi muhabbatdan.

paras.en: And how sweet it is to make up after quarrels, to own herself in the wrong or to forgive him! And they both are so happy all at once—as though they had met anew, been married over again; as though their love had begun afresh. And no one, no one should know what passes between husband and wife if they love one another. And whatever quarrels there may be between them they ought not to call in their own mother to judge between them and tell tales of one another. They are their own judges. Love is a holy mystery and ought to be hidden from all other eyes, whatever happens. That makes it holier and better. They respect one another more, and much is built on respect. And if once there has been love, if they have been married for love, why should love pass away? Surely one can keep it! It is rare that one cannot keep it.
paras.uz: Janjallardan keyin yarashish, o'zini aybdor deb tan olish yoki uni kechirish qanchalik shirin! Ikkalasi birdan shunchalik baxtli bo'lishadi — go'yo yangidan uchrashgandek, qaytadan turmush qurgandek; go'yo muhabbatlari yangidan boshlangandek. Agar er-xotin bir-birini sevsa, ular o'rtasida nima bo'layotganini hech kim, hech kim bilmasligi kerak. Ular o'rtasida qanday janjallar bo'lmasin, o'z onalarini hakam qilib chaqirib, bir-birlari ustidan chaqimchilik qilmasliklari kerak. Ular o'zlari o'zlariga hakam. Muhabbat — muqaddas sir va nima bo'lmasin, barcha boshqa ko'zlardan yashirilishi kerak. Bu uni muqaddasroq va yaxshiroq qiladi. Ular bir-birini ko'proq hurmat qiladi, hurmat ustiga esa ko'p narsa quriladi. Agar bir marta muhabbat bo'lgan bo'lsa, agar ular muhabbat bilan turmush qurgan bo'lsa, nega muhabbat o'tib ketishi kerak? Axir uni saqlab qolish mumkin! Uni saqlab qolib bo'lmaydigan hol kamdan-kam.

paras.en: And if the husband is kind and straightforward, why should not love last? The first phase of married love will pass, it is true, but then there will come a love that is better still. Then there will be the union of souls, they will have everything in common, there will be no secrets between them. And once they have children, the most difficult times will seem to them happy, so long as there is love and courage. Even toil will be a joy, you may deny yourself bread for your children and even that will be a joy, They will love you for it afterwards; so you are laying by for your future. As the children grow up you feel that you are an example, a support for them; that even after you die your children will always keep your thoughts and feelings, because they have received them from you, they will take on your semblance and likeness. So you see this is a great duty.
paras.uz: Agar er mehribon va to'g'riso'z bo'lsa, nega muhabbat davom etmasligi kerak? Turmush muhabbatining birinchi bosqichi o'tadi, to'g'ri, lekin keyin undan ham yaxshiroq muhabbat keladi. Keyin qalblar birligi bo'ladi, ularda hamma narsa umumiy bo'ladi, ular o'rtasida hech qanday sir bo'lmaydi. Bolalari bo'lgach esa, muhabbat va jasorat bo'lsa, eng qiyin paytlar ham ularga baxtli tuyuladi. Hatto mehnat ham quvonch bo'ladi, bolalaring uchun nondan voz kechishing mumkin va hatto bu ham quvonch bo'ladi. Ular keyin buning uchun seni sevadi; demak, sen kelajaging uchun jamg'aryapsan. Bolalar o'sgan sari sen ular uchun namuna, tayanch ekaningni his qilasan; hatto sen o'lganingdan keyin ham bolalaring doimo sening fikr va tuyg'ularingni saqlaydi, chunki ularni sendan olgan, ular sening qiyofang va o'xshashligingni oladi. Ko'ryapsanmi, bu katta burch.

paras.en: How can it fail to draw the father and mother nearer? People say it's a trial to have children. Who says that? It is heavenly happiness! Are you fond of little children, Liza? I am awfully fond of them. You know—a little rosy baby boy at your bosom, and what husband's heart is not touched, seeing his wife nursing his child! A plump little rosy baby, sprawling and snuggling, chubby little hands and feet, clean tiny little nails, so tiny that it makes one laugh to look at them; eyes that look as if they understand everything. And while it sucks it clutches at your bosom with its little hand, plays. When its father comes up, the child tears itself away from the bosom, flings itself back, looks at its father, laughs, as though it were fearfully funny, and falls to sucking again.
paras.uz: Bu qanday qilib ota va onani bir-biriga yaqinlashtirmasligi mumkin? Odamlar bola ko'rish sinov deyishadi. Kim aytadi buni? Bu samoviy baxt! Kichkina bolalarni yaxshi ko'rasanmi, Liza? Men ularni dahshatli yaxshi ko'raman. Bilasanmi — ko'kragingdagi kichkina pushti o'g'il bola va xotinining farzandini emizayotganini ko'rib, qaysi erning yuragi ta'sirlanmaydi! To'lagina pushti chaqaloq, yoyilib, tiqilib yotadi, to'lagina qo'lchalari va oyoqchalari, toza mitti tirnoqlari, shunchalik mittiki, ularga qarab kulging keladi; hamma narsani tushunayotgandek ko'rinadigan ko'zlar. Emayotganda kichkina qo'li bilan ko'kragingga yopishadi, o'ynaydi. Otasi kelganda, bola ko'krakdan o'zini yulib, orqaga tashlanadi, otasiga qaraydi, kuladi, go'yo dahshatli kulgili bo'lgandek, va yana emishga tushadi.

paras.en: Or it will bite its mother's breast when its little teeth are coming, while it looks sideways at her with its little eyes as though to say, 'Look, I am biting!' Is not all that happiness when they are the three together, husband, wife and child? One can forgive a great deal for the sake of such moments. Yes, Liza, one must first learn to live oneself before one blames others!"
paras.uz: Yoki tishchalari chiqayotganda onasining ko'kragini tishlab oladi, ko'zchalari bilan unga yonboshlab qarab, go'yo: «Qara, tishlayapman!» degandek. Ular uchalasi birga — er, xotin va bola bo'lganda, bularning hammasi baxt emasmi? Bunday lahzalar uchun ko'p narsani kechirish mumkin. Ha, Liza, boshqalarni ayblashdan oldin avval o'zing yashashni o'rganishing kerak!»

paras.en: "It's by pictures, pictures like that one must get at you," I thought to myself, though I did speak with real feeling, and all at once I flushed crimson. "What if she were suddenly to burst out laughing, what should I do then?" That idea drove me to fury. Towards the end of my speech I really was excited, and now my vanity was somehow wounded. The silence continued. I almost nudged her.
paras.uz: «Seni mana shunday tasvirlar, tasvirlar bilan qo'lga olish kerak», — deb o'yladim ichimda, garchi haqiqiy tuyg'u bilan gapirgan bo'lsam ham, va birdan qip-qizarib ketdim. «Agar u birdan kulib yuborsa-chi, unda nima qilaman?» Bu fikr meni g'azabga soldi. Nutqimning oxiriga kelib men haqiqatan hayajonlangan edim, endi esa shuhratparastligim qandaydir yaralandi. Sukunat davom etdi. Men uni deyarli turtib qo'ydim.

paras.en: "Why are you—" she began and stopped. But I understood: there was a quiver of something different in her voice, not abrupt, harsh and unyielding as before, but something soft and shamefaced, so shamefaced that I suddenly felt ashamed and guilty.
paras.uz: «Nega siz...» — deb boshladi u va to'xtadi. Lekin men tushundim: uning ovozida boshqa nimadir titrardi, avvalgidek keskin, qo'pol va qaysar emas, balki qandaydir mayin va uyatchan, shunchalik uyatchanki, men birdan o'zimni uyatli va aybdor his qildim.

paras.en: "What?" I asked, with tender curiosity.
paras.uz: «Nima?» — deb mehrli qiziqish bilan so'radim.

paras.en: "Why, you..."
paras.uz: «Axir, siz...»

paras.en: "What?"
paras.uz: «Nima?»

paras.en: "Why, you ... Speak somehow like a book," she said, and again there was a note of irony in her voice.
paras.uz: «Axir, siz... qandaydir kitobdagidek gapirasiz», — dedi u va yana ovozida kinoya ohangi bor edi.

paras.en: That remark sent a pang to my heart. It was not what I was expecting.
paras.uz: Bu izoh yuragimga sanchiq bo'lib tegdi. Men buni kutmagan edim.

paras.en: I did not understand that she was hiding her feelings under irony, that this is usually the last refuge of modest and chaste-souled people when the privacy of their soul is coarsely and intrusively invaded, and that their pride makes them refuse to surrender till the last moment and shrink from giving expression to their feelings before you. I ought to have guessed the truth from the timidity with which she had repeatedly approached her sarcasm, only bringing herself to utter it at last with an effort. But I did not guess, and an evil feeling took possession of me.
paras.uz: Men uning tuyg'ularini kinoya ostida yashirayotganini, bu odatda kamtar va pok qalbli odamlarning qalbining ichki dunyosiga qo'pol va surbetlarcha bostirib kirilganda so'nggi panohi ekanini va ularning g'ururi oxirgi lahzagacha taslim bo'lishni rad etishga va oldingizda tuyg'ularini ifodalashdan tortinishga majbur qilishini tushunmadim. Men haqiqatni u kinoyasiga bir necha marta tortinib yaqinlashgani va oxiri uni zo'r berib aytishga jur'at etganidan taxmin qilishim kerak edi. Lekin taxmin qilmadim va meni yovuz tuyg'u egalladi.

paras.en: "Wait a bit!" I thought.
paras.uz: «Shoshma!» — deb o'yladim.

gloss.ex: "I saw them carrying a coffin out yesterday and they nearly dropped it," I suddenly said aloud, not that I desire…
…the same as that dead woman. She was ... A girl like you. She died of consumption."
…e to; you will be more and more fast in the snares. It is an accursed bondage. I know it. I won't speak of anything else, maybe you won't understand, but tell m…
…water at the bottom a foot deep. You can't dig a dry grave in Volkovo Cemetery."
…. Speak somehow like a book," she said, and again there was a note of irony in her voice.

quiz.q: Where does Liza come from?
quiz.why_uz: «Rigadan».

quiz.q: What does Liza say about the narrator's way of speaking?
quiz.why_uz: «Siz qandaydir kitobdagidek gapirasiz».

chapters.recap_uz: Tunda, qorong'i xonada hikoyachi Liza bilan gaplasha boshlaydi. U tobut, ho'l qabr, sildan o'lgan qiz haqida gapirib, uni qo'rqitadi; keyin oila, ota mehri, er-xotin muhabbati va chaqaloq haqida ta'sirli manzaralar chizadi. Liza: «Siz kitobdagidek gapirasiz», — deydi.

chapters.title: The letter

paras.en: "Oh, hush, Liza! How can you talk about being like a book, when it makes even me, an outsider, feel sick? Though I don't look at it as an outsider, for, indeed, it touches me to the heart.... Is it possible, is it possible that you do not feel sick at being here yourself? Evidently habit does wonders! God knows what habit can do with anyone. Can you seriously think that you will never grow old, that you will always be good-looking, and that they will keep you here for ever and ever? I say nothing of the loathsomeness of the life here.... Though let me tell you this about it—about your present life, I mean; here though you are young now, attractive, nice, with soul and feeling, yet you know as soon as I came to myself just now I felt at once sick at being here with you! One can only come here when one is drunk.
paras.uz: «Oh, jim, Liza! Qanday qilib kitobdek deb gapirasan, axir bu hatto menga, begona odamga ham ko'ngil aynitadi-ku? Garchi men bunga begona sifatida qaramasam ham, chunki haqiqatan bu yuragimga tegadi... Nahotki, nahotki o'zing bu yerda bo'lishdan ko'nglingni aynitmasa? Aftidan, odat mo''jizalar yaratadi! Odat har kim bilan nima qila olishini Xudo biladi. Nahotki jiddiy ravishda hech qachon qarimaysan, doim chiroyli bo'lasan va seni bu yerda abadul-abad saqlashadi deb o'ylasang? Bu yerdagi hayotning jirkanchligi haqida hech narsa demayman... Garchi bu haqda — ya'ni hozirgi hayoting haqida — senga shuni aytay; bu yerda sen hozir yosh, jozibali, yoqimli, ruhli va tuyg'uli bo'lsang ham, bilasanmi, men hozirgina o'zimga kelishim bilanoq bu yerda sen bilan bo'lishdan darhol ko'nglim aynidi! Bu yerga faqat mast bo'lganda kelish mumkin.

paras.en: But if you were anywhere else, living as good people live, I should perhaps be more than attracted by you, should fall in love with you, should be glad of a look from you, let alone a word; I should hang about your door, should go down on my knees to you, should look upon you as my betrothed and think it an honour to be allowed to. I should not dare to have an impure thought about you. But here, you see, I know that I have only to whistle and you have to come with me whether you like it or not. I don't consult your wishes, but you mine. The lowest labourer hires himself as a workman, but he doesn't make a slave of himself altogether; besides, he knows that he will be free again presently. But when are you free? Only think what you are giving up here? What is it you are making a slave of?
paras.uz: Lekin agar sen boshqa joyda, yaxshi odamlar yashaganidek yashaganingda, balki men sendan nafaqat maftun bo'lardim, oshiq bo'lardim, bir so'zing u yoqda tursin, bir nigohingdan xursand bo'lardim; eshiging oldida poylab yurardim, oldingda tiz cho'kardim, senga qallig'im deb qarardim va bunga ruxsat berilishini sharaf deb bilardim. Sen haqingda nopok fikr qilishga ham jur'at etmasdim. Lekin bu yerda, ko'ryapsanmi, men faqat hushtak chalishim kerakligini bilaman, sen esa xohlaysanmi-yo'qmi, men bilan borishing kerak. Men sening istaklaringni so'ramayman, sen esa meniklarini. Eng past ishchi ham o'zini ishchi sifatida yollaydi, lekin o'zini butunlay qulga aylantirmaydi; bundan tashqari, u tez orada yana erkin bo'lishini biladi. Sen esa qachon erkinsan? O'ylab ko'r, bu yerda nimadan voz kechyapsan? Nimani qulga aylantiryapsan?

paras.en: It is your soul, together with your body; you are selling your soul which you have no right to dispose of! You give your love to be outraged by every drunkard! Love! But that's everything, you know, it's a priceless diamond, it's a maiden's treasure, love—why, a man would be ready to give his soul, to face death to gain that love. But how much is your love worth now? You are sold, all of you, body and soul, and there is no need to strive for love when you can have everything without love. And you know there is no greater insult to a girl than that, do you understand? To be sure, I have heard that they comfort you, poor fools, they let you have lovers of your own here. But you know that's simply a farce, that's simply a sham, it's just laughing at you, and you are taken in by it! Why, do you suppose he really loves you, that lover of yours?
paras.uz: Bu sening ruhing, tanang bilan birga; sen tasarruf qilishga haqqing bo'lmagan ruhingni sotyapsan! Sen muhabbatingni har bir mastning tahqirlashiga beryapsan! Muhabbat! Axir bu hamma narsa, bilasan-ku, bu bebaho olmos, bu qizning xazinasi, muhabbat — axir erkak shu muhabbatni qozonish uchun ruhini berishga, o'limga borishga tayyor. Lekin sening muhabbating endi qanchaga arziydi? Sen sotilgansan, butunlay, tanang va ruhing bilan, va muhabbatsiz hamma narsaga ega bo'lish mumkin bo'lganda muhabbat uchun intilishning hojati yo'q. Bilasanmi, qiz uchun bundan katta haqorat yo'q, tushunasanmi? To'g'ri, men eshitganman, sizlarni, bechora ahmoqlarni, yupatishadi, bu yerda o'z oshiqlaringiz bo'lishiga ruxsat berishadi. Lekin bilasan, bu shunchaki masxarabozlik, shunchaki soxtalik, bu shunchaki sening ustingdan kulish, sen esa bunga aldanasan! Nima, u, o'sha oshig'ing, seni haqiqatan sevadi deb o'ylaysanmi?

paras.en: I don't believe it. How can he love you when he knows you may be called away from him any minute? He would be a low fellow if he did! Will he have a grain of respect for you? What have you in common with him? He laughs at you and robs you—that is all his love amounts to! You are lucky if he does not beat you. Very likely he does beat you, too. Ask him, if you have got one, whether he will marry you. He will laugh in your face, if he doesn't spit in it or give you a blow—though maybe he is not worth a bad halfpenny himself. And for what have you ruined your life, if you come to think of it? For the coffee they give you to drink and the plentiful meals? But with what object are they feeding you up? An honest girl couldn't swallow the food, for she would know what she was being fed for.
paras.uz: Men ishonmayman. Seni har daqiqa undan chaqirib olishlari mumkinligini bilgan holda u seni qanday sevishi mumkin? Agar sevsa, u tuban odam bo'lardi! Unda senga zarracha hurmat bo'ladimi? U bilan nima umumiy joying bor? U ustingdan kuladi va seni talaydi — uning butun muhabbati shu! Agar seni urmasa, omading bor. Ehtimol, u seni uradi ham. Agar shunday odaming bo'lsa, undan senga uylanadimi, deb so'ra. U yuzingga tupurmasa yoki urmasa, yuzingga qarab kuladi — garchi o'zi bir pulga ham arzimasa ham. Va o'ylab qarasang, hayotingni nima uchun barbod qilding? Senga ichish uchun beriladigan qahva va mo'l ovqatlar uchunmi? Lekin seni qanday maqsadda semirtirishyapti? Halol qiz bu ovqatni yuta olmasdi, chunki uni nima uchun boqishayotganini bilardi.

paras.en: You are in debt here, and, of course, you will always be in debt, and you will go on in debt to the end, till the visitors here begin to scorn you. And that will soon happen, don't rely upon your youth—all that flies by express train here, you know. You will be kicked out. And not simply kicked out; long before that she'll begin nagging at you, scolding you, abusing you, as though you had not sacrificed your health for her, had not thrown away your youth and your soul for her benefit, but as though you had ruined her, beggared her, robbed her. And don't expect anyone to take your part: the others, your companions, will attack you, too, win her favour, for all are in slavery here, and have lost all conscience and pity here long ago. They have become utterly vile, and nothing on earth is viler, more loathsome, and more insulting than their abuse.
paras.uz: Sen bu yerda qarzdorsan va, albatta, doim qarzdor bo'lasan, va bu yerdagi mehmonlar seni mensimay qo'ygunicha, oxirigacha qarzdor bo'lib yurasan. Bu esa tez orada bo'ladi, yoshligingga ishonma — bilasan, bu yerda hammasi tezyurar poyezddek uchib o'tadi. Seni tepib haydashadi. Va shunchaki tepib haydashmaydi; bundan ancha oldin u senga tirg'ala boshlaydi, koyiydi, so'kadi, go'yo sen uning uchun sog'lig'ingni qurbon qilmagandek, uning foydasi uchun yoshliging va ruhingni sovurmagandek, balki go'yo sen uni xonavayron qilgandek, tilanchi qilgandek, talagandek. Hech kim sening tarafingni olishini kutma: boshqalar, sheriklaring ham senga hujum qilib, uning marhamatini qozonishadi, chunki bu yerda hammasi qullikda va bu yerda vijdon va rahmni allaqachon yo'qotgan. Ular butunlay tubanlashib ketgan va yer yuzida ularning so'kishidan tubanroq, jirkanchroq va haqoratliroq narsa yo'q.

paras.en: And you are laying down everything here, unconditionally, youth and health and beauty and hope, and at twenty-two you will look like a woman of five-and-thirty, and you will be lucky if you are not diseased, pray to God for that! No doubt you are thinking now that you have a gay time and no work to do! Yet there is no work harder or more dreadful in the world or ever has been. One would think that the heart alone would be worn out with tears. And you won't dare to say a word, not half a word when they drive you away from here; you will go away as though you were to blame. You will change to another house, then to a third, then somewhere else, till you come down at last to the Haymarket. There you will be beaten at every turn; that is good manners there, the visitors don't know how to be friendly without beating you.
paras.uz: Sen esa bu yerda hamma narsangni so'zsiz qo'yyapsan — yoshlik, sog'liq, go'zallik va umidni, yigirma ikki yoshingda o'ttiz besh yoshli ayoldek ko'rinasan va agar kasal bo'lmasang, omading bor, buning uchun Xudoga duo qil! Shubhasiz, sen hozir quvnoq vaqt o'tkazyapman va hech qanday ish qilmayman deb o'ylayapsan! Holbuki dunyoda bundan og'irroq yoki dahshatliroq ish yo'q va hech qachon bo'lmagan. Faqat yurakning o'zi ko'z yoshlardan yemirilib ketishi kerakdek tuyuladi. Seni bu yerdan haydashganda, bir og'iz so'z, yarim og'iz so'z ham aytishga jur'at etmaysan; go'yo aybdor bo'lgandek ketasan. Boshqa uyga o'tasan, keyin uchinchisiga, keyin boshqa joyga, oxiri Pichanbozorga tushib qolguningcha. U yerda seni har qadamda urishadi; bu u yerda odob, mehmonlar seni urmasdan do'stona bo'lishni bilishmaydi.

paras.en: You don't believe that it is so hateful there? Go and look for yourself some time, you can see with your own eyes. Once, one New Year's Day, I saw a woman at a door. They had turned her out as a joke, to give her a taste of the frost because she had been crying so much, and they shut the door behind her. At nine o'clock in the morning she was already quite drunk, dishevelled, half-naked, covered with bruises, her face was powdered, but she had a black-eye, blood was trickling from her nose and her teeth; some cabman had just given her a drubbing. She was sitting on the stone steps, a salt fish of some sort was in her hand; she was crying, wailing something about her luck and beating with the fish on the steps, and cabmen and drunken soldiers were crowding in the doorway taunting her. You don't believe that you will ever be like that?
paras.uz: U yerda shunchalik jirkanch ekaniga ishonmaysanmi? Bir kun borib o'zing qara, o'z ko'zing bilan ko'rasan. Bir marta, Yangi yil kuni, men eshik oldida bir ayolni ko'rdim. Uni shunchaki hazil uchun, juda ko'p yig'lagani uchun ayozni totib ko'rsin deb tashqariga haydab, orqasidan eshikni yopishgan edi. Ertalab soat to'qqizda u allaqachon butunlay mast, sochlari to'zg'igan, yarim yalang'och, ko'karishlar bilan qoplangan edi, yuzi upa surtilgan, lekin ko'zi ko'kargan, burni va tishlaridan qon sizib turardi; qandaydir izvoshchi hozirgina uni do'pposlagan edi. U tosh zinapoyada o'tirardi, qo'lida qandaydir sho'r baliq bor edi; u yig'lab, omadi haqida nimadir deb faryod qilar va baliq bilan zinapoyani urardi, eshik oldida esa izvoshchilar va mast askarlar to'planib, uni masxara qilishardi. Sen hech qachon shunday bo'lishingga ishonmaysanmi?

paras.en: I should be sorry to believe it, too, but how do you know; maybe ten years, eight years ago that very woman with the salt fish came here fresh as a cherub, innocent, pure, knowing no evil, blushing at every word. Perhaps she was like you, proud, ready to take offence, not like the others; perhaps she looked like a queen, and knew what happiness was in store for the man who should love her and whom she should love. Do you see how it ended?
paras.uz: Men ham ishonishni istamasdim, lekin qayerdan bilasan; balki o'n yil, sakkiz yil oldin sho'r baliqli o'sha ayol bu yerga farishtadek yangi, beg'ubor, pok, yovuzlikni bilmaydigan, har bir so'zdan qizaradigan holda kelgandir. Balki u ham sendek mag'rur, tez xafa bo'ladigan, boshqalarga o'xshamagan bo'lgandir; balki u malikadek ko'ringan va uni sevadigan va o'zi sevadigan odamni qanday baxt kutayotganini bilgandir. Qanday tugaganini ko'ryapsanmi?

paras.en: And what if at that very minute when she was beating on the filthy steps with that fish, drunken and dishevelled—what if at that very minute she recalled the pure early days in her father's house, when she used to go to school and the neighbour's son watched for her on the way, declaring that he would love her as long as he lived, that he would devote his life to her, and when they vowed to love one another for ever and be married as soon as they were grown up! No, Liza, it would be happy for you if you were to die soon of consumption in some corner, in some cellar like that woman just now. In the hospital, do you say? You will be lucky if they take you, but what if you are still of use to the madam here? Consumption is a queer disease, it is not like fever. The patient goes on hoping till the last minute and says he is all right.
paras.uz: Agar aynan o'sha daqiqada, u mast va sochlari to'zg'igan holda iflos zinapoyani o'sha baliq bilan urayotganda — agar aynan o'sha daqiqada u otasining uyidagi pok ilk kunlarini, maktabga borganini va qo'shnining o'g'li yo'lda uni poylab, butun umri davomida uni sevishini, hayotini unga bag'ishlashini aytganini va ular katta bo'lishlari bilanoq bir-birlarini abadiy sevishga va turmush qurishga qasam ichganlarini eslagan bo'lsa-chi! Yo'q, Liza, agar sen tez orada qandaydir burchakda, qandaydir podvalda, hozirgi o'sha ayol kabi sildan o'lsang, bu sen uchun baxt bo'lardi. Kasalxonada deysanmi? Agar seni olishsa, omading bor, lekin agar sen hali bu yerdagi madam uchun foydali bo'lsang-chi? Sil — g'alati kasallik, u isitmaga o'xshamaydi. Bemor oxirgi daqiqagacha umid qiladi va o'zini yaxshi deydi.

paras.en: He deludes himself And that just suits your madam. Don't doubt it, that's how it is; you have sold your soul, and what is more you owe money, so you daren't say a word. But when you are dying, all will abandon you, all will turn away from you, for then there will be nothing to get from you. What's more, they will reproach you for cumbering the place, for being so long over dying. However you beg you won't get a drink of water without abuse: 'Whenever are you going off, you nasty hussy, you won't let us sleep with your moaning, you make the gentlemen sick.' That's true, I have heard such things said myself. They will thrust you dying into the filthiest corner in the cellar—in the damp and darkness; what will your thoughts be, lying there alone?
paras.uz: U o'zini aldaydi. Bu esa madamingga aynan qo'l keladi. Shubhalanma, shunday; sen ruhingni sotgansan, buning ustiga qarzdorsan, shuning uchun bir og'iz so'z aytishga jur'at etmaysan. Lekin o'layotganingda, hamma seni tashlab ketadi, hamma sendan yuz o'giradi, chunki o'shanda sendan oladigan hech narsa qolmaydi. Bundan ham ortig'i, joyni band qilganing, shunchalik uzoq o'layotganing uchun seni ta'na qilishadi. Qanchalik yolvorma, so'kishsiz bir qultum suv ham olmaysan: «Qachon ketasan, jirkanch qanjiq, ingrashing bilan uxlatmaysan, janoblarning ko'nglini aynitasan.» Bu rost, bunday gaplarni o'zim eshitganman. Seni o'layotgan holda podvaldagi eng iflos burchakka — namlik va zulmatga tiqishadi; u yerda yolg'iz yotib, nimalarni o'ylaysan?

paras.en: When you die, strange hands will lay you out, with grumbling and impatience; no one will bless you, no one will sigh for you, they only want to get rid of you as soon as may be; they will buy a coffin, take you to the grave as they did that poor woman today, and celebrate your memory at the tavern. In the grave, sleet, filth, wet snow—no need to put themselves out for you—'Let her down, Vanuha; it's just like her luck—even here, she is head-foremost, the hussy. Shorten the cord, you rascal.' 'It's all right as it is.' 'All right, is it? Why, she's on her side! She was a fellow-creature, after all! But, never mind, throw the earth on her.' And they won't care to waste much time quarrelling over you. They will scatter the wet blue clay as quick as they can and go off to the tavern ...
paras.uz: O'lganingda, begona qo'llar seni to'ng'illab va sabrsizlik bilan yuvib-taraydi; hech kim seni duo qilmaydi, hech kim sen uchun xo'rsinmaydi, ular faqat sendan iloji boricha tezroq qutulishni istashadi; tobut sotib olishadi, bugungi o'sha bechora ayol kabi seni qabrga olib borishadi va maykhonada xotirangni nishonlashadi. Qabrda yomg'irli qor, loy, ho'l qor — sen uchun o'zlarini qiynash shart emas: «Tushir uni, Vanyuxa; bu uning omadiga o'xshaydi — bu yerda ham boshi pastga, qanjiq. Arqonni qisqartir, yaramas.» «Shundayligicha ham bo'ladi.» «Bo'ladimi? Axir u yonboshlab yotibdi! U ham inson edi-ku! Lekin mayli, ustiga tuproq tashla.» Ular sen uchun janjallashib ko'p vaqt sarflashni ham istamaydi. Ho'l ko'k loyni iloji boricha tezroq sochib, maykhonaga jo'nashadi...

paras.en: And there your memory on earth will end; other women have children to go to their graves, fathers, husbands. While for you neither tear, nor sigh, nor remembrance; no one in the whole world will ever come to you, your name will vanish from the face of the earth—as though you had never existed, never been born at all! Nothing but filth and mud, however you knock at your coffin lid at night, when the dead arise, however you cry: 'Let me out, kind people, to live in the light of day! My life was no life at all; my life has been thrown away like a dish-clout; it was drunk away in the tavern at the Haymarket; let me out, kind people, to live in the world again.'"
paras.uz: Shu bilan yer yuzidagi xotirang tugaydi; boshqa ayollarning qabriga boradigan bolalari, otalari, erlari bor. Sen uchun esa na ko'z yoshi, na xo'rsinish, na xotira; butun dunyoda hech kim hech qachon oldingga kelmaydi, isming yer yuzidan yo'qoladi — go'yo sen hech qachon mavjud bo'lmagandek, umuman tug'ilmagandek! Faqat iflos va loy, tunda, o'liklar turganda tobuting qopqog'ini qanchalik taqillatma, qanchalik qichqirma: «Meni chiqaringlar, yaxshi odamlar, kunduz yorug'ida yashay! Mening hayotim hayot emas edi; hayotim kir latta kabi uloqtirildi; u Pichanbozordagi maykhonada ichib bitirildi; meni chiqaringlar, yaxshi odamlar, yana dunyoda yashay.»»

paras.en: And I worked myself up to such a pitch that I began to have a lump in my throat myself, and ... And all at once I stopped, sat up in dismay and, bending over apprehensively, began to listen with a beating heart. I had reason to be troubled.
paras.uz: Va men o'zimni shunday darajaga yetkazdimki, o'zimning ham tomog'imga nimadir tiqila boshladi va... birdan to'xtadim, sarosimada o'tirib oldim va xavotir bilan engashib, yuragim urib tinglay boshladim. Bezovta bo'lishimga sabab bor edi.

paras.en: I had felt for some time that I was turning her soul upside down and rending her heart, and—and the more I was convinced of it, the more eagerly I desired to gain my object as quickly and as effectually as possible. It was the exercise of my skill that carried me away; yet it was not merely sport....
paras.uz: Men anchadan beri uning qalbini ag'dar-to'ntar qilayotganimni va yuragini parchalayotganimni his qilardim va — va bunga qanchalik ko'p ishonch hosil qilsam, maqsadimga iloji boricha tezroq va samaraliroq erishishni shunchalik ishtiyoq bilan istardim. Meni mahoratimni ishga solish olib ketgan edi; lekin bu shunchaki o'yin emas edi...

paras.en: I knew I was speaking stiffly, artificially, even bookishly, in fact, I could not speak except "like a book." But that did not trouble me: I knew, I felt that I should be understood and that this very bookishness might be an assistance. But now, having attained my effect, I was suddenly panic-stricken. Never before had I witnessed such despair! She was lying on her face, thrusting her face into the pillow and clutching it in both hands. Her heart was being torn. Her youthful body was shuddering all over as though in convulsions. Suppressed sobs rent her bosom and suddenly burst out in weeping and wailing, then she pressed closer into the pillow: she did not want anyone here, not a living soul, to know of her anguish and her tears. She bit the pillow, bit her hand till it bled (I saw that afterwards), or, thrusting her fingers into her dishevelled hair, seemed rigid with the effort of restraint, holding her breath and clenching her teeth.
paras.uz: Men qotib, sun'iy, hatto kitobiy gapirayotganimni bilardim, aslida men «kitobdek»dan boshqacha gapira olmasdim. Lekin bu meni bezovta qilmasdi: men bilardim, his qilardimki, meni tushunishadi va aynan shu kitobiylik yordam berishi mumkin. Lekin endi, ta'sirimga erishgach, birdan vahimaga tushdim. Men ilgari hech qachon bunday umidsizlikning guvohi bo'lmagan edim! U yuztuban yotib, yuzini yostiqqa tiqib, uni ikki qo'li bilan changallab olgan edi. Uning yuragi parchalanayotgan edi. Uning yosh tanasi go'yo talvasada butunlay titrardi. Bo'g'ilgan yig'i ko'ksini yorib, birdan faryod va nolaga aylanib chiqardi, keyin u yostiqqa yanada mahkamroq bosilardi: u bu yerda hech kimning, birorta ham tirik jonning iztirobi va ko'z yoshlaridan xabar topishini istamasdi. U yostiqni tishlar, qo'lini qonaguncha tishlardi (buni keyin ko'rdim) yoki barmoqlarini to'zg'igan sochlariga tiqib, o'zini tutishga zo'r berib, nafasini ushlab, tishlarini g'ijirlatib qotib qolgandek bo'lardi.

paras.en: I began saying something, begging her to calm herself, but felt that I did not dare; and all at once, in a sort of cold shiver, almost in terror, began fumbling in the dark, trying hurriedly to get dressed to go. It was dark; though I tried my best I could not finish dressing quickly. Suddenly I felt a box of matches and a candlestick with a whole candle in it. As soon as the room was lighted up, Liza sprang up, sat up in bed, and with a contorted face, with a half insane smile, looked at me almost senselessly. I sat down beside her and took her hands; she came to herself, made an impulsive movement towards me, would have caught hold of me, but did not dare, and slowly bowed her head before me.
paras.uz: Men nimadir deya boshladim, undan tinchlanishini so'radim, lekin jur'at etmasligimni his qildim; va birdan qandaydir sovuq titroq ichida, deyarli dahshat bilan, ketish uchun shoshilib kiyinishga urinib, qorong'ida paypaslay boshladim. Qorong'i edi; qanchalik urinmay, tez kiyinib bo'la olmadim. Birdan qo'limga gugurt qutisi va butun shamli shamdon tegdi. Xona yorishishi bilanoq Liza sakrab turib, karavotda o'tirdi va qiyshaygan yuz bilan, yarim telbavor tabassum bilan menga deyarli ma'nosiz qaradi. Men uning yoniga o'tirib, qo'llarini ushladim; u o'ziga keldi, menga beixtiyor intildi, meni ushlab olmoqchi bo'ldi, lekin jur'at etmadi va asta oldimda boshini egdi.

paras.en: "Liza, my dear, I was wrong ... Forgive me, my dear," I began, but she squeezed my hand in her fingers so tightly that I felt I was saying the wrong thing and stopped.
paras.uz: «Liza, azizim, men xato qildim... meni kechir, azizim», — deb boshladim, lekin u qo'limni barmoqlari bilan shunchalik qattiq qisdiki, noto'g'ri gap aytayotganimni his qilib, to'xtadim.

paras.en: "This is my address, Liza, come to me."
paras.uz: «Mana mening manzilim, Liza, menikiga kel.»

paras.en: "I will come," she answered resolutely, her head still bowed.
paras.uz: «Kelaman», — deb qat'iy javob berdi u, boshi hali ham egik.

paras.en: "But now I am going, good-bye ... Till we meet again."
paras.uz: «Lekin hozir ketyapman, xayr... ko'rishguncha.»

paras.en: I got up; she, too, stood up and suddenly flushed all over, gave a shudder, snatched up a shawl that was lying on a chair and muffled herself in it to her chin. As she did this she gave another sickly smile, blushed and looked at me strangely. I felt wretched; I was in haste to get away—to disappear.
paras.uz: Men o'rnimdan turdim; u ham turdi va birdan butunlay qizarib ketdi, seskandi, kursida yotgan ro'molni olib, unga iyagigacha o'randi. Buni qilarkan, u yana xasta jilmaydi, qizardi va menga g'alati qaradi. O'zimni ayanchli his qildim; ketishga — g'oyib bo'lishga shoshilardim.

paras.en: "Wait a minute," she said suddenly, in the passage just at the doorway, stopping me with her hand on my overcoat. She put down the candle in hot haste and ran off; evidently she had thought of something or wanted to show me something. As she ran away she flushed, her eyes shone, and there was a smile on her lips—what was the meaning of it? Against my will I waited: she came back a minute later with an expression that seemed to ask forgiveness for something. In fact, it was not the same face, not the same look as the evening before: sullen, mistrustful and obstinate. Her eyes now were imploring, soft, and at the same time trustful, caressing, timid. The expression with which children look at people they are very fond of, of whom they are asking a favour. Her eyes were a light hazel, they were lovely eyes, full of life, and capable of expressing love as well as sullen hatred.
paras.uz: «Bir daqiqa kuting», — dedi u birdan, yo'lakda, aynan eshik oldida, qo'lini paltoimga qo'yib meni to'xtatib. U shamni shoshilib qo'ydi va yugurib ketdi; aftidan, u nimanidir eslagan yoki menga nimanidir ko'rsatmoqchi edi. Yugurib ketarkan, u qizardi, ko'zlari porladi, lablarida tabassum bor edi — bu nimani anglatardi? Irodamga qarshi kutdim: u bir daqiqadan keyin go'yo nimadir uchun kechirim so'rayotgandek ifoda bilan qaytdi. Haqiqatan, bu kechagi oqshomdagi yuz emas, o'sha nigoh emas edi: qovog'i soliq, ishonchsiz va qaysar. Uning ko'zlari endi yolvoruvchi, mayin va ayni paytda ishonuvchan, erkalovchi, tortinchoq edi. Bolalar juda yaxshi ko'radigan va biror narsa so'rayotgan odamlariga shunday qarashadi. Uning ko'zlari och jigarrang edi, ular go'zal ko'zlar edi, hayotga to'la, muhabbatni ham, qovog'i soliq nafratni ham ifodalashga qodir.

paras.en: Making no explanation, as though I, as a sort of higher being, must understand everything without explanations, she held out a piece of paper to me. Her whole face was positively beaming at that instant with naive, almost childish, triumph. I unfolded it. It was a letter to her from a medical student or someone of that sort—a very high-flown and flowery, but extremely respectful, love-letter. I don't recall the words now, but I remember well that through the high-flown phrases there was apparent a genuine feeling, which cannot be feigned. When I had finished reading it I met her glowing, questioning, and childishly impatient eyes fixed upon me. She fastened her eyes upon my face and waited impatiently for what I should say.
paras.uz: Hech qanday tushuntirish bermasdan, go'yo men qandaydir oliy mavjudot sifatida hamma narsani tushuntirishsiz tushunishim kerakdek, u menga bir varaq qog'oz uzatdi. O'sha lahzada uning butun yuzi sodda, deyarli bolalarcha g'alaba bilan rosa porlab turardi. Men uni ochdim. Bu unga qandaydir tibbiyot talabasi yoki shunga o'xshash kimsadan kelgan maktub edi — juda balandparvoz va gulli, lekin nihoyatda hurmatli sevgi maktubi. So'zlarini hozir eslamayman, lekin balandparvoz iboralar orqali soxtalashtirib bo'lmaydigan haqiqiy tuyg'u ko'rinib turganini yaxshi eslayman. O'qib bo'lgach, menga tikilgan uning porlab turgan, so'roqli va bolalarcha sabrsiz ko'zlariga duch keldim. U ko'zlarini yuzimga qadab, nima deyishimni sabrsizlik bilan kutardi.

paras.en: In a few words, hurriedly, but with a sort of joy and pride, she explained to me that she had been to a dance somewhere in a private house, a family of "very nice people, who knew nothing, absolutely nothing, for she had only come here so lately and it had all happened ... And she hadn't made up her mind to stay and was certainly going away as soon as she had paid her debt..." And at that party there had been the student who had danced with her all the evening. He had talked to her, and it turned out that he had known her in old days at Riga when he was a child, they had played together, but a very long time ago—and he knew her parents, but about this he knew nothing, nothing whatever, and had no suspicion! And the day after the dance (three days ago) he had sent her that letter through the friend with whom she had gone to the party ...
paras.uz: Bir necha so'z bilan, shoshilib, lekin qandaydir quvonch va g'urur bilan u menga qayerdadir xususiy uyda, «hech narsani, mutlaqo hech narsani bilmaydigan juda yaxshi odamlar» oilasida raqs kechasida bo'lganini tushuntirdi, «chunki u bu yerga juda yaqinda kelgan va hammasi endigina... u qolishga hali qaror qilmagan va qarzini to'lashi bilanoq albatta ketadi...» O'sha kechada butun oqshom u bilan raqsga tushgan talaba bor edi. U u bilan gaplashgan va ma'lum bo'lishicha, u uni eski kunlarda, bolaligida Rigada tanigan, ular birga o'ynashgan, lekin juda uzoq vaqt oldin — u ota-onasini ham bilardi, lekin bu haqda u hech narsa, mutlaqo hech narsa bilmasdi va hech qanday shubhasi yo'q edi! Raqs kechasidan keyingi kun (uch kun oldin) u o'sha maktubni u kechaga birga borgan dugonasi orqali yuborgan edi...

paras.en: And ... Well, that was all.
paras.uz: Va... xo'sh, hammasi shu.

paras.en: She dropped her shining eyes with a sort of bashfulness as she finished.
paras.uz: Tugatarkan, u porlab turgan ko'zlarini qandaydir uyatchanlik bilan yerga tushirdi.

paras.en: The poor girl was keeping that student's letter as a precious treasure, and had run to fetch it, her only treasure, because she did not want me to go away without knowing that she, too, was honestly and genuinely loved; that she, too, was addressed respectfully. No doubt that letter was destined to lie in her box and lead to nothing. But none the less, I am certain that she would keep it all her life as a precious treasure, as her pride and justification, and now at such a minute she had thought of that letter and brought it with naive pride to raise herself in my eyes that I might see, that I, too, might think well of her. I said nothing, pressed her hand and went out. I so longed to get away ... I walked all the way home, in spite of the fact that the melting snow was still falling in heavy flakes. I was exhausted, shattered, in bewilderment. But behind the bewilderment the truth was already gleaming. The loathsome truth.
paras.uz: Bechora qiz o'sha talabaning maktubini qimmatbaho xazina sifatida saqlardi va yagona xazinasini olib kelish uchun yugurgan edi, chunki men uni ham halol va chin dildan sevishlarini, unga ham hurmat bilan murojaat qilishlarini bilmasdan ketishimni istamasdi. Shubhasiz, o'sha maktub uning qutisida yotib, hech narsaga olib kelmasligi kerak edi. Shunga qaramay, ishonchim komilki, u uni butun umri davomida qimmatbaho xazina sifatida, o'z g'ururi va oqlanishi sifatida saqlaydi, endi esa shunday daqiqada u o'sha maktubni eslab, ko'z oldimda o'zini ko'tarish uchun, men ko'rishim, men ham u haqida yaxshi o'ylashim uchun uni sodda g'urur bilan olib keldi. Men hech narsa demadim, qo'lini qisdim va chiqib ketdim. Ketishni shunchalik istardim... Eriyotgan qor hali ham og'ir parchalar bo'lib yog'ishiga qaramay, uyimgacha piyoda yurdim. Men holdan toygan, ezilgan, sarosimada edim. Lekin sarosima ortida allaqachon haqiqat yaltirab turardi. Jirkanch haqiqat.

gloss.ex: …soul which you have no right to dispose of! You give your love to be outraged by every drunkard! Love! But that's everything, you know, it's a priceless diamon…
…had just given her a drubbing. She was sitting on the stone steps, a salt fish of some sort was in her hand; she was crying, wailing something about her luck a…
…ect, I was suddenly panic-stricken. Never before had I witnessed such despair! She was lying on her face, thrusting her face into the pillow and clutching it in…
"This is my address, Liza, come to me."
…lmost childish, triumph. I unfolded it. It was a letter to her from a medical student or someone of that sort—a very high-flown and flowery, but extremely respe…

quiz.q: What does Liza show the narrator before he leaves?
o: A love letter from a student
quiz.why_uz: Tibbiyot talabasidan kelgan hurmatli sevgi maktubi.

quiz.q: How does Liza react to his speech?
quiz.why_uz: U yostiqqa yuzini bosib, umidsiz yig'laydi.

chapters.recap_uz: Hikoyachi Lizaga uning kelajagi — Pichanbozordagi podval, sildan o'lim, unutilgan qabr haqida dahshatli nutq so'zlaydi. Liza yostiqqa yuzini bosib, umidsiz yig'laydi. Ketish oldidan hikoyachi unga manzilini beradi; Liza esa unga talabadan kelgan hurmatli sevgi maktubini ko'rsatadi.

chapters.title: Waiting and Apollon

paras.en: It was some time, however, before I consented to recognise that truth. Waking up in the morning after some hours of heavy, leaden sleep, and immediately realising all that had happened on the previous day, I was positively amazed at my last night's sentimentality with Liza, at all those "outcries of horror and pity." "To think of having such an attack of womanish hysteria, pah!" I concluded. And what did I thrust my address upon her for? What if she comes? Let her come, though; it doesn't matter.... But obviously, that was not now the chief and the most important matter: I had to make haste and at all costs save my reputation in the eyes of Zverkov and Simonov as quickly as possible; that was the chief business. And I was so taken up that morning that I actually forgot all about Liza.
paras.uz: Biroq bu haqiqatni tan olishga rozi bo'lgunimcha ancha vaqt o'tdi. Bir necha soatlik og'ir, qo'rg'oshindek uyqudan keyin ertalab uyg'onib, oldingi kuni bo'lgan hamma narsani darhol anglagach, men kechagi kechadagi Liza bilan hissiyotchanligimdan, o'sha barcha «dahshat va rahm faryodlari»dan rosa hayratga tushdim. «Bunday xotinchalish isteriya xurujiga uchrash-a, tfu!» — deb xulosa qildim. Va nega unga manzilimni tiqishtirdim? Agar kelsa-chi? Mayli, kelaversin; farqi yo'q... Lekin, aniqki, hozir asosiy va eng muhim masala bu emas edi: men shoshilishim va har qanday holatda Zverkov va Simonov ko'zida obro'imni iloji boricha tezroq saqlab qolishim kerak edi; asosiy ish shu edi. O'sha kuni ertalab shunchalik band edimki, Liza haqida butunlay unutib qo'ydim.

paras.en: First of all I had at once to repay what I had borrowed the day before from Simonov. I resolved on a desperate measure: to borrow fifteen roubles straight off from Anton Antonitch. As luck would have it he was in the best of humours that morning, and gave it to me at once, on the first asking. I was so delighted at this that, as I signed the IOU with a swaggering air, I told him casually that the night before "I had been keeping it up with some friends at the Hotel de Paris; we were giving a farewell party to a comrade, in fact, I might say a friend of my childhood, and you know—a desperate rake, fearfully spoilt—of course, he belongs to a good family, and has considerable means, a brilliant career; he is witty, charming, a regular Lovelace, you understand; we drank an extra 'half-dozen' and ..."
paras.uz: Avvalo kecha Simonovdan qarz olganimni darhol qaytarishim kerak edi. Men umidsiz choraga qaror qildim: Anton Antonovichdan birdaniga o'n besh rubl qarz olish. Omadimga, o'sha kuni ertalab u eng yaxshi kayfiyatda edi va birinchi so'rashimdayoq darhol berdi. Bundan shunchalik xursand bo'ldimki, tilxatga kerilib imzo chekarkanman, unga yo'l-yo'lakay kecha «Parij mehmonxonasida do'stlar bilan ko'ngil ochganimni; bir o'rtog'imiz, aniqrog'i, bolalikdagi do'stim bilan xayrlashuv kechasi qilganimizni, bilasizmi — ashaddiy shalpang, dahshatli erka — albatta, yaxshi oiladan, ancha boy, yorqin martabasi bor; u o'tkir, maftunkor, haqiqiy Lovelas, tushunasizmi; biz ortiqcha «yarim dyujina» ichdik va...» dedim.

paras.en: And it went off all right; all this was uttered very easily, unconstrainedly and complacently.
paras.uz: Va hammasi yaxshi o'tdi; bularning hammasi juda oson, erkin va mamnunlik bilan aytildi.

paras.en: On reaching home I promptly wrote to Simonov.
paras.uz: Uyga yetgach, darhol Simonovga xat yozdim.

paras.en: To this hour I am lost in admiration when I recall the truly gentlemanly, good-humoured, candid tone of my letter. With tact and good-breeding, and, above all, entirely without superfluous words, I blamed myself for all that had happened. I defended myself, "if I really may be allowed to defend myself," by alleging that being utterly unaccustomed to wine, I had been intoxicated with the first glass, which I said, I had drunk before they arrived, while I was waiting for them at the Hotel de Paris between five and six o'clock. I begged Simonov's pardon especially; I asked him to convey my explanations to all the others, especially to Zverkov, whom "I seemed to remember as though in a dream" I had insulted. I added that I would have called upon all of them myself, but my head ached, and besides I had not the face to.
paras.uz: Shu soatgacha maktubimning chinakam janoblarcha, xushfe'l, ochiq ohangini eslaganimda hayratga tushaman. Nazokat va yaxshi tarbiya bilan va, eng muhimi, mutlaqo ortiqcha so'zlarsiz, men bo'lib o'tgan hamma narsa uchun o'zimni aybladim. Men o'zimni «agar haqiqatan o'zimni himoya qilishga ruxsat berilsa» deb, vinoga mutlaqo odatlanmaganim uchun birinchi qadahdan mast bo'lib qolganim bilan himoya qildim, uni, dedim, ular kelishidan oldin, Parij mehmonxonasida beshdan oltigacha ularni kutayotganimda ichganman. Ayniqsa Simonovdan kechirim so'radim; undan tushuntirishlarimni boshqalarga, ayniqsa «go'yo tushdagidek eslayotgan» Zverkovga, uni haqorat qilganimni yetkazishni so'radim. Ularning hammasini o'zim ziyorat qilgan bo'lardim, lekin boshim og'riyapti va bundan tashqari yuzim chidamaydi, deb qo'shimcha qildim.

paras.en: I was particularly pleased with a certain lightness, almost carelessness (strictly within the bounds of politeness, however), which was apparent in my style, and better than any possible arguments, gave them at once to understand that I took rather an independent view of "all that unpleasantness last night"; that I was by no means so utterly crushed as you, my friends, probably imagine; but on the contrary, looked upon it as a gentleman serenely respecting himself should look upon it. "On a young hero's past no censure is cast!"
paras.uz: Ayniqsa uslubimda ko'rinib turgan qandaydir yengillik, deyarli beparvolik (biroq qat'iy xushmuomalalik chegarasida) menga yoqdi, u har qanday mumkin bo'lgan dalillardan yaxshiroq ularga darhol men «kechagi o'sha butun noxushlik»ka ancha mustaqil qarashimni tushuntirib qo'yardi; men siz, do'stlarim, ehtimol tasavvur qilganingizdek, butunlay ezilgan emasman; aksincha, unga o'zini xotirjam hurmat qiladigan janob qanday qarashi kerak bo'lsa, shunday qarayman. «Yosh qahramonning o'tmishiga ta'na yo'q!»

paras.en: "There is actually an aristocratic playfulness about it!" I thought admiringly, as I read over the letter. "And it's all because I am an intellectual and cultivated man! Another man in my place would not have known how to extricate himself, but here I have got out of it and am as jolly as ever again, and all because I am 'a cultivated and educated man of our day.' And, indeed, perhaps, everything was due to the wine yesterday. H'm!" ... No, it was not the wine. I did not drink anything at all between five and six when I was waiting for them. I had lied to Simonov; I had lied shamelessly; and indeed I wasn't ashamed now.... Hang it all though, the great thing was that I was rid of it.
paras.uz: «Unda hatto aristokratik o'ynoqilik bor! — deb o'yladim maktubni qayta o'qib, hayratlanib. — Va hammasi men ziyoli va madaniyatli odam bo'lganim uchun! Mening o'rnimda boshqa odam qanday qutulishni bilmagan bo'lardi, men esa mana qutulib chiqdim va yana avvalgidek quvnoqman, hammasi men «zamonamizning madaniyatli va o'qimishli odami» bo'lganim uchun. Va haqiqatan, balki, hammasi kechagi vino tufayli edi. Hm!»... Yo'q, vino tufayli emas edi. Men beshdan oltigacha ularni kutayotganimda umuman hech narsa ichmagan edim. Simonovga yolg'on gapirdim; uyatsizlarcha yolg'on gapirdim; va haqiqatan hozir uyalmasdim... Jin ursin, asosiysi undan qutulganim edi.

paras.en: I put six roubles in the letter, sealed it up, and asked Apollon to take it to Simonov. When he learned that there was money in the letter, Apollon became more respectful and agreed to take it. Towards evening I went out for a walk. My head was still aching and giddy after yesterday. But as evening came on and the twilight grew denser, my impressions and, following them, my thoughts, grew more and more different and confused. Something was not dead within me, in the depths of my heart and conscience it would not die, and it showed itself in acute depression. For the most part I jostled my way through the most crowded business streets, along Myeshtchansky Street, along Sadovy Street and in Yusupov Garden. I always liked particularly sauntering along these streets in the dusk, just when there were crowds of working people of all sorts going home from their daily work, with faces looking cross with anxiety.
paras.uz: Maktubga olti rubl solib, muhrladim va Apollondan uni Simonovga olib borishni so'radim. Maktubda pul borligini bilgach, Apollon hurmatliroq bo'lib, uni olib borishga rozi bo'ldi. Kechga yaqin sayrga chiqdim. Boshim kechadan keyin hali ham og'rib, aylanardi. Lekin kech kirib, g'ira-shira quyuqlashgan sari taassurotlarim va ularga ergashib fikrlarim tobora boshqacha va chalkash bo'lib bordi. Ichimda nimadir o'lmagan edi, yuragim va vijdonimning tubida u o'lishni istamasdi va o'tkir tushkunlikda namoyon bo'lardi. Ko'pincha men eng gavjum savdo ko'chalari bo'ylab, Meshchanskaya ko'chasi, Sadovaya ko'chasi bo'ylab va Yusupov bog'ida itarilib yurdim. Men doim bu ko'chalarda g'ira-shirada, aynan har xil mehnatkash odamlar olomoni kundalik ishidan uyga, tashvishdan jahldor ko'rinadigan yuzlar bilan qaytayotganda sayr qilishni ayniqsa yaxshi ko'rardim.

paras.en: What I liked was just that cheap bustle, that bare prose. On this occasion the jostling of the streets irritated me more than ever, I could not make out what was wrong with me, I could not find the clue, something seemed rising up continually in my soul, painfully, and refusing to be appeased. I returned home completely upset, it was just as though some crime were lying on my conscience.
paras.uz: Menga aynan o'sha arzon g'ala-g'ovur, o'sha yalang'och nasr yoqardi. Bu safar ko'chalardagi turtkilar meni har qachongidan ko'ra ko'proq jahldor qildi, menga nima bo'layotganini tushuna olmadim, ip uchini topa olmadim, qalbimda nimadir og'riqli tarzda doimo ko'tarilib, tinchlanishni istamasdi. Uyga butunlay xafa holda qaytdim, go'yo vijdonimda qandaydir jinoyat yotgandek.

paras.en: The thought that Liza was coming worried me continually. It seemed queer to me that of all my recollections of yesterday this tormented me, as it were, especially, as it were, quite separately. Everything else I had quite succeeded in forgetting by the evening; I dismissed it all and was still perfectly satisfied with my letter to Simonov. But on this point I was not satisfied at all. It was as though I were worried only by Liza. "What if she comes," I thought incessantly, "well, it doesn't matter, let her come! H'm! It's horrid that she should see, for instance, how I live. Yesterday I seemed such a hero to her, while now, h'm! It's horrid, though, that I have let myself go so, the room looks like a beggar's. And I brought myself to go out to dinner in such a suit! And my American leather sofa with the stuffing sticking out.
paras.uz: Liza keladi degan fikr meni doimo bezovta qilardi. Kechagi barcha xotiralarim ichida aynan shu meni go'yo alohida, go'yo butunlay alohida qiynashi menga g'alati tuyulardi. Qolgan hamma narsani kechqurungacha butunlay unutishga muvaffaq bo'lgan edim; hammasini chetga surib qo'ydim va Simonovga yozgan maktubimdan hali ham to'liq mamnun edim. Lekin bu masalada umuman mamnun emas edim. Go'yo meni faqat Liza bezovta qilardi. «Agar kelsa-chi, — deb tinimsiz o'ylardim, — xo'sh, farqi yo'q, kelaversin! Hm! Uning, masalan, qanday yashashimni ko'rishi jirkanch. Kecha men unga shunday qahramon bo'lib ko'ringandim, endi esa, hm! Biroq o'zimni shunchalik qo'yib yuborganim jirkanch, xona tilanchinikiga o'xshaydi. Va men shunday kostyumda ziyofatga borishga jur'at etdim! Va paxtasi chiqib turgan amerikancha charm divanim.

paras.en: And my dressing-gown, which will not cover me, such tatters, and she will see all this and she will see Apollon. That beast is certain to insult her. He will fasten upon her in order to be rude to me. And I, of course, shall be panic-stricken as usual, I shall begin bowing and scraping before her and pulling my dressing-gown round me, I shall begin smiling, telling lies. Oh, the beastliness! And it isn't the beastliness of it that matters most! There is something more important, more loathsome, viler! Yes, viler! And to put on that dishonest lying mask again! ..."
paras.uz: Va meni yopmaydigan, shunday juldur xalatim, u bularning hammasini ko'radi va Apollonni ko'radi. O'sha hayvon albatta uni haqorat qiladi. U menga qo'pollik qilish uchun unga yopishadi. Men esa, albatta, odatdagidek vahimaga tushaman, uning oldida ta'zim qilib, xalatimni o'zimga o'ray boshlayman, jilmaya boshlayman, yolg'on gapira boshlayman. Oh, qanday jirkanchlik! Va eng muhimi jirkanchlik ham emas! Bundan muhimroq, jirkanchroq, tubanroq narsa bor! Ha, tubanroq! Va yana o'sha insofsiz yolg'on niqobni kiyish!..»

paras.en: When I reached that thought I fired up all at once.
paras.uz: Bu fikrga yetganimda, birdan alangalanib ketdim.

paras.en: "Why dishonest? How dishonest? I was speaking sincerely last night. I remember there was real feeling in me, too. What I wanted was to excite an honourable feeling in her.... Her crying was a good thing, it will have a good effect."
paras.uz: «Nega insofsiz? Qanday insofsiz? Kecha men samimiy gapirgandim. Esimda, menda ham haqiqiy tuyg'u bor edi. Men unda sharafli tuyg'u uyg'otmoqchi edim... Uning yig'lashi yaxshi narsa edi, bu yaxshi ta'sir qiladi.»

paras.en: Yet I could not feel at ease. All that evening, even when I had come back home, even after nine o'clock, when I calculated that Liza could not possibly come, still she haunted me, and what was worse, she came back to my mind always in the same position. One moment out of all that had happened last night stood vividly before my imagination; the moment when I struck a match and saw her pale, distorted face, with its look of torture. And what a pitiful, what an unnatural, what a distorted smile she had at that moment! But I did not know then, that fifteen years later I should still in my imagination see Liza, always with the pitiful, distorted, inappropriate smile which was on her face at that minute.
paras.uz: Shunga qaramay o'zimni xotirjam his qila olmadim. O'sha butun oqshom, hatto uyga qaytganimdan keyin ham, hatto soat to'qqizdan keyin ham, Liza endi kelishi mumkin emasligini hisoblaganimda ham, u meni ta'qib qilardi va eng yomoni, u xayolimga doim bir xil holatda qaytardi. Kecha bo'lgan hamma narsadan bir lahza tasavvurim oldida yorqin turardi: men gugurt chaqib, uning qiynoq ifodali rangpar, qiyshaygan yuzini ko'rgan lahza. O'sha lahzada uning qanday ayanchli, qanday g'ayritabiiy, qanday qiyshaygan tabassumi bor edi! Lekin o'shanda men o'n besh yildan keyin ham tasavvurimda Lizani doim o'sha daqiqada yuzida bo'lgan ayanchli, qiyshaygan, o'rinsiz tabassum bilan ko'rishimni bilmasdim.

paras.en: Next day I was ready again to look upon it all as nonsense, due to over-excited nerves, and, above all, as exaggerated. I was always conscious of that weak point of mine, and sometimes very much afraid of it. "I exaggerate everything, that is where I go wrong," I repeated to myself every hour. But, however, "Liza will very likely come all the same," was the refrain with which all my reflections ended. I was so uneasy that I sometimes flew into a fury: "She'll come, she is certain to come!" I cried, running about the room, "if not today, she will come tomorrow; she'll find me out! The damnable romanticism of these pure hearts! Oh, the vileness—oh, the silliness—oh, the stupidity of these 'wretched sentimental souls!' Why, how fail to understand? How could one fail to understand? ..."
paras.uz: Ertasi kuni men yana bularning hammasiga bema'nilik, haddan tashqari qo'zg'algan asablar natijasi va, eng muhimi, bo'rttirilgan narsa sifatida qarashga tayyor edim. Men doim o'zimdagi bu zaif nuqtani anglardim va ba'zan undan juda qo'rqardim. «Men hamma narsani bo'rttiraman, men shu yerda adashaman», — deb o'zimga har soat takrorlardim. Lekin baribir «Liza, ehtimol, baribir keladi» — barcha mulohazalarim tugaydigan naqorat edi. Shunchalik bezovta edimki, ba'zan g'azabga tushardim: «U keladi, albatta keladi! — deb qichqirardim xona bo'ylab yugurib. — Bugun bo'lmasa, ertaga keladi; meni topib oladi! Bu pok yuraklarning la'nati romantizmi! Oh, qanday tubanlik — oh, qanday bema'nilik — oh, bu «ayanchli hissiyotchan qalblar»ning qanday ahmoqligi! Axir qanday tushunmaslik mumkin? Qanday qilib tushunmaslik mumkin?..»

paras.en: But at this point I stopped short, and in great confusion, indeed.
paras.uz: Lekin shu yerda men to'xtab qoldim, haqiqatan katta sarosimada.

paras.en: And how few, how few words, I thought, in passing, were needed; how little of the idyllic (and affectedly, bookishly, artificially idyllic too) had sufficed to turn a whole human life at once according to my will. That's virginity, to be sure! Freshness of soil!
paras.uz: Va butun bir inson hayotini darhol irodamga ko'ra burish uchun qanchalik kam, qanchalik kam so'z kerak bo'ldi, deb o'yladim yo'l-yo'lakay; qanchalik oz idilliya (yana sun'iy, kitobiy, soxta idilliya) yetarli bo'ldi. Mana bokiralik, albatta! Tuproqning yangiligi!

paras.en: At times a thought occurred to me, to go to her, "to tell her all," and beg her not to come to me. But this thought stirred such wrath in me that I believed I should have crushed that "damned" Liza if she had chanced to be near me at the time. I should have insulted her, have spat at her, have turned her out, have struck her!
paras.uz: Ba'zan xayolimga uning oldiga borib, «hammasini aytib berish» va menikiga kelmasligini so'rash fikri kelardi. Lekin bu fikr menda shunday g'azab uyg'otardiki, agar o'sha paytda «la'nati» Liza yonimda bo'lganida, uni ezib tashlagan bo'lardim deb ishonardim. Uni haqorat qilgan, unga tupurgan, haydab chiqargan, urgan bo'lardim!

paras.en: One day passed, however, another and another; she did not come and I began to grow calmer. I felt particularly bold and cheerful after nine o'clock, I even sometimes began dreaming, and rather sweetly: I, for instance, became the salvation of Liza, simply through her coming to me and my talking to her.... I develop her, educate her. Finally, I notice that she loves me, loves me passionately. I pretend not to understand (I don't know, however, why I pretend, just for effect, perhaps). At last all confusion, transfigured, trembling and sobbing, she flings herself at my feet and says that I am her saviour, and that she loves me better than anything in the world. I am amazed, but.... "Liza," I say, "can you imagine that I have not noticed your love?
paras.uz: Biroq bir kun o'tdi, ikkinchisi, uchinchisi; u kelmadi va men tinchlana boshladim. Soat to'qqizdan keyin o'zimni ayniqsa jasur va quvnoq his qilardim, hatto ba'zan orzu qila boshlardim, yana ancha shirin: men, masalan, shunchaki u menikiga kelib, men u bilan gaplashganim tufayli Lizaning najotkoriga aylanardim... Men uni rivojlantiraman, tarbiyalayman. Nihoyat, u meni sevishini, ehtiros bilan sevishini payqayman. Men tushunmagandek o'zimni ko'rsataman (biroq nega ko'rsatishimni bilmayman, balki shunchaki ta'sir uchun). Nihoyat u butunlay sarosimada, o'zgarib, titrab va yig'lab, oyoqlarim ostiga tashlanib, men uning qutqaruvchisi ekanimni va meni dunyodagi hamma narsadan ko'proq sevishini aytadi. Men hayratga tushaman, lekin... «Liza, — deyman, — nahotki men sening muhabbatingni payqamaganman deb tasavvur qila olsang?

paras.en: I saw it all, I divined it, but I did not dare to approach you first, because I had an influence over you and was afraid that you would force yourself, from gratitude, to respond to my love, would try to rouse in your heart a feeling which was perhaps absent, and I did not wish that ... Because it would be tyranny ... It would be indelicate (in short, I launch off at that point into European, inexplicably lofty subtleties à la George Sand), but now, now you are mine, you are my creation, you are pure, you are good, you are my noble wife.
