paras.uz: Men hammasini ko'rdim, taxmin qildim, lekin senga birinchi bo'lib yaqinlashishga jur'at etmadim, chunki menda senga ta'sir bor edi va sen minnatdorchilikdan muhabbatimga javob berishga o'zingni majbur qilishingdan, yuragingda, balki, yo'q bo'lgan tuyg'uni uyg'otishga urinishingdan qo'rqdim, men esa buni istamadim... chunki bu zulm bo'lardi... bu nazokatsizlik bo'lardi (xullas, shu yerda men Jorj Sand uslubidagi Yevropacha, tushuntirib bo'lmas darajada yuksak nozikliklarga berilib ketaman), lekin endi, endi sen meniki, sen mening ijodimsan, sen poksan, sen yaxshisan, sen mening olijanob xotinimsan.

paras.en: 'Into my house come bold and free, / Its rightful mistress there to be'."
paras.uz: «Uyimga dadil va erkin kir, / Unda haqli bekaga aylan».»

paras.en: Then we begin living together, go abroad and so on, and so on. In fact, in the end it seemed vulgar to me myself, and I began putting out my tongue at myself.
paras.uz: Keyin biz birga yashay boshlaymiz, chet elga ketamiz va hokazo, va hokazo. Xullas, oxiri bu menga o'zimga ham tuban tuyuldi va o'zimga til chiqara boshladim.

paras.en: Besides, they won't let her out, "the hussy!" I thought. They don't let them go out very readily, especially in the evening (for some reason I fancied she would come in the evening, and at seven o'clock precisely). Though she did say she was not altogether a slave there yet, and had certain rights; so, h'm! Damn it all, she will come, she is sure to come!
paras.uz: Bundan tashqari, uni chiqarishmaydi, «qanjiqni!» — deb o'yladim. Ularni unchalik bajonidil chiqarishmaydi, ayniqsa kechqurun (negadir u kechqurun, aniq soat yettida keladi deb tasavvur qilardim). Garchi u hali u yerda butunlay qul emasligini va ma'lum huquqlari borligini aytgan bo'lsa ham; demak, hm! Jin ursin, u keladi, albatta keladi!

paras.en: It was a good thing, in fact, that Apollon distracted my attention at that time by his rudeness. He drove me beyond all patience! He was the bane of my life, the curse laid upon me by Providence. We had been squabbling continually for years, and I hated him. My God, how I hated him! I believe I had never hated anyone in my life as I hated him, especially at some moments. He was an elderly, dignified man, who worked part of his time as a tailor. But for some unknown reason he despised me beyond all measure, and looked down upon me insufferably. Though, indeed, he looked down upon everyone. Simply to glance at that flaxen, smoothly brushed head, at the tuft of hair he combed up on his forehead and oiled with sunflower oil, at that dignified mouth, compressed into the shape of the letter V, made one feel one was confronting a man who never doubted of himself.
paras.uz: Haqiqatan, o'sha paytda Apollon qo'polligi bilan e'tiborimni chalg'itgani yaxshi bo'ldi. U sabrimni butunlay tugatdi! U hayotimning balosi, Taqdir menga yuklagan la'nat edi. Biz yillar davomida doimo janjallashib kelardik va men undan nafratlanardim. Xudoyim, undan qanday nafratlanardim! Menimcha, hayotimda hech kimdan undan nafratlanganimdek nafratlanmaganman, ayniqsa ba'zi lahzalarda. U keksa, salobatli odam edi, vaqtining bir qismida tikuvchilik qilardi. Lekin qandaydir noma'lum sababdan u meni hamma me'yordan tashqari mensimasdi va menga chidab bo'lmas darajada yuqoridan qarardi. Biroq, haqiqatan, u hammaga yuqoridan qarardi. Faqat o'sha zig'ir rangli, silliq taralgan boshga, peshonasiga tarab, kungaboqar yog'i surtgan sochi tutamiga, V harfi shaklida qisilgan o'sha salobatli og'ziga qarashning o'zi odamga hech qachon o'zidan shubhalanmagan kishi bilan yuzma-yuz turganini his qildirardi.

paras.en: He was a pedant, to the most extreme point, the greatest pedant I had met on earth, and with that had a vanity only befitting Alexander of Macedon. He was in love with every button on his coat, every nail on his fingers—absolutely in love with them, and he looked it! In his behaviour to me he was a perfect tyrant, he spoke very little to me, and if he chanced to glance at me he gave me a firm, majestically self-confident and invariably ironical look that drove me sometimes to fury. He did his work with the air of doing me the greatest favour, though he did scarcely anything for me, and did not, indeed, consider himself bound to do anything. There could be no doubt that he looked upon me as the greatest fool on earth, and that "he did not get rid of me" was simply that he could get wages from me every month. He consented to do nothing for me for seven roubles a month.
paras.uz: U eng chekka darajadagi pedant edi, yer yuzida uchratgan eng katta pedant, buning ustiga faqat Makedoniyalik Iskandarga munosib shuhratparastligi bor edi. U kamzulidagi har bir tugmaga, barmoqlaridagi har bir tirnoqqa oshiq edi — mutlaqo oshiq va bu ko'rinib turardi! Menga munosabatida u mukammal zolim edi, men bilan juda kam gaplashardi va agar tasodifan menga qarab qolsa, menga qat'iy, ulug'vor o'ziga ishongan va doimo kinoyali nigoh tashlardi, bu meni ba'zan g'azabga solardi. U ishini go'yo menga eng katta iltifot qilayotgandek qilardi, garchi men uchun deyarli hech narsa qilmasa ham va, haqiqatan, hech narsa qilishga o'zini majbur deb hisoblamasa ham. Uning meni yer yuzidagi eng katta ahmoq deb bilishiga va «mendan qutulmasligi» shunchaki har oy mendan maosh olishi mumkinligi uchun ekaniga shubha bo'lishi mumkin emas edi. U oyiga yetti rublga men uchun hech narsa qilmaslikka rozi edi.

paras.en: Many sins should be forgiven me for what I suffered from him. My hatred reached such a point that sometimes his very step almost threw me into convulsions. What I loathed particularly was his lisp. His tongue must have been a little too long or something of that sort, for he continually lisped, and seemed to be very proud of it, imagining that it greatly added to his dignity. He spoke in a slow, measured tone, with his hands behind his back and his eyes fixed on the ground. He maddened me particularly when he read aloud the psalms to himself behind his partition. Many a battle I waged over that reading! But he was awfully fond of reading aloud in the evenings, in a slow, even, sing-song voice, as though over the dead. It is interesting that that is how he has ended: he hires himself out to read the psalms over the dead, and at the same time he kills rats and makes blacking.
paras.uz: Undan chekkan azoblarim uchun menga ko'p gunohlar kechirilishi kerak. Nafratim shunday darajaga yetdiki, ba'zan uning qadam tovushining o'zi meni deyarli talvasaga solardi. Ayniqsa uning shivillashidan jirkanardim. Tili biroz uzunroq yoki shunga o'xshash narsa bo'lsa kerak, chunki u doimo shivillardi va bundan juda faxrlanardi shekilli, bu uning qadr-qimmatiga ancha qo'shadi deb tasavvur qilardi. U qo'llarini orqasiga qilib, ko'zlarini yerga qadab, sekin, o'lchovli ohangda gapirardi. U meni ayniqsa to'siq ortida o'ziga zaburni ovoz chiqarib o'qiganda telba qilardi. O'sha o'qish uchun ko'p janglar olib borganman! Lekin u kechqurunlari sekin, bir tekis, go'yo o'lik ustidagidek kuylab ovoz chiqarib o'qishni dahshatli yaxshi ko'rardi. Qiziq, u shunday tugadi: u o'liklar ustida zabur o'qish uchun yollanadi va ayni paytda kalamush o'ldiradi va etik moyi tayyorlaydi.

paras.en: But at that time I could not get rid of him, it was as though he were chemically combined with my existence. Besides, nothing would have induced him to consent to leave me. I could not live in furnished lodgings: my lodging was my private solitude, my shell, my cave, in which I concealed myself from all mankind, and Apollon seemed to me, for some reason, an integral part of that flat, and for seven years I could not turn him away.
paras.uz: Lekin o'sha paytda men undan qutula olmasdim, go'yo u borlig'im bilan kimyoviy birikkandek edi. Bundan tashqari, hech narsa uni meni tashlab ketishga rozi qila olmasdi. Men jihozlangan ijara xonalarda yashay olmasdim: mening kvartiram mening shaxsiy yolg'izligim, chig'anog'im, g'orim edi, unda men butun insoniyatdan yashirinardim va Apollon menga negadir o'sha kvartiraning ajralmas qismidek tuyulardi va yetti yil davomida uni haydab chiqara olmadim.

paras.en: To be two or three days behind with his wages, for instance, was impossible. He would have made such a fuss, I should not have known where to hide my head. But I was so exasperated with everyone during those days, that I made up my mind for some reason and with some object to punish Apollon and not to pay him for a fortnight the wages that were owing him. I had for a long time—for the last two years—been intending to do this, simply in order to teach him not to give himself airs with me, and to show him that if I liked I could withhold his wages. I purposed to say nothing to him about it, and was purposely silent indeed, in order to score off his pride and force him to be the first to speak of his wages.
paras.uz: Masalan, uning maoshini ikki-uch kun kechiktirish imkonsiz edi. U shunday g'avg'o ko'tarardiki, boshimni qayerga yashirishni bilmay qolardim. Lekin o'sha kunlarda hammadan shunchalik g'azablangan edimki, negadir va qandaydir maqsad bilan Apollonni jazolashga va unga qarzdor bo'lgan maoshni ikki hafta to'lamaslikka qaror qildim. Men buni ancha vaqtdan — so'nggi ikki yildan beri qilmoqchi edim, shunchaki uni men bilan kekkaymaslikka o'rgatish va xohlasam, maoshini ushlab qolishim mumkinligini ko'rsatish uchun. Men u haqda unga hech narsa demaslikni niyat qildim va haqiqatan ataylab jim turdim, uning g'ururini yengish va uni maoshi haqida birinchi bo'lib gapirishga majbur qilish uchun.

paras.en: Then I would take the seven roubles out of a drawer, show him I have the money put aside on purpose, but that I won't, I won't, I simply won't pay him his wages, I won't just because that is "what I wish," because "I am master, and it is for me to decide," because he has been disrespectful, because he has been rude; but if he were to ask respectfully I might be softened and give it to him, otherwise he might wait another fortnight, another three weeks, a whole month....
paras.uz: Keyin men tortmadan yetti rublni chiqarib, unga pulni ataylab chetga qo'yganimni, lekin bermasligimni, bermasligimni, shunchaki uning maoshini to'lamasligimni ko'rsatardim, bermayman, chunki «men shuni xohlayman», chunki «men xo'jayinman va qaror qilish menga bog'liq», chunki u hurmatsizlik qilgan, chunki u qo'pollik qilgan; lekin agar u hurmat bilan so'rasa, balki yumshab, unga berardim, aks holda u yana ikki hafta, yana uch hafta, butun bir oy kutishi mumkin edi...

paras.en: But angry as I was, yet he got the better of me. I could not hold out for four days. He began as he always did begin in such cases, for there had been such cases already, there had been attempts (and it may be observed I knew all this beforehand, I knew his nasty tactics by heart). He would begin by fixing upon me an exceedingly severe stare, keeping it up for several minutes at a time, particularly on meeting me or seeing me out of the house. If I held out and pretended not to notice these stares, he would, still in silence, proceed to further tortures. All at once, à propos of nothing, he would walk softly and smoothly into my room, when I was pacing up and down or reading, stand at the door, one hand behind his back and one foot behind the other, and fix upon me a stare more than severe, utterly contemptuous.
paras.uz: Lekin qanchalik jahlim chiqmasin, baribir u mendan ustun keldi. Men to'rt kun ham chiday olmadim. U bunday hollarda doim qanday boshlasa, shunday boshladi, chunki bunday hollar avval ham bo'lgan, urinishlar bo'lgan (qayd etish mumkinki, men bularning hammasini oldindan bilardim, uning jirkanch taktikasini yoddan bilardim). U menga nihoyatda qattiq nigoh qadashdan boshlardi va uni bir necha daqiqa davomida, ayniqsa meni uchratganda yoki uydan kuzatganda, ushlab turardi. Agar men chidab, bu nigohlarni payqamagandek ko'rsatsam, u hali ham jim holda keyingi qiynoqlarga o'tardi. Birdan, hech narsadan-hech narsa yo'q, men u yoqdan-bu yoqqa yurganimda yoki o'qiyotganimda, u xonamga ohista va silliq kirib, eshik oldida, bir qo'li orqasida va bir oyog'i ikkinchisining orqasida turib, menga qattiqdan ham ortiq, mutlaqo nafratli nigoh qadardi.

paras.en: If I suddenly asked him what he wanted, he would make me no answer, but continue staring at me persistently for some seconds, then, with a peculiar compression of his lips and a most significant air, deliberately turn round and deliberately go back to his room. Two hours later he would come out again and again present himself before me in the same way. It had happened that in my fury I did not even ask him what he wanted, but simply raised my head sharply and imperiously and began staring back at him. So we stared at one another for two minutes; at last he turned with deliberation and dignity and went back again for two hours.
paras.uz: Agar men birdan undan nima istashini so'rasam, u menga javob bermasdi, balki bir necha soniya qat'iyat bilan menga tikilishda davom etardi, keyin lablarini o'ziga xos qisib va eng ma'noli ko'rinish bilan, qasddan o'girilib, qasddan o'z xonasiga qaytib ketardi. Ikki soatdan keyin u yana chiqib, yana oldimda xuddi shunday paydo bo'lardi. Shunday bo'lardiki, g'azabimda men undan nima istashini so'ramasdim ham, shunchaki boshimni keskin va amirona ko'tarib, unga qarab tikila boshlardim. Shunday qilib biz ikki daqiqa bir-birimizga tikilib turardik; oxiri u shoshilmay va salobat bilan o'girilib, yana ikki soatga qaytib ketardi.

paras.en: If I were still not brought to reason by all this, but persisted in my revolt, he would suddenly begin sighing while he looked at me, long, deep sighs as though measuring by them the depths of my moral degradation, and, of course, it ended at last by his triumphing completely: I raged and shouted, but still was forced to do what he wanted.
paras.uz: Agar men bularning hammasidan ham aqlga kelmasam, balki isyonimda davom etsam, u birdan menga qarab xo'rsina boshlardi, uzun, chuqur xo'rsinishlar, go'yo ular bilan mening axloqiy tanazzulimning chuqurligini o'lchayotgandek, va, albatta, oxiri bu uning to'liq g'alabasi bilan tugardi: men g'azablanib qichqirardim, lekin baribir u istagan narsani qilishga majbur bo'lardim.

paras.en: This time the usual staring manoeuvres had scarcely begun when I lost my temper and flew at him in a fury. I was irritated beyond endurance apart from him.
paras.uz: Bu safar odatdagi tikilish manevrlari endigina boshlanganida, men o'zimni yo'qotib, unga g'azab bilan tashlandim. Usiz ham chidab bo'lmas darajada jahlim chiqib turgan edi.

paras.en: "Stay," I cried, in a frenzy, as he was slowly and silently turning, with one hand behind his back, to go to his room. "Stay! Come back, come back, I tell you!" And I must have bawled so unnaturally, that he turned round and even looked at me with some wonder. However, he persisted in saying nothing, and that infuriated me.
paras.uz: «To'xta, — deb qichqirdim telbavor, u bir qo'li orqasida, o'z xonasiga borish uchun sekin va jimgina o'girilayotganda. — To'xta! Qayt, qayt, senga aytyapman!» Va men shunchalik g'ayritabiiy baqirgan bo'lsam kerakki, u o'girildi va hatto menga biroz hayrat bilan qaradi. Biroq u hech narsa demaslikda davom etdi va bu meni g'azablantirdi.

paras.en: "How dare you come and look at me like that without being sent for? Answer!"
paras.uz: «Chaqirilmasdan kelib, menga shunday qarashga qanday jur'at etasan? Javob ber!»

paras.en: After looking at me calmly for half a minute, he began turning round again.
paras.uz: Menga yarim daqiqa xotirjam qaragach, u yana o'girila boshladi.

paras.en: "Stay!" I roared, running up to him, "don't stir! There. Answer, now: what did you come in to look at?"
paras.uz: «To'xta! — deb o'kirdim unga yugurib borib. — Qimirlama! Mana. Endi javob ber: nimaga qarash uchun kirding?»

paras.en: "If you have any order to give me it's my duty to carry it out," he answered, after another silent pause, with a slow, measured lisp, raising his eyebrows and calmly twisting his head from one side to another, all this with exasperating composure.
paras.uz: «Agar menga biror buyrug'ingiz bo'lsa, uni bajarish mening burchim», — deb javob berdi u yana bir jim pauzadan keyin, sekin, o'lchovli shivillash bilan, qoshlarini ko'tarib va boshini xotirjam u yoqdan-bu yoqqa burib, bularning hammasini g'azablantiruvchi xotirjamlik bilan.

paras.en: "That's not what I am asking you about, you torturer!" I shouted, turning crimson with anger. "I'll tell you why you came here myself: you see, I don't give you your wages, you are so proud you don't want to bow down and ask for it, and so you come to punish me with your stupid stares, to worry me and you have no sus-pic-ion how stupid it is—stupid, stupid, stupid, stupid! ..."
paras.uz: «Men sendan buni so'rayotganim yo'q, qiynoqchi! — deb qichqirdim g'azabdan qip-qizarib. — Bu yerga nega kelganingni o'zim aytaman: ko'ryapsanmi, men senga maoshingni bermayapman, sen shunchalik mag'rursanki, ta'zim qilib so'rashni istamaysan, shuning uchun ahmoqona tikilishlaring bilan meni jazolash, meni bezovta qilish uchun kelasan va bu qanchalik ahmoqona ekanidan zarracha ham shub-ha-lan-mai-san — ahmoqona, ahmoqona, ahmoqona, ahmoqona!..»

paras.en: He would have turned round again without a word, but I seized him.
paras.uz: U indamasdan yana o'girilgan bo'lardi, lekin men uni ushlab oldim.

paras.en: "Listen," I shouted to him. "Here's the money, do you see, here it is," (I took it out of the table drawer); "here's the seven roubles complete, but you are not going to have it, you ... Are ... Not ... Going ... To ... Have it until you come respectfully with bowed head to beg my pardon. Do you hear?"
paras.uz: «Eshit, — deb unga qichqirdim. — Mana pul, ko'ryapsanmi, mana u», (men uni stol tortmasidan chiqardim) «mana to'liq yetti rubl, lekin sen uni olmaysan, sen... uni... olmaysan... toki hurmat bilan, boshingni egib, mendan kechirim so'rab kelmaguningcha. Eshityapsanmi?»

paras.en: "That cannot be," he answered, with the most unnatural self-confidence.
paras.uz: «Bunday bo'lishi mumkin emas», — deb javob berdi u eng g'ayritabiiy o'ziga ishonch bilan.

paras.en: "It shall be so," I said, "I give you my word of honour, it shall be!"
paras.uz: «Shunday bo'ladi, — dedim men, — senga sharafim haqqi so'z beraman, shunday bo'ladi!»

paras.en: "And there's nothing for me to beg your pardon for," he went on, as though he had not noticed my exclamations at all. "Why, besides, you called me a 'torturer,' for which I can summon you at the police-station at any time for insulting behaviour."
paras.uz: «Va mening sizdan kechirim so'raydigan hech narsam yo'q, — deb davom etdi u, go'yo xitoblarimni umuman payqamagandek. — Axir, bundan tashqari, siz meni «qiynoqchi» deb atadingiz, buning uchun men sizni istalgan vaqtda haqoratli xatti-harakat uchun politsiya mahkamasiga chaqirtira olaman.»

paras.en: "Go, summon me," I roared, "go at once, this very minute, this very second! You are a torturer all the same! A torturer!"
paras.uz: «Bor, chaqirt, — deb o'kirdim, — darhol bor, shu daqiqada, shu soniyada! Baribir sen qiynoqchisan! Qiynoqchi!»

paras.en: But he merely looked at me, then turned, and regardless of my loud calls to him, he walked to his room with an even step and without looking round.
paras.uz: Lekin u faqat menga qaradi, keyin o'girilib, baland chaqiriqlarimga qaramay, bir tekis qadam bilan va orqasiga qaramasdan o'z xonasiga ketdi.

paras.en: "If it had not been for Liza nothing of this would have happened," I decided inwardly. Then, after waiting a minute, I went myself behind his screen with a dignified and solemn air, though my heart was beating slowly and violently.
paras.uz: «Agar Liza bo'lmaganida, bularning hech biri bo'lmasdi», — deb ichimda qaror qildim. Keyin bir daqiqa kutib, yuragim sekin va qattiq ursa ham, o'zim salobatli va tantanali ko'rinish bilan uning to'sig'i ortiga bordim.

paras.en: "Apollon," I said quietly and emphatically, though I was breathless, "go at once without a minute's delay and fetch the police-officer."
paras.uz: «Apollon, — dedim ohista va urg'u bilan, garchi nafasim tiqilib qolgan bo'lsa ham, — darhol, bir daqiqa ham kechiktirmay borib, politsiya nazoratchisini olib kel.»

paras.en: He had meanwhile settled himself at his table, put on his spectacles and taken up some sewing. But, hearing my order, he burst into a guffaw.
paras.uz: U bu orada stoli yoniga o'rnashib, ko'zoynagini taqib, qandaydir tikuvni qo'liga olgan edi. Lekin buyrug'imni eshitib, xaxolab kulib yubordi.

paras.en: "At once, go this minute! Go on, or else you can't imagine what will happen."
paras.uz: «Darhol, shu daqiqada bor! Bor, aks holda nima bo'lishini tasavvur ham qila olmaysan.»

paras.en: "You are certainly out of your mind," he observed, without even raising his head, lisping as deliberately as ever and threading his needle. "Whoever heard of a man sending for the police against himself? And as for being frightened—you are upsetting yourself about nothing, for nothing will come of it."
paras.uz: «Siz albatta aqldan ozgansiz, — dedi u hatto boshini ko'tarmasdan, odatdagidek shoshilmay shivillab va ignasiga ip o'tkazib. — Kim eshitgan odam o'ziga qarshi politsiya chaqirtirganini? Qo'rqishga kelsak — siz behuda o'zingizni bezovta qilyapsiz, chunki bundan hech narsa chiqmaydi.»

paras.en: "Go!" I shrieked, clutching him by the shoulder. I felt I should strike him in a minute.
paras.uz: «Bor!» — deb chinqirdim uni yelkasidan ushlab. Bir daqiqadan keyin uni urib yuborishimni his qildim.

paras.en: But I did not notice the door from the passage softly and slowly open at that instant and a figure come in, stop short, and begin staring at us in perplexity I glanced, nearly swooned with shame, and rushed back to my room. There, clutching at my hair with both hands, I leaned my head against the wall and stood motionless in that position.
paras.uz: Lekin o'sha lahzada yo'lakdan eshik ohista va sekin ochilib, bir qiyofa kirib kelganini, to'xtab qolganini va bizga sarosimada tikila boshlaganini payqamadim. Qaradim, uyatdan deyarli hushimdan ketdim va o'z xonamga yugurib qaytdim. U yerda ikki qo'lim bilan sochimni changallab, boshimni devorga suyab, shu holatda qimirlamay turib qoldim.

paras.en: Two minutes later I heard Apollon's deliberate footsteps. "There is some woman asking for you," he said, looking at me with peculiar severity. Then he stood aside and let in Liza. He would not go away, but stared at us sarcastically.
paras.uz: Ikki daqiqadan keyin Apollonning shoshilmas qadam tovushlarini eshitdim. «Sizni qandaydir ayol so'rayapti», — dedi u menga o'ziga xos qattiqlik bilan qarab. Keyin u chetga chiqib, Lizani kiritdi. U ketishni istamay, bizga kinoya bilan tikilib turdi.

paras.en: "Go away, go away," I commanded in desperation. At that moment my clock began whirring and wheezing and struck seven.
paras.uz: «Ket, ket», — deb umidsizlik ichida buyurdim. O'sha lahzada soatim g'irillab, xirillay boshladi va yettini urdi.

quiz.q: Why does the narrator withhold Apollon's wages?
o: To punish him and force him to ask first
quiz.why_uz: U Apollonning g'ururini sindirish va birinchi bo'lib so'rashga majbur qilish uchun.

quiz.q: When does Liza arrive?
o: Exactly during the quarrel, as the clock strikes seven
quiz.why_uz: Janjal o'rtasida, soat yettini urganda.

chapters.recap_uz: Hikoyachi Simonovga uzrli maktub yozadi, lekin Liza kelishi fikri uni qiynaydi. U Lizani «qutqarish» haqida orzu qiladi. Keksa xizmatkori Apollon bilan maosh ustida janjal avjiga chiqadi — aynan shu paytda, soat yettida, Liza kirib keladi.

chapters.title: The confession

paras.en: "Into my house come bold and free, / Its rightful mistress there to be."
paras.uz: «Uyimga dadil va erkin kir, / Unda haqli bekaga aylan.»

paras.en: I stood before her crushed, crestfallen, revoltingly confused, and I believe I smiled as I did my utmost to wrap myself in the skirts of my ragged wadded dressing-gown—exactly as I had imagined the scene not long before in a fit of depression. After standing over us for a couple of minutes Apollon went away, but that did not make me more at ease. What made it worse was that she, too, was overwhelmed with confusion, more so, in fact, than I should have expected. At the sight of me, of course.
paras.uz: Men uning oldida ezilgan, shashti qaytgan, jirkanch darajada sarosimada turardim va, menimcha, juldur paxtali xalatimning etaklariga o'ranishga bor kuchim bilan urinarkan, jilmaydim — xuddi yaqinda tushkunlik xurujida bu sahnani tasavvur qilganimdek. Ikki daqiqacha tepamizda turgach, Apollon ketdi, lekin bu meni xotirjamroq qilmadi. Ahvolni yanada yomonlashtirgan narsa shu ediki, u ham sarosimaga tushgan edi, aslida men kutganimdan ham ko'proq. Albatta, meni ko'rib.

paras.en: "Sit down," I said mechanically, moving a chair up to the table, and I sat down on the sofa. She obediently sat down at once and gazed at me open-eyed, evidently expecting something from me at once. This naivete of expectation drove me to fury, but I restrained myself.
paras.uz: «O'tiring», — dedim mexanik ravishda, stol yoniga kursi surib, o'zim divanga o'tirdim. U darhol itoatkorona o'tirib, menga ko'zlarini katta ochib qaradi, aftidan mendan darhol nimadir kutib. Kutishning bu soddaligi meni g'azabga soldi, lekin o'zimni tutdim.

paras.en: She ought to have tried not to notice, as though everything had been as usual, while instead of that, she ... And I dimly felt that I should make her pay dearly for all this.
paras.uz: U payqamaslikka harakat qilishi kerak edi, go'yo hamma narsa odatdagidek bo'lgandek, buning o'rniga esa u... Va men bularning hammasi uchun uni qimmatga to'latishimni noaniq his qildim.

paras.en: "You have found me in a strange position, Liza," I began, stammering and knowing that this was the wrong way to begin. "No, no, don't imagine anything," I cried, seeing that she had suddenly flushed. "I am not ashamed of my poverty.... On the contrary, I look with pride on my poverty. I am poor but honourable.... One can be poor and honourable," I muttered. "However ... Would you like tea?...."
paras.uz: «Siz meni g'alati ahvolda topdingiz, Liza», — deb boshladim, duduqlanib va bu noto'g'ri boshlanish ekanini bilib. «Yo'q, yo'q, hech narsa o'ylamang», — deb qichqirdim, uning birdan qizarib ketganini ko'rib. «Men qashshoqligimdan uyalmayman... Aksincha, men qashshoqligimga g'urur bilan qarayman. Men kambag'alman, lekin sharafliman... Kambag'al va sharafli bo'lish mumkin», — deb g'o'ldiradim. «Biroq... choy ichasizmi?..»

paras.en: "No," she was beginning.
paras.uz: «Yo'q», — deb boshlagan edi u.

paras.en: "Wait a minute."
paras.uz: «Bir daqiqa kuting.»

paras.en: I leapt up and ran to Apollon. I had to get out of the room somehow.
paras.uz: Men sakrab turib, Apollonning oldiga yugurdim. Qandaydir tarzda xonadan chiqishim kerak edi.

paras.en: "Apollon," I whispered in feverish haste, flinging down before him the seven roubles which had remained all the time in my clenched fist, "here are your wages, you see I give them to you; but for that you must come to my rescue: bring me tea and a dozen rusks from the restaurant. If you won't go, you'll make me a miserable man! You don't know what this woman is.... This is—everything! You may be imagining something.... But you don't know what that woman is! ..."
paras.uz: «Apollon, — deb isitmali shoshilinchlik bilan shivirladim, butun vaqt mushtimda qisilgan holda qolgan yetti rublni uning oldiga tashlab, — mana maoshing, ko'ryapsanmi, senga beryapman; lekin buning uchun sen menga yordamga kelishing kerak: restorandan menga choy va o'nta suxari olib kel. Agar bormasang, meni baxtsiz odamga aylantirasan! Sen bu ayol kimligini bilmaysan... Bu — hamma narsa! Sen nimanidir o'ylayotgandirsan... Lekin sen o'sha ayol kimligini bilmaysan!..»

paras.en: Apollon, who had already sat down to his work and put on his spectacles again, at first glanced askance at the money without speaking or putting down his needle; then, without paying the slightest attention to me or making any answer, he went on busying himself with his needle, which he had not yet threaded. I waited before him for three minutes with my arms crossed A la Napoleon. My temples were moist with sweat. I was pale, I felt it. But, thank God, he must have been moved to pity, looking at me. Having threaded his needle he deliberately got up from his seat, deliberately moved back his chair, deliberately took off his spectacles, deliberately counted the money, and finally asking me over his shoulder: "Shall I get a whole portion?" Deliberately walked out of the room. As I was going back to Liza, the thought occurred to me on the way: shouldn't I run away just as I was in my dressing-gown, no matter where, and then let happen what would?
paras.uz: Allaqachon ishiga o'tirib, yana ko'zoynagini taqib olgan Apollon avvaliga gapirmasdan yoki ignasini qo'ymasdan pulga ko'z qiri bilan qaradi; keyin menga zarracha e'tibor bermasdan yoki javob bermasdan, hali ip o'tkazmagan ignasi bilan ovora bo'lishda davom etdi. Men uning oldida Napoleondek qo'llarimni qovushtirib uch daqiqa kutdim. Chakkalarim terdan namlangan edi. Men oqargan edim, buni his qildim. Lekin, Xudoga shukur, u menga qarab rahmi kelgan bo'lsa kerak. Ignasiga ip o'tkazgach, u shoshilmay o'rnidan turdi, shoshilmay kursisini orqaga surdi, shoshilmay ko'zoynagini yechdi, shoshilmay pulni sanadi va nihoyat yelkasi osha mendan: «Butun porsiya olaymi?» deb so'rab, shoshilmay xonadan chiqdi. Lizaning oldiga qaytayotganimda yo'lda xayolimga fikr keldi: shunday xalatda, qayerga bo'lsa ham qochib ketsammikan, keyin nima bo'lsa bo'laversin?

paras.en: I sat down again. She looked at me uneasily. For some minutes we were silent.
paras.uz: Men yana o'tirdim. U menga bezovta qaradi. Bir necha daqiqa jim qoldik.

paras.en: "I will kill him," I shouted suddenly, striking the table with my fist so that the ink spurted out of the inkstand.
paras.uz: «Men uni o'ldiraman», — deb birdan qichqirdim, mushtim bilan stolni shunday urdimki, siyohdondan siyoh sachrab chiqdi.

paras.en: "What are you saying!" She cried, starting.
paras.uz: «Nima deyapsiz!» — deb qichqirdi u cho'chib.

paras.en: "I will kill him! Kill him!" I shrieked, suddenly striking the table in absolute frenzy, and at the same time fully understanding how stupid it was to be in such a frenzy. "You don't know, Liza, what that torturer is to me. He is my torturer.... He has gone now to fetch some rusks; he ..."
paras.uz: «Uni o'ldiraman! O'ldiraman!» — deb chinqirdim, birdan mutlaq telbalikda stolni urib, va ayni paytda bunday telbalikda bo'lish qanchalik ahmoqona ekanini to'liq tushunib. «Siz bilmaysiz, Liza, o'sha qiynoqchi men uchun nima. U mening qiynoqchim... U hozir suxari olib kelgani ketdi; u...»

paras.en: And suddenly I burst into tears. It was an hysterical attack. How ashamed I felt in the midst of my sobs; but still I could not restrain them.
paras.uz: Va birdan men yig'lab yubordim. Bu isterik xuruj edi. Yig'im o'rtasida qanchalik uyaldim; lekin baribir uni to'xtata olmadim.

paras.en: She was frightened.
paras.uz: U qo'rqib ketdi.

paras.en: "What is the matter? What is wrong?" She cried, fussing about me.
paras.uz: «Nima bo'ldi? Nima bo'ldi?» — deb qichqirdi u atrofimda parvona bo'lib.

paras.en: "Water, give me water, over there!" I muttered in a faint voice, though I was inwardly conscious that I could have got on very well without water and without muttering in a faint voice. But I was, what is called, putting it on, to save appearances, though the attack was a genuine one.
paras.uz: «Suv, suv bering, ana u yerda!» — deb zaif ovozda g'o'ldiradim, garchi ichimda suvsiz ham, zaif ovozda g'o'ldiramasdan ham yaxshi bo'lishimni anglasam ham. Lekin men, ta'bir joiz bo'lsa, ko'rinishni saqlash uchun o'zimni shunday ko'rsatardim, garchi xuruj haqiqiy bo'lsa ham.

paras.en: She gave me water, looking at me in bewilderment. At that moment Apollon brought in the tea. It suddenly seemed to me that this commonplace, prosaic tea was horribly undignified and paltry after all that had happened, and I blushed crimson. Liza looked at Apollon with positive alarm. He went out without a glance at either of us.
paras.uz: U menga hayrat bilan qarab, suv berdi. O'sha lahzada Apollon choy olib kirdi. Birdan menga bo'lib o'tgan hamma narsadan keyin bu oddiy, nasriy choy dahshatli darajada nomunosib va arzimas bo'lib tuyuldi va men qip-qizarib ketdim. Liza Apollonga rosa xavotir bilan qaradi. U ikkalamizga ham qaramasdan chiqib ketdi.

paras.en: "Liza, do you despise me?" I asked, looking at her fixedly, trembling with impatience to know what she was thinking.
paras.uz: «Liza, meni mensimaysizmi?» — deb so'radim unga tikilib, u nima o'ylayotganini bilish sabrsizligidan titrab.

paras.en: She was confused, and did not know what to answer.
paras.uz: U sarosimaga tushdi va nima deb javob berishni bilmadi.

paras.en: "Drink your tea," I said to her angrily. I was angry with myself, but, of course, it was she who would have to pay for it. A horrible spite against her suddenly surged up in my heart; I believe I could have killed her. To revenge myself on her I swore inwardly not to say a word to her all the time. "She is the cause of it all," I thought.
paras.uz: «Choyingizni iching», — dedim unga jahl bilan. Men o'zimdan jahlim chiqqan edi, lekin, albatta, buning uchun u to'lashi kerak edi. Birdan yuragimda unga qarshi dahshatli g'araz ko'tarildi; menimcha, uni o'ldira olardim. Undan o'ch olish uchun ichimda butun vaqt unga bir og'iz ham so'z aytmaslikka qasam ichdim. «Hammasiga u sababchi», — deb o'yladim.

paras.en: Our silence lasted for five minutes. The tea stood on the table; we did not touch it. I had got to the point of purposely refraining from beginning in order to embarrass her further; it was awkward for her to begin alone. Several times she glanced at me with mournful perplexity. I was obstinately silent. I was, of course, myself the chief sufferer, because I was fully conscious of the disgusting meanness of my spiteful stupidity, and yet at the same time I could not restrain myself.
paras.uz: Sukutimiz besh daqiqa davom etdi. Choy stolda turardi; biz unga tegmadik. Men uni yanada xijolat qilish uchun ataylab gapni boshlamaslik darajasiga yetgan edim; yolg'iz o'zi boshlash unga noqulay edi. Bir necha marta u menga g'amgin sarosima bilan qaradi. Men qaysarlik bilan jim turdim. Albatta, eng ko'p azob chekayotgan men o'zim edim, chunki g'arazli ahmoqligimning jirkanch tubanligini to'liq anglardim, shunga qaramay ayni paytda o'zimni tuta olmasdim.

paras.en: "I want to... Get away ... From there altogether," she began, to break the silence in some way, but, poor girl, that was just what she ought not to have spoken about at such a stupid moment to a man so stupid as I was. My heart positively ached with pity for her tactless and unnecessary straightforwardness. But something hideous at once stifled all compassion in me; it even provoked me to greater venom. I did not care what happened. Another five minutes passed.
paras.uz: «Men... u yerdan... butunlay ketmoqchiman», — deb boshladi u sukunatni qandaydir tarzda buzish uchun, lekin, bechora qiz, aynan shu haqda bunday ahmoqona lahzada men kabi ahmoq odamga gapirmasligi kerak edi. Uning nozikliksiz va keraksiz to'g'riligiga achinib, yuragim rosa og'ridi. Lekin nimadir xunuk narsa darhol ichimdagi barcha rahm-shafqatni bo'g'di; u meni hatto battarroq zaharga undadi. Nima bo'lishi menga baribir edi. Yana besh daqiqa o'tdi.

paras.en: "Perhaps I am in your way," she began timidly, hardly audibly, and was getting up.
paras.uz: «Balki sizga xalaqit berayotgandirman», — deb tortinib, zo'rg'a eshitiladigan qilib boshladi u va o'rnidan tura boshladi.

paras.en: But as soon as I saw this first impulse of wounded dignity I positively trembled with spite, and at once burst out.
paras.uz: Lekin yaralangan qadr-qimmatning bu birinchi turtkisini ko'rishim bilanoq men g'arazdan rosa titradim va darhol portladim.

paras.en: "Why have you come to me, tell me that, please?" I began, gasping for breath and regardless of logical connection in my words. I longed to have it all out at once, at one burst; I did not even trouble how to begin. "Why have you come? Answer, answer," I cried, hardly knowing what I was doing. "I'll tell you, my good girl, why you have come. You've come because I talked sentimental stuff to you then. So now you are soft as butter and longing for fine sentiments again. So you may as well know that I was laughing at you then. And I am laughing at you now. Why are you shuddering? Yes, I was laughing at you! I had been insulted just before, at dinner, by the fellows who came that evening before me.
paras.uz: «Nega menikiga kelding, ayt-chi, iltimos?» — deb boshladim, nafasim tiqilib va so'zlarimdagi mantiqiy bog'liqlikka e'tibor bermasdan. Men hammasini birdan, bir portlashda aytib tashlashni istardim; qanday boshlashni ham o'ylamadim. «Nega kelding? Javob ber, javob ber, — deb qichqirdim, nima qilayotganimni zo'rg'a bilib. — Men senga aytaman, yaxshi qizim, nega kelding. Sen o'shanda men senga hissiyotchan gaplar gapirganim uchun kelding. Shuning uchun endi sen sariyog'dek yumshoqsan va yana chiroyli tuyg'ularga tashnasan. Shunday ekan, bilib qo'y, men o'shanda ustingdan kulgan edim. Hozir ham ustingdan kulyapman. Nega titrayapsan? Ha, ustingdan kulgan edim! Undan oldin, ziyofatda, o'sha kechasi mendan oldin kelgan yigitlar meni haqorat qilishgan edi.

paras.en: I came to you, meaning to thrash one of them, an officer; but I didn't succeed, I didn't find him; I had to avenge the insult on someone to get back my own again; you turned up, I vented my spleen on you and laughed at you. I had been humiliated, so I wanted to humiliate; I had been treated like a rag, so I wanted to show my power.... That's what it was, and you imagined I had come there on purpose to save you. Yes? You imagined that? You imagined that?"
paras.uz: Men sizlarnikiga ulardan birini, bir zobitni do'pposlash niyatida kelgandim; lekin muvaffaq bo'lmadim, uni topmadim; o'zimnikini qaytarib olish uchun kimdandir haqorat uchun o'ch olishim kerak edi; sen chiqib qolding, men jahlimni sendan oldim va ustingdan kuldim. Meni xo'rlashgan edi, shuning uchun men xo'rlamoqchi edim; menga latta kabi munosabatda bo'lishgan edi, shuning uchun men kuchimni ko'rsatmoqchi edim... Mana nima edi, sen esa men u yerga seni qutqarish uchun ataylab kelgan deb tasavvur qilding. Shundaymi? Shunday tasavvur qildingmi? Shunday tasavvur qildingmi?»

paras.en: I knew that she would perhaps be muddled and not take it all in exactly, but I knew, too, that she would grasp the gist of it, very well indeed. And so, indeed, she did. She turned white as a handkerchief, tried to say something, and her lips worked painfully; but she sank on a chair as though she had been felled by an axe. And all the time afterwards she listened to me with her lips parted and her eyes wide open, shuddering with awful terror. The cynicism, the cynicism of my words overwhelmed her....
paras.uz: Men u, balki, chalkashib, hammasini aniq tushunmasligini bilardim, lekin uning mohiyatini juda yaxshi tushunishini ham bilardim. Haqiqatan ham shunday bo'ldi. U ro'moldek oqarib ketdi, nimadir demoqchi bo'ldi, lablari og'riqli qimirladi; lekin u go'yo bolta bilan qulatilgandek kursiga cho'kdi. Keyingi butun vaqt u meni lablari ochiq va ko'zlari katta ochilgan holda, dahshatli qo'rquvdan titrab tingladi. So'zlarimning kinizmi, kinizmi uni bosib ketdi...

paras.en: "Save you!" I went on, jumping up from my chair and running up and down the room before her. "Save you from what? But perhaps I am worse than you myself. Why didn't you throw it in my teeth when I was giving you that sermon: 'But what did you come here yourself for? Was it to read us a sermon?' Power, power was what I wanted then, sport was what I wanted, I wanted to wring out your tears, your humiliation, your hysteria—that was what I wanted then! Of course, I couldn't keep it up then, because I am a wretched creature, I was frightened, and, the devil knows why, gave you my address in my folly. Afterwards, before I got home, I was cursing and swearing at you because of that address, I hated you already because of the lies I had told you.
paras.uz: «Seni qutqarish! — deb davom etdim kursimdan sakrab turib, uning oldida xona bo'ylab u yoqdan-bu yoqqa yugurib. — Nimadan qutqarish? Lekin balki men o'zim sendan ham yomonroqdirman. Nega men senga o'sha va'zni o'qiyotganimda yuzimga otmading: «Siz o'zingiz bu yerga nima uchun keldingiz? Bizga va'z o'qish uchunmi?» Kuch, o'shanda menga kuch kerak edi, o'yin kerak edi, sening ko'z yoshlaringni, xo'rligingni, isteriyangni siqib chiqarmoqchi edim — o'shanda menga shu kerak edi! Albatta, o'shanda men buni davom ettira olmadim, chunki men ayanchli mavjudotman, qo'rqib ketdim va, shayton biladi nega, ahmoqligimdan senga manzilimni berdim. Keyin, uyga yetguncha, o'sha manzil uchun seni so'kib, la'natladim, senga aytgan yolg'onlarim uchun sendan allaqachon nafratlanardim.

paras.en: Because I only like playing with words, only dreaming, but, do you know, what I really want is that you should all go to hell. That is what I want. I want peace; yes, I'd sell the whole world for a farthing, straight off, so long as I was left in peace. Is the world to go to pot, or am I to go without my tea? I say that the world may go to pot for me so long as I always get my tea. Did you know that, or not? Well, anyway, I know that I am a blackguard, a scoundrel, an egoist, a sluggard. Here I have been shuddering for the last three days at the thought of your coming. And do you know what has worried me particularly for these three days? That I posed as such a hero to you, and now you would see me in a wretched torn dressing-gown, beggarly, loathsome.
paras.uz: Chunki men faqat so'zlar bilan o'ynashni, faqat orzu qilishni yaxshi ko'raman, lekin bilasanmi, menga aslida nima kerak — hammangiz jahannamga ketishingiz. Menga shu kerak. Menga tinchlik kerak; ha, tinch qo'yishsa bas, butun dunyoni darhol bir tiyinga sotgan bo'lardim. Dunyo vayron bo'lsinmi, yoki men choysiz qolaymi? Men aytamanki, dunyo vayron bo'laversin, faqat men doim choyimni ichsam bas. Buni bilarmiding yoki yo'qmi? Xo'sh, har holda, men o'zimning muttaham, yaramas, xudbin, yalqov ekanimni bilaman. Mana men so'nggi uch kun davomida sening kelishing haqidagi fikrdan titrab yurdim. Va bilasanmi, shu uch kun davomida meni ayniqsa nima bezovta qildi? Men sening oldingda shunday qahramon bo'lib ko'ringanim, endi esa sen meni ayanchli yirtiq xalatda, tilanchidek, jirkanch holda ko'rishing.

paras.en: I told you just now that I was not ashamed of my poverty; so you may as well know that I am ashamed of it; I am more ashamed of it than of anything, more afraid of it than of being found out if I were a thief, because I am as vain as though I had been skinned and the very air blowing on me hurt. Surely by now you must realise that I shall never forgive you for having found me in this wretched dressing-gown, just as I was flying at Apollon like a spiteful cur. The saviour, the former hero, was flying like a mangy, unkempt sheep-dog at his lackey, and the lackey was jeering at him! And I shall never forgive you for the tears I could not help shedding before you just now, like some silly woman put to shame! And for what I am confessing to you now, I shall never forgive you either!
paras.uz: Hozirgina senga qashshoqligimdan uyalmayman dedim; shunday ekan, bilib qo'y, men undan uyalaman; men undan hamma narsadan ko'ra ko'proq uyalaman, undan, agar o'g'ri bo'lganimda fosh bo'lishdan ko'ra ko'proq qo'rqaman, chunki men go'yo terim shilib olingandek va ustimga esgan havoning o'zi og'ritadigandek shuhratparastman. Axir hozirga kelib sen meni bu ayanchli xalatda, aynan g'arazli it kabi Apollonga tashlanayotganimda topganing uchun seni hech qachon kechirmasligimni tushungan bo'lsang kerak. Qutqaruvchi, sobiq qahramon qo'tir, to'zg'igan cho'pon itidek xizmatkoriga tashlanardi, xizmatkor esa uning ustidan masxara qilardi! Va hozirgina sharmanda qilingan qandaydir ahmoq ayol kabi oldingda to'kmay qola olmagan ko'z yoshlarim uchun seni hech qachon kechirmayman! Va hozir senga tan olayotganlarim uchun ham seni hech qachon kechirmayman!

paras.en: Yes—you must answer for it all because you turned up like this, because I am a blackguard, because I am the nastiest, stupidest, absurdest and most envious of all the worms on earth, who are not a bit better than I am, but, the devil knows why, are never put to confusion; while I shall always be insulted by every louse, that is my doom! And what is it to me that you don't understand a word of this! And what do I care, what do I care about you, and whether you go to ruin there or not? Do you understand? How I shall hate you now after saying this, for having been here and listening. Why, it's not once in a lifetime a man speaks out like this, and then it is in hysterics! ... What more do you want? Why do you still stand confronting me, after all this? Why are you worrying me? Why don't you go?"
paras.uz: Ha — sen hammasi uchun javob berishing kerak, chunki shunday chiqib qolding, chunki men muttahamman, chunki men yer yuzidagi barcha qurtlarning eng jirkanchi, eng ahmog'i, eng bema'nisi va eng hasadgo'yiman, ular mendan zarracha ham yaxshi emas, lekin, shayton biladi nega, hech qachon sarosimaga tushmaydi; men esa doim har bir bit tomonidan haqoratlanaman, bu mening qismatim! Va bulardan bir so'zini ham tushunmasliging menga nima! Va sen menga nima, u yerda halok bo'lasanmi yoki yo'qmi, menga nima? Tushunyapsanmi? Buni aytganimdan keyin, bu yerda bo'lganing va tinglaganing uchun sendan endi qanchalik nafratlanaman. Axir odam umrida bir marta ham shunday ochiq gapirmaydi, gapirsa ham isteriyada!.. Yana nima istaysan? Bularning hammasidan keyin nega hali ham ro'paramda turibsan? Nega meni qiynayapsan? Nega ketmayapsan?»

paras.en: But at this point a strange thing happened. I was so accustomed to think and imagine everything from books, and to picture everything in the world to myself just as I had made it up in my dreams beforehand, that I could not all at once take in this strange circumstance. What happened was this: Liza, insulted and crushed by me, understood a great deal more than I imagined. She understood from all this what a woman understands first of all, if she feels genuine love, that is, that I was myself unhappy.
paras.uz: Lekin shu nuqtada g'alati narsa yuz berdi. Men hamma narsani kitoblardan o'ylash va tasavvur qilishga, dunyodagi hamma narsani orzularimda oldindan qanday to'qigan bo'lsam, shunday ko'z oldimga keltirishga shunchalik odatlangan edimki, bu g'alati holatni birdan anglay olmadim. Sodir bo'lgan narsa shu edi: men haqorat qilgan va ezgan Liza men tasavvur qilganimdan ancha ko'proq narsani tushundi. U bularning hammasidan ayol, agar haqiqiy muhabbat his qilsa, birinchi navbatda nimani tushunsa, shuni tushundi, ya'ni men o'zim baxtsiz ekanimni.

paras.en: The frightened and wounded expression on her face was followed first by a look of sorrowful perplexity. When I began calling myself a scoundrel and a blackguard and my tears flowed (the tirade was accompanied throughout by tears) her whole face worked convulsively. She was on the point of getting up and stopping me; when I finished she took no notice of my shouting: "Why are you here, why don't you go away?" But realised only that it must have been very bitter to me to say all this. Besides, she was so crushed, poor girl; she considered herself infinitely beneath me; how could she feel anger or resentment? She suddenly leapt up from her chair with an irresistible impulse and held out her hands, yearning towards me, though still timid and not daring to stir.... At this point there was a revulsion in my heart too. Then she suddenly rushed to me, threw her arms round me and burst into tears. I, too, could not restrain myself, and sobbed as I never had before.
paras.uz: Yuzidagi qo'rqqan va yaralangan ifodadan keyin avval g'amgin sarosima ko'rinishi keldi. Men o'zimni yaramas va muttaham deb atay boshlaganimda va ko'z yoshlarim oqqanida (butun nutq boshidan oxirigacha ko'z yoshlari bilan kechdi), uning butun yuzi talvasali qimirladi. U o'rnidan turib, meni to'xtatish arafasida edi; men tugatganimda u «Nega bu yerdasan, nega ketmayapsan?» degan qichqirig'imga e'tibor bermadi, balki faqat bularning hammasini aytish men uchun juda achchiq bo'lgan bo'lishi kerakligini angladi. Bundan tashqari, u shunchalik ezilgan edi, bechora qiz; u o'zini mendan cheksiz pastda deb hisoblardi; u qanday qilib g'azab yoki ranjish his qila olardi? U birdan chidab bo'lmas turtki bilan kursidan sakrab turib, qo'llarini cho'zdi, menga intilib, lekin hali ham tortinib va qimirlashga jur'at etmay... Shu nuqtada mening yuragimda ham burilish yuz berdi. Keyin u birdan menga otildi, qo'llarini bo'ynimga tashladi va yig'lab yubordi. Men ham o'zimni tuta olmadim va hech qachon yig'lamaganimdek yig'ladim.

paras.en: "They won't let me ... I can't be good!" I managed to articulate; then I went to the sofa, fell on it face downwards, and sobbed on it for a quarter of an hour in genuine hysterics. She came close to me, put her arms round me and stayed motionless in that position. But the trouble was that the hysterics could not go on for ever, and (I am writing the loathsome truth) lying face downwards on the sofa with my face thrust into my nasty leather pillow, I began by degrees to be aware of a far-away, involuntary but irresistible feeling that it would be awkward now for me to raise my head and look Liza straight in the face. Why was I ashamed? I don't know, but I was ashamed. The thought, too, came into my overwrought brain that our parts now were completely changed, that she was now the heroine, while I was just a crushed and humiliated creature as she had been before me that night—four days before.... And all this came into my mind during the minutes I was lying on my face on the sofa.
paras.uz: «Ular menga yo'l qo'yishmaydi... Men yaxshi bo'la olmayman!» — deb zo'rg'a gapira oldim; keyin divanga borib, unga yuztuban yiqildim va chorak soat haqiqiy isteriyada yig'ladim. U yonimga kelib, meni quchoqladi va shu holatda qimirlamay qoldi. Lekin muammo shunda ediki, isteriya abadiy davom eta olmasdi va (men jirkanch haqiqatni yozyapman) divanda yuzimni jirkanch charm yostig'imga tiqib yuztuban yotarkanman, men asta-sekin uzoq, beixtiyor, lekin chidab bo'lmas tuyg'uni — endi boshimni ko'tarib, Lizaning yuziga to'g'ri qarash menga noqulay bo'lishini anglay boshladim. Nega uyaldim? Bilmayman, lekin uyaldim. Charchagan miyamga yana shu fikr keldiki, bizning rollarimiz endi butunlay almashgan, endi u qahramon, men esa o'sha kechada — to'rt kun oldin — u mening oldimda bo'lganidek ezilgan va xo'rlangan mavjudotman... Bularning hammasi divanda yuztuban yotgan daqiqalarimda xayolimga keldi.

paras.en: My God! Surely I was not envious of her then.
paras.uz: Xudoyim! Nahotki men o'shanda unga hasad qilgan bo'lsam.

paras.en: I don't know, to this day I cannot decide, and at the time, of course, I was still less able to understand what I was feeling than now. I cannot get on without domineering and tyrannising over someone, but ... There is no explaining anything by reasoning and so it is useless to reason.
paras.uz: Bilmayman, shu kungacha hal qila olmayman, o'shanda esa, albatta, nima his qilayotganimni hozirgidan ham kamroq tushuna olardim. Men kimgadir hukmronlik va zulm qilmasdan yashay olmayman, lekin... Mulohaza bilan hech narsani tushuntirib bo'lmaydi, shuning uchun mulohaza qilish foydasiz.

paras.en: I conquered myself, however, and raised my head; I had to do so sooner or later ... And I am convinced to this day that it was just because I was ashamed to look at her that another feeling was suddenly kindled and flamed up in my heart ... A feeling of mastery and possession. My eyes gleamed with passion, and I gripped her hands tightly. How I hated her and how I was drawn to her at that minute! The one feeling intensified the other. It was almost like an act of vengeance. At first there was a look of amazement, even of terror on her face, but only for one instant. She warmly and rapturously embraced me.
paras.uz: Biroq men o'zimni yengdim va boshimni ko'tardim; ertami-kechmi buni qilishim kerak edi... Va shu kungacha ishonchim komilki, aynan unga qarashdan uyalganim uchun yuragimda birdan boshqa tuyg'u alangalanib, yonib ketdi... hukmronlik va egalik tuyg'usi. Ko'zlarim ehtiros bilan yaltiradi va men uning qo'llarini mahkam qisdim. O'sha daqiqada undan qanday nafratlanardim va unga qanday intilardim! Bir tuyg'u ikkinchisini kuchaytirardi. Bu deyarli qasos harakatiga o'xshardi. Avvaliga uning yuzida hayrat, hatto dahshat ifodasi paydo bo'ldi, lekin faqat bir lahzaga. U meni iliq va vajd bilan quchoqladi.

quiz.q: What does the narrator confess to Liza?
o: That he had humiliated her for power and sport
quiz.why_uz: Unga kuch va o'yin kerak bo'lgani, uni xo'rlash uchun gapirgani.

quiz.q: What does Liza understand from his outburst?
quiz.why_uz: Haqiqiy muhabbat his qilgan ayol birinchi tushunadigan narsani — u o'zi baxtsiz ekanini.

chapters.recap_uz: Hikoyachi xalatda, sharmandali ahvolda Lizani qabul qiladi, isterik yig'laydi, keyin unga hamma haqiqatni — kuch va o'yin uchun uni xo'rlaganini — aytadi. Lekin Liza uning o'zi baxtsiz ekanini tushunadi va uni quchoqlaydi. U ham yig'laydi, keyin esa uyat tuyg'usi hukmronlik va egalik tuyg'usiga aylanadi.

chapters.title: The five-rouble note

paras.en: A quarter of an hour later I was rushing up and down the room in frenzied impatience, from minute to minute I went up to the screen and peeped through the crack at Liza. She was sitting on the ground with her head leaning against the bed, and must have been crying. But she did not go away, and that irritated me. This time she understood it all. I had insulted her finally, but ... There's no need to describe it. She realised that my outburst of passion had been simply revenge, a fresh humiliation, and that to my earlier, almost causeless hatred was added now a personal hatred, born of envy.... Though I do not maintain positively that she understood all this distinctly; but she certainly did fully understand that I was a despicable man, and what was worse, incapable of loving her.
paras.uz: Chorak soatdan keyin men telbavor sabrsizlikda xona bo'ylab u yoqdan-bu yoqqa yugurardim, har daqiqa parda oldiga borib, yoriqdan Lizaga qarardim. U boshini karavotga suyab yerda o'tirardi va yig'layotgan bo'lsa kerak. Lekin u ketmasdi va bu meni jahldor qilardi. Bu safar u hammasini tushundi. Men uni nihoyat haqorat qildim, lekin... buni tasvirlashning hojati yo'q. U mening ehtiros portlashim shunchaki qasos, yangi xo'rlash bo'lganini va mening oldingi, deyarli sababsiz nafratimga endi hasaddan tug'ilgan shaxsiy nafrat qo'shilganini angladi... Garchi men u bularning hammasini aniq tushundi deb qat'iy da'vo qilmasam ham; lekin u men tuban odam ekanimni va, bundan ham yomoni, uni sevishga qodir emasligimni albatta to'liq tushundi.

paras.en: I know I shall be told that this is incredible—but it is incredible to be as spiteful and stupid as I was; it may be added that it was strange I should not love her, or at any rate, appreciate her love. Why is it strange? In the first place, by then I was incapable of love, for I repeat, with me loving meant tyrannising and showing my moral superiority. I have never in my life been able to imagine any other sort of love, and have nowadays come to the point of sometimes thinking that love really consists in the right—freely given by the beloved object—to tyrannise over her.
paras.uz: Bilaman, menga bu aql bovar qilmaydi deyishadi — lekin men kabi g'arazli va ahmoq bo'lish aql bovar qilmaydi; men uni sevmaganim yoki, har holda, uning muhabbatini qadrlamaganim g'alati, deb qo'shimcha qilish mumkin. Nega g'alati? Birinchidan, o'shanga kelib men sevishga qodir emas edim, chunki takrorlayman, men uchun sevish zulm qilish va axloqiy ustunligimni ko'rsatish degani edi. Men hayotimda hech qachon boshqacha muhabbatni tasavvur qila olmaganman va hozirgi kunda ba'zan muhabbat haqiqatan ham sevilgan ob'ekt tomonidan erkin berilgan — unga zulm qilish huquqidan iborat, deb o'ylash darajasiga yetganman.

paras.en: Even in my underground dreams I did not imagine love except as a struggle. I began it always with hatred and ended it with moral subjugation, and afterwards I never knew what to do with the subjugated object. And what is there to wonder at in that, since I had succeeded in so corrupting myself, since I was so out of touch with "real life," as to have actually thought of reproaching her, and putting her to shame for having come to me to hear "fine sentiments"; and did not even guess that she had come not to hear fine sentiments, but to love me, because to a woman all reformation, all salvation from any sort of ruin, and all moral renewal is included in love and can only show itself in that form.
paras.uz: Hatto yer osti orzularimda ham men muhabbatni kurashdan boshqa narsa sifatida tasavvur qilmasdim. Men uni doim nafrat bilan boshlab, axloqiy bo'ysundirish bilan tugatardim, keyin esa bo'ysundirilgan ob'ekt bilan nima qilishni hech qachon bilmasdim. Bunda nimasi ajablanarli, agar men o'zimni shunchalik buzishga muvaffaq bo'lgan bo'lsam, «haqiqiy hayot»dan shunchalik uzilgan bo'lsamki, uni «chiroyli tuyg'ular»ni eshitish uchun menikiga kelgani uchun ta'na qilish va sharmanda qilishni haqiqatan o'ylagan bo'lsam; va u chiroyli tuyg'ularni eshitish uchun emas, balki meni sevish uchun kelganini taxmin ham qilmadim, chunki ayol uchun har qanday tuzalish, har qanday halokatdan najot va har qanday axloqiy yangilanish muhabbatda jamlangan va faqat shu shaklda namoyon bo'lishi mumkin.

paras.en: I did not hate her so much, however, when I was running about the room and peeping through the crack in the screen. I was only insufferably oppressed by her being here. I wanted her to disappear. I wanted "peace," to be left alone in my underground world. Real life oppressed me with its novelty so much that I could hardly breathe.
paras.uz: Biroq xona bo'ylab yugurib, pardadagi yoriqdan qarab turganimda men undan unchalik nafratlanmasdim. Uning bu yerda ekani meni faqat chidab bo'lmas darajada ezardi. Men uning g'oyib bo'lishini istardim. Men «tinchlik»ni, yer osti dunyomda yolg'iz qolishni istardim. Haqiqiy hayot o'zining yangiligi bilan meni shunchalik ezardiki, zo'rg'a nafas olardim.

paras.en: But several minutes passed and she still remained, without stirring, as though she were unconscious. I had the shamelessness to tap softly at the screen as though to remind her.... She started, sprang up, and flew to seek her kerchief, her hat, her coat, as though making her escape from me.... Two minutes later she came from behind the screen and looked with heavy eyes at me. I gave a spiteful grin, which was forced, however, to keep up appearances, and I turned away from her eyes.
paras.uz: Lekin bir necha daqiqa o'tdi va u hali ham qimirlamay, go'yo hushsiz holda qolardi. Men go'yo eslatgandek pardani ohista taqillatishdek uyatsizlik qildim... U cho'chib, sakrab turdi va go'yo mendan qochayotgandek ro'moli, shlyapasi, paltosini izlab uchib ketdi... Ikki daqiqadan keyin u parda ortidan chiqib, menga og'ir ko'zlar bilan qaradi. Men g'arazli irjaydim, biroq bu ko'rinishni saqlash uchun majburiy edi, va uning ko'zlaridan yuz o'girdim.

paras.en: "Good-bye," she said, going towards the door.
paras.uz: «Xayr», — dedi u eshik tomon borib.

paras.en: I ran up to her, seized her hand, opened it, thrust something in it and closed it again. Then I turned at once and dashed away in haste to the other corner of the room to avoid seeing, anyway....
paras.uz: Men uning oldiga yugurdim, qo'lini ushlab, ochdim, unga nimanidir tiqdim va yana yumdim. Keyin darhol o'girilib, har holda ko'rmaslik uchun shoshilib xonaning narigi burchagiga otildim...

paras.en: I did mean a moment since to tell a lie—to write that I did this accidentally, not knowing what I was doing through foolishness, through losing my head. But I don't want to lie, and so I will say straight out that I opened her hand and put the money in it ... From spite. It came into my head to do this while I was running up and down the room and she was sitting behind the screen. But this I can say for certain: though I did that cruel thing purposely, it was not an impulse from the heart, but came from my evil brain. This cruelty was so affected, so purposely made up, so completely a product of the brain, of books, that I could not even keep it up a minute—first I dashed away to avoid seeing her, and then in shame and despair rushed after Liza. I opened the door in the passage and began listening.
paras.uz: Men bir lahza oldin yolg'on gapirmoqchi edim — buni tasodifan, ahmoqligimdan, boshimni yo'qotganimdan nima qilayotganimni bilmasdan qildim, deb yozmoqchi edim. Lekin yolg'on gapirishni istamayman, shuning uchun to'g'ridan-to'g'ri aytaman: men uning qo'lini ochib, pulni unga qo'ydim... g'arazdan. Bu fikr xona bo'ylab u yoqdan-bu yoqqa yugurib, u parda ortida o'tirganida boshimga kelgan edi. Lekin buni aniq ayta olaman: garchi men bu shafqatsiz ishni ataylab qilgan bo'lsam ham, bu yurakdan kelgan turtki emas edi, balki yovuz miyamdan keldi. Bu shafqatsizlik shunchalik sun'iy, shunchalik ataylab to'qilgan, shunchalik to'liq miyaning, kitoblarning mahsuli ediki, men uni hatto bir daqiqa ham davom ettira olmadim — avval uni ko'rmaslik uchun otildim, keyin uyat va umidsizlik ichida Lizaning ortidan yugurdim. Yo'lakdagi eshikni ochib, quloq sola boshladim.

paras.en: "Liza! Liza!" I cried on the stairs, but in a low voice, not boldly. There was no answer, but I fancied I heard her footsteps, lower down on the stairs.
paras.uz: «Liza! Liza!» — deb zinapoyada qichqirdim, lekin past ovozda, dadil emas. Javob bo'lmadi, lekin menga zinapoyada pastroqda uning qadam tovushlarini eshitgandek tuyuldi.

paras.en: "Liza!" I cried, more loudly.
paras.uz: «Liza!» — deb balandroq qichqirdim.

paras.en: No answer. But at that minute I heard the stiff outer glass door open heavily with a creak and slam violently; the sound echoed up the stairs.
paras.uz: Javob yo'q. Lekin o'sha daqiqada qattiq tashqi shisha eshik g'ichirlab og'ir ochilib, qattiq yopilganini eshitdim; tovush zinapoyada aks-sado berdi.

paras.en: She had gone. I went back to my room in hesitation. I felt horribly oppressed.
paras.uz: U ketgan edi. Men ikkilanib o'z xonamga qaytdim. O'zimni dahshatli ezilgan his qildim.

paras.en: I stood still at the table, beside the chair on which she had sat and looked aimlessly before me. A minute passed, suddenly I started; straight before me on the table I saw.... In short, I saw a crumpled blue five-rouble note, the one I had thrust into her hand a minute before. It was the same note; it could be no other, there was no other in the flat. So she had managed to fling it from her hand on the table at the moment when I had dashed into the further corner.
paras.uz: Men stol yonida, u o'tirgan kursi yonida qotib turib, oldimga maqsadsiz qaradim. Bir daqiqa o'tdi, birdan cho'chib ketdim; to'g'ri oldimda stolda ko'rdim... Xullas, men bir daqiqa oldin uning qo'liga tiqqan g'ijimlangan ko'k besh rubllik qog'oz pulni ko'rdim. Bu o'sha pul edi; boshqasi bo'lishi mumkin emas edi, kvartirada boshqasi yo'q edi. Demak, u men narigi burchakka otilgan lahzada uni qo'lidan stolga tashlashga ulgurgan edi.

paras.en: Well! I might have expected that she would do that. Might I have expected it? No, I was such an egoist, I was so lacking in respect for my fellow-creatures that I could not even imagine she would do so. I could not endure it. A minute later I flew like a madman to dress, flinging on what I could at random and ran headlong after her. She could not have got two hundred paces away when I ran out into the street.
paras.uz: Xo'sh! Men uning shunday qilishini kutishim mumkin edi. Kutishim mumkin edimi? Yo'q, men shunchalik xudbin edim, hamjinslarimga shunchalik hurmatsiz edimki, uning shunday qilishini tasavvur ham qila olmasdim. Men bunga chiday olmadim. Bir daqiqadan keyin telbadek kiyinishga uchdim, qo'limga tushganini tavakkal ustimga ilib, uning ortidan boshim bilan yugurdim. Men ko'chaga yugurib chiqqanimda u ikki yuz qadamdan uzoqqa ketgan bo'lishi mumkin emas edi.

paras.en: It was a still night and the snow was coming down in masses and falling almost perpendicularly, covering the pavement and the empty street as though with a pillow. There was no one in the street, no sound was to be heard. The street lamps gave a disconsolate and useless glimmer. I ran two hundred paces to the cross-roads and stopped short.
paras.uz: Tun jimjit edi, qor uyum-uyum bo'lib, deyarli tik yog'ib, yo'lak va bo'm-bo'sh ko'chani go'yo yostiq bilan qoplardi. Ko'chada hech kim yo'q edi, hech qanday tovush eshitilmasdi. Ko'cha fonarlari g'amgin va foydasiz miltillardi. Men chorrahaga ikki yuz qadam yugurib, to'xtab qoldim.

paras.en: Where had she gone? And why was I running after her?
paras.uz: U qayerga ketdi? Va nega men uning ortidan yugurayapman?

paras.en: Why? To fall down before her, to sob with remorse, to kiss her feet, to entreat her forgiveness! I longed for that, my whole breast was being rent to pieces, and never, never shall I recall that minute with indifference. But—what for? I thought. Should I not begin to hate her, perhaps, even tomorrow, just because I had kissed her feet today? Should I give her happiness? Had I not recognised that day, for the hundredth time, what I was worth? Should I not torture her?
paras.uz: Nega? Uning oldiga yiqilish, pushaymonlik bilan yig'lash, oyoqlarini o'pish, kechirim so'rab yolvorish uchun! Men shuni istardim, butun ko'ksim parchalanayotgan edi va men hech qachon, hech qachon o'sha daqiqani befarq eslamayman. Lekin — nima uchun? — deb o'yladim. Balki men undan nafratlana boshlamasmidim, ehtimol, hatto ertaga, aynan bugun uning oyoqlarini o'pganim uchun? Men unga baxt berarmidim? O'sha kuni yuzinchi marta o'zimning qanchaga arzishimni tan olmadimmi? Men uni qiynamasmidim?

paras.en: I stood in the snow, gazing into the troubled darkness and pondered this.
paras.uz: Men qorda turib, bezovta zulmatga tikilib, bu haqda o'yladim.

paras.en: "And will it not be better?" I mused fantastically, afterwards at home, stifling the living pang of my heart with fantastic dreams. "Will it not be better that she should keep the resentment of the insult for ever? Resentment—why, it is purification; it is a most stinging and painful consciousness! Tomorrow I should have defiled her soul and have exhausted her heart, while now the feeling of insult will never die in her heart, and however loathsome the filth awaiting her—the feeling of insult will elevate and purify her ... By hatred ... H'm! ... Perhaps, too, by forgiveness.... Will all that make things easier for her though? ..."
paras.uz: «Yaxshiroq bo'lmaydimi? — deb xayoliy mulohaza qildim keyin uyda, yuragimning tirik og'rig'ini xayoliy orzular bilan bo'g'ib. — Uning haqorat alamini abadiy saqlashi yaxshiroq bo'lmaydimi? Alam — axir bu poklanish; bu eng achishtiruvchi va og'riqli ong! Ertaga men uning ruhini bulg'agan va yuragini holdan toydirgan bo'lardim, endi esa haqorat tuyg'usi uning yuragida hech qachon o'lmaydi va uni qanchalik jirkanch iflos kutmasin — haqorat tuyg'usi uni ko'taradi va poklaydi... nafrat bilan... hm!.. Balki kechirim bilan ham... Lekin bularning hammasi unga ishni osonlashtiradimi?..»

paras.en: And, indeed, I will ask on my own account here, an idle question: which is better—cheap happiness or exalted sufferings? Well, which is better?
paras.uz: Haqiqatan ham, men bu yerda o'zimdan bo'sh savol beraman: qaysi biri yaxshiroq — arzon baxtmi yoki yuksak azoblarmi? Xo'sh, qaysi biri yaxshiroq?

paras.en: So I dreamed as I sat at home that evening, almost dead with the pain in my soul. Never had I endured such suffering and remorse, yet could there have been the faintest doubt when I ran out from my lodging that I should turn back half-way? I never met Liza again and I have heard nothing of her. I will add, too, that I remained for a long time afterwards pleased with the phrase about the benefit from resentment and hatred in spite of the fact that I almost fell ill from misery.
paras.uz: O'sha oqshom uyda, qalbimdagi og'riqdan deyarli o'lgan holda o'tirib, shunday orzu qildim. Men hech qachon bunday azob va pushaymonlikni boshdan kechirmagan edim, shunga qaramay kvartiramdan yugurib chiqqanimda yarim yo'ldan qaytishimga zarracha shubha bo'lishi mumkinmidi? Men Lizani boshqa hech qachon uchratmadim va u haqda hech narsa eshitmadim. Shuni ham qo'shimcha qilamanki, iztirobdan deyarli kasal bo'lib qolganimga qaramay, keyin uzoq vaqt alam va nafratdan foyda haqidagi iboradan mamnun bo'lib yurdim.

paras.en: Even now, so many years later, all this is somehow a very evil memory. I have many evil memories now, but ... Hadn't I better end my "Notes" here? I believe I made a mistake in beginning to write them, anyway I have felt ashamed all the time I've been writing this story; so it's hardly literature so much as a corrective punishment. Why, to tell long stories, showing how I have spoiled my life through morally rotting in my corner, through lack of fitting environment, through divorce from real life, and rankling spite in my underground world, would certainly not be interesting; a novel needs a hero, and all the traits for an anti-hero are expressly gathered together here, and what matters most, it all produces an unpleasant impression, for we are all divorced from life, we are all cripples, every one of us, more or less.
paras.uz: Hatto hozir, shuncha yildan keyin ham, bularning hammasi qandaydir juda yomon xotira. Hozir menda ko'p yomon xotiralar bor, lekin... «Qaydlarim»ni shu yerda tugatganim yaxshi emasmi? Menimcha, ularni yozishni boshlab xato qildim, har holda, bu hikoyani yozayotgan butun vaqt davomida uyaldim; demak, bu adabiyotdan ko'ra ko'proq tuzatuvchi jazo. Axir burchagimda axloqan chirib, munosib muhitning yo'qligi, haqiqiy hayotdan uzilish va yer osti dunyomdagi zirqirovchi g'araz tufayli hayotimni qanday buzganimni ko'rsatuvchi uzun hikoyalar aytish, albatta, qiziq bo'lmasdi; romanga qahramon kerak, bu yerda esa antiqahramon uchun barcha xususiyatlar ataylab yig'ilgan va eng muhimi, bularning hammasi yoqimsiz taassurot qoldiradi, chunki hammamiz hayotdan uzilganmiz, hammamiz mayibmiz, har birimiz ozmi-ko'pmi.

paras.en: We are so divorced from it that we feel at once a sort of loathing for real life, and so cannot bear to be reminded of it. Why, we have come almost to looking upon real life as an effort, almost as hard work, and we are all privately agreed that it is better in books. And why do we fuss and fume sometimes? Why are we perverse and ask for something else? We don't know what ourselves. It would be the worse for us if our petulant prayers were answered. Come, try, give any one of us, for instance, a little more independence, untie our hands, widen the spheres of our activity, relax the control and we ... Yes, I assure you ... We should be begging to be under control again at once. I know that you will very likely be angry with me for that, and will begin shouting and stamping.
paras.uz: Biz undan shunchalik uzilganmizki, darhol haqiqiy hayotga qandaydir jirkanish his qilamiz va shuning uchun bizga u haqda eslatilishiga chiday olmaymiz. Axir biz haqiqiy hayotga deyarli mashaqqat, deyarli og'ir mehnat sifatida qarash darajasiga yetganmiz va hammamiz ichimizda kitoblarda yaxshiroq, deb kelishganmiz. Nega biz ba'zan bezovta bo'lamiz va jahl qilamiz? Nega biz injiqlik qilib, boshqa narsa so'raymiz? Nima ekanini o'zimiz ham bilmaymiz. Agar injiq duolarimiz ijobat bo'lsa, bizga yomonroq bo'lardi. Qani, sinab ko'ring, masalan, har birimizga biroz ko'proq mustaqillik bering, qo'limizni yeching, faoliyat doiramizni kengaytiring, nazoratni bo'shating, biz esa... ha, sizni ishontiraman... darhol yana nazorat ostida bo'lishni so'rab yolvorardik. Bilaman, siz, ehtimol, buning uchun mendan jahlingiz chiqib, qichqirib, oyoq tepa boshlaysiz.

paras.en: Speak for yourself, you will say, and for your miseries in your underground holes, and don't dare to say all of us—excuse me, gentlemen, I am not justifying myself with that "all of us." As for what concerns me in particular I have only in my life carried to an extreme what you have not dared to carry halfway, and what's more, you have taken your cowardice for good sense, and have found comfort in deceiving yourselves. So that perhaps, after all, there is more life in me than in you. Look into it more carefully! Why, we don't even know what living means now, what it is, and what it is called? Leave us alone without books and we shall be lost and in confusion at once. We shall not know what to join on to, what to cling to, what to love and what to hate, what to respect and what to despise.
paras.uz: O'zingiz va yer osti inlaringizdagi baxtsizliklaringiz uchun gapiring, deysiz, va «hammamiz» deyishga jur'at etmang — kechirasiz, janoblar, men o'zimni bu «hammamiz» bilan oqlamayapman. Shaxsan menga kelsak, men hayotimda faqat siz yarmigacha olib borishga jur'at etmagan narsani chekkaga olib bordim, buning ustiga siz qo'rqoqligingizni sog'lom fikr deb qabul qildingiz va o'zingizni aldashdan tasalli topdingiz. Shunday qilib, balki, oxir-oqibat, menda sizdagidan ko'proq hayot bordir. Diqqatliroq qarang! Axir biz hozir yashash nima ekanini, u nima va u qanday ataladi — buni ham bilmaymiz. Bizni kitoblarsiz yolg'iz qoldiring, biz darhol adashib, sarosimaga tushamiz. Nimaga qo'shilishni, nimaga yopishishni, nimani sevishni va nimadan nafratlanishni, nimani hurmat qilishni va nimani mensimaslikni bilmay qolamiz.

paras.en: We are oppressed at being men—men with a real individual body and blood, we are ashamed of it, we think it a disgrace and try to contrive to be some sort of impossible generalised man. We are stillborn, and for generations past have been begotten, not by living fathers, and that suits us better and better. We are developing a taste for it. Soon we shall contrive to be born somehow from an idea. But enough; I don't want to write more from "Underground."
paras.uz: Biz odam bo'lishdan — haqiqiy, o'ziga xos tana va qonga ega odam bo'lishdan ezilamiz, bundan uyalamiz, buni sharmandalik deb hisoblaymiz va qandaydir imkonsiz umumlashgan odam bo'lishga urinamiz. Biz o'lik tug'ilganmiz va avlodlar davomida tirik otalardan tug'ilmayapmiz va bu bizga tobora ko'proq yoqadi. Biz bunga did orttiryapmiz. Tez orada qandaydir tarzda g'oyadan tug'ilishni o'ylab topamiz. Lekin bas; men «Yer osti»dan boshqa yozishni istamayman.

paras.en: [The notes of this paradoxalist do not end here, however. He could not refrain from going on with them, but it seems to us that we may stop here.]
paras.uz: [Biroq bu paradoksalistning qaydlari shu yerda tugamaydi. U ularni davom ettirishdan o'zini tiya olmadi, lekin bizningcha, shu yerda to'xtasak bo'ladi.]

chapters.recap_uz: Hikoyachi Lizaning qo'liga g'araz bilan pul tiqadi. U ketgach, stolda g'ijimlangan besh rubllikni ko'radi. Qorda uning ortidan yuguradi, lekin to'xtaydi: «arzon baxtmi yoki yuksak azoblarmi?» U Lizani boshqa hech qachon ko'rmaydi. Yakunda u hammamiz hayotdan uzilgan «o'lik tug'ilganlar» ekanimizni aytadi va qaydlarini to'xtatadi.
